title: fix(metrics): select MeanAverageRecall targets before copying
body:
## Description

`MeanAverageRecall` deep-copies the entire target `Detections` before filtering each COCO size range. That copies masks that will be discarded and can raise `TypeError` if unused image metadata contains a non-copyable object, such as a lock.

Compute the same inclusive area ranges from the original targets, then slice the matching rows on a shallow copy. The selected fields stay aligned, including masks, class IDs, and per-row data. This keeps the original mask values and avoids reissuing construction warnings for previously accepted non-bool masks.

## Testing

- Both metadata cases fail on `develop` with `TypeError: cannot pickle '_thread.lock' object` and pass with the fix. Separate BOXES and MASKS checks treat extra warnings as errors and confirm the behavior of accepted legacy masks.
- On a fixture of eight images with four dense target masks each, the size-filter path went from 24 full target-mask copies to zero, with identical recall scores. Selected rows still require storage.
- Ran the full test suite twice: 6,741 passed and 281 skipped each time. The mAR tests also passed with OpenCV installed. `pre-commit run --all-files` passed on both runs.

- [x] Added regression tests and ran the full suite locally
- [x] Added an Unreleased changelog entry

title: fix(utils): keep exact fitted size in `resize_image` and `letterbox_image`
body:
## Description

`sv.resize_image` with `keep_aspect_ratio=True` calculates the fitted axis from a float ratio: `int(resolution_wh[0] / image_ratio)`. The ratio is inexact, so the result can land just below a whole number, and `int()` drops 1 pixel. `640 / (640 / 427)` is `426.99999999999994`, so a 640x427 image fitted into 640x640 becomes 640x426.

`sv.letterbox_image` uses this function. So a 640x427 image letterboxed to 640x640 is resampled to 640x426 and then padded. The width already fits, so the image should only be padded. 640x427 is a common image size in COCO.

```python
import numpy as np

import supervision as sv

image = np.random.default_rng(0).integers(0, 256, size=(427, 640, 3), dtype=np.uint8)

print(sv.resize_image(image, (640, 427), keep_aspect_ratio=True).shape)
print(sv.resize_image(image, (640, 640), keep_aspect_ratio=True).shape)

letterboxed = sv.letterbox_image(image, (640, 640))
print(np.array_equal(letterboxed[106:533], image))
# develop:
# (426, 640, 3)
# (426, 640, 3)
# False
# this PR:
# (427, 640, 3)
# (427, 640, 3)
# True
```

The first line resizes an image to its own resolution, and it still loses a row.

## Motivation and Context

The error occurs only when the exact fitted size is a whole number. That is the case for a target with the image's aspect ratio (its own size, 2x, half size) and for a target whose long side equals the image's long side. These are the most common letterbox calls. On `develop`:

- Resizing to its own resolution changes the shape for 598 of the 14,400 sizes from 1x1 to 120x120.
- For images 640 pixels wide, letterboxing to 640x640 resamples 22 of the 640 heights, among them 424, 427 and 429.
- Portrait images fail too, through the other branch: 245x480 fitted into 480x480 gives 244x480.

I found this with a metamorphic check: resizing to a target with the same aspect ratio must keep that ratio exactly. There is no issue for it.

## Changes Made

- `resize_image` (`src/supervision/utils/image.py`): compare the aspect ratios and derive the fitted axis with integer products, `target_width * height // width`, instead of float ratios. The fitted axis is still rounded down and still clamped to 1 pixel (#2564), so all other fits give the same size as before.
- Docstring note: the fitted axis is rounded down, and a target with the image's aspect ratio returns exactly the target size.
- Tests: 5 cases where the exact fitted size is whole (same resolution, width already fits, double resolution, height already fits, a 1x93 strip), and a `letterbox_image` test that a 640x427 image in 640x640 keeps every source pixel.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: `6 failed`. With this change: `6 passed`.
- Sweep against an exact `fractions.Fraction` floor of the fit, 4,000 cases (own size, random targets, 1x to 3x targets): `develop` 97 wrong, this PR 0 wrong.
- In the 2,750 of those cases where the exact fit is a whole number, `PIL.ImageOps.contain` also gives this PR's size.
- 3,000 random fits from `develop` to this PR: 3 sizes change, all whole-number fits, each by +1 pixel. The other 2,997 are identical.
- `pytest` (full suite and doctests, NumPy 2.5.4, NumPy backend without OpenCV): `develop` `6737 passed, 281 skipped`; this PR `6743 passed, 281 skipped`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass, mypy included.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API (no API change; docstring note updated)
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

- Not tested with OpenCV installed. The size is calculated before `cv2.resize`, so the fix does not depend on the backend. The letterbox test needs a same-size `INTER_LINEAR` resize to copy the pixels, which OpenCV does.
- `sv.scale_image` also uses `int()` on a float product (`int(width * scale_factor)`). Its factor is a float that the caller gives, so I left it out of this PR.

title: fix(converters): prevent integer overflow in `xyxy_to_xywh`
body:
## Description

`xyxy_to_xywh` subtracts corners in the input dtype. Valid ordered signed-integer boxes can therefore produce negative widths and heights through integer wraparound:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

box = np.array([[-100, -100, 100, 100]], dtype=np.int8)
sv.xyxy_to_xywh(box)
# Before: array([[-100, -100, -56, -56]], dtype=int8)
# After:  array([[-100, -100, 200, 200]])  # int64
```

## Motivation and Context

Box coordinates can extend outside the image, so a box crossing zero can have a valid span larger than the source integer dtype can represent. The same subtraction also wraps at int64 boundaries.

This was found while investigating numeric edge cases; there is no linked issue. The output policy follows the existing integer promotion used by the inverse `xywh_to_xyxy` conversion.

## Changes Made

- Compute integer extents in int64 when all input coordinates are within a conservative safe range.
- Use exact Python integer arithmetic for extreme coordinates, then return int64 if all output values fit, otherwise float64. Compute differences before float conversion so small spans at large origins are retained.
- Preserve floating input dtypes, input arrays and empty `(0, 4)` shapes.
- Document the integer output dtype change and add an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

- On the original implementation, seven of the initial 12 new cases fail; five controls pass. Failures include wrapped signed extents and integer dtype expectations.
- Added a further uint64 control for a small span above the int64 range.
- `pytest tests/detection/utils/test_converters.py -q`: 205 passed.
- `pytest -p pytest_cov --cov=supervision -q`: 6,751 passed, 280 skipped, 48 warnings; 94% coverage.
- Configured `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: all hooks passed.
- Additional seeded comparison: 1,600 boxes across eight integer dtypes matched exact Python-integer reference calculations with the documented output conversion.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Validation used the existing isolated Python 3.12 environment with NumPy 2.3.1 and the NumPy image backend. Inherited ROS `PYTHONPATH` and automatic pytest plugin loading were disabled for test processes; pytest-cov was loaded explicitly. Focused tests and pre-commit were rerun after a test parameter formatting adjustment. No dependency or lockfile changes are included.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

Integer inputs now return int64, or float64 if any output value is outside the int64 range. Float64 may round large integer values; this avoids wraparound but is not an arbitrary-precision output format. Floating inputs keep their dtype and existing arithmetic behavior.

title: fix(json-sink): reject metadata that overwrites detection fields
body:
## Description

`JSONSink` silently replaces built-in detection fields when `detections.data` or `custom_data` contains the same names. For example, a detection with confidence `0.9` is saved with confidence `999`:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[10., 20., 30., 40.]]),
    confidence=np.array([0.9]),
)
with sv.JSONSink("output.json") as sink:
    sink.append(detections, custom_data={"confidence": 999})
```

This change rejects the conflicting batch with `ValueError` before it changes buffered rows, including for empty batches.

## Motivation and Context

The parser creates the built-in fields, then assigns metadata keys into the same dictionary without checking for collisions. The original detection values can therefore disappear without a warning. This applies the same reserved-name policy introduced for `CSVSink` in #2934 to JSON output.

Found while investigating serialization edge cases; there is no linked issue.

## Changes Made

- Reject collisions with `x_min`, `y_min`, `x_max`, `y_max`, `class_id`, `confidence`, and `tracker_id` in the public JSON row parser.
- Keep ordinary extra fields and the existing precedence of `custom_data` for shared non-reserved metadata keys.
- Add regression tests, document the error in the parser and `append`, and add an Unreleased changelog entry with migration guidance.

## Testing

- Original implementation: 30 new collision-rejection cases fail; the ordinary-metadata precedence control passes.
- Fixed implementation, `pytest tests/detection/test_json.py tests/detection/test_csv.py -q`: 108 passed.
- `pytest -p pytest_cov --cov=supervision -q`: 6,769 passed, 280 skipped, 48 warnings; 94% coverage.
- Configured `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: all hooks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Tests cover all seven reserved names from either metadata source, empty and populated batches, preservation of previously buffered rows in the saved JSON, combined conflicting names in the public parser, and normal metadata precedence.

Validation used the existing isolated Python 3.12 environment with NumPy 2.3.1 and the NumPy image backend. Inherited ROS `PYTHONPATH` and automatic pytest plugin loading were disabled for test processes; pytest-cov was loaded explicitly. The full suite ran before a test-only dictionary typing adjustment; the focused 108 tests and all-file pre-commit passed after that adjustment. No dependency or lockfile changes are included.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

Callers intentionally using a built-in name for extra metadata should rename it, for example to `calibrated_confidence`. This is a deliberate validation change; the serialized layout of accepted data is unchanged.

title: releasing `0.31.7` [rebase & merge]
body:
# v0.31.7: pycocotools-matching mAP, stricter key point and CSV inputs, and edge-case fixes for zones and dataset exports

## 📋 Summary

A fixes-only patch: mAP now matches pycocotools more closely, and several zone, key point and export edge cases stop failing.

- **MeanAveragePrecision** uses pycocotools size buckets and the COCO crowd IoU for oriented-box crowd targets.
- **PolygonZone** keeps its full mask when polygon coordinates reach their integer limit.
- Key point selection and **CSVSink** now raise on inputs they used to silently misread.
- **DetectionDataset** exports keep box area for empty COCO masks and, with simplification on, bridge more mask holes.
- The OpenCV-free `contourArea` and `convertScaleAbs` fallbacks agree with OpenCV in more cases.

Drop-in upgrade, but check the Migration guide if you compare mAP values, pass extra CSV fields or select key points with boolean masks.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### `MeanAveragePrecision` matches `pycocotools` more closely

`sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision` now puts objects in the small, medium and large buckets that `pycocotools` gives them: a prediction's own geometry (box, mask or oriented-box polygon) decides, and its `data["area"]` is ignored. Target `data["area"]` is read as float64, so an area such as `9216.0004` is no longer scored as both medium and large. With `MetricTarget.ORIENTED_BOUNDING_BOXES`, targets with `data["iscrowd"]` set use the COCO crowd IoU, so a prediction inside a crowd region is ignored instead of counted as a false positive. (#2939, #2941)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MeanAveragePrecision, MetricTarget

# A small target with a perfect prediction, plus a higher-scored medium false positive
# whose area metadata claims it is small.
masks = np.zeros((2, 128, 128), dtype=bool)
masks[0, 0:20, 0:20] = True
masks[1, 60:100, 60:100] = True
predictions = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 20, 20], [60, 60, 100, 100]], dtype=float),
    mask=masks,
    class_id=np.array([0, 0]),
    confidence=np.array([0.5, 0.9]),
    data={"area": np.array([400.0, 300.0])},
)
targets = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 20, 20]], dtype=float),
    mask=masks[:1],
    class_id=np.array([0]),
)
result = (
    MeanAveragePrecision(metric_target=MetricTarget.MASKS)
    .update(predictions, targets)
    .compute()
)
result.small_objects.map50_95  # 1.0: the medium false positive no longer counts as small
```

### Misread inputs raise, and scalar key point indexing works

`sv.CSVSink` raises `ValueError` when additional data uses a built-in column name such as `confidence` or `x_min`, instead of writing a duplicate column that shadows the detection value. `sv.KeyPoints` selection rejects a nonempty one-dimensional boolean mask whose length does not match the number of skeletons or keypoints, instead of silently selecting a subset, and a zero-dimensional NumPy integer row index combined with a keypoint list or mask now works. (#2934, #2943, #2930)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0]]), confidence=np.array([0.9])
)
with sv.CSVSink("detections.csv") as sink:
    sink.append(
        detections, {"confidence": 0.1}
    )  # ValueError: Additional data uses reserved CSV column names confidence.
```

### `PolygonZone` survives integer coordinate limits

`sv.PolygonZone` computes its mask bounds as Python integers, so a polygon whose coordinates reach their dtype limit, for example `uint8` 255, keeps its full mask instead of overflowing, raising an error or silently creating a smaller zone. (#2945)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

polygon = np.array([[0, 0], [255, 0], [255, 3], [0, 3]], dtype=np.uint8)
sv.PolygonZone(polygon).mask.shape  # (5, 257)
```

### The OpenCV-free fallbacks agree with OpenCV in more cases

The `contourArea` fallback adds the shoelace terms in OpenCV's order and reads integer points as float32, so `sv.filter_polygons_by_area` no longer flips at a `min_area` or `max_area` boundary between backends. The `convertScaleAbs` fallback scales in float32 with a single-rounding multiply-add, so values on a `.5` tie such as `95 * 1.3` round to the same `uint8` as OpenCV. (#2936, #2935)

### Labels and dataset exports

`sv.LabelAnnotator` and `sv.RichLabelAnnotator` with `smart_position=True` keep an oversized label at the frame's left and top edges, and shaped right-to-left text in `RichLabelAnnotator` keeps its leading characters at the visible right edge. `DetectionDataset.as_yolo` and `as_pascal_voc` retry a failed mask-hole seam search with traced contours, so more masks export when you simplify them with `approximation_percentage`, and `as_coco` uses box area for empty mask placeholders that have no finite stored area. (#2940, #2933, #2942)

## 🔄 Migration guide

Nothing was removed, renamed or deprecated, but a few fixes change what existing code returns or accepts:

- **Different values:** `MeanAveragePrecision` sizes a prediction by its geometry and ignores its `data["area"]`, and reads target `data["area"]` as float64, so small, medium and large mAP can move. (#2939) Oriented-box mAP on `iscrowd` targets can rise, never fall, because crowd overlaps are ignored. (#2941) `as_coco` writes box area, not `0`, for empty mask placeholders. (#2942) Oversized labels with `smart_position=True` stop at the left and top frame edges. (#2940)
- **New errors:** `CSVSink` raises `ValueError` for extra fields named like a built-in column. (#2934) `KeyPoints` selection raises `IndexError` for a nonempty boolean mask of the wrong length. (#2943)
- **Without OpenCV:** the `contourArea` fallback can flip `filter_polygons_by_area` at a boundary (#2936), and the `convertScaleAbs` fallback rounds some `uint8` results one level differently, up or down (#2935). Regenerate stored references made with the NumPy fallback.

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🔧 Fixed

**Metrics**

- `MeanAveragePrecision` puts objects in the small, medium and large buckets `pycocotools` gives them: prediction area comes from its own geometry (box, mask or oriented-box polygon), and target `data["area"]` is read as float64. (#2939)
- `MeanAveragePrecision` with `MetricTarget.ORIENTED_BOUNDING_BOXES` uses the COCO crowd IoU for targets with `data["iscrowd"]` set, so predictions inside a crowd region are ignored instead of counted as false positives. (#2941)

**Key points, zones and sinks**

- `PolygonZone` preserves mask dimensions when integer polygon coordinates reach their dtype limit, instead of overflowing. (#2945)
- `KeyPoints` rejects nonempty one-dimensional boolean selection masks whose length does not match the number of skeletons or keypoints; keypoint selection on `KeyPoints.empty()` stays empty. (#2943)
- `KeyPoints` accepts a zero-dimensional NumPy integer row index combined with a list or boolean mask of keypoints, preserving coordinates and aligned fields instead of raising `ValueError`. (#2930)
- `CSVSink` raises `ValueError` when additional data uses a built-in column name such as `confidence` or `x_min`, instead of writing duplicate columns. (#2934)

**Annotators and the NumPy fallback without OpenCV**

- `LabelAnnotator` and `RichLabelAnnotator` with `smart_position=True` keep an oversized label at the frame's left and top edges; shaped right-to-left text in `RichLabelAnnotator` retains its leading characters at the visible right edge. (#2940)
- The `contourArea` fallback returns exactly what `cv2.contourArea` returns, so `filter_polygons_by_area` agrees across backends at its boundaries. (#2936)
- The `convertScaleAbs` fallback scales in float32 with a single-rounding multiply-add, like OpenCV's fused float32 path. (#2935)

**Dataset exports**

- `DetectionDataset.as_yolo` and `as_pascal_voc` retry a failed mask-hole seam search with traced contours when simplification removes usable vertices; `as_yolo` and `as_pascal_voc` still raise if no seam is found, and `as_coco` also tries this for `iscrowd=0` annotations. (#2933)
- `DetectionDataset.as_coco` uses bounding-box area for empty mask placeholders when no finite stored area is available and no segmentation is exported. (#2942)

### 📚 Docs

- The "Edit this page" links now point at the `develop` branch. (#2944)
- The SAHI notebook shows the corrected tile size output. (#2937)
- The SAHI notebook calls `InferenceSlicer` with `overlap_wh` and no longer passes the removed `overlap_ratio_wh`, so its cells run again, and outputs from the old 2560-pixel image were cleared. (#2938)
- The `CSVSink` how-to now says that extra fields named like a built-in column raise `ValueError`, and the `snap_boxes` and `MeanAveragePrecisionResult` docstrings describe oversized boxes and the inclusive size limits.

## 🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors Pranjal Mishra, Chris Censullo and viwe-monai!

- **Pranjal Mishra** (@pmxlr8, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pranjalmishra2002/)) — matched `MeanAveragePrecision` size buckets and oriented-box crowd IoU to `pycocotools`.
- **Mohammad Sohail Shaikh** (@sohailshk, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohdsohailshk/)) — kept oversized labels at the frame's left edge and bridged mask holes in dataset exports.
- **Vlad Voropaev** (@voropaevv, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thevladvoropaev/)) — rejected `CSVSink` extra fields that shadow built-in columns and kept box area for empty COCO mask placeholders.
- **Ahmet Mert Özacar** (@AhmetMert01) — validated boolean key point selection masks and accepted scalar NumPy row indices.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-aswanth-raj/)) — kept `PolygonZone` masks intact at integer coordinate limits.
- **kevin** (@kevin9327) — made the OpenCV-free `contourArea` and `convertScaleAbs` fallbacks match OpenCV.
- **Chris Censullo** (@censullo) — corrected the tile size output in the SAHI notebook.
- **viwe-monai** (@viwe-monai) — pointed the "Edit this page" links at the `develop` branch.
- **Jirka Borovec** (@Borda, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/jirka-borovec)) — updated dependency pins and prepared the release.

*Automated contributions: pre-commit.ci, claude, Codex*

title: fix(detection): prevent integer overflow in PolygonZone mask bounds
body:
## Description

`sv.PolygonZone` can silently create a smaller zone when its integer coordinates reach their dtype limit. This 256-pixel square produces a `(1, 1)` mask and rejects a detection inside it:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

polygon = np.array([[0, 0], [255, 0], [255, 255], [0, 255]], dtype=np.uint8)
zone = sv.PolygonZone(polygon)
detections = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[10, 10, 30, 30]]))
print(zone.mask.shape, zone.trigger(detections))
# Before: (1, 1) [False]
# After: (257, 257) [ True]
```

The constructor adds its two-pixel margin to NumPy scalars in the polygon's dtype. Unsigned values wrap; signed values can become negative and raise during allocation.

## Motivation and Context

The coordinate storage dtype should not change which pixels belong to a zone. The constructor already stores the polygon as native integers, but computed its mask dimensions from the original narrow values.

## Changes Made

- Convert integer maxima to Python integers before adding the existing margin.
- Keep floating-coordinate arithmetic, polygon storage, rasterization, anchor handling and public signatures unchanged.
- Add 12 regressions covering both axes, four signed/unsigned dtypes, exact mask pixels and public counting, plus a changelog entry.

## Testing

- All 12 new cases fail against pristine production for the expected overflow or incorrect region, then pass with the fix. The rectangle's inclusive pixel extent supplies an independent mask oracle.
- `pytest tests/detection/test_polygonzone.py tests/detection/test_polygon_zone_annotator.py -q`: 51 passed.
- `pytest -q -p pytest_cov.plugin --cov=supervision --cov-report=term:skip-covered`: 7,318 passed, 15 skipped and 10 failed, with 95% package coverage and 100% PolygonZone module coverage. Fresh pristine `develop` gives 7,306 passes and the same 10 failure IDs. Four are fallback line/ellipse comparisons; six fail because the installed OpenCV 4.12 reference encoder rejects bool images. No previously passing test fails.
- 352 existing-input controls retain exact masks, stored polygons and counts across integer/floating arrays, list/tuple inputs, noncontiguous arrays, repeated triggers, empty detections, pickle and camera transforms. Nine non-native byte-order controls, boolean rejection and three negative-fractional-coordinate cases also stay unchanged. Native and fallback rasterization both pass the eight new mask-bound scenarios.
- All repository hooks pass, including mypy. Node provisioning needed a temporary stable-version pin because nodeenv cannot parse the automatically selected alpha; tracked hook configuration is unchanged. Whitespace checks pass.

Validation used Windows, Python 3.13.3, NumPy 2.2.6, pycocotools 2.0.11 and faster-coco-eval 1.8.0. `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` avoids an unrelated installed Hydra/ANTLR plugin conflict; the coverage plugin was loaded explicitly.

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally. The 10 pristine failures above remain.
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API. The existing public API and coordinate contract are unchanged.
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`.

## Additional Notes

The fix adds no full-mask copy or per-frame trigger work. Alternating local constructor medians were 4.68 to 5.04 microseconds for a 32x32 polygon and 20.24 to 20.35 microseconds for a 640x640 polygon. These are constructor diagnostics, not end-to-end inference measurements. I did not run other operating systems or dependency-floor environments locally.

AI assistance disclosure: AI-assisted development tools were used during investigation and implementation. The reported tests were run against the final diff.

title: docs: point the "Edit this page" links at the develop branch
body:
## Problem

Every docs page's "Edit this page" button (the pencil, `content.action.edit`) resolves to `edit_uri + page path` = `https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/tree/main/docs/<page>.md` — a read-only tree URL on the `main` branch.

`main` is **831 commits behind** `develop` (last commit: "bump `0.27.0.post2`", 2026-03-14) and lacks every docs page added since, so on most pages the button **404s**. For example, on the live site for [use_compact_masks](https://supervision.roboflow.com/latest/how_to/use_compact_masks/):

```
https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/tree/main/docs/how_to/use_compact_masks.md   -> 404
```

This is wrong on two counts:

1. **Wrong branch** — the docs are built from `develop`: the `git-committers` plugin in the same file pins `branch: develop`, and the published pages (e.g. `docs/how_to/use_compact_masks.md`, `docs/depth/core.md`) only exist there.
2. **Wrong view** — `tree` renders a read-only file view instead of the editor the button promises.

## Fix

```yaml
-edit_uri: https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/tree/main/docs
+edit_uri: https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/edit/develop/docs
```

The button now targets `https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/edit/develop/docs/<page>.md`, which resolves for every published page (verified 200 for `docs/how_to/use_compact_masks.md`) and opens GitHub's editor.

Verified that no other docs page, README, or notebook links to `tree/main`/`blob/main` repo files that are missing on `main` (the README's Colab badge targets `demo.ipynb`, which exists on `main`).

title: fix(key_points): validate boolean selection mask lengths
body:
## Description

`KeyPoints.select` and bracket indexing silently accept nonempty one-dimensional boolean masks whose length does not match the selected axis. For example, a one-element row mask selects the first of two skeletons instead of reporting the mismatch:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

key_points = sv.KeyPoints(
    xy=np.arange(12, dtype=np.float32).reshape(2, 3, 2)
)
key_points[[True, False]]  # valid: select the first skeleton
key_points[[True]]         # previously silently accepted; now raises IndexError
key_points[:, [True]]      # previously silently accepted for three keypoints
```

Overlong masks with trailing `False` values and mismatched all-`False` masks also passed silently.

## Motivation and Context

The boolean masks were converted with `np.flatnonzero` before checking their lengths. That conversion loses the original length, so the subsequent integer indexing cannot detect a mismatched mask. This can hide filtering mistakes. The existing two-dimensional boolean-mask path already validates its dimensions.

This was found while investigating indexing edge cases; there is no linked issue.

## Changes Made

- Reject mismatched nonempty one-dimensional boolean row and anchor masks before conversion to integer indices, using an explanatory `IndexError`.
- Preserve empty boolean masks, valid masks, the existing two-dimensional mask path, and anchor-selection behavior on `KeyPoints.empty()`.
- Add regression tests, document the error in `select`, and add an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

- Original implementation: all 32 new rejection cases fail because no `IndexError` is raised; four empty-mask compatibility cases pass.
- Fixed implementation: `pytest tests/key_points -q` — 489 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pytest -p pytest_cov --cov=supervision -q` — 6,686 passed, 278 skipped, 48 warnings; 94% coverage.
- Additional live NumPy comparison: 750 one-dimensional mask cases matched indexing outcomes on populated, empty-row and empty-anchor arrays.
- Configured `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: all hooks passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Validation used the existing isolated Python 3.12 environment, NumPy 2.3.1, and the NumPy image backend. Inherited ROS `PYTHONPATH` and automatic pytest plugin loading were disabled for the test process; pytest-cov was loaded explicitly. No dependency or lockfile changes are included.

- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

The change intentionally leaves empty boolean masks valid, consistent with NumPy indexing. It does not redefine scalar or higher-dimensional boolean indexing.

title: fix(metrics): use the COCO crowd IoU for oriented-box mAP
body:
## Description

`sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision` with `MetricTarget.ORIENTED_BOUNDING_BOXES` uses the standard IoU for crowd targets (`data["iscrowd"]`). A code comment says crowd regions are not supported for oriented boxes. Boxes and masks use the COCO crowd IoU: the intersection over the prediction area. So a prediction inside a crowd region is ignored for boxes and masks, but it is a false positive for oriented boxes. The same data then gets a lower mAP as oriented boxes than as boxes.

Repro: axis-aligned oriented boxes, so the boxes and `pycocotools` give the expected value.

```python
import numpy as np

import supervision as sv
from supervision.config import ORIENTED_BOX_COORDINATES
from supervision.metrics import MeanAveragePrecision, MetricTarget


def corners(xyxy):
    return np.array([[[a, b], [c, b], [c, d], [a, d]] for a, b, c, d in xyxy], dtype=float)


target_xyxy = [[100, 100, 140, 140], [0, 0, 64, 64]]
prediction_xyxy = [[8, 8, 40, 40], [40, 40, 72, 72], [100, 100, 140, 140]]
targets = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array(target_xyxy, dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0, 0]),
    data={ORIENTED_BOX_COORDINATES: corners(target_xyxy), "iscrowd": np.array([0, 1])},
)
predictions = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array(prediction_xyxy, dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0, 0, 0]),
    confidence=np.array([0.9, 0.85, 0.8]),
    data={ORIENTED_BOX_COORDINATES: corners(prediction_xyxy)},
)
for target in (MetricTarget.BOXES, MetricTarget.ORIENTED_BOUNDING_BOXES):
    result = MeanAveragePrecision(metric_target=target).update(predictions, targets).compute()
    print(target.value, round(result.map50_95, 4), round(result.map50, 4))
# develop:
# boxes 0.6 1.0
# obb 0.3333 0.3333
# this PR:
# boxes 0.6 1.0
# obb 0.6 1.0
```

`pycocotools` gives 0.6 and 1.0 for these boxes.

## Motivation and Context

Crowd targets come from COCO-style data: `sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco` stores `data["iscrowd"]`. The same rule must hold for all metric targets, or oriented-box scores cannot be compared with box scores. `MeanAverageRecall`, `Precision`, `Recall` and `F1Score` already give the same scores for axis-aligned oriented boxes and for boxes when crowd targets are present.

I found this with a random-scene check: axis-aligned oriented boxes must score exactly like their boxes. There is no issue for it.

## Changes Made

- `_oriented_box_iou_with_jaccard` (new, private, in `mean_average_precision.py`): the oriented-box counterpart of `_mask_iou_with_jaccard`. For crowd targets it divides the exact intersection by the prediction area plus `np.spacing(1)`, as `box_iou_batch_with_jaccard` does. It clips to `[0, 1]`, as `oriented_box_iou_batch` does, because intersections use float32-rounded polygons. Other targets keep the `oriented_box_iou_batch` IoU.
- `_oriented_box_pair_intersections` (new, private, in `iou_and_nms.py`): the per-pair intersection loop of `oriented_box_iou_batch`, moved out without changes. It returns the candidate pairs and their intersection areas, not a dense matrix, so NMS memory does not grow. `oriented_box_iou_batch` now calculates its IoU or IoS from these pairs.
- Tests: the crowd IoU of one partial overlap (0.5 for crowd, 1/3 for standard), a `pycocotools` parity test for axis-aligned oriented boxes with a crowd target (all 6 AP values), and a rotated crowd target with a prediction inside it.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: `3 failed`. With this change: `3 passed`.
- `oriented_box_iou_batch` output is bit-identical to `develop` (`np.array_equal`) on 1,600 matrices: IoU and IoS, self and cross comparison, float32, float64 and int64 corners, origins up to 1e6, 0 to 11 boxes per side.
- Speed, 3,000 rotated boxes, best of 7 runs, 2 alternating rounds: self comparison 0.67 to 0.72 s, cross comparison 1.10 to 1.13 s. `develop`: 0.66 to 0.67 s and 1.11 to 1.21 s. No change beyond noise.
- `pytest` (full suite and doctests, NumPy 2.5.4, NumPy backend without OpenCV): `6652 passed, 279 skipped`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass, mypy included.
- Random scenes, not added to the suite: 300 box scenes with 15% crowd targets, tied scores and sides near 32 and 96. For each scene, `MeanAveragePrecision`, `MeanAverageRecall`, `Precision`, `Recall` and `F1Score` ran on the boxes and on the same boxes as oriented boxes. On `develop`, mAP differs in 60 of 300 scenes, and 0 differ without crowd targets. With this change, 0 of 300 scenes differ for all 5 metrics.

- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API (no API change)
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

- This PR is independent of #2939 (mAP size buckets). Both touch `mean_average_precision.py` in different functions.

title: fix(annotators): keep labels wider than the frame at its left edge
body:
## Description

`LabelAnnotator(smart_position=True)` and `RichLabelAnnotator(smart_position=True)` move each label box into the frame with `snap_boxes`, which promises to prioritize the top and left edges. A label box that starts outside the frame is moved to x=0 even when it is wider than the frame, but one that starts inside it and runs past the right edge was shifted left by the whole overflow, so a box wider than the frame ended up with a negative x1 and lost the first characters of its text. The same happened for tall boxes at the bottom edge.

```python
import numpy as np
from supervision.annotators.utils import snap_boxes

xyxy = np.array([[-20, 10, 350, 50], [10, 10, 400, 50], [10, 10, 40, 300]])
snap_boxes(xyxy, (320, 240))
# before: [[  0.  10. 370.  50.]   starts outside the frame: kept at the left edge
#          [-70.  10. 320.  50.]   starts inside the frame: pushed past the left edge
#          [ 10. -50.  40. 240.]]  same on the vertical axis
# after:  [[  0.  10. 370.  50.]
#          [  0.  10. 390.  50.]
#          [ 10.   0.  40. 290.]]
```

With this change the shift for a box crossing the right or bottom edge stops at the left or top edge, so a box that cannot fit keeps its left (top) edge visible and only its end is cut.

## Motivation and Context

On a small frame (thumbnail, crop) a long label with `smart_position=True` showed its tail instead of its beginning. Boxes that fit the frame, and boxes starting outside it, are unchanged.

## Changes Made

- `snap_boxes`: limit the right and bottom shifts so x1 and y1 stay at or above 0.
- Tests: `TestSnapBoxes` covers the existing shifts and the two new cases (wider and taller than the frame, starting inside it). `snap_boxes` had no unit test in `tests/`, only its doctest.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: `2 failed, 3 passed` (`assert False` on the two boxes starting inside the frame). With this change: `5 passed`.
- `pytest tests/annotators tests/key_points src/supervision/annotators`: `855 passed, 1 skipped`.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, mdformat, mypy and codespell pass.
- Full suite on the branch: `pytest tests src` -> 7301 passed, 35 skipped.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

`snap_boxes` is only called from `_adjust_labels_in_frame`; the keypoint `VertexLabelAnnotator` does not use it.

Arabic and Hebrew lines in `RichLabelAnnotator` are right-aligned in their box, so for those a label wider than the frame now shows its end, as it already did when the box started left of the frame; keeping their start would need per-label alignment in `snap_boxes`, left out here.

title: fix(metrics): size mAP buckets with the areas pycocotools uses
body:
## Description

`sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision` puts some objects in a different size bucket than `pycocotools` does. This changes the small, medium and large mAP. There are 2 causes:

1. **Prediction area metadata.** A prediction with `data["area"]` uses that value as its area. `pycocotools` `COCO.loadRes` ignores the area of a result. It calculates the area again from the result's `bbox` or `segmentation`. An unmatched prediction counts as a false positive only in the buckets that contain its area, so the metadata moves false positives between buckets.
2. **Target areas in float32.** Target `data["area"]` is cast to float32. float32 rounds an area within about 1e-4 of 32² or 96² onto the limit. The COCO area ranges include their limits, so the target is scored in 2 buckets. `pycocotools` keeps the area as a Python float.

Repro, with `pycocotools` through `tests/metrics/coco_reference.py`:

```python
import numpy as np

import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MeanAveragePrecision
from tests.metrics.coco_reference import evaluate_detections

# 1. A medium false positive whose area metadata says it is small.
targets = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 20, 20]], dtype=float), class_id=np.array([0]))
predictions = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 20, 20], [60, 60, 100, 100]], dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0, 0]),
    confidence=np.array([0.5, 0.9]),
    data={"area": np.array([400.0, 300.0])},
)
result = MeanAveragePrecision().update(predictions, targets).compute()
reference = evaluate_detections(predictions, targets)
print(result.small_objects.map50_95, reference.stats[3])
# develop: 0.5 0.9999999999999998
# this PR:  1.0 0.9999999999999998

# 2. A target area just above 96².
targets = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 96, 96]], dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
    data={"area": np.array([9216.0004])},
)
predictions = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 96, 96]], dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
    confidence=np.array([0.9]),
)
result = MeanAveragePrecision().update(predictions, targets).compute()
reference = evaluate_detections(predictions, targets)
print(result.medium_objects.map50_95, reference.stats[4])
# develop: 1.0 -1.0
# this PR:  -1  -1.0
```


## Motivation and Context

Size-bucket mAP must match COCO, or the small, medium and large numbers cannot be compared with published results. Detections get `data["area"]` from COCO files: `sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco(..., use_iscrowd=True)` stores it. `sv.metrics.MeanAverageRecall` already reads target areas as float64 (`get_detection_areas`).

I found both causes with a random-scene comparison against `pycocotools`. There is no issue for them.

## Changes Made

- `MeanAveragePrecision._prepare_predictions`: a prediction is always sized by its box, mask or oriented box (`_content_area`). Prediction `data["area"]` is no longer read.
- `MeanAveragePrecision._prepare_targets`: target `data["area"]` is read as float64.
- `tests/metrics/coco_reference.py`: prediction `data["area"]` now goes to `pycocotools` in the result records. So the live package, not the helper, decides what to do with it.
- Tests: 6 parity tests against `pycocotools`. Prediction area metadata with boxes and with masks. Target areas just below and just above 32² and 96².
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.
- Out of scope: `EvaluationDataset.load_predictions` still keeps an `area` key that a caller gives it. `MeanAveragePrecision` now always gives it the geometry area.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: `6 failed`. With this change: `6 passed`.
- `pytest tests/metrics`: `756 passed` (`750 passed` on `develop`).
- `pytest` (full suite and doctests, NumPy 2.5.4, NumPy backend without OpenCV): `6655 passed, 279 skipped`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass, mypy included.
- Random scenes, not added to the suite: 300 box scenes and 300 mask scenes. Each scene has 1 to 3 images, 1 to 3 classes, sides near 32 and 96, 15% crowd targets and tied scores. Half of the target areas are moved to within 3e-4 of a limit, and every prediction has random `data["area"]`. On `develop`, 241 of the 300 box scenes differ from `pycocotools`. With this change, 0 box scenes and 0 mask scenes differ in any of the 6 AP values. `MeanAverageRecall` on the same scenes: 0 differences.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API (no API change)
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

- The random-scene comparison could become a seeded test in the suite. I left it out to keep this PR small. I can add it in a follow-up if you want it.

title: fix(cv2): sum contourArea fallback terms in OpenCV's order
body:
## Description

The NumPy fallback for `cv2.contourArea` computes the shoelace sum as `dot(x, roll(y)) - dot(y, roll(x))`. That gives the right area up to rounding, but not the bits `cv2.contourArea` returns, so the two backends disagree on exact comparisons:

```python
import numpy as np, cv2
from supervision._cv2._geometry import _contour_area

c = np.array([[-79.4, 13.4], [-11.1, 54.3], [22.5, 255.0], [149.9, 149.7]], dtype=np.float32)
_contour_area(c)     # 14588.169383316039 on develop
cv2.contourArea(c)   # 14588.16938331604

c = np.array([[0, 0], [16777217, 0], [16777217, 3], [0, 3]], dtype=np.int32)
_contour_area(c)     # 50331651.0 on develop
cv2.contourArea(c)   # 50331648.0
```

OpenCV reads every point as float32 (integer points included), starts from the last point, adds `prev.x * p.y - prev.y * p.x` in float64 one term at a time, and halves the sum at the end.

## Motivation and Context

The fallback is meant to match OpenCV when `cv2` isn't installed. `sv.filter_polygons_by_area` compares `contourArea` with `min_area` / `max_area`, so a last-bit difference can keep a polygon on one backend and drop it on the other. In a differential run against opencv-python 5.0.0 (3,000 random contours of 3 to 39 points, float32 `(N, 1, 2)`, int32 and float32 `(N, 2)`, both `oriented` values, 18,000 calls), the fallback differed in 6,932 calls on `develop` and in none with this change.

## Changes Made

- `_contour_area` in `_cv2/_geometry.py`: integer contours are cast to float32 first, the terms are `prev_x * y - prev_y * x` with `prev` rolled by one, and they are summed left to right with `np.cumsum` (NumPy's `np.sum` is pairwise, which rounds differently). Float64 input, which OpenCV rejects, is still accepted as before.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

## Testing

- Two new cases in `test_contour_area_matches_opencv` (the float32 and int32 contours above, compared with `==`). Both fail on `develop` and pass here.
- `pytest tests/cv2 tests/detection`: 3531 passed (I deselected `test_ordinary_suite_passes_when_cv2_is_blocked`, which needs optional packages my env lacks and fails the same way on `develop`).
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy src/supervision/_cv2/_geometry.py` clean.

- [x] Added/updated tests; `tests/cv2` and `tests/detection` pass locally (I did not run the full suite)

- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

title: fix(cv2): scale in float32 in the convertScaleAbs fallback like OpenCV
body:
## Description

The NumPy fallback for `cv2.convertScaleAbs` computes `|src * alpha + beta|` in float64. OpenCV does it in float32 for every source depth (`cvtabs_32f` with float `alpha`/`beta`), then rounds half to even. When the float64 result sits exactly on a `.5` tie but the float32 one does not, the fallback rounds the other way and comes out one higher:

```python
import numpy as np, cv2
from supervision._cv2._image import _convert_scale_abs

src = np.array([[95, 190]], dtype=np.uint8)
_convert_scale_abs(src, -1.3, -0.5)          # [[124, 248]] on develop
cv2.convertScaleAbs(src, alpha=-1.3, beta=-0.5)  # [[123, 247]]
```

`95 * 1.3` is `123.5` in float64 but `123.49999` in float32 (`1.3f` is slightly below 1.3).

## Motivation and Context

The fallback is meant to match OpenCV when `cv2` isn't installed. `draw/utils.py` calls `convertScaleAbs` on alpha and blended values, so an off-by-one there changes overlay pixels between the two backends. In a differential run against `cv2.convertScaleAbs` (opencv-python 5.0.0) over random `uint8`, `int8`, `uint16`, `int16`, `float32` and `float64` inputs, (1,800 random 4x5 arrays with random `alpha` and `beta`), the fallback disagreed in 11 on `develop` and in none with this change.

## Changes Made

- `_convert_scale_abs` in `_cv2/_image.py`: cast the image, `alpha` and `beta` to float32 before the multiply-add, as OpenCV does. Rounding and saturation are unchanged.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

Not covered: `int32` inputs whose scaled value is 2**31 or more. OpenCV's float-to-int rounding overflows there and returns 0, while the fallback saturates to 255. I left that alone.

- New `test_fallback_convert_scale_abs_rounds_in_float32_like_opencv` (tie inputs plus 200 random values, for `uint8`, `int16`, `float32` and `float64`, compared with `cv2.convertScaleAbs`). All 5 cases fail on `develop` and pass here.

title: fix(dataset): bridge holes from traced contours when simplified ones have no seam
body:
## Description

`DetectionDataset.as_yolo` and `as_pascal_voc` join each mask hole to its outline along a zero-width seam (#2703). The contours are simplified first when `approximation_percentage > 0`. On a ragged mask whose hole sits behind 1-pixel walls, simplification drops every outline vertex a straight seam from the hole could reach on foreground pixels, so `approximate_mask_with_polygons` raises and the whole export stops:

```python
import tempfile

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

import supervision as sv

rows = [
    ".......",
    ".#.###.",
    ".#####.",
    "...###.",
    ".#..##.",
    ".####..",
    "..#..#.",
    "..#.#..",
    ".#####.",
    ".......",
]
mask = np.array([[[pixel == "#" for pixel in row] for row in rows]])
root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
image_path = f"{root}/blob.png"
Image.new("RGB", (7, 10)).save(image_path)
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[1, 1, 5, 8]], dtype=float), class_id=np.array([0]), mask=mask
)
dataset = sv.DetectionDataset(
    classes=["blob"], images=[image_path], annotations={image_path: detections}
)
dataset.as_yolo(annotations_directory_path=f"{root}/labels", approximation_percentage=0.5)
# supervision.dataset.utils._SeamNotFoundError: No foreground-contained seam found for a mask hole.
```

With this change, a component whose simplified contours leave no seam is bridged from its traced contours instead. The export finishes, and the object reloads with its hole (exact mask round trip through YOLO, Pascal VOC and COCO).

## Motivation and Context

#2879 made `as_coco` catch this error because one mask must not abort the export of a whole dataset, but YOLO and Pascal VOC still raise, and COCO then writes the hole as a separate part that readers fill. On noisy 20-60 px masks the error hits 1.6 % of masks at `approximation_percentage=0.5` and 16 % at `0.75`; with exact contours (`0.0`) none of 2017 failed. The traced contours run along foreground pixels, so they keep the seams that simplification removes: bridging them never failed on 34,590 noisy masks of 5 to 300 px.

Closes #2932

## Changes Made

- `approximate_mask_with_polygons`: when bridging the simplified contours of a component raises `_SeamNotFoundError`, bridge its traced contours. Only that component is returned unsimplified; components that bridge stay simplified as before. The docstring says so.
- Tests: the helper on a ragged mask at `approximation_percentage` 0.5 and 0.75 (one polygon that fills back to the mask), and `as_yolo` / `as_pascal_voc` round trips of that mask with `approximation_percentage=0.5`.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.
- Out of scope: the COCO fallback from #2879 stays as the last resort, and `as_labelme`, which never simplifies, is unchanged.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: `4 failed` (`_SeamNotFoundError: No foreground-contained seam found for a mask hole.`), with OpenCV and with the NumPy backend. With this change: `4 passed` on both.
- `pytest tests/dataset`: `657 passed` with OpenCV and with the NumPy backend.
- `pytest tests src` (full suite and doctests, OpenCV 5.0.0, NumPy 2.5.4): `7280 passed, 35 skipped`.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, mdformat, mypy and codespell pass.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

The fallback writes that one component with all its traced points, so the object keeps its exact shape and hole but is not simplified. I considered catching the error in the YOLO and VOC writers like COCO does, but there a hole written as its own polygon becomes an extra instance (the bug #2703 fixed). Smooth masks with holes, rings with 1 to 3 px walls and blobs with speckle holes never hit this path in my tests, so their output does not change.

title: fix(key_points): support scalar NumPy row indices with multiple anchors
body:
## Description

Selecting multiple keypoints with a zero-dimensional NumPy integer row index raises `ValueError: Cross index must be 1 dimensional`, although the equivalent Python integer works:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

key_points = sv.KeyPoints(
    xy=np.arange(12, dtype=np.float32).reshape(2, 3, 2)
)
key_points[0, [2, 0]]            # works
key_points[np.array(0), [2, 0]]  # previously raised ValueError
```

This change makes the second selection work while preserving the selected coordinates and aligned fields.

## Motivation and Context

Zero-dimensional integer arrays already work for row-only selection and scalar-anchor selection. Combining one with an anchor list or array reaches `np.ix_`, which requires one-dimensional inputs. This bug was found while checking indexing edge cases; there is no linked issue.

## Changes Made

- Normalize zero-dimensional integer row arrays to a one-element array before Cartesian indexing.
- Add 16 regression cases covering `select` and bracket indexing, positive and negative rows, integer lists/arrays and boolean lists/arrays, with 3D coordinates and aligned confidence, visibility, class and metadata fields.
- Add an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

- On the original `develop` implementation: all 16 new cases fail at `np.ix_` with the reported `ValueError`.
- With the fix, `pytest tests/key_points -q`: 453 passed, 1 skipped.
- `pytest -p pytest_cov --cov=supervision -q`: 6,646 passed, 278 skipped, 48 warnings; 94% coverage.
- Configured `pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`: all hooks passed, including mypy.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Validation used the existing isolated Python 3.12 environment with NumPy 2.3.1 and the NumPy image backend. Inherited ROS `PYTHONPATH` and automatic pytest plugin loading were disabled for the test process; pytest-cov was loaded explicitly. No dependencies or lockfiles were changed.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API — not applicable; no new API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

The change is limited to integer row arrays with zero dimensions; it does not broaden the accepted index types.

title: releasing `0.31.6` [rebase & merge]
body:
# v0.31.6: Key points on empty frames, zero-shot Transformers results, and drawing on grayscale and palette scenes

## 📋 Summary

A fixes-only patch: fewer crashes on empty frames, more Transformers models that load, and annotators that draw on any scene.

- **KeyPoints** filters stop raising `TypeError` on video frames with no people.
- Grounding DINO and RF-DETR segmentation results load, and OWLv2 detections get real class names.
- `DetectionsSmoother` keeps unconfirmed tracks as separate boxes instead of one averaged box.
- Labels and images draw on grayscale, BGRA and Pillow palette scenes.
- Integer boxes no longer wrap around, and narrow-integer mask shifts no longer crash.

It's a drop-in upgrade, but check the Migration guide if you use ViTPose class IDs, YOLO-NAS confidences or compare stored outputs.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Key points survive empty frames

`sv.KeyPoints.empty()` now holds empty `class_id`, `keypoint_confidence` and `detection_confidence` arrays instead of `None`, and selecting key points from it returns an empty result. Pose connectors such as `sv.KeyPoints.from_ultralytics` return it for every frame without people, so the documented filters raised `TypeError` mid-video. ViTPose poses from `sv.KeyPoints.from_transformers` now all get class ID `0` instead of `0..N-1`, and `sv.KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas` keeps each pose score as `detection_confidence`, so `with_nms` works on YOLO-NAS poses. (#2911, #2920, #2914, #2909)

```python
import supervision as sv

key_points = sv.KeyPoints.empty()  # what pose connectors return for an empty frame
len(key_points[key_points.detection_confidence > 0.5])
# 0.31.6: 0  -> correct, an empty frame has nothing to filter
# 0.31.5: TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'
#         -> bug, the confidence arrays were None
key_points[:, [0, 1]].xy.shape
# 0.31.6: (0, 0, 2)  -> correct, no poses so nothing to select
# 0.31.5: IndexError  -> bug, selection crashed on an empty frame
```

### Zero-shot and RF-DETR results from Transformers

`sv.Detections.from_transformers` now reads results of `post_process_grounded_object_detection`. Grounding DINO results used to raise `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'cpu'`; they now load with the matched phrases as class names and `class_id=None`. OWL-ViT, OWLv2 and OmDet-Turbo keep the text query index as `class_id` and take class names from `text_labels`; `id2label=model.config.id2label` used to name them `LABEL_0`, `LABEL_1`. RF-DETR instance segmentation results requested with `return_binary_maps=True` load too. If a result has no recognized fields, the error now points to the official `rfdetr` package, whose `predict()` returns `sv.Detections` directly. (#2913, #2912, #2921)

```python
import supervision as sv

# results = processor.post_process_grounded_object_detection(...)[0]  # Grounding DINO
detections = sv.Detections.from_transformers(results)
detections.data["class_name"]  # matched phrases, e.g. ["a cat", "a dog"]
detections.class_id  # None
```

### `DetectionsSmoother` keeps unconfirmed tracks apart

Detections with a negative `tracker_id`, which some trackers use for tracks they haven't confirmed yet, now pass through `sv.DetectionsSmoother` unchanged. They used to share one history and come back as a single averaged box. Frames where only some tracks keep oriented-box corners no longer raise a merge error. (#2926, #2923)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

smoother = sv.DetectionsSmoother()
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10], [100, 0, 110, 10]], dtype=float),
    tracker_id=np.array([-1, -1]),  # not confirmed by the tracker yet
)
smoother.update_with_detections(detections).xyxy.tolist()
# 0.31.6: [[0.0, 0.0, 10.0, 10.0], [100.0, 0.0, 110.0, 10.0]]
#         -> correct, two objects stay two boxes
# 0.31.5: [[50.0, 0.0, 60.0, 10.0]]
#         -> bug, both were averaged into one phantom box
```

### Drawing on grayscale, BGRA and palette scenes

`sv.RichLabelAnnotator` annotates grayscale scenes, shaped `(H, W)` or `(H, W, 1)` or given as a Pillow grayscale image, and `sv.draw_image` draws on grayscale and BGRA scenes. Boxes and labels on Pillow palette images now come out in the colors you asked for, not black. Labels such as `0` or `False` show up as text instead of empty boxes. (#2916, #2906, #2907, #2892)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

scene = np.zeros((100, 100), dtype=np.uint8)  # grayscale frame
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[10.0, 10.0, 60.0, 60.0]]), class_id=np.array([0])
)
sv.RichLabelAnnotator().annotate(scene, detections, labels=["car"]).shape
# 0.31.6: (100, 100)  -> correct, grayscale scene annotated in place
# 0.31.5: TypeError: color must be int or single-element tuple
#         -> bug, grayscale scenes were not supported
```

## 🔄 Migration guide

Nothing was removed, renamed or deprecated, but a few fixes change what existing code returns:

- **Different values:** ViTPose poses from `KeyPoints.from_transformers` all get `class_id` `0`; use `np.arange(len(key_points))` if you used it as a per-person index. (#2914) `KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas(...).as_detections().confidence` reports the model score instead of the mean key point confidence. (#2909) OWL-ViT, OWLv2 and OmDet-Turbo class names come from `text_labels`, even when you pass `id2label`. (#2913) `xywh_to_xyxy` returns `int64` for integer input, or `float64` when a corner exceeds the `int64` range. (#2922)
- **Different rows and shapes:** `DetectionsSmoother` returns unconfirmed detections as their own rows, after the smoothed tracks. (#2926) `KeyPoints.empty()` fields are empty arrays, not `None`. (#2911) With OpenCV, `resize_image`, `scale_image` and `letterbox_image` keep `(H, W, 1)` input as `(H, W, 1)`. (#2905)
- **Different counts, colors and labels:** `PolygonZone` no longer counts anchors in `(-1, 0)`. (#2924) `ColorPalette.from_matplotlib` rounds colors like `to_hex`, so some move by one level. (#2903) Labels such as `0` or `False`, drawn as empty boxes before, now show their text. (#2892)
- **Without OpenCV:** `mask_to_polygons` returns polygons in OpenCV's `RETR_TREE` order (#2900), image writes save most non-`uint8` images instead of failing, though multi-channel non-`uint8` TIFFs still fail (#2901), and `HeatMapAnnotator` colors move closer to OpenCV (#2904). Regenerate stored references made with the NumPy fallback.
- **New error:** drawing on a Pillow palette image whose palette is full and has no opaque entry raises `ValueError` instead of drawing wrong colors. (#2907)

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🌱 Changed

- `Detections.from_transformers` suggests the official `rfdetr` package when a result has no recognized fields, and its docs recommend `rfdetr` for RF-DETR models. (#2921)

### 🔧 Fixed

**Key points**

- `KeyPoints.empty()` holds empty `class_id`, `keypoint_confidence` and `detection_confidence` arrays instead of `None`, so confidence filters no longer raise `TypeError` on frames without poses. (#2911)
- Selecting key points from an empty result, as in `key_points[:, [0, 1]]`, returns an empty result instead of raising `IndexError`. (#2920)
- `KeyPoints.from_transformers` gives every ViTPose pose class ID `0`; with the old `0..N-1` IDs, keypoint mAP against person targets scored too low and per-class `EdgeAnnotator` edges raised `ValueError`. (#2914)
- `KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas` keeps each pose score as `detection_confidence`, so `with_nms` no longer raises `ValueError` on YOLO-NAS poses. (#2909)

**Model connectors**

- `Detections.from_transformers` reads zero-shot results from `post_process_grounded_object_detection`: Grounding DINO no longer raises `AttributeError`, and OWL-ViT, OWLv2 and OmDet-Turbo take class names from `text_labels`. (#2913)
- `Detections.from_transformers` reads RF-DETR instance segmentation results with `return_binary_maps=True`, pairing binary maps with `segments_info` by position; an empty `(0, H, W)` stack gives empty masks. (#2912)
- `Classifications.from_clip` and `Classifications.from_timm` accept bfloat16 outputs, including mixed-precision inference, and return float32 probabilities for them. (#2894)

**Tracking, zones and box math**

- `DetectionsSmoother` returns detections with a negative `tracker_id` unchanged instead of averaging them into one box; when those rows carry oriented corners, confirmed tracks without corner history get their smoothed axis-aligned bounds as corners. (#2926)
- `DetectionsSmoother` returns all tracked boxes when only some smoothed tracks keep oriented corners, using smoothed axis-aligned bounds instead of raising a merge error. (#2923)
- `PolygonZone` excludes negative subpixel anchors before rounding, so an anchor just outside the top or left edge is no longer counted as pixel zero. (#2924)
- `xywh_to_xyxy` promotes integer coordinates before adding widths and heights: a `uint8` box `[200, 20, 100, 40]` becomes `[200, 20, 300, 60]` instead of wrapping its right edge to `44`. (#2922)
- `move_masks` computes slice bounds without integer overflow, so narrow integer offsets work on larger frames and no-overlap shifts with narrow or unsigned integer offsets return empty masks instead of raising. (#2918)
- `JSONSink` keeps an exception raised inside a `with` block when writing or closing the file also fails; the cleanup error is logged. (#2902)

**Annotators and colors**

- `RichLabelAnnotator` annotates grayscale scenes, `(H, W)`, `(H, W, 1)` or Pillow grayscale modes, instead of raising `TypeError` or `ValueError`. (#2916)
- Annotators draw the requested colors on Pillow palette images (`P`, `PA`) instead of other colors or black. (#2907)
- `draw_image` draws on grayscale and BGRA scenes instead of raising a NumPy broadcast error. (#2906)
- `LabelAnnotator` and `RichLabelAnnotator` draw labels such as `0`, `np.int64(0)`, `0.0` and `False` as text instead of empty background boxes. (#2892)
- `ColorPalette.from_matplotlib` rounds colors to 8-bit values as Matplotlib's `to_hex` does instead of truncating them. (#2903)

**Images and the NumPy fallback without OpenCV**

- `resize_image`, `scale_image` and `letterbox_image` return `(H, W, 1)` for `(H, W, 1)` input on OpenCV installs too, and `tint_image` and `grayscale_image` accept `(H, W, 1)` images. (#2905)
- Image writes without OpenCV, such as `ImageSink.save_image` and dataset exports, keep 16-bit PNGs and save a saturated 8-bit copy for JPEG, BMP and WebP, instead of raising `TypeError` or returning `False`. (#2901)
- `mask_to_polygons` lists polygons in OpenCV's `RETR_TREE` order without OpenCV too, and one- and two-pixel contours are `int32`. (#2900)
- `HeatMapAnnotator` colors without OpenCV follow OpenCV's float32 HSV-to-BGR arithmetic instead of coming out one level off. (#2904)
- `create_batches` yields each full batch before consuming the next item, so stopping early leaves the rest of the source intact. (#2893)

### 📚 Docs

- New how-to section on attaching tracker IDs back to key points in [Track Objects](https://supervision.roboflow.com/latest/how_to/track_objects/). (#2896)

## 🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors Mohammad Sohail Shaikh, Vlad Voropaev, Ahmet Mert Özacar and peterolkhov!

- **Oke Iyanuoluwa Enoch** (@Iyanuoluwa007, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/iyanuoluwa-enoch-oke/)) – drawing on grayscale, BGRA and Pillow palette scenes, selecting key points from empty results, and OpenCV-matching contours, image writes and HSV conversion in the NumPy fallback.
- **Mohammad Sohail Shaikh** (@sohailshk, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohdsohailshk/)) – kept YOLO-NAS pose scores, gave `KeyPoints.empty()` empty arrays, and kept unconfirmed tracks out of `DetectionsSmoother` averaging.
- **NIKHIL** (@Nikhi00718, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikhil-v-engineer)) – loaded zero-shot and RF-DETR segmentation results in `from_transformers` and fixed ViTPose class IDs.
- **Vlad Voropaev** (@voropaevv, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thevladvoropaev/)) – fixed `DetectionsSmoother` on mixed oriented-box tracks and `PolygonZone` edge anchors.
- **Mohammad Hijjawi** (@MohammadHijjawi97, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohammadhijjawi)) – drew falsy labels as text and rounded Matplotlib palette colors like `to_hex`.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-aswanth-raj/)) – accepted bfloat16 classification outputs and fixed overflow in `move_masks`.
- **Devulapalli Naga Sri Vaishnavi** (@Vaishnavi220506, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/vaishnavi-d-9a42a9374)) – kept `with` block errors in `JSONSink` and made `create_batches` stop consuming early.

title: fix(smoother): leave unconfirmed tracks with a negative tracker_id unsmoothed
body:
## Description

Trackers give tracks they have not confirmed yet a negative `tracker_id`, and several different objects can share it. `sv.DetectionsSmoother` keeps one history per `tracker_id`, so every unconfirmed detection of a frame goes into the same history. They come back as a single row whose box is the average of unrelated boxes:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

smoother = sv.DetectionsSmoother(length=3)
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10], [100, 100, 110, 110], [200, 0, 210, 10]], dtype=float),
    tracker_id=np.array([-1, -1, 7]),
)
result = smoother.update_with_detections(detections)
print(len(detections), len(result))          # 3 2
print(result.xyxy[result.tracker_id == -1])  # [[50. 50. 60. 60.]]
```

The two objects at `x=0` and `x=100` become one box at `x=50`, and one detection disappears. With this change the result has 3 rows: the confirmed track smoothed as before, then the two unconfirmed detections unchanged.

## Motivation and Context

The smoother's own example filters `detections.tracker_id != -1` first, but a pipeline that forgets it, or keeps unconfirmed tracks on purpose, silently loses detections and draws boxes where nothing is. `LineZone.trigger` ignores negative IDs (#2623); `TraceAnnotator` skips `-1` tracks itself (#2586, so users do not need to filter them first); `ColorLookup.TRACK` draws them in `PENDING_TRACK_COLOR`. supervision expects pending tracks to reach annotators, and the documented filter keeps working, but a smoother should not silently change the row count. The smoother still pools them.

Closes #2925

## Changes Made

- `DetectionsSmoother.update_with_detections`: detections with `tracker_id < 0` are kept out of the per-track history and are returned unchanged after the smoothed tracks. The docstring says so.
- If the smoothed tracks lost their oriented corners (mixed history), the unconfirmed rows drop them too, so `Detections.merge` still sees the same data keys.
- Tests: unconfirmed boxes come back unchanged and unmerged, leave no history, a frame with only unconfirmed detections passes through equal to its input, the oriented-corner case, and a confidence-less unconfirmed row beside a track that has confidence.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.
- Out of scope: dropping unconfirmed detections (the caller decides that, as the docs example does) and the `LineZone` / `TraceAnnotator` code.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: `4 failed, 66 passed` in `tests/detection/tools/test_smoother.py` (e.g. `assert [-1, 7] == [7, -1, -1]`). With this change: `70 passed`.
- `pytest tests src` (full suite and doctests, OpenCV 5.0.0.93, NumPy 2.5.4): `7245 passed, 35 skipped` (before the last test; detection folder + doctests re-run after: `2740 passed, 2 skipped`).
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, mypy, mdformat, codespell and the doctest fence check pass.

body:
## Description

`sv.xywh_to_xyxy(np.array([[200, 20, 100, 40]], dtype=np.uint8))` currently returns `[200, 20, 44, 60]`: addition wraps before the result is stored. The resulting crop is empty and IoU against `[200, 20, 300, 60]` is zero. This change preserves the expected 100-pixel width.

title: fix(key_points): select keypoints from empty results without raising
body:
## Description

Selecting joints with `key_points[:, [0, 1]]`, the pattern shown in the `KeyPoints.__getitem__` docs, raises `IndexError` on a frame with no poses:

```python
import supervision as sv

# what the pose connectors return for a frame without poses
key_points = sv.KeyPoints.empty()

key_points[:, [0, 1]]  # IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 0
```

So a pipeline that keeps certain joints crashes on the first empty frame of a video. It is the same situation as the confidence filters fixed in #2911.

`KeyPoints.empty()` has `xy` of shape `(0, 0, 2)`, so there is no keypoint axis for the selector to index.

**Fix** (in `KeyPoints.select`): when the object has neither skeletons nor a keypoint axis, the keypoint selector is ignored and the result stays empty. An empty object that does have a keypoint axis, such as `(0, 17, 2)`, already worked and is unchanged, and so is out-of-range indexing on non-empty objects.

## Type of change

title: fix(detection): prevent integer offset overflow when moving masks
body:
## Description

`sv.move_masks` raises on an ordinary frame when the offset uses a narrow integer dtype. For example, this raises `OverflowError: Python integer 640 out of bounds for int8` on current `develop`:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

masks = np.zeros((1, 480, 640), dtype=bool)
masks[0, 20:25, 40:45] = True
sv.move_masks(masks, np.array([1, 2], dtype=np.int8), (640, 480)).sum()
```

The expected foreground count is `25`. NumPy performs the slice-bound arithmetic in the offset's dtype, which cannot hold the frame width. Negative signed limits and unsigned shifts past the frame can also overflow.

## Motivation and Context

The dense-mask path in `move_detections` reaches the same helper, while its compact-mask path already handles the same move correctly. An offset's storage dtype should not limit the frame dimensions or change which mask pixels survive clipping.

## Changes Made

- Extract Python integer scalars for integer offsets and frame dimensions before computing slice bounds.
- Keep the existing clipping algorithm, output allocation and input immutability. Floating offsets keep their existing errors rather than being truncated.
- Add focused cases for larger frames, boundary shifts, floating offsets and NumPy frame dimensions, plus an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

- Ten regressions fail against pristine production code for the expected integer arithmetic errors and pass with this change. Eight new compatibility cases also pass on pristine code.
- Mask, box and inference-slicer modules: **279 passed**.
- Full suite with coverage: **7,131 passed, 15 skipped, four failed**, with 95% overall coverage. Pristine `develop` gives 7,113 passes and the same four failures: clipped/random thick-line and thin/random ellipse fallback comparisons in `tests/cv2/test_drawing.py`.
- 165 existing-input comparisons retain exact output bytes; six floating-offset errors stay unchanged. All 1,088 boundary cases match an independent pixel-coordinate oracle. Three dense/compact `move_detections` controls agree exactly.
- All repository hooks pass. Only Node environment provisioning needed a temporary stable-version pin because nodeenv cannot parse the automatically selected alpha version; the tracked hook configuration is unchanged.

Commands use Python 3.13.3 with NumPy 2.2.6. `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` avoids an unrelated installed Hydra/ANTLR plugin conflict; the coverage plugin is loaded explicitly for the full run.

title: fix(annotators): draw rich labels on grayscale scenes
body:
## Description

`sv.RichLabelAnnotator` raises on grayscale scenes, while `sv.LabelAnnotator` and the other annotators draw on them:

| scene | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `(H, W)` array, Pillow `L` or `1` | `TypeError: color must be int or single-element tuple` | label drawn |
| Pillow `LA` | `TypeError: color must be int, or tuple of one or two elements` | label drawn, opaque |
| Pillow `I`, `I;16` | `TypeError: color must be int or single-element tuple` | label drawn, scaled to the 16-bit range |
| Pillow `F` | `TypeError: must be real number, not tuple` | label drawn |
| `(H, W, 1)` array | `ValueError: Expected shape (H,W), (H,W,3), or (H,W,4)` | label drawn, shape kept |

`_draw_labels` always passed an RGB tuple to `ImageDraw`, which grayscale modes reject.

**Fix:**

- The new `_pillow_fill` in `src/supervision/annotators/core.py` returns a fill valid for the scene's mode. Grayscale takes the blue channel, as `_color_for_canvas` does, so rich labels match what `sv.LabelAnnotator` draws on the same scene. `I` and `I;16` scale it by 257, as `_paste_annotated_pixels` does.
- `ensure_pil_image_for_class_method` converts an `(H, W, 1)` array through a view without the singleton axis and writes the result back into it.

RGB and RGBA scenes, including right-to-left text through `khatt`, get the same fill as before.

title: fix(key_points): give every ViTPose pose class ID 0 in `from_transformers`
body:
## Description

`sv.KeyPoints.from_transformers` gives each ViTPose pose of an image its own class, `0..N-1`, so class-aware code treats the people in one image as different categories.

```python
# RT-DETR person boxes -> ViTPose, as in the `from_transformers` docstring example
pose_results = pose_processor.post_process_pose_estimation(outputs, boxes=[boxes])
key_points = sv.KeyPoints.from_transformers(pose_results[0])
key_points.class_id                                   # array([0, 1, 2, 3])
len(key_points[key_points.class_id == 0])             # 1 of 4 people

targets = sv.KeyPoints(xy=key_points.xy, class_id=np.zeros(len(key_points), dtype=int))
metric = sv.metrics.KeyPointMeanAveragePrecision()
metric.update(key_points, targets)
metric.compute().map50_95                             # 0.257 for poses identical to the targets

sv.EdgeAnnotator(edges={0: Skeleton.COCO.value}).annotate(scene, key_points)
# ValueError: No edges defined for class_id=1.
```

Keypoint mAP matches predictions to targets of the same class, so only the pose numbered 0 can match a person target and four perfect poses score 0.257 instead of 1.0. `EdgeAnnotator` looks up per-class skeletons by `class_id`, so it raises on the second person.

## Motivation and Context

`post_process_pose_estimation` returns no object class: its `labels` are key point indices. The poses are for the boxes the caller passed, which belong to the one category the pose model was trained on. Ultralytics pose models give that category, person, class ID `0`. No linked issue.

## Changes Made

- Every pose from `from_transformers` now has class ID `0`.
- The docstring's `Returns` section says so, and no longer lists class names, which the method never set.
- The existing multi-pose test now expects `[0, 0]`, and an Unreleased changelog entry was added.

This changes the IDs of all poses after the first. Code that used the per-person ID as an index can use `np.arange(len(key_points))`.

## Testing

`PekingU/rtdetr_r50vd_coco_o365` person boxes into `usyd-community/vitpose-base-simple` on `bus.jpg` (transformers 5.22.2, torch 2.15.0 CPU), scored against the same poses as person targets:

| | `develop` `3be9e0e39` | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class_id` | `[0 1 2 3]` | `[0 0 0 0]` |
| `KeyPointMeanAveragePrecision` mAP 50:95 | 0.257 | 1.0 |
| `key_points[key_points.class_id == 0]` | 1 of 4 | 4 of 4 |
| `EdgeAnnotator(edges={0: ...})` on two poses | `ValueError` | draws |

- Updated test on clean `develop`: 1 failed (`[0, 1]` instead of `[0, 0]`).
- `uv run pytest tests/key_points -q`: 427 passed, 1 skipped.
- `uv run pytest src tests --cov=supervision -q --tb=short`: 6,503 passed, 248 skipped, 94% coverage; clean base: 6,503 passed, 248 skipped.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: passed (with `SKIP=prettier`: its Node download fails on this machine, and no YAML or TOML file changed).
- Checked implementation commit `f326ee3fd`.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

The sequential IDs had a test (`test_multiple_poses_are_stacked_with_sequential_class_ids`, which I added in #2671). That test recorded the existing output rather than a requirement: the key point annotators do not color by class, so the per-person IDs had no visible use.

`None` was the other option, as `from_mediapipe` uses for poses without handedness. I chose `0` because `EdgeAnnotator` with per-class `edges` also raises on `None`, and `as_detections()` would give detections that `BoxAnnotator`'s default class color lookup rejects.

Validation used Windows, Python 3.13, NumPy 2.3.1, and the fallback image backend.
