title: fix(detection): read zero-shot detections from `from_transformers`
body:
## Description

`sv.Detections.from_transformers` raises on every Grounding DINO result, and drops the class names of the other zero-shot detectors.

```python
import torch
import supervision as sv
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoModelForZeroShotObjectDetection, AutoProcessor

processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("IDEA-Research/grounding-dino-tiny")
model = AutoModelForZeroShotObjectDetection.from_pretrained("IDEA-Research/grounding-dino-tiny")
image = Image.open("bus.jpg")
inputs = processor(images=image, text=[["a person", "a bus"]], return_tensors="pt")
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)
result = processor.post_process_grounded_object_detection(
    outputs, inputs.input_ids, threshold=0.4, text_threshold=0.3,
    target_sizes=[(image.height, image.width)],
)[0]

sv.Detections.from_transformers(result)
# AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'cpu'
```

`post_process_grounded_object_detection` names each detection in `text_labels`. Grounding DINO repeats those phrases in `labels` as a list of strings, and `process_transformers_detection_result` called `.cpu()` on it. OWLv2 and OmDet-Turbo put the index of the matched text query in `labels`, so they load, but `text_labels` was ignored: with no `id2label` the detections had no `class_name`, and with the documented `id2label=model.config.id2label` they were named `LABEL_0`, `LABEL_1`.

## Motivation and Context

Grounding DINO, OWLv2 and OmDet-Turbo are the Transformers zero-shot detectors, and `from_transformers` is the documented way to bring Transformers results into supervision. No linked issue.

## Changes Made

- Class names come from `text_labels` when the result has them, in preference to `id2label`.
- Integer `labels` (OWL-ViT, OWLv2, OmDet-Turbo) remain the class IDs, so a detection's `class_id` is the index of its text query.
- Phrase `labels` (Grounding DINO) give `class_id=None`, as Florence-2 `<OD>` results do, since the model reports phrases rather than indices. Phrase `labels` without `text_labels`, as Transformers returned them before `text_labels` was added, still become the class names.
- Grounding DINO's `labels` entry is read with `dict.get`, which skips the `FutureWarning` its result dict raises when `labels` is read.
- Closed-set results (DETR, RT-DETR, YOLOS) are unchanged.
- Docstring note in `from_transformers`, and an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

Real models (transformers 5.22.2, torch 2.15.0 CPU, `bus.jpg`), `from_transformers(result, id2label=model.config.id2label)`:

| Model | `develop` `3be9e0e39` | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IDEA-Research/grounding-dino-tiny` | `AttributeError`, plus the `labels` `FutureWarning` | 4 detections, `class_id=None`, names `['a bus', 'a person', 'a person', 'a person']`, no warning |

title: fix(detection): read RF-DETR binary instance maps in `from_transformers`
body:
## Description

`sv.Detections.from_transformers` raises on RF-DETR instance segmentation results requested with `return_binary_maps=True`:

```python
import torch
import supervision as sv
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, RfDetrForInstanceSegmentation

processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained("Roboflow/rf-detr-seg-nano")
model = RfDetrForInstanceSegmentation.from_pretrained("Roboflow/rf-detr-seg-nano")
image = Image.open("bus.jpg")
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt"))
result = processor.post_process_instance_segmentation(
    outputs, threshold=0.5, target_sizes=[(image.height, image.width)],
    return_binary_maps=True,
)[0]
# result["segmentation"].shape == (5, 1080, 810); segment ids are [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

sv.Detections.from_transformers(result, id2label=model.config.id2label)
# IndexError: index 5 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 5
```

With `return_binary_maps=True`, the post-processor stacks one binary map per kept instance in `segments_info` order. `process_transformers_v5_semantic_or_instance_segmentation_result` indexed that stack with each segment's `id`. That only matches the position when ids start at 0, as in Mask2Former and MaskFormer. RF-DETR numbers its segments from 1, so every RF-DETR result with at least one instance raised.

## Motivation and Context

`return_binary_maps=True` is how RF-DETR's Transformers processor returns overlapping instance masks, matching the output of the `rfdetr` package; the default segment-id map loses pixels where instances overlap. No linked issue.

## Changes Made

- Take the k-th binary map for the k-th `segments_info` entry instead of indexing by segment id. Mask2Former and MaskFormer results are unchanged, since their ids equal their positions.
- An empty `(0, H, W)` binary-map stack now gives `(0, H, W)` masks. Previously the mask shape was built from all three axes, giving a four-dimensional array that failed in `mask_to_xyxy`.
- The binary-map test runs with segment ids from 0 and from 1, plus an empty-stack test, and an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

`Roboflow/rf-detr-seg-nano` on `bus.jpg` (transformers 5.22.2, torch 2.15.0 CPU):

- `develop` `3be9e0e39`: `IndexError: index 5 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 5`.
- This branch: 5 detections (`bus`, 4 × `person`) with mask areas `[262769, 49828, 35291, 21281, 11104]`, equal to the five binary maps in order. The default segment-id map gives `[262769, 49828, 34898, 21281, 11048]`; the difference is the overlapping pixels the binary maps keep.

- New tests on clean `develop`: 2 failed (`IndexError` for ids from 1, `ValueError` for the empty stack).
- `uv run pytest tests/detection/tools/test_transformers.py tests/detection/test_from_adapters.py -q`: 73 passed.
- `uv run pytest src tests --cov=supervision -q --tb=short`: 6,505 passed, 248 skipped, 94% coverage; clean base: 6,503 passed, 248 skipped.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: passed (with `SKIP=prettier`: its Node download fails on this machine, and no YAML or TOML file changed).
- Checked implementation commit `5270dc6a7`.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

Mask2Former, MaskFormer and RF-DETR are the Transformers models whose `post_process_instance_segmentation` accepts `return_binary_maps`; all three append each map and its `segments_info` entry in the same loop iteration, which is the ordering this relies on. A count mismatch between maps and entries would still be rejected by the `Detections` length check.

Validation used Windows, Python 3.13, NumPy 2.3.1, and the fallback image backend.

title: fix(key_points): give KeyPoints.empty() empty confidence and class arrays
body:
## Description

`sv.KeyPoints.empty()` leaves `class_id`, `keypoint_confidence` and `detection_confidence` as `None`. Every pose connector returns `KeyPoints.empty()` for a frame without poses, so the filters shown in the `KeyPoints` docs raise on such frames:

```python
import supervision as sv

key_points = sv.KeyPoints.empty()  # e.g. from_ultralytics on a frame with no people

key_points[key_points.detection_confidence > 0.5]
# TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'
key_points.visible = key_points.keypoint_confidence > 0.3
# TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'
```

`sv.Detections.empty()` holds empty `confidence` and `class_id` arrays, so `detections[detections.confidence > 0.5]` already works on an empty frame. This PR makes `KeyPoints.empty()` do the same: empty `class_id`, `(0, 0)` `keypoint_confidence` and empty `detection_confidence`.

## Motivation and Context

In a video loop, a single frame without people stops the documented pipeline (`from_ultralytics`, then a confidence filter, then annotators). The patterns that crash come straight from the docs: the class docstring's `key_points.visible = key_points.keypoint_confidence > 0.3`, and the `__getitem__` examples `key_points[key_points.detection_confidence > 0.7]` and `key_points[key_points.keypoint_confidence > 0.3]`. Since #2633 the connectors fill `detection_confidence` on frames with poses, so the empty frame is the only case where it is still `None`.

Closes #2910

## Changes Made

- `KeyPoints.empty()` returns empty `class_id` (int), `keypoint_confidence` `(0, 0)` and `detection_confidence` (float32) arrays; `visible` stays `None` (all visible) and `data` stays empty. The docstring example shows the new field.
- Test: filtering `KeyPoints.empty()` by `detection_confidence` or `keypoint_confidence` returns an empty object.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

## Testing

- New test on `develop`: `2 failed` (`TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'`). With this change: `2 passed`.
- `pytest` (full suite): `6506 passed, 247 skipped`. No existing test depended on the `None` fields; `merge`, `with_nms`, `as_detections`, slicing and keypoint mAP already treat an empty object as empty.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, mypy, codespell and the doctest fence check pass.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

- The empty object now has empty arrays even for sources that never provide a score (e.g. MediaPipe). That matches `Detections.empty()`, which carries an empty `confidence` for models without scores. `KeyPoints.merge` skips empty inputs, so merging frames is unaffected.
- `KeyPoints.empty() == KeyPoints(xy=np.empty((0, 0, 2)))` is now `False`, because the fields differ, as it already is for `Detections`. Connector tests compare against `KeyPoints.empty()` itself and still pass.

title: fix(key_points): keep YOLO-NAS pose scores as detection confidence
body:
## Description

`sv.KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas` ignores `prediction.scores`, so `detection_confidence` is always `None` on YOLO-NAS pose output. As a result, `KeyPoints.with_nms()` cannot be used on it, and `KeyPoints.as_detections()` reports the mean key point confidence instead of the score the model returned.

Minimal repro (the result has the same attributes as super-gradients' `PoseEstimationPrediction`, which always carries one score per pose):

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

prediction = SimpleNamespace(
    poses=np.array(
        [[[10, 10, 0.9], [20, 20, 0.8]], [[11, 11, 0.9], [21, 21, 0.8]]], np.float32
    ),
    scores=np.array([0.95, 0.6], np.float32),
)
key_points = sv.KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas(
    SimpleNamespace(prediction=prediction, class_names=None)
)
print(key_points.detection_confidence)        # None
print(key_points.as_detections().confidence)  # [0.85 0.85]
key_points.with_nms(class_agnostic=True)
# ValueError: KeyPoints detection_confidence must be given for NMS to be executed.
```

With this change: `[0.95 0.6]`, `[0.95 0.6]`, and `with_nms` keeps 1 of the 2 overlapping poses.

## Motivation and Context

#2633 made `from_ultralytics`, `from_inference` and `from_detectron2` keep the detection score and listed `from_yolo_nas` as out of scope. This does the same for YOLO-NAS. `sv.Detections.from_yolo_nas` already keeps its confidence.

Closes #2908

## Changes Made

- `KeyPoints.from_yolo_nas`: `detection_confidence` comes from `prediction.scores`; updated its `Returns` docstring.
- `tests/helpers.py`: `_FakeYoloNasKeyPoint` takes `scores`, like the real prediction.
- `test_from_yolo_nas_input` now expects the pose score as `detection_confidence`.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.
- Out of scope: `from_transformers` and `from_mediapipe`; ViTPose and MediaPipe results carry no per-pose score.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/key_points/test_core.py -k from_yolo_nas` on `develop` with the updated test: `1 failed, 1 passed` (`assert KeyPoints(...) == KeyPoints(...)`, `detection_confidence` is `None`). With this change: `2 passed`.
- `pytest` (full suite): `6504 passed, 247 skipped`.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, mypy, codespell and the doctest fence check pass.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

`prediction.scores` is read directly, because it is a required field of `PoseEstimationPrediction` (unlike `labels`, which the connector already treats as optional).

title: fix(utils): draw annotator colors on Pillow palette scenes
body:
## Description

Annotators drew the wrong colors on Pillow palette images (mode `P`, such as indexed PNGs and GIFs, and `PA`). A green `sv.BoxAnnotator` box came out black, even when the image's palette held that exact green:

| scene | palette | box color | drawn before | drawn now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P`, 2 colors | no green | `(0, 255, 0)` | `(0, 0, 0)` | `(0, 255, 0)` |
| `P`, 3 colors | contains `(0, 255, 0)` | `(0, 255, 0)` | `(0, 0, 0)` | `(0, 255, 0)` |

Annotators draw on a BGR copy of the scene, and `_paste_annotated_pixels` writes the changed pixels back with `scene.paste`. Pasting RGB into a `P` image makes Pillow convert it to its generic web palette first. The resulting indices are then shown through the scene's own palette, which gives other colors, or black when the index is past the end of a short palette.

**Fix** (in `src/supervision/utils/conversion.py`): `P` and `PA` scenes now get a patch of indices into their own palette, from the new helper `_palette_index_patch`:

- Drawn colors are added to the palette while it has room, which is what `ImageDraw` does on these images.
- Once the palette is full, or if it stores alpha per entry, a color takes the nearest opaque entry.
- Transparent entries are never used (a GIF transparency index or PNG per-index alpha), so an annotation can't land on one and vanish. A full palette with no opaque entry raises `ValueError`, since nothing drawn on it could show.
- Colors are matched in batches of 4,096, so a blurred or iconified region with many distinct colors stays within a small distance table.

The scene is still updated in place and keeps its mode, and pixels the annotator did not draw keep their index. Other modes are unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How has this change been tested

- New `TestAnnotatePalettePillowScene` in `tests/utils/test_conversion.py`: color already in the palette, color added to the palette, full palette taking the nearest entry, both transparency forms, `PA` scenes, a PNG save and reload, a palette with no opaque entry, and more colors than one matching batch. They fail on `develop` and pass here, with and without OpenCV.
- `tests/utils`, `tests/annotators` and `tests/draw` pass on both backends. The ruff, docformatter, mypy and codespell hooks pass.

title: fix(draw): draw images on grayscale and BGRA scenes
body:
## Description

`sv.draw_image` was the only draw helper that failed on grayscale and BGRA scenes. `draw_line`, `draw_rectangle`, `draw_filled_rectangle`, `draw_polygon` and `draw_filled_polygon` all accept them. On both backends it raised a bare NumPy broadcast error:

| scene | error |
|---|---|
| `(H, W)` | `operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (20,30,1) (20,30)` |
| `(H, W, 1)` | `could not broadcast input array from shape (20,30,3) into shape (20,30,1)` |
| `(H, W, 4)` BGRA | `operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (20,30,4) (20,30,3)` |

The blend multiplied the scene region by a `(h, w, 1)` alpha and added the image's three colour channels, so only `(H, W, 3)` scenes fit.

**Fix** (in `src/supervision/draw/utils.py`): the scene region is blended as `(h, w, channels)`. A new helper, `_overlay_in_scene_channels`, gives the image the scene's channel count:

- **Grayscale scene:** the scene gets the image's gray luminance (`COLOR_BGR2GRAY`), as `IconAnnotator` already does on grayscale scenes.
- **BGRA scene:** an opaque alpha is blended in too, so drawn pixels become opaque in proportion to the image's alpha and `opacity` (the "over" operator for alpha). An `opacity` of 0 leaves the scene untouched.
- **BGR scene:** the result is bit-identical to before (checked against the previous output on OpenCV).

The result is reshaped back to the scene region, since OpenCV's `convertScaleAbs` drops a single channel axis. The `scene` argument docs now list the accepted layouts.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How has this change been tested

- New `TestDrawImageSceneLayouts` in `tests/draw/test_utils.py`:
  - An opaque blue image on `(H, W)` and `(H, W, 1)` scenes gives exactly `cvtColor(..., BGR2GRAY)`, keeps the scene shape and leaves pixels outside the rectangle unchanged.
  - A 50% blend on a gray scene gives the expected level.
  - On a BGRA scene, an opaque draw sets the image colour and alpha 255, and `opacity=0` keeps both the colour and the original alpha.
  - All 5 fail on `develop` and pass here, with and without OpenCV.
- `tests/draw` and `tests/annotators` pass on both backends (458 passed each). The `draw/utils.py` doctests pass. The ruff, docformatter, mypy and codespell hooks pass.

**BGRA compositing:** on a BGRA scene the draw now uses straight-alpha "over" compositing, weighting each color by how much it shows and dividing by the resulting alpha. A translucent `(255, 0, 0, 128)` on a transparent scene stays `(255, 0, 0, 128)` instead of darkening to `(128, 0, 0, 128)`. Opaque scenes get the same result as the plain blend. New cases in `tests/draw/test_utils.py` cover transparent, translucent and opaque scenes and a fully transparent draw, on both backends.

title: fix(utils): keep (H, W, 1) grayscale images intact in image utilities
body:
## Description

Grayscale images shaped `(H, W, 1)`, which the annotators accept, were handled inconsistently by the image utilities.

**Shape depends on the backend**: `sv.resize_image`, `sv.scale_image` and `sv.letterbox_image` call `cv2.resize` and `cv2.copyMakeBorder`. OpenCV drops the trailing axis of a one-channel image, but the NumPy fallback keeps it:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

gray = np.zeros((48, 64, 1), dtype=np.uint8)
sv.resize_image(gray, (32, 20)).shape
# with opencv-python: (20, 32)
# without:            (20, 32, 1)
```

**Crash on both backends**: `sv.tint_image` and `sv.grayscale_image` convert `(H, W)` grayscale to BGR, but `(H, W, 1)` input fell through to the colour path:
- `tint_image` raised `could not broadcast input array from shape (3,) into shape (48,64,1)`.
- `grayscale_image` raised OpenCV's `Bad number of channels` error (or the fallback's `ValueError`).

`_overlay_image` already works around the same `cv2.resize` behaviour for icon crops.

**Fix** (in `src/supervision/utils/image.py`):

- `_keep_single_channel_axis` restores the `(H, W, 1)` axis after `cv2.resize` / `cv2.copyMakeBorder`, so resize, scale and letterbox return `(H, W, 1)` for `(H, W, 1)` input on both backends.
- `_is_single_channel` makes `tint_image` and `grayscale_image` treat `(H, W, 1)` like `(H, W)`.
- The `letterbox_image`, `tint_image` and `grayscale_image` docstrings now list `(H, W, 1)` input.

`(H, W)`, BGR and BGRA inputs are unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How has this change been tested

- New `TestSingleChannelArrays` in `tests/utils/test_image.py`:
  - Resize (plain and keep-aspect-ratio), scale and letterbox of an `(H, W, 1)` image must equal the `(H, W)` result with its axis kept.
  - Tint and grayscale of an `(H, W, 1)` image must equal the `(H, W)` result.
- Both test files were run with and without OpenCV: on `develop`, 6 of the new tests fail with OpenCV and 2 without; all 68 tests in the file pass here on both.
- `tests/utils`, `tests/annotators`, `tests/draw` and `tests/key_points` pass on the fallback (1251 passed). `tests/utils` and `tests/annotators` pass with OpenCV (716 passed).
- The `image.py` doctests pass. The ruff, docformatter, mypy and codespell hooks pass.

title: fix(cv2): convert HSV to BGR with OpenCV's float32 arithmetic
body:
## Description

Without OpenCV installed, `sv.HeatMapAnnotator` draws slightly different colours than with it: 1,769 pixels of a 160x120 test scene differ by one level. The heat map converts its hue mask with `cv2.cvtColor(hsv, COLOR_HSV2BGR)`, and the NumPy fallback of that conversion computes in float64 and rounds, while OpenCV computes in float32. The existing `hsv-to-bgr` test already allowed `atol=1` for this.

OpenCV's `HSV2RGB_b` (8-bit) works like this:

- It scales hue by `6 / 180` and saturation and value by `1 / 255` in float32, then picks each channel from `v`, `v*(1-s)`, `v*(1-s*f)` and `v*(1-s*(1-f))`.
- Its vector loop converts whole blocks of pixels and **truncates** `255 * channel`. On the x86-64 wheels this is AVX2 with blocks of 32 pixels per row.
- The scalar loop that handles the leftover `width % 32` pixels of each row **rounds**.

For example, with hue 1 at full saturation and value (`[1, 255, 255]`), OpenCV gives green 8 inside a row and 9 at the end of a row. The fallback always gave 9.

**Fix**: `_hsv_to_bgr` now repeats OpenCV's float32 steps. For 8-bit images it truncates whole 32-pixel blocks of each row and rounds the rest. Float32 images, which have no final rounding, now match OpenCV bit for bit; before, they matched only to within `1e-5`.

**Result on OpenCV 5.0 (Windows x86-64, AVX2):**

- Every one of the 16,777,216 8-bit HSV values, including hues 180 to 255 that wrap around, matches exactly at row widths 1, 5, 16, 31, 32, 33, 64, 100, 160, 640, 1000 and 4096, and on a non-contiguous view.
- 490,000 random float32 pixels match bit for bit.
- `HeatMapAnnotator` output now matches OpenCV pixel for pixel.

**Known limits**:

- OpenCV's Linux wheels fuse `1 - s * f` into one multiply-add (CI shows it: 777 of 5.7M uint8 values and about 6% of float32 values differ there). The Windows and macOS wheels don't, and neither does this fallback. On Linux, a few results therefore differ by one 8-bit level or about 6e-8 in float32. Before this PR, about 74% of 8-bit values in vector blocks differed.
- Builds that convert other block sizes can differ by one level in the last pixels of a row.
- OpenCV's own scalar and vector code disagree on negative float32 hues, so those are not guaranteed to match.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How has this change been tested

- New `TestFallbackHSVToBGRMatchesOpenCVExactly` in `tests/cv2/test_color.py` compares exactly against live `cv2.cvtColor`. It covers an H x S x V grid in 256-pixel rows (whole vector blocks on every build), row widths 1, 7 and 33 (scalar row ends), and the full-saturation hues `HeatMapAnnotator` uses.
- The checks allow the Linux FMA differences: at most one level (or 2^-22 in float32), and at least 99.9% of uint8 values (90% of float32 values) exactly equal. They pass on Windows, macOS and Linux CI. The `hsv-to-bgr` case now uses `atol=0`.
- On `develop`, 4 of these fail and all pass here.
- A sweep of 21 annotators with default settings, and 17 with non-default settings on BGR, `(H, W)` and `(H, W, 1)` scenes, now matches OpenCV pixel for pixel on the fallback backend.
- The `_color.py` doctest passes. The ruff, docformatter, mypy and codespell hooks pass.

title: fix(color): round matplotlib palette colors like `to_hex`
body:
## Description

`sv.ColorPalette.from_matplotlib` converted colormap channels to 8-bit with `int(x * 255)`, which truncates. Matplotlib stores many channels as `n / 255` floats that land just below the integer (`0.0902 * 255 == 22.999...`), so those channels came out one level low and the palette did not match Matplotlib's own hex codes, which `matplotlib.colors.to_hex` produces with `round(x * 255)`.

Repro:

```python
import supervision as sv
from matplotlib import colormaps
from matplotlib.colors import to_hex

print(sv.ColorPalette.from_matplotlib("Accent", 8).colors[6].as_hex(), to_hex(colormaps["Accent"].colors[6]))
print([c.as_hex() for c in sv.ColorPalette.from_matplotlib("viridis", 5).colors])
print([to_hex(colormaps["viridis"](i / 4)) for i in range(5)])
```

Before:
```
#bf5b16 #bf5b17
['#440154', '#3a528b', '#20908c', '#5ec961', '#fde724']
['#440154', '#3b528b', '#21918c', '#5ec962', '#fde725']
```

After:
```
#bf5b17 #bf5b17
['#440154', '#3b528b', '#21918c', '#5ec962', '#fde725']
['#440154', '#3b528b', '#21918c', '#5ec962', '#fde725']
```

## Motivation and Context

A palette created from a named Matplotlib colormap should draw the same colors Matplotlib shows for it. Across `tab10`, `tab20`, `Set1`-`Set3`, `Pastel1`, `Dark2`, `Paired`, `Accent`, `viridis` and `plasma`, 9 of 106 sampled colors were one level off (matplotlib 3.10.3).

## Changes Made

- `ColorPalette.from_matplotlib` rounds each channel with `round(x * 255)`, as `matplotlib.colors.to_hex` does, instead of truncating.
- Updated the `from_matplotlib` doctest: the second viridis color is now `Color(r=59, g=82, b=139)` (`#3b528b`).

title: fix(json-sink): preserve errors during cleanup
body:
## Description

When a `JSONSink` block raises while a buffered value cannot be serialized, `__exit__` replaces the original exception with the serialization `TypeError`. This makes the processing failure harder to handle or diagnose.

```python
with sv.JSONSink("out.json") as sink:
    sink.append(detections, custom_data={"invalid": object()})
    raise RuntimeError("processing failed")
```

The caller should receive `RuntimeError`, with the cleanup error logged. This follows the existing `CSVSink` behavior.

## Motivation and Context

title: fix(cv2): write non-uint8 images like OpenCV in the imwrite fallback
body:
## Description

Without OpenCV installed, `sv.ImageSink.save_image`, dataset exports and the confusion-matrix plot write images through the NumPy fallback of `cv2.imwrite` / `cv2.imencode`. That fallback hands the array straight to Pillow, so any image that is not `uint8` fails:

| image | OpenCV | fallback before this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 16-bit BGR or BGRA, `.png` | 16-bit PNG | `TypeError: Cannot handle this data type` |
| `float32` / `float64` / `int16` / `int32` / `bool` BGR, any format | 8-bit file, saturated | `TypeError` |
| 16-bit or float grayscale, `.jpg` / `.bmp` / `.png` (float) | 8-bit file, saturated | returns `False` |

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

with sv.ImageSink(target_dir_path="out") as sink:
    sink.save_image(np.full((4, 4, 3), 1000, dtype=np.uint16), "depth.png")
# fallback: TypeError: Cannot handle this data type: (1, 1, 3), <u2
```

OpenCV writes PNG as 8- or 16-bit and JPEG, BMP and WebP as 8-bit only. It converts any other sample type to `uint8` (`convertTo`: round half to even, saturate, NaN to 0) and logs "Unsupported depth image for selected encoder is fallbacked to CV_8U".

**Fix** (in `src/supervision/_cv2/_image.py`):

- `_opencv_encoder_values` applies that conversion for PNG, JPEG, BMP and WebP. Other formats, including TIFF, keep the array's type as before. Boolean images are written as 0 and 1, as OpenCV does.
- Pillow has no 16-bit colour modes, so `_encode_png_16bit_color` assembles 16-bit BGR/BGRA PNGs directly: an `IHDR`, a single zlib `IDAT` of unfiltered big-endian scanlines, and `IEND`.
- `_imwrite` and `_imencode` share the new `_save_like_opencv`. A `TypeError` from Pillow now returns `False` / `(False, None)`, OpenCV's failure contract, instead of escaping. This affects, for example, a multi-channel `float32` TIFF that Pillow cannot write.

Not changed here: reading a 16-bit colour PNG back with the fallback still gives 8 bits, because Pillow decodes it that way. Files written by this PR are read back in full by OpenCV (see the tests).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How has this change been tested

- New `TestFallbackEncoderSampleTypes` in `tests/cv2/test_image.py`:
  - **Encode parity:** for `uint16`, `int16`, `int32`, `float32`, `float64` and `bool`, in PNG, BMP and lossless WebP, at 1 and 3 channels, the bytes from `_imencode` must decode, via `cv2.imdecode(..., IMREAD_UNCHANGED)`, to exactly what OpenCV's own encoding decodes to.
  - **16-bit colour PNG:** 16-bit BGR and BGRA files written by `_imwrite` are read back unchanged by `cv2.imread`.
  - **Pillow failure:** `_imwrite` returns `False` for a `float32` BGR TIFF.
  - 33 of these fail on `develop` and all pass here.
- A wider sweep covering 8 sample types, 4 channel layouts and PNG, JPEG, BMP and WebP matches OpenCV everywhere (JPEG within one level, since the encoders differ).
- On the fallback backend, `sv.ImageSink.save_image` now writes a `uint16` BGR PNG and a `float32` JPEG.
- The `src/supervision/_cv2/_image.py` doctests pass. The ruff, docformatter, mypy and codespell hooks pass.

title: fix(cv2): return fallback contours in OpenCV's RETR_TREE order
body:
## Description

On installs without OpenCV, `sv.mask_to_polygons` lists polygons in a different order than it does with `opencv-python` installed. The NumPy `findContours` fallback returned borders in raster discovery order. OpenCV's `RETR_TREE` instead links each new border as the first child of its parent, so its list is a depth-first pre-order walk with siblings in reverse discovery order.

```python
import numpy as np
from supervision._cv2._contours import _find_contours

mask = np.array([[1, 0, 1, 0]], dtype=np.uint8)
[c.reshape(-1, 2).tolist() for c in _find_contours(mask, 3, 2)[0]]
# OpenCV:   [[[2, 0]], [[0, 0]]]
# fallback: [[[0, 0]], [[2, 0]]]  (before this PR)
```

On 2,000 random masks, 685 came back fully reversed and 1,191 more had the same contours in another order. The first polygon, and anything that relies on outline/hole order, therefore depended on the backend.

**Fix**: the raster scan now tracks Suzuki-Abe's last crossed border (`LNBD`), including step 1(b)'s update when a hole starts on an already traced pixel. Each border's parent is derived from it, and the borders are emitted in OpenCV's tree order. The tracing itself is unchanged.

**Also fixed**: one- and two-pixel contours were `int64`. They skip the SIMPLE compression that cast the longer ones to `int32`. All contours are now `int32`, as on OpenCV.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How has this change been tested

- New `TestFindContoursMatchesOpenCVOrder` in `tests/cv2/test_contours.py` compares the exact contour list (order, points and dtype) with live `cv2.findContours`. It covers single and diagonal pixels, sibling blobs, a hole touching the frame, islands inside a hole and 200 seeded random masks. 6 cases fail on `develop` and pass here.
- Separately, 9,000 random masks up to 30x30 match OpenCV exactly.
- Speed is unchanged: a 1080x1920 ring mask takes 0.05 s (0.04 s before) and a 300x300 noise mask takes 0.90 s (0.82 s before).
- `tests/detection`, `tests/dataset`, `tests/cv2` and `tests/annotators` pass on the fallback backend (3818 passed). The ruff, docformatter, mypy and codespell hooks pass.

body:
This pull request adds robust support for loading semantic segmentation results as detection objects in the `supervision` library, making it easier to work with outputs from Roboflow Inference and similar sources. The main addition is the `Detections.from_semantic_segmentation` method, which converts a semantic segmentation map (base64 PNG or array) into one detection per class id, with options for class naming, confidence, and mask format. The PR also includes thorough tests, documentation updates, and internal utilities for decoding and processing segmentation maps.

**New Semantic Segmentation Support:**

* Added `Detections.from_semantic_segmentation`, allowing users to load a semantic segmentation map (such as Roboflow Inference's `segmentation_mask`) as one detection per class id, with options for class naming, confidence masks, background handling, and compact mask representation. This method closely follows Roboflow's Workflows converter logic. (`src/supervision/detection/core.py` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c7ebb73290af86929406f9eecc9b2253482eb4ddf4d1bc9f1f1e86e9c99ccedR865-R941) `docs/changelog.md` [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-77f023b99d3d58008351d3e82fc06e6d06ba1bc2da9e41be6329b7fa4f419f05L10-R10)
* `Detections.from_inference` now raises a clear `ValueError` if called with a semantic segmentation result, guiding users to the new loader. (`src/supervision/detection/core.py` [src/supervision/detection/core.pyR823-R835](diffhunk://#diff-3c7ebb73290af86929406f9eecc9b2253482eb4ddf4d1bc9f1f1e86e9c99ccedR823-R835))

**Internal Utilities:**

* Added `decode_semantic_label_map` and `process_semantic_segmentation` utilities to decode base64 PNGs and split label maps into per-class masks, boxes, and metadata, supporting both dense and compact mask formats. (`src/supervision/detection/utils/internal.py` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7464a4e6cf087bc7e2a83526f41dfc3d151eec62fcc721914144c96b13522145R1-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7464a4e6cf087bc7e2a83526f41dfc3d151eec62fcc721914144c96b13522145R541-R679)

**Testing:**

* Introduced a comprehensive test suite for `Detections.from_semantic_segmentation`, covering base64 and array inputs, background handling, class naming, confidence calculation, compact masks, error cases, and 16-bit PNG support. (`tests/detection/test_core.py` [tests/detection/test_core.pyR3605-R3753](diffhunk://#diff-24bd34292c9b023da8b1f1e19ac238e8f05814ff8fd243773e64856d2512f117R3605-R3753))

**Documentation:**

* Updated documentation to reference the new method, clarify usage with segmentation models, and add a semantic segmentation cookbook link. (`docs/detection/annotators.md` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e1aa7c778fc25c31d827d3e63ffd4e048994cefc7e8328314eee96f675b58848R186-R191) `src/supervision/detection/core.py` [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3c7ebb73290af86929406f9eecc9b2253482eb4ddf4d1bc9f1f1e86e9c99ccedL130-R133) `docs/theme/cookbooks.html` [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-58cc09c6e5f33a41343869c14c6adc3cba6848864351244694c0990c909335f0R77-R80)

These changes significantly improve the library's support for semantic segmentation workflows, making it easier and safer to convert segmentation results into standard detection objects for further processing and visualization.

title: docs(track_objects): show how to attach tracker IDs back to keypoints
body:
## Description

The keypoint section of the object-tracking how-to tracks the boxes from `KeyPoints.as_detections()` and draws boxes and traces, but it never puts the tracker IDs back on the skeletons. Per-person pose work needs that, and the obvious shortcut, `key_points.data["tracker_id"] = detections.tracker_id`, silently assigns IDs to the wrong person:

- `as_detections()` leaves out skeletons without any usable keypoint, so later rows shift by one;
- `ByteTrackTracker` may return rows in a different order (matched tracks first).

Minimal repro with the page's tracker settings (`track_activation_threshold=0.25, minimum_consecutive_frames=1`): after two frames with skeletons A and B, a frame listing `[B, A]` gives A's ID to B and B's to A, and a frame listing `[empty, A, B]` gives A's ID to the empty skeleton.

This PR adds a short section, "Attach Tracker IDs to Keypoints", that stores each skeleton's row index in `key_points.data` before the conversion and maps the IDs back through it.

## Motivation and Context

`KeyPoints` currently has no dedicated `tracker_id` field. This recipe carries the IDs through the existing `data` dictionaries, keeping the change within the current containers and the external tracker API. Showing how to finish the route avoids a silent mismatch that tests on single-person clips would not catch. It propagates whatever IDs the tracker assigns; it does not change tracking quality or prevent ID switches.

## Changes Made

- `docs/how_to/track_objects.md`: new `### Attach Tracker IDs to Keypoints` section after "Bonus: Smoothing", with Ultralytics and Inference tabs that mirror the page's existing snippets (same model ids and tracker settings; self-contained, so no names come from earlier blocks).
- The snippet guards `len(detections) > 0`: for a frame without people, `as_detections()` returns `Detections.empty()`, which has no `row` field, so indexing it would raise `KeyError`.
- The text notes that new tracks start with `tracker_id=-1` and get an ID on a later successfully matched frame, so the final filter skips them until then.
- `date_modified` bumped.
- Out of scope: no library change and no changelog entry (documentation-only, per AGENTS.md).

## Testing

- Extracted both new code blocks from the markdown and ran them as written, stubbing only model loading/inference (`YOLO`, `get_roboflow_model`, `from_ultralytics`/`from_inference`) and `sv.process_video`, on synthetic frames: two people, rows in swapped order, an empty skeleton, a new person listed first, and frames with nobody. Every skeleton got the tracker's ID for its own box; no errors. Run with supervision 0.31.5 and with `develop` (`PYTHONPATH=src`), and with trackers 2.6.1 and 2.7.0.
- Without the `len(detections) > 0` guard, frames with no people raise `KeyError: 'row'` on both trackers versions; on 2.6.1 so do frames whose only skeleton is empty.
- `mdformat` (mkdocs plugins, repo settings) and `codespell` pass on the changed file.
- I did not build the mkdocs site locally.

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (documentation-only; no code changed)
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [ ] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skipped: pure documentation change)

## Additional Notes

- I considered proposing a helper (e.g. returning row indices from `as_detections()` or a `KeyPoints` tracker field) instead of a recipe. Given the #2290/#2291 history I kept this to documentation; happy to turn it into a small helper if you prefer.
- `as_detections()` returns `Detections.empty()` without custom data when there are no instances or no key points per instance. When the key point axis is non-empty but every point is invalid, conversion keeps the `data` fields with zero rows; the tracker may still return a fresh empty result without them. The guard handles these empty results. Aligning the empty paths in `as_detections()` may be worth a separate change; I left it out of this PR.
- Related: #2895 (CONTRIBUTING guidance for key point outputs).
- The snippet writes `row` and `tracker_id` keys into `key_points.data`, overwriting any existing keys with those names.

title: Accept bfloat16 classification probabilities
body:
### Description

`Classifications.from_timm` and `Classifications.from_clip` raise `TypeError: Got unsupported ScalarType BFloat16` for bfloat16 logits, including a timm ResNet18 run under CPU or CUDA autocast. The factories apply softmax and then call `Tensor.numpy()`, but NumPy has no native bfloat16 dtype.

```python
import torch
import supervision as sv

logits = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0]], dtype=torch.bfloat16)
sv.Classifications.from_timm(logits)
```

I widen only the resulting bfloat16 probabilities to float32 before NumPy conversion in both factories. The softmax still uses the input precision. Float16, float32 and float64 outputs, class IDs, first-batch selection and existing empty-output behavior stay unchanged. No public signature, saved model or dependency changes.

### Motivation and Context

Mixed-precision timm inference should produce classifications without requiring a separate caller-side cast. The same conversion correction covers CLIP's sibling factory.

### Changes Made

- Convert bfloat16 probabilities to float32 at the existing NumPy boundary.
- Document the returned dtype and add real-tensor precision and empty-output regressions.
- Add an Unreleased changelog entry.

### Testing

Windows, Python 3.13.3, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, NumPy 2.2.6 and timm 1.0.22:

- `pytest tests/classification src/supervision/classification -q`: 43 passed. Before the runtime correction, eight new bfloat16 cases fail with the conversion error and the other 24 new cases pass.
- A 320-case CPU/CUDA matrix covers both factories, four floating-point dtypes, contiguous/strided tensors, empty through 1,000-class outputs and gradient-bearing inputs. All pass twice per case. The 240 ordinary outputs match pristine bytes, shapes and dtypes exactly.
- Real timm ResNet18 CPU/CUDA bfloat16 autocast now succeeds. Four float16/float32/float64 controls match the pristine adapter on the same model outputs. Models use `pretrained=False`, with no weights download.

- Every repository hook passes with only the Node provisioning version pinned to 22.20.0 in a temporary copy of the unchanged hook configuration. Automatic provisioning otherwise selects a Node alpha version that nodeenv cannot parse; the repository configuration stays unchanged.

A dedicated Ubuntu/Python 3.13 job installs the CPU PyTorch wheel only in its test environment and directly runs all 32 tensor-precision regressions. title: fix(utils): yield batches without consuming the next item
body:
## Description

`create_batches` reads one item beyond a full batch before yielding it. For example, after `next(create_batches(source, 2))` on an iterator over `[1, 2, 3, 4]`, the next item left in `source` is `4` rather than `3`. If reading the next item raises, the already complete batch is lost.

## Motivation and Context

A caller may stop after a batch or consume a stream that fails or blocks while producing the next item. A completed batch should not depend on reading another item.

## Changes Made

- Yield a full batch immediately after appending its last item.

title: fix(annotators): draw falsy non-string labels such as `0` as text
body:
## Description

`wrap_text` returned an empty line for any falsy value before converting non-strings with `str()`, so `LabelAnnotator` and `RichLabelAnnotator` drew an empty background box for a label of `0`, `np.int64(0)` or `0.0` (and `False`). Non-string labels are otherwise supported since #1932.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.annotators.utils import wrap_text

wrap_text(0), wrap_text(np.int64(0)), wrap_text(0.0)
# before: ([''], [''], [''])
# after:  (['0'], ['0'], ['0.0'])

detections = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[10, 30, 60, 60]], float), class_id=np.array([0]))
scene = np.zeros((80, 100, 3), np.uint8)
annotator = sv.LabelAnnotator()
np.array_equal(
    annotator.annotate(scene.copy(), detections, labels=[0]),
    annotator.annotate(scene.copy(), detections, labels=["0"]),
)
# before: False (empty label box), after: True
```

## Motivation and Context

Passing class ids or numeric values as labels hides the label of the first class (id `0`) while every other id is drawn.

## Changes Made

- `wrap_text` now returns `[""]` up front only for `None`; other values are converted with `str()` before the empty-string check.
- Added `wrap_text` cases for `0`, `np.int64(0)`, `0.0`, `False` and wrapped `0`, and a `LabelAnnotator` / `RichLabelAnnotator` test that an integer `0` label renders the same as `"0"`.
- Changelog entry under Unreleased.

## Testing

title: releasing `0.31.5` [rebase & merge]
body:
# v0.31.5: Line counts through occlusion, the exact clipper for oriented boxes, and right-to-left labels

## 📋 Summary

Right-to-left labels, line counting that survives occlusion, and a batch of edge-case fixes across annotators, exports and the NumPy fallback.

- **LineZone** counts objects that are hidden for a few frames while they cross the line.
- Arabic and Hebrew labels render correctly with the new `rtl` extra.
- Oriented-box IoU, NMS and metrics now use the exact clipper on OpenCV installs.
- Annotating a Pillow image keeps its transparency and untouched pixels.
- Heat maps and ellipse halos now work on grayscale scenes.

It's a drop-in upgrade, but check the Migration guide if you count line crossings, score oriented boxes on OpenCV, or compare stored outputs.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Right-to-left labels with the new `rtl` extra

`sv.RichLabelAnnotator` now draws Arabic and Hebrew labels correctly on RGB and RGBA images when the new `rtl` extra is installed. Pillow only joins Arabic letters and orders right-to-left text when it's built with Raqm, and most Windows installs and many containers lack it. There, `"سيارة 0.92"` came out as isolated letters in reverse order. Lines with Arabic or Hebrew are now shaped in the label's font, using fallback Arabic and Hebrew fonts from `khatt` for missing glyphs, and right-aligned in the background box. Other image modes fall back to Pillow, with a warning that suggests RGB or RGBA when Raqm is missing. Without the extra, a one-time warning names it. (#2864)

```python
# pip install "supervision[rtl]"
import supervision as sv

label_annotator = sv.RichLabelAnnotator(font_path="NotoNaskhArabic-Regular.ttf")
annotated = label_annotator.annotate(
    scene=image, detections=detections, labels=["سيارة 0.92"]
)
```

### `LineZone` counts objects occluded while crossing

If a tracker disappears for a few frames while crossing the line, it's now still counted. By default `sv.LineZone` drops a tracker's stored side after `max(30, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` consecutive absent frames. It used to drop it after `max(2, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)`, which is 2 at the default threshold. The new `max_absent_frames` parameter sets this. Counts can rise against 0.31.4 on the same input. (#2873)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

line = sv.LineZone(start=sv.Point(0, 50), end=sv.Point(100, 50))


def detection(y):
    return sv.Detections(
        xyxy=np.array([[40.0, y - 10, 60.0, y]]), tracker_id=np.array([1])
    )


line.trigger(detection(40))  # above the line
for _ in range(5):  # occluded for five frames
    line.trigger(sv.Detections.empty())
line.trigger(detection(80))  # reappears below the line
line.in_count, line.out_count
# (0, 1)  (0.31.4: (0, 0))

# Restore the old retention:
sv.LineZone(start=sv.Point(0, 50), end=sv.Point(100, 50), max_absent_frames=2)
```

### The exact clipper for oriented boxes on OpenCV installs

`sv.oriented_box_iou_batch`, OBB NMS and OBB metrics now use the same convex clipper on OpenCV installs that the NumPy fallback uses. With OpenCV, rotated boxes with nearly collinear overlapping edges, and boxes with both sides far below one coordinate unit, could get an IoU of 0 or 1. The clipper is roughly 10x slower per candidate pair than the OpenCV call, so crowded scenes can take seconds. Oriented-box precision, recall, F1 and mean average recall also keep corner precision at large coordinate origins. (#2882, #2887)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv


def rotated(width, height, degrees, center=(200.0, 200.0)):
    t = np.deg2rad(degrees)
    u = np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t)]) * width / 2
    v = np.array([-np.sin(t), np.cos(t)]) * height / 2
    c = np.array(center)
    return np.array([[c - u - v, c + u - v, c + u + v, c - u + v]])


t = np.deg2rad(10)
a = rotated(100, 40, 10)
b = a + np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t)]) * 50  # true IoU is 0.3333
sv.oriented_box_iou_batch(a, b)[0, 0]
# 0.3333  (0.31.4 with OpenCV: 1.0)
```

### Pillow scenes keep the pixels annotators do not draw

Annotators handed a `PIL.Image` now change only the pixels they draw. A transparent RGBA or LA background stays transparent, and a 16-bit (`I;16`) or 32-bit (`I`) image keeps the depth of its untouched pixels, with drawn pixels scaled back to the 16-bit range. Before, the whole image went through an 8-bit round trip. (#2883)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from PIL import Image

scene = Image.new("RGBA", (100, 100), (0, 0, 0, 0))
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[20.0, 20.0, 60.0, 60.0]]), class_id=np.array([0])
)
annotated = sv.BoxAnnotator().annotate(scene, detections)
annotated.getpixel((0, 0))
# (0, 0, 0, 0)  (0.31.4: (0, 0, 0, 255))
```

## 🔄 Migration guide

No public symbol was removed or renamed, and nothing is deprecated. A few fixes change what existing code returns or draws:

- **Different counts:** `LineZone` keeps a tracker's side for `max(30, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` absent frames instead of 2, so `in_count` and `out_count` can rise on the same input. Pass `max_absent_frames=max(2, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` to restore the old retention. (#2873)
- **Different scores and speed on OpenCV installs:** oriented-box IoU, NMS and metrics use the exact clipper, roughly 10x slower per candidate pair. Regenerate any stored IoU, NMS and mAP references. (#2882, #2887)
- **Different pixels and files:** Pillow scenes keep unannotated pixels (#2883), `as_coco` writes mask holes joined to their outline (#2879), and the GHUM skeleton gains its left wrist to left index edge (#2876).
- **New error without OpenCV:** the `cvtColor` fallback reads float32 `COLOR_HSV2BGR` input as OpenCV does (hue in degrees, other values in `[0, 1]`) and raises `ValueError` for depths OpenCV rejects. Convert float32 HSV to that scale, or cast to `uint8`, first. (#2885)
- **Video reads:** `get_video_frames_generator` stops at the requested end instead of reading excluded frames. (#2874)

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🚀 Added

- **`rtl` extra.** `pip install "supervision[rtl]"` installs `khatt`, and `RichLabelAnnotator` then shapes Arabic and Hebrew lines in the label font, with fallback fonts from `khatt` for missing glyphs. Without the extra and without Raqm, a one-time warning names it. (#2864)
- **`LineZone(max_absent_frames=...)`.** Sets how many consecutive missing frames pass before a tracker's crossing state is dropped; values below 1 raise `ValueError`. (#2873)

### 🌱 Changed

- `LineZone` default retention goes from `max(2, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` to `max(30, minimum_crossing_threshold + 1)` absent frames, so occluded objects are counted. (#2873)
- `oriented_box_iou_batch`, OBB NMS and OBB metrics use the convex clipper of the NumPy fallback on OpenCV installs, so IoU can differ for affected pairs; expect roughly 10x the cost per candidate pair. (#2882)

### 🔧 Fixed

**Annotators**

- Annotators given a `PIL.Image` change only the pixels they draw: RGBA and LA transparency stays, and `I;16` and `I` images keep the depth of untouched pixels. (#2883)
- `HeatMapAnnotator` and `VertexEllipseHaloAnnotator` annotate grayscale scenes, shaped `(H, W)`, `(H, W, 1)` or a Pillow `"L"` image, instead of raising `ValueError`. (#2872, #2878)

**Detections, zones and metrics**

- `oriented_box_iou_batch` on OpenCV installs no longer reports an IoU of 0 or 1 for rotated boxes with nearly collinear overlapping edges, or for boxes with both sides far below one coordinate unit. (#2882)
- Oriented-box precision, recall, F1 and mean average recall keep corner precision at large coordinate origins, so perfect predictions there are no longer misses or filed under the wrong object-size category. (#2887)
- `np.sum` works on a `CompactMask`, with or without `axis`, and matches the dense mask for `dtype`, `out`, `keepdims`, `initial` and `where`; it raised `TypeError` before. (#2880)
- `Detections.get_anchors_coordinates(Position.CENTER_OF_MASS)` returns an empty `(0, 2)` array for an empty batch without masks instead of raising `ValueError`; a populated batch without masks still raises. (#2877)
- `CSVSink` keeps an exception raised inside a `with` block when cleanup also raises; the cleanup exception is logged. (#2869)

**Datasets and exports**

- `as_coco` keeps the holes of masks written as polygons with `iscrowd=0`, joining them to the outline instead of writing extra polygon parts that readers fill in; a hole that cannot be joined warns and keeps the old parts. (#2879)
- Hole bridging in `as_yolo`, `as_pascal_voc` and `as_labelme` retries top-down, so valid masks with an enclosed hole listed before its outer hole no longer raise `ValueError`. (#2879)
- COCO export computes box width, height and area with Python scalars: without a mask or stored area, a `300×300` `float16` or `int16` box exports an area of `90000` instead of infinity or `24464`. (#2867)

**Key points, video and windows**

- `Skeleton.GHUM` (in `supervision.key_points.skeletons`) connects the left wrist to the left index finger; `EdgeAnnotator` had drawn a bone from the right elbow to the right pinky on 33-keypoint poses. (#2876)
- `get_video_frames_generator` stops reading and skipping at the requested end. (#2874)
- `ImageWindow.show` draws the frame on the call that opens the window, opens at the frame's size up to the screen size without growing on each redraw, and fits frames with a one-pixel dimension. (#2881)

**NumPy fallback without OpenCV**

- `cvtColor` accepts BGRA input for `COLOR_BGR2GRAY` and `(H, W, 1)` input for `COLOR_GRAY2BGR`, so `grayscale_image` no longer fails on BGRA frames. (#2866)
- `blur` on `uint16` and `int16` images uses exact integer window sums and OpenCV's scaling precision. (#2875)
- `cvtColor` reads float32 `COLOR_HSV2BGR` input as OpenCV does. (#2885)

## 🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors Mohammad Essam, Barsam Ershadi and oha!

- **Barsam Ershadi** (@BarsamErshadi, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/barsam-ershadi/)) – grayscale heat maps and halos, COCO mask holes, `np.sum` on `CompactMask`, empty-batch center-of-mass anchors, window fixes, the GHUM wrist edge and the oriented-box overlap clipper.
- **kevin** (@kevin9327) – made the `cvtColor` and `blur` fallbacks follow OpenCV for BGRA, gray, 16-bit and float32 input.
- **Mohammad Essam** (@DrEssam97, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohammad-essam97)) – shaped Arabic and Hebrew labels in `RichLabelAnnotator` with the `rtl` extra.
- **NIKHIL** (@Nikhi00718, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikhil-v-engineer)) – made `LineZone` count objects occluded while they cross.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-aswanth-raj/)) – kept oriented-box metric precision at large coordinate origins.
- **LEE, WEI-HONG** (@AuricTW) – fixed COCO area overflow and kept `with` block exceptions in `CSVSink`.
- **Mohammad Hijjawi** (@MohammadHijjawi97, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohammadhijjawi)) – kept unannotated pixels of Pillow scenes unchanged.
- **Devulapalli Naga Sri Vaishnavi** (@Vaishnavi220506, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/vaishnavi-d-9a42a9374)) – stopped the video frame generator at the requested end.
- **oha** (@duriantaco) – removed unused code.
- **Jirka Borovec** (@Borda, [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/jirka-borovec)) – prepared the release.

title: fix(metrics): preserve oriented-box precision in recall and classification metrics
body:
## Description

`Precision`, `Recall`, `F1Score` and `MeanAverageRecall` round oriented-box corners to float32 before computing overlap. Perfect float64 predictions at large coordinate origins can score zero, and subpixel overlaps can become false matches on a 64k-pixel mosaic. The oriented-area utilities also subtract large absolute products, which can move targets into the wrong size bucket.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.config import ORIENTED_BOX_COORDINATES
from supervision.metrics import Precision, MetricTarget

origin = 1_000_000_000
corners = np.array([[[0, 0], [1, 0], [1, 1], [0, 1]]], dtype=np.float64) + origin
boxes = np.array([[origin, origin, origin + 1, origin + 1]], dtype=np.float64)
targets = sv.Detections(xyxy=boxes, class_id=np.array([0]),
                       data={ORIENTED_BOX_COORDINATES: corners})
predictions = sv.Detections(xyxy=boxes.copy(), class_id=np.array([0]),
                           confidence=np.array([0.9]),
                           data={ORIENTED_BOX_COORDINATES: corners.copy()})
result = Precision(metric_target=MetricTarget.ORIENTED_BOUNDING_BOXES).update(
    predictions, targets).compute()
print(result.precision_at_50)  # 0.0 before, 1.0 after
```

## Motivation and Context

The underlying oriented-box IoU already preserves coordinate precision by working in a local frame. This change carries the original corner dtype through the four remaining metric callers, following the mAP correction in #2717.

## Changes Made

- Preserve copied corner dtypes in both metric content readers while retaining float16 promotion before extent subtraction.
- Translate floating-point corners before area calculations in both size helpers, preserving the exact integer path.
- Add regressions for perfect matches, subpixel false matches, signed/unsigned integer origins, float16 extents in both byte orders and size buckets.

## Testing

- Eighteen regressions fail on pristine `develop`; twelve existing-user controls pass.
- Metric tests and doctests: 773 passed.
- 420 existing-input metric results, including repeated compute and reset/reuse, match pristine code exactly.
- Both nearest test modules pass 68 cases with and without OpenCV.
- Full suite on `8a3c35f`: 6,921 passed, 15 skipped and four drawing failures reproduced on pristine source. The final sync to `50b4f2a` changes no metric owner; 1,080 metric/shared-core tests pass with one skip afterward.
- All-file hooks pass using Node 22.18.0 for the hook environment; the default Node installer currently fails on an upstream alpha-version parsing error.

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (the four baseline drawing failures above remain).
- [ ] Updated docs for new or changed public API (no public API changes).
- [x] Added a changelog entry under Unreleased.

## Additional Notes

Box/mask metric paths, explicit annotation areas and the accepted float32 IoU-threshold comparison from #2752 remain unchanged. Existing files and caches need no migration. This cannot recover precision already lost in caller-provided corners. Mixed signed/unsigned integer corner dtypes remain subject to the existing overlap helper's precision limits.

title: fix(cv2): read float32 HSV like OpenCV in `cvtColor` fallback
body:
## Description

The NumPy fallback for `cv2.cvtColor(..., COLOR_HSV2BGR)` always reads the input as OpenCV's 8-bit HSV (hue in `[0, 180)`, saturation and value in `[0, 255]`) and scales the result to `[0, 255]`. OpenCV also accepts float32 HSV, where hue is in degrees (`[0, 360)`) and saturation, value and the BGR output are in `[0, 1]`. Without OpenCV a float32 image comes out wrong:

```python
import numpy as np
from supervision._cv2._color import _cvt_color
from supervision._cv2.constants import _COLOR_HSV2BGR

hsv = np.array([[[120, 0.5, 0.8]]], dtype=np.float32)
_cvt_color(hsv, _COLOR_HSV2BGR)       # [[[0.8, 0.798, 0.798]]] on develop
cv2.cvtColor(hsv, cv2.COLOR_HSV2BGR)  # [[[0.4, 0.8, 0.4]]]
```

OpenCV rejects every other depth (`uint16`, `float64`, ...) for this conversion, while the fallback returned numbers computed on the 8-bit scale.

## Motivation and Context

The fallback is meant to behave like OpenCV when `cv2` isn't installed. `HeatMapAnnotator` only passes `uint8` here, so nothing in the library hits the float path today; this keeps the private helper honest for the depths OpenCV supports.

## Changes Made

- `_hsv_to_bgr` in `_cv2/_color.py`: for float32 input, hue is divided by 60 and saturation/value are used as is, and the output is not scaled by 255. The `uint8` path is unchanged.
- `_cvt_color` raises `ValueError("HSV2BGR conversion requires an 8-bit or float32 image")` for other dtypes, where OpenCV raises `cv2.error`.

## Testing

- New `test_fallback_hsv_to_bgr_matches_opencv_for_float32_images` (32x32 random float32 HSV plus three fixed pixels, `atol=1e-5` against `cv2.cvtColor`) and `test_fallback_hsv_to_bgr_rejects_dtypes_opencv_rejects` (`uint16`, `float64`). All 3 fail on `develop` and pass here.
- `pytest tests/cv2`: 816 passed; the one failure, `test_ordinary_suite_passes_when_cv2_is_blocked`, is my local env missing `pycocotools`/`faster_coco_eval` and fails the same way on `develop`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy src/supervision/_cv2/_color.py` clean.

- [x] Added/updated tests; `tests/cv2` passes locally (I did not run the full suite)
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API (private helper only)
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; I reviewed the change and ran the tests above.

title: fix(utils): keep unannotated pixels of Pillow scenes unchanged
body:
## Description

Annotating a `PIL.Image` rewrote every pixel of the image, not only the ones the annotator drew. `ensure_cv2_image_for_class_method` draws on the 8-bit copy `pillow_to_cv2` makes, then pastes that whole copy back, so every pixel goes through the 8-bit round trip. A transparent RGBA or LA image became fully opaque, and a 16-bit (`I;16`) or 32-bit (`I`) image lost its low byte everywhere.

```python
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[2.0, 2, 12, 12]]), class_id=np.array([0]))

scene = Image.new("RGBA", (20, 20), (0, 0, 0, 0))
sv.BoxAnnotator(thickness=1).annotate(scene, detections)
scene.getpixel((18, 18))
# develop: (0, 0, 0, 255)    this PR: (0, 0, 0, 0)

scene = Image.fromarray(np.full((20, 20), 40000, dtype=np.uint16))
sv.BoxAnnotator(thickness=1, color=sv.Color.WHITE).annotate(scene, detections)
scene.getpixel((18, 18)), scene.getpixel((2, 7))
# develop: (156, 255)        this PR: (40000, 65535)
```

## Motivation and Context

#2614 noted this as out of scope: "the annotator wrapper pastes the 8-bit result back into the caller's image, so annotating an `I;16` image in place still yields a dark 16-bit image." The same paste also makes transparent backgrounds opaque.

## Changes Made

- `utils/conversion.py`: the class-method wrapper keeps the 8-bit copy from before annotation. A new `_paste_annotated_pixels` helper pastes back only the pixels that changed, through a mask. Drawn pixels of the deep integer modes (`I`, `I;16*`) are scaled by 257, which reverses the high-byte reduction in `pillow_to_cv2`.
- `tests/utils/test_conversion.py`: `TestAnnotatePillowScene` covers transparent RGBA and LA, 16-bit and 32-bit integer scenes, and the 16-bit value of a drawn pixel.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

Unchanged: drawn pixels in RGB, RGBA, L and P scenes, NumPy scenes, and `ensure_cv2_image_for_standalone_function`, which returns a new image.

## Testing

- The new tests fail on `develop` (`(0, 0, 0, 255) == (0, 0, 0, 0)`, `(0, 255) == (0, 0)`, `156 == 40000`, `255 == 65535`) and pass with this change.
- `uv run pytest` without OpenCV installed (NumPy fallback): 6323 passed, 231 skipped (`develop`: 6318 passed, 231 skipped).
- `pre-commit` on the changed files: ruff, ruff format, docformatter and codespell pass; mypy reports the same errors as `develop`, none in these files.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (without OpenCV installed)
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

For each Pillow scene the wrapper now copies the 8-bit array once and compares it after annotation. That is small next to the conversions this path already does. The public API is unchanged, so the docs checkbox is left unticked.

title: fix(detection): use the exact clipper for oriented box overlap on OpenCV
body:
## Description

With OpenCV installed, `sv.oriented_box_iou_batch` can return an IoU of 0 or 1 for pairs whose true IoU is neither. It happens in two cases:

- Rotated boxes whose overlapping edges are collinear up to rounding, such as a box and its copy shifted along its own axis.
- Boxes with both sides far below one coordinate unit. A 0.002x0.001 box scores 0 against itself, while a 0.005x0.0025 box scores 1.

The wrong value reaches OBB `MeanAveragePrecision` and `oriented_box_non_max_suppression` with no warning. The NumPy fallback already returns the right values in both cases, so the two backends disagree. The cause is the `cv2.intersectConvexConvex` call: calling it directly on float32 polygons returned area 4000 where the true intersection is 2000, and 0 for the tiny box. I did not read the OpenCV source, so I can't say why it does this.

This PR calls the repo's `_intersect_convex_convex` on both backends. It makes the OBB path slower on OpenCV installs, see the trade-off below.

Minimal repro:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv


def rotated(width, height, degrees, center=(200.0, 200.0)):
    t = np.deg2rad(degrees)
    u = np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t)]) * width / 2
    v = np.array([-np.sin(t), np.cos(t)]) * height / 2
    c = np.array(center)
    return np.array([[c - u - v, c + u - v, c + u + v, c - u + v]])


t = np.deg2rad(10)
a = rotated(100, 40, 10)
b = a + np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t)]) * 50  # true IoU (100-50)/(100+50) = 0.3333
print(sv.oriented_box_iou_batch(a, b)[0, 0])

tiny = rotated(0.002, 0.001, 30, center=(0.5, 0.5))
print(sv.oriented_box_iou_batch(tiny, tiny.copy())[0, 0])  # true IoU 1.0
```

Output of a slightly longer version of that script. Before, on opencv-python 5.0.0 (opencv-python-headless 4.14.0 printed the same lines):

```
backend: opencv
100x40 at 15 deg, shifted 20 along its axis: true IoU 0.6667, got 1.0000, mAP 1.00
100x40 at 25 deg, shifted 50 along its axis: true IoU 0.3333, got 0.0000, mAP 0.00
100x40 at 10 deg, shifted 50 along its axis: true IoU 0.3333, got 1.0000, mAP 1.00
identical 0.002x0.001 box: IoU 0.0000, mAP 0.00
same-angle pairs shifted along their axis with IoU off by >0.01: 142/1000
```

After, on 5.0.0, 4.14.0 and the fallback (the fallback printed these values before the change too, with `backend: fallback`):

```
backend: opencv
100x40 at 15 deg, shifted 20 along its axis: true IoU 0.6667, got 0.6667, mAP 0.40
100x40 at 25 deg, shifted 50 along its axis: true IoU 0.3333, got 0.3333, mAP 0.00
100x40 at 10 deg, shifted 50 along its axis: true IoU 0.3333, got 0.3333, mAP 0.00
identical 0.002x0.001 box: IoU 1.0000, mAP 1.00
same-angle pairs shifted along their axis with IoU off by >0.01: 0/1000
```

## Motivation and Context

The `oriented_box_iou_batch` docstring says overlap areas are computed exactly. I searched open issues and PRs and found no report of this. Open PR #2455 edits the same file to add Weighted Box Fusion, but its diff does not touch `oriented_box_iou_batch`.

## Changes Made

- `oriented_box_iou_batch` calls `_intersect_convex_convex` from `supervision._cv2._geometry` instead of `cv2.intersectConvexConvex`. The `_cv2` import in that module is now unused, so `ruff` removed it.
- I removed the OpenCV reference from the docstring note and rewrote the comment on the final clip. The clip is still needed: on identical float64 boxes the raw ratio exceeded 1 in 203 of 400 cases, by at most 1.8e-7.
- I added regression tests for analytic IoU on along-axis pairs, tiny boxes and OBB NMS.
- I removed the `intersectConvexConvex` monkeypatch and its import from `tests/cv2/test_contours.py`, since no library code reads that attribute any more.

Left out of scope: other `cv2` call sites are untouched, and the float32 buffers stay as they are. So very thin boxes can still score wrong on both backends. On 150 identical float64 boxes with centers up to 1500, thickness 1e-3 to 3e-3 left 33 off by more than 1e-3 (at most 0.009), and thickness 1e-4 to 3e-4 left 60 (at most 0.14). `cv2` was off on one more box in each set, by up to 0.67. `grep` finds no other `src` caller of `intersectConvexConvex` outside the `_cv2` wrapper.

## Trade-off for maintainers to judge

This makes OBB overlap slower on OpenCV installs, because a per-pair Python clipper replaces a C++ call. Fallback users already pay this cost, and their code path does not change. The cost follows candidate pairs (boxes whose axis-aligned envelopes overlap), not box count, and raw detections going into NMS can cluster. So the crowded rows below matter more than the sparse ones.

Interleaved runs on a shared 8-core machine, best of 15 for the sparse rows, best of 2 for the crowded self-comparison, one run for NMS. All boxes are random rotated rectangles with sides from 20 to 120. The crowded set is 1000 boxes on a 300x300 canvas.

opencv-python 5.0.0, with the fallback for comparison:

| Workload | Candidate pairs | Current | This PR (clipper) | Routing prototype | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `oriented_box_iou_batch`, 300x300, sparse | 2542 | 0.010 s (3.9 us/pair) | 0.115 s (45 us/pair) | 0.062 s (24 us/pair) | 0.127 s |
| self-comparison, 500 boxes, sparse | 2266 | 0.011 s (4.7 us/pair) | 0.104 s (46 us/pair) | 0.079 s (35 us/pair) | 0.114 s |
| self-comparison, 1000 boxes, crowded | 130439 | 0.498 s (3.8 us/pair) | 6.41 s (49 us/pair) | 3.58 s (27 us/pair) | 6.85 s |
| `oriented_box_non_max_suppression`, same 1000 boxes | not counted | 0.78 s | 9.43 s | 5.32 s | 7.68 s |

opencv-python-headless 4.14.0:

| Workload | Current | This PR (clipper) | Routing prototype |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 300x300, sparse | 0.014 s | 0.168 s | 0.085 s |
| self-comparison, 500 boxes, sparse | 0.013 s | 0.134 s | 0.099 s |
| self-comparison, 1000 boxes, crowded | 0.745 s | 9.66 s | 5.42 s |
| NMS, same 1000 boxes | 0.84 s | 8.50 s | 3.77 s |

Treat these as rough and compare within a row. The fallback runs the same clipper code, so its gap to the clipper column is noise. The machine was busy: the same 300x300 clipper case took from 0.115 s to 0.264 s across my runs on 5.0.0. The slowdown was 9.5x to 13x in these tables. A separate run on 5.0.0 with other workloads gave about 7x for 1000 sparse boxes and about 15x for 200x200 pairs that all overlap. So expect roughly 10x, with a wide spread.

**Alternative: route only risky pairs to the clipper and keep `cv2` for the rest.** I did not implement this here. My scratch prototype sends a pair to the clipper if an edge of one box and an edge of the other have `|sin(angle)| <= 1e-3`, or if either box's extent is under 1 unit. It had no errors above 0.01 in any scenario below. The saving depends on the workload: on 5.0.0 about 46% on 300x300, about 44% on the crowded self-comparison, and about 24% on the 500-box self-comparison. That last one is lower because the 500 diagonal pairs are identical boxes, and those always go to the clipper: exactly 500 of its 2266 pairs were routed there. Only 4 of 2542 pairs and 1166 of 130439 pairs were routed on the other two. The risk check is unvectorized NumPy and took about 30 to 36 us per pair measured alone in a separate run, so most of the remaining time on the other pairs is the check itself, and vectorizing it should narrow the gap. I have not tried that. I picked both thresholds by experiment, and I have no proof they catch every failing pair, since I don't know the exact condition inside OpenCV. That is why this PR uses the simpler option. If the cost matters more to you, I can switch.

Measured IoU error against an exact reference, 400 random pairs per scenario, counting errors above 0.01. Results were identical on 5.0.0 and 4.14.0:

| Scenario | Current OpenCV | Clipper | Routing prototype |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| along-axis shift, float64 | 63 | 0 | 0 |
| along-axis shift, float32 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| perpendicular shift, float64 | 69 | 0 | 0 |
| near-parallel (angle offset 1e-6 to 1e-1 deg), float64 | 7 | 0 | 0 |
| general random overlap, float64 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| tiny boxes, float64 | 161 | 0 | 0 |

The reference is my own rational-arithmetic polygon clipper on the original coordinates. It uses the same Sutherland-Hodgman method as `_intersect_convex_convex`, so it rules out rounding but is not an independent algorithm. The along-axis regression tests compare with the analytic value instead.

**Behaviour change:** OBB metric and NMS results on OpenCV installs can change for the affected pairs, which is the point of the fix. In the repro above, mAP goes from 1.00 to 0.40. On 5000 ordinary random float32 pairs, IoU from the two clippers differed by at most 2.1e-7. NaN and Inf coordinates still give 0.0.

Non-convex and self-intersecting quads remain documented as undefined, and their scores do change on OpenCV installs. Over 300 ordered pairs of a jittered concave quad and a rectangle, the two clippers differed by more than 0.01 on 159, by up to 1.0. Against a 400x400 even-odd raster estimate, the clipper was off by more than 0.05 on 103 and `cv2` on 58, so this is an input where `cv2` was closer. Bowtie quads (152 differed; 155 vs 156 off) and random non-convex quads (153 differed; 109 vs 100 off) came out about even. Anyone feeding noisy quads should expect these scores to move.

## Testing

New tests before the fix, on opencv-python 5.0.0 (`pytest tests/detection/utils/test_iou_and_nms.py -k "collinear_edges or tiny_identical"`):

```
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxIouBatch::test_matches_analytic_iou_for_collinear_edges[reported-as-identical-at-15-deg] - assert np.float64(0.9999998779296938) == 0.6666666666666666 ± 1.0e-04
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxIouBatch::test_matches_analytic_iou_for_collinear_edges[reported-as-identical-at-10-deg] - assert np.float64(1.0) == 0.3333333333333333 ± 1.0e-04
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxIouBatch::test_matches_analytic_iou_for_collinear_edges[reported-as-disjoint-at-25-deg] - assert np.float64(0.0) == 0.3333333333333333 ± 1.0e-04
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxIouBatch::test_matches_analytic_iou_for_collinear_edges[underestimated-at-20-deg] - assert np.float64(0....5072251512077) == 0.8181818181818182 ± 1.0e-04
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxIouBatch::test_matches_analytic_iou_for_random_collinear_edges[float32] - AssertionError: (Mismatched elements: 18 / 1000)
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxIouBatch::test_matches_analytic_iou_for_random_collinear_edges[float64] - AssertionError: (Mismatched elements: 163 / 1000)
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxIouBatch::test_tiny_identical_boxes_score_one[float32] - assert np.float64(0.0) == 1.0 ± 0.001
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxIouBatch::test_tiny_identical_boxes_score_one[float64] - assert np.float64(0.0) == 1.0 ± 0.001
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxNonMaxSuppression::test_uses_true_overlap_for_collinear_edges[keeps-low-true-overlap] - assert [True, False] == [True, True]
FAILED ...::TestOrientedBoxNonMaxSuppression::test_uses_true_overlap_for_collinear_edges[suppresses-high-true-overlap] - assert [True, True] == [True, False]
10 failed, 228 deselected in 0.39s
```

I shortened the test path to `...` and condensed the two random-case messages to their mismatch counts. The same 10 tests passed on the fallback before the fix, and they pass on both backends after it (`10 passed, 228 deselected`).

Full suite with this change:

- opencv-python 5.0.0: `6892 passed, 2 skipped`
- fallback: `6329 passed, 230 skipped`

Hooks (`pre-commit run --files` on the changed files): 12 passed, 10 skipped because no files matched, 0 failed.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

Limits of what I checked:

- On 4.x I only tried opencv-python-headless 4.14.0, and only with the repro, the error table and the timings, not the test suite. I did not test older 4.x releases.
- CI's platforms and Python versions are untested. All of this ran on one macOS machine.
- It may be worth reporting the `intersectConvexConvex` behaviour to OpenCV. I have not done that.
