title: fix(depth): reject integer arrays passed unwrapped to `DepthMap.from_ultralytics`
body:
## Description

`DepthMap.from_ultralytics` read `getattr(depth, "data", depth)`. A plain `np.ndarray` has its own `.data` attribute (a dtype-less `memoryview`), so when `result.depth` was a bare array, `_to_numpy` got the memoryview, skipped its integer check, and loaded integer codes as metres.

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

depth = np.array([[0, 1000], [2000, 3000]], dtype=np.uint16)
d = sv.DepthMap.from_ultralytics(SimpleNamespace(depth=depth))
print(d.kind, d.value_at(1, 1))
# before: DepthKind.DEPTH_M 3000.0
# after:  ValueError: Model depth must be a float array, got uint16. ...
```

The same array wrapped as `result.depth.data` already raised this error. This PR makes the bare-array path match.

## Motivation and Context

Integer depth is rejected everywhere else in `DepthMap` (constructor, `_to_numpy`, the wrapped Ultralytics path), so codes such as millimetres or 16-bit PNG values are not mistaken for metres. This path was the one exception.

Closes #2794

## Changes Made

- `from_ultralytics`: use `result.depth` directly when it is already an `np.ndarray`, and read `.data` only otherwise. Real Ultralytics results, whose `.data` is a float tensor, are unchanged.
- `tests/depth/test_core.py`: add an `unwrapped-integer-array` case to `TestDepthMapFromUltralytics.test_rejects_invalid_results`.
- Out of scope: the existing `test_loads_a_raw_array_without_a_data_attribute` is slightly misnamed (NumPy arrays do have `.data`), but it still covers the bare float array path, so I left it as is.

## Testing

```
uv run pytest tests/depth -k Ultralytics   # on develop: 1 failed (unwrapped-integer-array), 6 passed
uv run pytest tests/depth                  # with fix: 398 passed
uv run pytest --doctest-modules src/supervision/depth   # 11 passed
uv run pytest                              # 6343 passed, 2 skipped
ruff check / ruff format --check           # pass
```

mypy and docformatter hooks were not run locally (the hooks are pinned to Python 3.11, which isn't installed here). The change is a one-line branch with no new types.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API (no public API change)
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

Found while auditing silent fallbacks in `src/supervision/depth/`.

title: fix(vlm): crop Gemini 2.5/3.5 masks to the image when box_2d leaves 0-1000
body:
## Description

`from_google_gemini_2_5` (also used by `GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_5`) placed each mask with `np_mask[y_min:y_max, x_min:x_max] = ...` after resizing the PNG to the whole box. A `box_2d` coordinate above 1000 or below 0 made the resized mask larger than the slice, or made a negative slice start wrap to an empty slice, so NumPy raised `ValueError: could not broadcast input array` and the whole response was lost, including every valid item.

Minimal repro (full script in the issue), 1920x1080, one valid item plus one item with box `[500, 500, 1001, 1001]`:

- Before: `ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (541,961) into shape (540,960)`; `[-1, -1, 500, 500]` raises `... into shape (0,0)`.
- After: both parse. The valid item's mask is unchanged (82944 pixels), the overshooting item gets the part of its mask inside the image (518400 pixels), and `xyxy` is `[192.0, 108.0, 576.0, 324.0]` and `[960.0, 540.0, 1921.9, 1081.1]`.

## Motivation and Context

Models occasionally overshoot the 0-1000 range, and one such item should not discard a whole response. The function's own contract is exactly one mask per kept item, with every other malformed-mask path degrading to an all-false mask; the Gemini 3.6 parser (`polygon_to_mask`) and the box-only path already accept the same box.

Closes #2792 

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/detection/vlm.py`, `from_google_gemini_2_5`: compute the part of the box inside the image; if none is inside, append an all-false mask (same as the existing empty-box path); otherwise resample straight from the matching part of the PNG (`Image.resize(..., box=...)`) into that part and assign it. A box fully inside the image uses the full-PNG `box`, so its mask is the same as before: checked on 1500 random in-range responses (random PNGs, image sizes and boxes), old and new masks and boxes identical.
- Because only the visible part is resampled, a huge box (`[0, 0, 10**9, 10**9]`) allocates at most the image size.
- Docstring sentence on the cropping behaviour; changelog entry under `Unreleased`.
- Tests: new `TestGeminiMasksForBoxesOutsideImage` in `tests/detection/test_vlm.py` (20 cases): boxes at exactly 1000, overshooting by 1 and by 10, negative, overshooting on both sides, huge (each for Gemini 2.5 and 3.5); boxes wholly outside the image (four positions); the cropped mask is the matching slice of the PNG and not a squashed copy; a response mixing valid, overshooting and wholly-outside items keeps the valid items' masks and boxes; `xyxy` stays equal to the box-only parse.
- Left out on purpose: `xyxy` is not clipped (the box-only and 3.6 paths return it unclipped; see Additional Notes). Other malformed `box_2d` values (too few elements, `NaN`/`Infinity`) fail in other places and are not part of this change.

## Testing

Ran on macOS, Python 3.12, `uv pip install -e` of this branch:

- New tests on `develop` (source change stashed): `18 failed, 2 passed` (the 2 are the exactly-1000 regression cases); with this change: `20 passed`.
- `pytest tests/detection/test_vlm.py` plus `pytest --doctest-modules src/supervision/detection/vlm.py`: 203 passed.
- `pytest tests/detection`: 2401 passed, 2 skipped.
- Whole `tests` folder: 5811 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed: `tests/cv2/test_integration.py::test_ordinary_suite_passes_when_cv2_is_blocked`, which also fails on unmodified `develop` in my environment. Three metrics test files could not be collected here (missing optional reference packages) and were left out: `test_keypoint_mean_average_precision.py`, `test_mean_average_precision_limits.py`, `test_sklearn_parity.py`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `docformatter --check` and `codespell` on the touched files: clean. `mypy` on `vlm.py`: one error, `Skipping analyzing "deprecate"` (missing stubs in my environment), identical on unmodified `develop`; nothing from the changed lines.
- Not run: the full `pre-commit run --all-files` (mdformat for the changelog, prettier, etc.).

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

(First box left unticked: the full suite is not clean in my environment, see Testing.)

## Additional Notes

- Design choice: crop the mask, keep `xyxy` as returned. The box-only parse and Gemini 3.6 return the same unclipped `xyxy`, so a response parses to the same boxes with or without masks. Clipping `xyxy` to the image would be a separate, wider behaviour change; happy to add it here if you prefer.
- A wholly-outside box keeps its slot with an all-false mask rather than being dropped, so `mask` stays aligned with `xyxy`, `class_id` and `confidence`.
- The visible part of the mask is resampled from the corresponding slice of the PNG, so it lines up with where the full box would have drawn it; this is covered by a test that would fail if the whole PNG were squashed into the visible part.
- Not changed: `from_deepseek_vl_2` and Gemini 3.6/3.7 use `polygon_to_mask` and do not slice-assign, so the same crash does not occur there (checked by running them).

title: ci: harden workflows and reduce redundant checks
body:
CI keeps push test runs available for regression tracing while cancelling superseded PR checks.

- Apply link and GitHub configuration path filters only to PRs. Keep required test and docs checks unconditional, and add missing job timeouts.
- Reduce the pytest matrix from 18 to 14 jobs. Linux retains Python 3.10 through 3.13; macOS and Windows retain 3.10 and 3.13. This removes four version/platform combinations while keeping every Python minor and OS represented. OpenCV backend cases and isolated wheel checks still run on every OS. Standard GitHub-hosted runners remain in use.
- Pin actions to commit SHAs, scope write permissions to the jobs that need them, and disable checkout credential persistence except for documentation pushes. Cache test dependencies and disable release build and publishing caches.
- Pass branch names, dispatch confirmation, and release metadata through quoted environment variables. Keep the privileged conflict labeler API-only, with no checkout or execution of PR code.
- Retain distribution artifacts for three days and keep shared workflow guidance in `AGENTS.md`, with `CLAUDE.md` as its existing redirect.

Validation on the current head: 98 GitHub configuration tests and script doctests pass, including docs-publishing regressions. Workflow assertions confirm PR-only cancellation and filtering, unfiltered push checks that each get their own concurrency group, the 14-job matrix, unchanged runner labels, immutable action pins, timeouts, and three-day retention. Actionlint, zizmor, and pre-commit on all PR files pass.

title: fix(annotators): draw crops and icons on grayscale scenes
body:
## Description

`CropAnnotator` and `IconAnnotator` fail on grayscale scenes: `(H, W)` arrays, `(H, W, 1)` arrays, and Pillow `"L"` images. Both go through `_overlay_image`, which assumed a three- or four-channel scene and overlay. `MaskAnnotator`, `HaloAnnotator`, `BlurAnnotator`, `PixelateAnnotator` and the OpenCV-drawn annotators already work on the same scenes.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[30, 30, 50, 50]], dtype=np.float32), class_id=np.array([0]))
scene = np.full((80, 80), 100, dtype=np.uint8)
sv.CropAnnotator().annotate(scene.copy(), detections)
sv.IconAnnotator(icon_resolution_wh=(8, 8)).annotate(scene.copy(), detections, icon_path="icon.png")  # any BGRA PNG
```

Before (develop, same with OpenCV and with the NumPy fallback):

```
CropAnnotator (H,W): IndexError: tuple index out of range
CropAnnotator (H,W,1): IndexError: tuple index out of range
CropAnnotator PIL L: IndexError: tuple index out of range
IconAnnotator (H,W): ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (8,8,8) (8,8,3)
IconAnnotator (H,W,1): ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (8,8,3) into shape (8,8,1)
IconAnnotator PIL L: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (8,8,8) (8,8,3)
```

After:

```
CropAnnotator (H,W): OK shape (80, 80)
CropAnnotator (H,W,1): OK shape (80, 80, 1)
CropAnnotator PIL L: OK shape (80, 80)
IconAnnotator (H,W): OK shape (80, 80)
IconAnnotator (H,W,1): OK shape (80, 80, 1)
IconAnnotator PIL L: OK shape (80, 80)
Crop on gray scene == crop on its BGR copy, channel 0: True
Icon on gray scene: [29 64 100] == icon on BGR scene converted to gray: [29 64 100]
```

## Motivation and Context

`_overlay_image` read `overlay.shape[2]`, which a crop of a 2-D scene does not have. It also wrote a BGR icon into a single-channel region, and it broadcast the alpha as `(H, W, 1)` against a 2-D region. For `(H, W, 1)` scenes, `cv2.resize` drops the singleton channel axis of the scaled crop, so its shape no longer matches the scene. Grayscale scenes are already supported elsewhere (`pillow_to_cv2`, #2725, #2755), so these two annotators were the odd ones out.

## Changes Made

- `_overlay_image` brings the overlay into the scene's channel layout through a new helper, `_match_overlay_to_scene_channels`. On a grayscale scene, a BGR overlay (an icon) becomes its gray luminance (`COLOR_BGR2GRAY`, as `HaloAnnotator` does), and a grayscale overlay (a crop) is reshaped to `(H, W)` or `(H, W, 1)`. The alpha blend broadcasts for 2-D scenes too.
- BGR scenes are unchanged; the existing exact-value blend and boundary tests still pass.
- Out of scope: `BackgroundOverlayAnnotator`, `HeatMapAnnotator` and `RichLabelAnnotator` also fail on grayscale scenes, for different reasons.

## Testing

- New tests in `tests/annotators/test_core.py` (`TestSingleChannelOverlayAnnotators`) and `tests/utils/test_image.py`. On develop, 9 of them fail with the errors above; with this change all pass.
- `uv run pytest`: 5912 passed, 133 skipped (NumPy fallback backend); `tests/annotators` and `tests/utils/test_image.py` also pass with `opencv-python` installed.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, codespell and the other hooks pass.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

Icons are converted by luminance rather than by taking the blue channel. The blue channel is what OpenCV writes for a palette colour on a grayscale image, but an icon is image content, and its luminance matches converting the BGR-scene result to gray.

title: Fix float box midpoints overflowing to inf
body:
Box centers are computed as `(x1 + x2) / 2`, so a finite, representable midpoint overflows the coordinate dtype. For a valid float16 box `[32000, 0, 64000, 10]`, `sv.scale_boxes(..., factor=1.0)` returns `[[inf, 0, inf, 10]]`, `Detections.get_anchors_coordinates(Position.CENTER)` returns `[inf, 5]`, and `spread_out_boxes` returns `-inf` corners. Large float32 (`[1e38, 0, 3e38, 10]`) and float64 (`[1e308, 0, 1.6e308, 10]`) boxes are affected the same way even though their true midpoints are representable.

`LineZone` and `PolygonZone` counts and smart label placement read those anchors, so they silently stop working, and `factor=1.0` no longer being the identity breaks a documented contract.

The fix halves each corner before adding in `_box_midpoint`, `scale_boxes` and `spread_out_boxes`. Halving is exact in binary floating point, so the output is bit-identical whenever the previous sum did not overflow: 200k random float32/float64 pairs, 150 `scale_boxes` cases and 60 `spread_out_boxes` cases show no difference.

The integer form of this expression was already fixed in #2541 and float16 `box_area` in #2764; these floating-point midpoints were left out.

`test_large_float16_boxes_keep_finite_midpoints` fails before the change and passes after it; `tests/detection/utils/test_boxes.py` 123 passed; full suite 6257 passed, 1 skipped (baseline 6256, 1). `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both files.

Drafted with AI assistance; I reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

title: fix(smoother): Prevent overflow in oriented corner alignment
body:
## Description

`DetectionsSmoother` can turn a translated rectangle into a diamond when oriented corners use float16 or int16. The squared corner-distance comparison overflows before it chooses the matching corner order.

For example, smooth a 400 by 200 rectangle with a second frame translated 160 pixels vertically and a different starting corner. The expected mean corners are `[(0, 80), (400, 80), (400, 280), (0, 280)]`. With float16, the current result is `[(0, 180), (200, 80), (400, 180), (200, 280)]`.

## Motivation and Context

Corner correspondence should depend on geometry rather than the coordinate dtype or cyclic starting corner. This was found through code analysis and reproduced through `update_with_detections`.

## Changes Made

- Compute corner distances in at least float32, while returning the selected original corners so their dtype stays unchanged.
- Add 16 cases covering float16, int16, float32 and float64, cyclic starts and both windings.
- Add an Unreleased changelog entry. Smoothing policy, public APIs and stored formats stay unchanged.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/detection/tools/test_smoother.py -q`: 64 passed. On pristine source, seven new cases fail and nine already pass.

title: fix(video): release captures when frame setup fails
body:
## Description

`get_video_frames_generator()` opens a capture inside `_validate_and_setup_video()`, before entering its decoding `try/finally`. If range validation or a backend metadata/seek call raises during setup, the capture is never explicitly released.

With a retained real capture for a 10-frame video, requesting `end=11` raises `Requested frames are outbound`, but `capture.isOpened()` remains `True` on `develop`. With this change it is `False` immediately after the exception. The regression retains the handle so garbage collection cannot hide the missing cleanup.

## Motivation and Context

Callers recovering from invalid ranges or backend setup failures should not retain open decoder resources. Existing decoding/early-close cleanup does not cover setup failures.

## Changes Made

- Release the capture if setup fails, then re-raise the original error.
- Preserve the setup error if release also fails, logging that secondary failure consistently with the existing decoding cleanup.
- Keep successful setup ownership and frame-range behavior unchanged.
- Test real captures with synchronous/prefetched reading, backend failures, interruption, cleanup failure and successful ranges.

title: fix(json-sink): preserve appended rows when metadata buffers are reused
body:
## Description

`JSONSink.append()` retains references to mutable metadata until the sink closes. Reusing a NumPy embedding buffer for the next frame therefore changes rows that were already appended, silently writing the latest embedding for both frames.

```python
import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "detections.json"
    detections = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10]]))
    embedding = np.array([[1.0, 2.0]])
    with sv.JSONSink(str(path)) as sink:
        sink.append(detections, {"embedding": embedding})
        embedding[:] = 9
        sink.append(detections, {"embedding": embedding})
    print([row["embedding"] for row in json.loads(path.read_text())])
```

Before: `[[9.0, 9.0], [9.0, 9.0]]`. After: `[[1.0, 2.0], [9.0, 9.0]]`.

## Motivation and Context

Frame-processing pipelines can reuse buffers or update nested metadata after appending a result. Appended rows should preserve those results. The same aliasing affects `detections.data`, sliced sequences and broadcast nested containers.

## Changes Made

- Deep-copy the parsed row batch at the append boundary, without copying the source detections or masks.
- Document snapshot semantics; keep JSON encoding deferred until close.
- Add regression coverage for both metadata sources, nested NumPy/list values, and sliced/broadcast sequences.

## Testing

- Base `893a9b1`: new regression tests **5 failed**.
- Fixed tree: JSON/CSV and new snapshot tests **62 passed**.
- Public API smoke test: reused buffers retain both values; empty detections and NumPy scalar serialization remain correct.
- `PYTHONPATH=src ../supervision-contributions-20261021/.venv/bin/python -m pytest --cov=supervision -q`: **5907 passed, 133 skipped** (Python 3.12, frozen dev/metrics dependencies, no OpenCV). The unchanged base has **5902 passed, 133 skipped**.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` and a separate run including the new test file: **passed**, including mypy, Ruff and formatting.

- [x] Updated the affected public API docstring
- [x] Added an Unreleased changelog entry

## Additional Notes

This does not change the close/reopen lifecycle addressed by #2771. Copying the parsed batch adds the necessary snapshot allocation while preserving the existing output schema and NumPy encoder.

title: fix(dataset): use devkit box extents for Pascal VOC export and import
body:
## Description

`object_to_pascal_voc` added 1 to all four box coordinates on export, and `detections_from_xml_obj` subtracted 1 from all four on import. Pascal VOC indices are 1-based and inclusive: a zero-indexed box covering pixels `x0 .. x0 + w - 1` is encoded as `xmin = x0 + 1`, `xmax = x0 + w`, so only the minimum corner carries the offset. The old behaviour made a supervision-to-supervision round trip look exact, while every exported box read one pixel wider and taller in devkit-based readers (Detectron2's VOC loader shifts only `xmin`/`ymin`), and devkit-encoded files loaded one pixel smaller here.

Minimal repro (from the issue): a COCO box at `x=10, y=20, w=30, h=40` was written as `11, 21, 41, 61`; the devkit encoding is `11, 21, 40, 60`. With this PR it is written as `11, 21, 40, 60`, and a devkit-encoded file loads back as `[10, 20, 40, 60]`.

## Motivation and Context

Closes #2756

## Changes Made

- `object_to_pascal_voc`: shift only `xmin`/`ymin` by 1 on write. The offset is applied after corner ordering, so reversed boxes still get ordered corners.
- `detections_from_xml_obj`: shift only `xmin`/`ymin` back on read, mirroring the writer.
- Polygon vertices are deliberately unchanged: they are point coordinates, not box extents, so the +1 still applies to every vertex.
- Updated the expectations that encoded the old convention (`test_pascal_voc.py`, one case in `test_coco.py`) and added `TestPascalVocDevkitConvention` regression tests covering the issue example, reading a devkit-encoded file, and export/reload round trips.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased` in `docs/changelog.md`, including the compatibility note below.

## Testing

- New regression tests fail on `develop` (writer produced `41`/`61`, reader produced `39`/`59` for the maximum corner) and pass with this change.
- `tests/dataset/`: 593 passed.
- Full suite (excluding `tests/metrics`, which requires the `metrics` extra): 4783 passed, 1 failure in `tests/cv2/test_integration.py` that is also present on the unmodified `develop` baseline in the same environment.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

Compatibility: annotations written by earlier supervision versions carry the old +1 in `xmax` and `ymax`; those maximum corners now load one pixel larger than before. This is the trade-off the issue recommends, since the previous files were already one pixel too large for every other VOC reader.

title: releasing `0.31.1` [rebase & merge]
body:
# v0.31.1 — Recall that matches COCO, boxes that don't overflow

## 📋 Summary

A bug-fix release: recall scores now agree with COCO, and half-precision boxes stop overflowing.

- **`MeanAverageRecall`** skips crowd regions and matches predictions in confidence order, like `pycocotools`.
- COCO segmentations loaded without an `area` field no longer make mAP return `-1`.
- `float16` boxes keep finite areas, and mAP and `with_nmm` stop overflowing on narrow coordinate types.
- Mask and halo annotators draw on grayscale scenes, and vertex annotators accept `(x, y, z)` points.
- Without OpenCV, ellipses and thick circles render like OpenCV 5, and grayscale images save correctly.

Drop-in upgrade, no code changes. mAR values can move: up on COCO data with crowd annotations, and in either direction where confidence order now decides which prediction claims a target.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Recall that matches COCO

`sv.metrics.MeanAverageRecall` used to count COCO crowd regions as missed objects and to pair predictions with the highest-IoU target first. It now leaves out targets with `data["iscrowd"]` or `data["ignore"]` set, the same rule `MeanAveragePrecision` uses. It also matches predictions in descending confidence order with COCO's tie rule, and counts an oriented-box IoU of exactly 0.55, 0.6, 0.8 or 0.85 as a match at that threshold. One target, one crowd target and a perfect prediction now score 1.0 instead of 0.5. (#2750, #2758, #2752)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MeanAverageRecall

targets = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10], [20, 20, 30, 30]], dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0, 0]),
    data={"iscrowd": np.array([0, 1])},
)
predictions = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10]], dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
    confidence=np.array([0.9]),
)
MeanAverageRecall().update(predictions, targets).compute().mAR_at_100  # 1.0
```

### Half-precision boxes that stay finite

A 256×256 box in `float16` has an area of 65,536, which is past `float16`'s maximum, so `Detections.box_area` returned `inf` and area filters dropped it. Box areas of `float16` detections are now computed and returned in `float32`, and `MeanAveragePrecision` and `with_nmm` no longer overflow on `float16` or narrow integer coordinates either. COCO segmentations loaded with masks but without an `area` field now get it from the decoded mask, so those targets stay in their size bucket instead of turning mAP into `-1`. (#2764, #2743, #2753, #2763)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 256, 256], [0, 0, 0.01, 0.01]], dtype=np.float16)
)
detections.box_area  # array([6.5536000e+04, 1.0004273e-04], dtype=float32)
```

### Grayscale scenes and 3D keypoints in annotators

`sv.MaskAnnotator` and `sv.HaloAnnotator` raised `ValueError` on single-channel images. They now accept `(H, W)`, `(H, W, 1)` and Pillow `"L"` scenes, painting the gray value OpenCV would write for the same color. `VertexAnnotator` and the vertex-ellipse annotators draw `(x, y, z)` keypoints from their x and y, where they used to fail on tuple unpacking. (#2755, #2759)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

scene = np.zeros((100, 100), dtype=np.uint8)
mask = np.zeros((1, 100, 100), dtype=bool)
mask[0, 20:60, 20:60] = True
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[20, 20, 60, 60]], dtype=float), mask=mask, class_id=np.array([0])
)
sv.MaskAnnotator().annotate(scene.copy(), detections).shape  # (100, 100)

key_points = sv.KeyPoints(xy=np.array([[[10, 10, 0.5], [50, 50, 1.0]]], dtype=np.float32))
sv.VertexAnnotator().annotate(np.zeros((64, 64, 3), dtype=np.uint8), key_points)
```

### Drawing without OpenCV, closer to OpenCV

The NumPy fallback used when OpenCV is not installed now ports OpenCV's ellipse rasterization, and thick circle outlines are centred on the radius instead of shrinking inward by half their thickness. Both match OpenCV 5.0 pixel for pixel in the reference tests. Without OpenCV, this changes the pixels drawn by `EllipseAnnotator`, `RoundBoxAnnotator`, the vertex-ellipse keypoint annotators, `CircleAnnotator` and `DotAnnotator` outlines. Image writing now accepts `(H, W, 1)` grayscale arrays and saves BGRA images as JPEG, and video reading handles files whose audio stream comes before the video stream. (#2740, #2765, #2754, #2746)

## 🔄 Migration guide

No migration required for this release.

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🔧 Fixed

**`MeanAverageRecall` and COCO**

- `sv.metrics.MeanAverageRecall` counted COCO crowd and ignored targets as missed objects and paired predictions by highest IoU first; it now skips those targets and matches in descending confidence order with COCO's last-target tie rule, as COCO does. (#2750, #2758)
- Oriented-box `MeanAverageRecall`, `Precision`, `Recall` and `F1Score` missed matches whose IoU was exactly 0.55, 0.6, 0.8 or 0.85, because the IoU was `float64` and the thresholds `float32`. (#2752)

**Overflow-safe boxes**

- `Detections.box_area` and box-based `Detections.area` overflowed to infinity for ordinary `float16` boxes; they now compute and return `float32`. (#2764)
- `sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision` overflowed box extents and areas for `float16` or narrow integer coordinates, so perfect large boxes scored `-1` or landed in the wrong size bucket. (#2743)
- `sv.Detections.with_nmm` overflowed its area-weighted confidence for `float16` boxes and, at extreme coordinates, for integer and `float32` boxes. (#2753)
- COCO loading with masks left segmented annotations without an `area` field with a `NaN` area, which pushed them out of every mAP size bucket; the area now comes from the decoded mask. (#2763)

**Masks and polygons**

- `resize_masks` returned an empty array when downscaling very narrow masks; it now keeps at least one pixel per axis. (#2762)
- `sv.filter_polygons_by_area` and `sv.polygon_to_xyxy` raised `ValueError` on empty polygons; they now treat them as zero area and an all-zero box. (#2761)

**Annotators**

- `sv.MaskAnnotator` and `sv.HaloAnnotator` raised `ValueError` on grayscale scenes. (#2755)
- `VertexAnnotator` and the vertex-ellipse annotators raised a tuple-unpacking error on three-coordinate keypoints; they now draw from x and y. (#2759)
- `sv.MaskAnnotator` widened its blend region to the boxes of all-empty masks, including `CompactMask`, copying and blending outside the foreground. (#2741)

**Without OpenCV**

- The fallback `ellipse` painted different pixels from OpenCV for thick strokes, fills and arcs; it now ports OpenCV's rasterization. (#2740)
- The fallback `circle` grew thick outlines inward from the bounding box, shrinking them by half their thickness; they are now centred on the radius. (#2765)
- Image writing rejected `(H, W, 1)` grayscale arrays and lost BGRA images saved as JPEG. (#2754)
- Video reading failed on files whose audio stream comes before the first video stream. (#2746)

## 🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors, Ghanashyam V Narayan and jorge!

- **Kaushik Reddy Lingireddy** (@Lingikaushikreddy) — made `MeanAverageRecall` skip crowd targets and match by confidence, and fixed oriented-box threshold matching.
- **peng xiang** (@px12811) — ported OpenCV's ellipse rasterization to the fallback and fixed mAR tie-breaking.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07) — fixed three-coordinate keypoint drawing and narrow-mask resizing.
- **Mohammad Hijjawi** (@MohammadHijjawi97) — made `MaskAnnotator` and `HaloAnnotator` work on grayscale scenes.
- **kevin** (@kevin9327) — centred thick fallback circles on their radius.
- **Ghanashyam V Narayan** (@ghanashyam03) — made the polygon helpers accept empty polygons.
- **jorge** (@jorge-asenjo) — kept empty compact masks out of the mask blend region.

title: fix(dataset): raise when an image cannot be written during export
body:
## Description

In-memory dataset exports ignore a `False` result from `cv2.imwrite`. An export can therefore return normally even though an image was never saved. Both the shared detection-image exporter and classification folder exporter now raise `OSError` containing the destination path, matching `ImageSink`.

Minimal reproduction (the destination image path already exists as a directory):

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    output = Path(directory)
    (output / "image.png").mkdir()
    dataset = sv.DetectionDataset(
        classes=[],
        images={"image.png": np.zeros((4, 4, 3), dtype=np.uint8)},
        annotations={"image.png": sv.Detections.empty()},
    )
    dataset.as_yolo(images_directory_path=str(output))
```

Before: returns `None`, with no image file written. After: raises `OSError: Failed to save image to path: .../image.png`.

## Motivation and Context

Report incomplete exports at the point of failure, so users can correct the destination instead of discovering missing training images later.

## Changes Made

- Check image-write results in `save_dataset_images` and `ClassificationDataset.as_folder_structure`, and document the exception.

title: fix(json-sink): make write_and_close a no-op once the file is closed
body:
## Description

`sv.JSONSink.write_and_close()` closes the file, but it only checked `if self.file:`, which stays true for a closed file object. So calling it inside a `with` block, for example to flush the results before the block ends, made the block's exit call it a second time, and `json.dump` raised `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file.`:

```python
with sv.JSONSink("out.json") as sink:
    sink.append(detections)
    sink.write_and_close()
# ValueError: I/O operation on closed file.
```

`sv.CSVSink.close()` already returns early when the file is closed; this gives `JSONSink.write_and_close()` the same guard.

## Change

`write_and_close()` returns without doing anything when the sink was never opened or its file is already closed. The first call still writes the rows and closes the file in a `finally`, as before.

## Tests

`tests/detection/test_json.py::TestJSONSinkLifecycle::test_write_and_close_inside_with_block_keeps_output` calls `write_and_close()` twice inside a `with` block and checks the file holds the appended row. It fails on `develop` with the `ValueError` above and passes with the fix. `tests/detection/test_json.py tests/detection/test_csv.py`: 58 passed. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` on the touched files are clean.

title: fix(detection): align compact mask IoU with dense contract
body:
## Description

`mask_iou_batch` has two implementations: dense NumPy masks and memory-efficient `CompactMask` masks. The compact implementation did not preserve the dense API contract in three production-relevant cases:

- Different image canvases were accepted instead of raising `ValueError`.
- Unsupported overlap metrics were only rejected after the bounding-box pre-filter found a pair, so disjoint inputs silently returned zeros.
- Python integer/float arithmetic could make an exact-threshold NMS decision differ from the dense float32 path.

Minimal repro for the threshold divergence:

```python
masks = np.zeros((2, 1, 10), dtype=bool)
masks[0, 0, 0] = True
masks[1, 0, :] = True
boxes = np.array([[0, 0, 9, 0], [0, 0, 9, 0]], dtype=np.float32)
compact = CompactMask.from_dense(masks, boxes, image_shape=(1, 10))

mask_non_max_suppression(predictions, masks, iou_threshold=0.1)
# array([False, True])
mask_non_max_suppression(predictions, compact, iou_threshold=0.1)
# array([ True, True])  # before this change
```

## Motivation

`CompactMask` is used to keep segmentation workloads memory-efficient, including NMS and metrics. A backend-specific result can silently change which detections survive or hide invalid caller input. Aligning the compact path with the dense path makes the optimized representation safe to substitute in the next release.

## Changes

- Validate shared `(H, W)` image shape before compact IoU work.
- Validate `IOU`/`IOS` before bounding-box pair filtering.
- Use the same float32-versus-float64 pixel-count policy as the dense implementation for overlap arithmetic.
- Add regression tests for all three behaviours and document the fix in the Unreleased changelog.

## Testing

- On the clean base `1fb42a45`, the three new regression tests fail (`3 failed, 225 deselected`).
- `uv run --frozen pytest tests/detection/utils/test_iou_and_nms.py -q` — 228 passed.
- `uv run --frozen pytest tests/detection/test_core.py tests/detection/test_inference_slicer_compact.py tests/detection/utils/test_internal.py -q` — 429 passed, 1 warning.
- `uv run --frozen pytest src/ tests/ --cov=supervision --cov-report=term-missing -q` — 6060 passed, 1 skipped, 38 warnings.
- `uv run pre-commit run --files src/supervision/detection/utils/iou_and_nms.py tests/detection/utils/test_iou_and_nms.py docs/changelog.md` — all applicable hooks passed.

title: fix(cv2): centre a thick fallback circle on its radius like OpenCV
body:
## Description

Without `opencv-python`, `sv` draws through the NumPy/Pillow fallback in `supervision._cv2`. Its `_circle` draws an outline with Pillow's `ellipse(..., width=thickness)`, which grows the stroke **inward** from the bounding box. OpenCV strokes a thick circle **centred on the radius** (half the thickness on each side). So every thick circle the fallback draws (`CircleAnnotator`, `DotAnnotator` outlines, key-point drawing, ...) is shrunk by half its thickness.

Measured against `cv2.circle` on a 30×30 canvas, radii 0–11, two centres:

| thickness | pixels differing before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2 | 1038 | 0 |
| 3 | 1959 | 0 |
| 5 | 3387 | 0 |

e.g. `_circle(img, (15, 15), 10, color, thickness=5)` should cover roughly radius 7.5–12.5; the fallback painted 5–10, leaving `(15, 27)` empty and painting `(15, 21)`.

## Change

For `thickness > 1`, `_circle` now delegates to the module's own `_ellipse` with `axes=(radius, radius)` and a full 0–360 arc. That is what OpenCV does internally (`circle` → `ellipse2Poly` + `ThickLine` for thick outlines), and `_ellipse` already reproduces it exactly, so the result is pixel-identical to `cv2.circle`. Filled circles and 1-px outlines are unchanged.

## Tests

`tests/cv2/test_drawing.py`:
- `test_fallback_thick_circle_is_centred_on_its_radius`: runs without OpenCV and checks pixels just outside and well inside the radius.
- `test_fallback_thick_circle_matches_opencv` (`@requires_cv2`): pixel-for-pixel against `cv2.circle` for thickness 2/3/5 × radius 1/4/9.

Before the fix: 10 failed. After: `tests/cv2/test_drawing.py` 108 passed; `tests/cv2 tests/annotators tests/draw` 949 passed. The 1 other failure, `test_ordinary_suite_passes_when_cv2_is_blocked`, fails the same way on unmodified `develop` in my environment. ruff check/format clean.

AI assistance: this change was prepared with an AI coding assistant and reviewed and tested by me.

title: fix(detection): prevent float16 overflow in box areas
body:
## Description

`Detections.box_area` multiplies float16 extents in float16, so a 256x256 box produces `inf` instead of `65536`. Tiny positive areas underflow to zero, and subtracting opposite-sign coordinates can overflow before multiplication.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 300, 300]], dtype=np.float16))
print(detections.area)  # develop: [inf]; fixed: [90000.]
print(len(detections[detections.area > 80000.0]))  # develop: 0; fixed: 1
```

## Motivation and Context

Area-based filtering silently drops ordinary objects in half-precision detector outputs. The mask and oriented-box area paths already use wider arithmetic.

## Changes Made

- Promote float16 coordinates to float32 before subtracting extents and multiplying areas.
- Document the promoted result dtype; retain integer, float32 and float64 behavior.
- Cover both byte orders, overflow, underflow, filtering, empty input and input preservation.

## Testing

- New regressions on clean `develop` (`1fb42a45f`): 18 failed, 2 passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/detection/test_core.py tests/detection/test_geometry_dispatch.py -q --tb=short`: 313 passed.
- `uv run pytest src/ tests/ --cov=supervision -q --tb=short`: 5749 passed, 123 skipped, 94% coverage (clean base: 5729 passed, 123 skipped).

title: fix(dataset): derive missing COCO areas from decoded masks
body:
## Description

COCO segmentation annotations without optional `area` metadata load with `area=NaN`. The shared evaluator excludes those targets from every area range, so even perfect predictions score mAP `-1`.

A minimal annotation is `{"id": 1, "image_id": 1, "category_id": 1, "bbox": [0, 0, 100, 100], "segmentation": [[0, 0, 49, 0, 49, 49, 0, 49]]}` for a 100x100 image. After `DetectionDataset.from_coco(...)`, `targets.data["area"]` is `[nan]` on `develop`; this change records `[2500.]`. Giving the imported targets confidence `0.9` and evaluating them against themselves with `MeanAveragePrecision` then scores `1.0` instead of `-1`, for both `MetricTarget.BOXES` and `MetricTarget.MASKS`.

## Motivation and Context

The COCO loader accepts omitted `area` fields and the exporter already derives missing areas from decoded masks. Imported labels must also carry usable areas for evaluation and object-size categorization.

## Changes Made

- Decode masks before constructing area metadata, then count each segmented mask whose annotation omitted `area`.
- Preserve explicit annotation areas, bounding-box fallback for box-only annotations, and raw segmentation when masks are not decoded.
- Cover polygon, uncompressed/compressed RLE, mixed annotations and the public COCO-import-to-mAP path.

## Testing

title: fix(detection): handle empty polygons in `filter_polygons_by_area` and `polygon_to_xyxy`
body:
## Problem
`sv.filter_polygons_by_area` crashes with `ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity` when any polygon in the input list has zero vertices (shape `(0, 2)`). This happens because `_to_local_cv2_polygon` calls `polygon.min(axis=0)` unconditionally without checking for empty polygons.
Similarly, `sv.polygon_to_xyxy` crashes with the same reduction `ValueError` when given an empty polygon instead of returning an all-zero bounding box matching Supervision's empty geometry convention (e.g. in `mask_to_xyxy`).

## Root cause
- In `_to_local_cv2_polygon`, `polygon.min(axis=0)` lacks a guard for `len(polygon) == 0`. An empty polygon has area `0.0` in OpenCV (`cv2.contourArea(np.empty((0, 2), dtype=np.float32)) == 0.0`). Returning `(np.empty((0, 2), dtype=np.float32), np.zeros(2, dtype=polygon.dtype))` allows `cv2.contourArea` to evaluate `0.0`, so `filter_polygons_by_area` filters empty polygons cleanly according to `min_area` / `max_area` without crashing.
- In `polygon_to_xyxy`, calling `np.min(polygon, axis=0)` on a zero-size array raises `ValueError`. Checking `len(polygon) == 0` and returning `np.zeros(4, dtype=output_dtype)` produces an all-zeros box while preserving caller dtype.

## Change
- In `src/supervision/detection/utils/polygons.py`: added an empty-array check in `_to_local_cv2_polygon` to return `(np.empty((0, 2), dtype=np.float32), np.zeros(2, dtype=polygon.dtype))` when `len(polygon) == 0`.
- In `src/supervision/detection/utils/converters.py`: added an empty-array check in `polygon_to_xyxy` to return `np.zeros(4, dtype=output_dtype)` when `len(polygon) == 0`.
- Added regression tests in `tests/detection/utils/test_polygons.py` and `tests/detection/utils/test_converters.py` covering empty polygons with area constraints and dtype preservation.

## Regression coverage
- `tests/detection/utils/test_polygons.py::test_filter_polygons_by_area`: parameterized with empty polygon cases (min_area filter, max_area filter, and mixed empty + valid polygons).
- `tests/detection/utils/test_converters.py::test_polygon_to_xyxy`: parameterized with `empty-polygon-int` and `empty-polygon-float32` verifying all-zeros bounding box output and dtype preservation.

## Validation
- `pytest tests/detection/utils/test_polygons.py tests/detection/utils/test_converters.py` — 221 passed
- `pytest tests/detection tests/geometry` — 2378 passed, 1 skipped
- `git diff --check` — clean

title: feat(detection): draw zones and lines at camera-mapped positions
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #2657: with a moving camera, zones and lines are now counted in reference-frame coordinates, but the annotators still drew them at their fixed pixel positions.

This PR adds the same optional `coord_transform` to `PolygonZoneAnnotator.annotate` and `LineZoneAnnotator.annotate`. The zone's vertices, the line's endpoints and their count labels are mapped with `coord_transform.abs_to_rel` and drawn where the camera sees them.

## Motivation and Context

Refs #2656 (the drawing part; #2657 covered counting). `LineZoneAnnotatorMulticlass` is not covered yet.

## Changes Made

- `coord_transform=None` on both `annotate` methods (last parameter); `None` keeps drawing and the returned array unchanged.
- Off-screen parts are clipped by the drawing backend, as for any geometry outside the frame.
- If any mapped point that will be drawn is non-finite or beyond ±2**20 px, that zone or line is not drawn for the frame (checked before rounding). The bound keeps coordinates within int32 and bounds drawing work for both backends.
- Oriented line labels (`text_orient_to_line=True`) are kept inside the frame only while the point they are anchored on (the line's mapped midpoint, or its end with `text_centered=False`) is on-screen; when it leaves the frame, they leave with the line instead of sticking to the edge. Without a transform, labels behave as before.
- Known limitation, documented in the code: a homography can map points behind the camera to finite, mirrored coordinates, which the points-only protocol cannot detect, so a zone crossing the horizon may be drawn folded.
- Docs: the "Follow a moving camera" how-to section and a changelog entry.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest` with and without OpenCV; ruff, mypy, codespell, docformatter and mdformat.
- New tests check explicit pixels: mapped outline, fill and labels, partly and fully off-screen zones and lines, NaN, inf and just-beyond-limit points, fractional and tie coordinates, and transforms that modify their input.
- With `coord_transform=None`, I compared the rendered output with `develop` locally on both backends (with and without OpenCV) across thicknesses, opacities and label options: byte-identical.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API

The private helpers `_get_line_angle`, `_calculate_anchor_in_frame` and `_draw_oriented_label` now take the line's `Vector` instead of the `LineZone`, so they can draw the mapped line, and the label angle is computed once in `annotate` and passed down; nothing else calls them.

title: fix(key_points): render three-coordinate points using x and y
body:
## Description

`KeyPoints` accepts `(N, K, 3)` coordinates, but `VertexAnnotator` and the shared covariance-ellipse renderer unpack every point into two values. They raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` for this accepted representation.

I use the first two coordinate columns for image-space drawing. This fixes vertex, ellipse area, ellipse outline and ellipse halo annotation. Edge and label annotators also use only x/y for missing-point and finiteness checks, so a third coordinate does not change visibility. Existing two-coordinate rendering and covariance handling stay unchanged.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

points = sv.KeyPoints(xy=np.array([[[25.0, 30.0, 0.2]]], dtype=np.float32))
scene = np.zeros((64, 64, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
sv.VertexAnnotator().annotate(scene, points)
```

## Motivation and Context

The coordinate validator accepts both two and three channels. Image annotators place pixels using x and y, while callers retain the extra coordinate in the original container. Selection already preserves that coordinate depth.

## Changes Made

- Limit unpacking and edge/label visibility checks to x/y.
- Add 16 vertex/ellipse cases and 48 edge/label cases for float32/float64, missing points, non-finite depth and explicit visibility. Compare images with two-coordinate input and check input preservation.

title: fix(metrics): match COCO target ties in mAR
body:
## Description

After #2750 added confidence-ordered mAR matching, equal-IoU targets still chose the first eligible target instead of COCO's last-target tie rule. A higher-confidence prediction could therefore consume the only target available to a later prediction and undercount recall.

This PR now builds on the merged #2750. It reverses the eligible target indices before selecting the maximum IoU, preserving confidence order, per-class detection limits, and crowd/ignore handling. The shared matcher and other metrics are unchanged.

For targets `[0, 0, 10, 10]` and `[10, 0, 20, 10]`, with predictions `[0, 0, 20, 10]` and `[0, 0, 10, 10]` at scores `0.9` and `0.8`, current develop returns AR `[0.05, 0.50, 0.50]`; this fix and pycocotools return `[0.05, 0.55, 0.55]`.

## Motivation and Context

Refs #2701 and follows up on #2750. Conflicts with #2750 have been resolved while retaining its crowd/ignore support and tests.

## Changes Made

- Match COCO's equal-IoU target tie rule in the existing confidence-ordered matcher.
- Retain box/mask/OBB confidence-order regression coverage and add equal-IoU cases with ordinary, crowd, and ignored targets.
- Correct the expected AR in #2750's overlapping-target test: official COCO gives `[0.1, 0.6, 0.6]` because its first prediction has equal IoU with both targets.
- Update the matcher docstring and changelog.

title: fix(annotators): draw masks and halos on grayscale scenes
body:
## Description

`MaskAnnotator` and `HaloAnnotator` raise `ValueError` on grayscale scenes: `(H, W)` arrays, `(H, W, 1)` arrays, and Pillow `"L"` images (which `pillow_to_cv2` turns into `(H, W)` arrays). `BoxAnnotator`, `PolygonAnnotator` and `ColorAnnotator` already work on the same scenes.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

mask = np.zeros((1, 10, 10), dtype=bool)
mask[0, 2:8, 2:8] = True
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[2, 2, 7, 7]], dtype=np.float32), mask=mask, class_id=np.array([0])
)
scene = np.zeros((10, 10), dtype=np.uint8)
sv.MaskAnnotator().annotate(scene, detections)
sv.HaloAnnotator().annotate(scene, detections)
```

Before (develop):

```
MaskAnnotator (H, W) array: ValueError: NumPy boolean array indexing assignment cannot assign 3 input values to the 36 output values where the mask is true
MaskAnnotator (H, W, 1) array: ValueError: shape mismatch: value array of shape (3,) could not be broadcast to indexing result of shape (36,1)
MaskAnnotator PIL 'L' image: ValueError: NumPy boolean array indexing assignment cannot assign 3 input values to the 36 output values where the mask is true
HaloAnnotator (H, W) array: ValueError: NumPy boolean array indexing assignment cannot assign 3 input values to the 36 output values where the mask is true
HaloAnnotator (H, W, 1) array: ValueError: shape mismatch: value array of shape (3,) could not be broadcast to indexing result of shape (36,1)
HaloAnnotator PIL 'L' image: ValueError: NumPy boolean array indexing assignment cannot assign 3 input values to the 36 output values where the mask is true
```

After (color `sv.Color(r=10, g=20, b=200)`):

```
MaskAnnotator (H, W) array: shape (10, 10), center 200, edge 0
MaskAnnotator (H, W, 1) array: shape (10, 10, 1), center [200], edge [0]
MaskAnnotator PIL 'L' image: shape (10, 10), center 200, edge 0
HaloAnnotator (H, W) array: shape (10, 10), center 0, edge 53
HaloAnnotator (H, W, 1) array: shape (10, 10, 1), center [0], edge [53]
HaloAnnotator PIL 'L' image: shape (10, 10), center 0, edge 53
PolygonAnnotator (H, W) outline value: 200
```

## Motivation and Context

`_paint_masks_by_area` writes `color.as_bgr()`, a three-value color, into every canvas pixel under a mask. A single-channel canvas cannot take three values. The other annotators draw through OpenCV (`cv2.rectangle`, `cv2.fillPoly`), and OpenCV writes the color's first (blue) value on a one-channel image. Grayscale scenes are already supported elsewhere: `pillow_to_cv2` returns `(H, W)` arrays for single-channel Pillow modes, and #2725 fixed the same layouts in `BlurAnnotator` and `PixelateAnnotator`.

## Changes Made

- `_paint_masks_by_area` now paints a grayscale canvas with the first channel of the color, so a mask gets the same gray value as the box or polygon outline for that detection.
- `MaskAnnotator`: restore the singleton channel axis that OpenCV's `addWeighted` drops before writing the blend back.
- `HaloAnnotator`: restore the channel axis after `blur`, clear the mask area with a scalar, and take the halo alpha straight from the single channel instead of `COLOR_BGR2GRAY`.
- Docstrings of both `annotate` methods describe the grayscale layouts.
- BGR scenes take exactly the same code path as before. BGRA scenes are out of scope.

## Testing

- New `TestSingleChannelMaskAnnotators` (12 cases): mask and halo on `(H, W)` and `(H, W, 1)` scenes, with dense masks and `CompactMask`, must equal channel 0 of the same annotation on the BGR copy of the scene. A gray mask must take `color.b`, like `PolygonAnnotator` and `ColorAnnotator`. A Pillow `"L"` image must come back as an `"L"` image.
- On `develop`: 6 failed, 2 passed (the polygon and color reference cases). With this change: 12 passed, with OpenCV 5.0 and with the NumPy fallback.
- `pytest` full suite with OpenCV: 6069 passed, 1 skipped. Without OpenCV: 5741 passed, 123 skipped.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, codespell and the other hooks pass. mypy reports no new errors.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

On a grayscale scene a color has no single obvious gray. I used the first (blue) channel because that is what every OpenCV-drawn annotator already writes, so masks, boxes and polygons on the same frame agree. Converting colors to luminance would need the same change in all of those annotators, which is beyond this fix. `CropAnnotator`, `BackgroundOverlayAnnotator`, `HeatMapAnnotator` and `RichLabelAnnotator` also fail on grayscale scenes; I left them for separate PRs.

title: fix(cv2): preserve grayscale and BGRA images when encoding
body:
## Description

Without OpenCV, the Pillow-backed encoders fail to save valid `(H, W, 4)` BGRA images as JPEG and raise `TypeError` for `(H, W, 1)` grayscale images. An in-memory dataset export can therefore return successfully without a usable output image because its writer's `False` result is ignored.

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

dataset = sv.DetectionDataset(
    classes=["object"],
    images={"image.jpg": np.full((8, 10, 4), 120, dtype=np.uint8)},
    annotations={"image.jpg": sv.Detections.empty()},

# Without OpenCV, before this fix: out/image.jpg cannot be read.

OpenCV accepts one-, three- and four-channel images. Pillow expects grayscale arrays to be two-dimensional and cannot encode RGBA directly as JPEG. Dataset export should retain its images when users run with the default OpenCV-free installation.

title: fix(detection): prevent overflow in NMM confidence weights
body:
## Description

`Detections.with_nmm()` calculates merge confidence from box areas, but subtracts the corners in the input dtype before widening to `float64`. Signed integer extents can wrap and half-precision extents can become infinite, producing the wrong score or `NaN`.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[-30000, 0, 30000, 1], [-15000, 0, 30000, 1]], dtype=np.int16),
    confidence=np.array([0.9, 0.6]),
    class_id=np.array([0, 0]),
)
print(detections.with_nmm().confidence)  # Before: [0.9]; expected: about [0.7714286]
```

## Motivation and Context

The merged detection's score should use its actual box areas regardless of the coordinate dtype. This affects downstream filtering of merged detections, including tiled inference pipelines.

## Changes Made

- Widen floating corners before subtracting; subtract integer corners as Python integers to retain narrow extents above `2**53`.
- Keep area weighting, winner selection, geometry union and output conventions intact.
- Add public NMM regressions for horizontal/vertical extents and guards for narrow signed/unsigned 64-bit boxes.

`MeanAverageRecall`, `Precision`, `Recall` and `F1Score` compared a float64 oriented-box IoU with float32 IoU thresholds. float32 rounds 0.55, 0.6, 0.8 and 0.85 up, so an OBB prediction with IoU exactly on one of those thresholds missed it, while the same geometry as `BOXES` matched. title: fix(metrics): leave crowd and ignored targets out of `MeanAverageRecall`
body:
## Description

`MeanAverageRecall` now leaves COCO ignore regions out of recall. These are targets with `data["iscrowd"]` or `data["ignore"]` set, the same rule `MeanAveragePrecision` applies. They were counted as misses, so mAR on COCO data with crowd annotations came out lower than `pycocotools` AR. With one normal target, one crowd target and a perfect prediction, `mAR_at_100` was 0.5; `pycocotools` gives 1.0, and so does this PR.

## Motivation and Context

Closes #2749

`DetectionDataset.from_coco` keeps `iscrowd` by default, and #2689 / #2701 set `pycocotools` AR as the reference for this metric.

## Changes Made

- `MeanAverageRecall._compute` drops ignore-region targets before the size filter, through a new `_drop_ignored_targets`.
  - This matches COCO for recall. COCO tries non-ignored targets first and only lets a prediction match an ignore region when no regular target is left for it, and a prediction on an ignore region adds nothing to recall.
  - A class whose only targets are crowd regions drops out of the mean, as COCO reports -1 for it.
- Class docstring: one paragraph on crowd and ignore targets.
- Tests: crowd and `ignore` targets are not misses; a class with only crowd targets is left out of the mean.
- `docs/changelog.md` entry.
- Out of scope: `Precision`, `Recall` and `F1Score` also ignore `iscrowd`. They aren't COCO metrics, so I left them alone. Happy to follow up if you want the same rule there.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: all 3 fail with recall `[0.5, 0.5, 0.5]` instead of `[1, 1, 1]`.
- With this change: `uv run pytest tests/metrics`, 661 passed. Full suite: `uv run pytest`, 5697 passed, 105 skipped (`develop`: 5694 passed, 105 skipped).
- Against `pycocotools` 2.0.11 on a seeded harness (0–3 crowd targets per image, 100 trials, boxes):
  - `develop`: mismatches in 77 trials.
  - This PR: 2 trials. Both remaining differences come from the matcher pairing the highest IoU first rather than in confidence order, the leftover #2701 noted. I'll file that separately.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` passes.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

title: fix(dataset): round Pascal VOC bndbox corners instead of truncating them
body:
## Description

`object_to_pascal_voc` wrote `<bndbox>` corners with `int()`, which truncates. A fractional box lost up to a pixel per corner, and a box read from 6-decimal YOLO labels could be written with `xmin=0`, outside 1-indexed VOC. The corners are now rounded to the nearest integer pixel.

```python
elem = object_to_pascal_voc(np.array([10.9, 10.9, 20.9, 20.9]), name="cat")
[elem.find(f"bndbox/{t}").text for t in ("xmin", "ymin", "xmax", "ymax")]
# develop:  ['11', '11', '21', '21']
# this PR:  ['12', '12', '22', '22']
```

## Motivation and Context

Closes #2747

YOLO → VOC conversion is where this bites. `from_yolo` returns corners a hair off the integer pixel, so the integer box `[0, 0, 37, 29]` from an Ultralytics label came back from VOC as `[-1, -1, 37, 28]`. It now round-trips to `[0, 0, 37, 29]`.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/dataset/formats/pascal_voc.py`: `str(round(x))` instead of `str(int(x))` for the four `<bndbox>` corners, and a docstring note.
- `tests/dataset/formats/test_pascal_voc.py`: parametrized test for rounding up, rounding down, and the YOLO float-noise box.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.
- Left alone: `<polygon>` points are already written unrounded, as before.

## Testing

- New test on `develop`: 2 of 3 cases fail (`('11', '11', '21', '21') != ('12', '12', '22', '22')` and `('0', '0', '38', '29') != ('1', '1', '38', '30')`). The rounds-down case passes on both and guards against a ceil-based fix.
- With this change: `uv run pytest tests/dataset/formats/test_pascal_voc.py`, 58 passed.
- Full suite: `uv run pytest`, 5697 passed, 105 skipped (`develop`: 5694 passed, 105 skipped).
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` passes.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

Python's `round` rounds halves to even (`10.5` → `10`), the same as `np.round`. An exact half-pixel corner has no better answer either way, so I kept the standard behaviour rather than adding a half-up rule.

title: fix(video): read files with audio before the video stream
body:
## Description

Without OpenCV, videos whose first video stream follows an audio stream cannot be decoded. The PyAV fallback passes the video's global container index to `decode(video=...)`, but that selector indexes only video streams. In an audio-first MP4, the first video has container index `1` and video index `0`: `read()` silently returns `False`, and reading the dimensions raises `IndexError: tuple index out of range`.

Select video stream `0`, consistently with `streams.video[0]`, for initial decoding, frame-count fallback, display-rotation metadata and decoder reset during backward seeking.

## Motivation and Context

Stream order is valid container metadata and should not prevent `VideoInfo.from_video_path`, `get_video_frames_generator` or the fallback capture from reading the file. This affects the default installation without OpenCV. No external model or download is needed to reproduce it: write an AAC stream before an MPEG-4 stream in a local MP4, then read it with the fallback.

## Changes Made

- Correct the four PyAV decode selectors.
- Add real MP4 and Matroska fixtures with audio-first and video-first stream orders, checking dimensions, frame count, reads and backward seeking.
- Cover the public video APIs with synchronous and prefetched reads.
- Add an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

Windows, Python 3.13.15, PyAV 18.0.0, NumPy fallback backend (OpenCV absent). Commands use the existing development environment's Python with this worktree's `src` on `PYTHONPATH`.

- Clean `develop` at `6ecb27963`: `python -m pytest tests/cv2/test_video.py -k audio_before_video -q --tb=short` — 4 failed with the stream-index error, 2 passed.
- Fixed: `python -m pytest tests/cv2/test_video.py tests/utils/test_video.py -q --tb=short` — 112 passed, 5 skipped.
- Clean baseline: `python -m pytest src tests --cov=supervision -q --tb=short` — 5694 passed, 105 skipped.
- Fixed full suite: `python -m pytest src tests --cov=supervision -q --tb=short` — 5700 passed, 105 skipped.
- `python -m pre_commit run --all-files` — all hooks passed, including mypy.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docstrings for the corrected behavior
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

The capture continues to select the first video stream. Codec selection, audio remuxing and the OpenCV backend are unchanged.

title: feat(dataset): add `KeyPointsDataset` with YOLO pose support
body:
Closes #1438

`supervision` could load detection, segmentation and classification datasets, but
not keypoint ones. `DetectionDataset.from_yolo` reads a pose dataset by keeping the
box of each label and discarding the keypoint values outright, so the keypoints of a
pose dataset were unreachable.

`KeyPointsDataset` is the keypoint counterpart of `DetectionDataset`: lazy image
loading, `__len__`, `__getitem__`, `__iter__`, `__eq__`, `split`, `merge`,
`from_yolo` and `as_yolo`. Per @LinasKo's note on the issue, images are a list of
paths only — the deprecated in-memory dict is not carried over.

This is a fresh design rather than a revival of #1477. That PR was closed as having
"drifted too far", and @shaddu agreed YOLO pose data needed a new approach, so
nothing from it is reused here.

### Three things a pose label holds that `KeyPoints` has no field for

**The box.** Kept under the existing `XYXY_DATA_FIELD`, which is already documented
as per-skeleton boxes in `KeyPoints.data` and already read by
`KeyPointMeanAveragePrecision`. No new constant.

**The visibility flag.** YOLO and COCO write a ternary `0`/`1`/`2` while
`KeyPoints.visible` is boolean, so `visible` is the `flag == 2` reading and the raw
value is kept under a new `KEYPOINT_VISIBILITY_DATA_FIELD`. Without it `as_yolo`
cannot tell an unlabelled keypoint (`0`) from a labelled-but-occluded one (`1`).

**`kpt_shape` and `flip_idx`.** Held on the dataset as `keypoint_count`,
`value_dim` and `flip_idx`, so `as_yolo` writes a `data.yaml` that reads back.
`flip_idx` is validated as a permutation of the keypoint indices on load — a
repeated or out-of-range entry would silently drop or duplicate a joint in every
mirrored sample — and is carried through `split` and `merge`, which refuses to merge
datasets that disagree on it. A dataset declaring no `flip_idx` does not gain one.

A dataset therefore survives `from_yolo` → `as_yolo` with each annotation line
rewritten unchanged, to the six significant digits the writer emits, pinned for both
`[K, 2]` and `[K, 3]`. That exceeds the five decimals `object_to_yolo` writes for
detection labels; a source label carrying more precision is rewritten rounded, which
a test pins explicitly.

### Shared with the detection loader rather than reimplemented

The box goes through `yolo._parse_box`, which rejects a non-finite or
negative-extent box before it can reach `data['xyxy']` with its corners reversed —
where `box_iou_batch` would report zero overlap and `KeyPointMeanAveragePrecision`
would silently score it wrong. The writer orders corners through
`_sort_box_corners`, as `object_to_yolo` does, so it cannot emit a file the
library's own loader then refuses. The list of loadable image extensions is now one
constant both loaders import.

`save_dataset_images` read `dataset._images_in_memory` directly; it now reads it
through `getattr`, since a lazy-only dataset has no such store. `DetectionDataset`
behaviour is unchanged.

### Usage

```python
import supervision as sv

ds = sv.KeyPointsDataset.from_yolo(
    images_directory_path="images",
    annotations_directory_path="labels",
    data_yaml_path="data.yaml",
)

path, image, key_points = ds[0]
key_points.xy                            # (N, K, 2) in pixels
key_points.visible                       # (N, K) bool, flag == 2
key_points.data["keypoint_visibility"]   # (N, K) uint8, raw 0/1/2
key_points.data["xyxy"]                  # (N, 4) object boxes

train, test = ds.split(split_ratio=0.8)
ds.as_yolo("out/images", "out/labels", "out/data.yaml")
```

`KeyPoints` flows unchanged into the existing `VertexAnnotator` and `EdgeAnnotator`.

### Verification

- 70 new tests; `tests/dataset`, `tests/metrics` and `tests/key_points` green.
- Round trip pinned for `[K, 2]`, `[K, 3]` and `flip_idx`, comparing the written
  file exactly rather than stripped.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` clean, mypy included.
- Rebased on `develop` after the `0.31.0` release and re-verified.

### Addressed from review

The automated review raised six findings. All six reproduced and are fixed:
`(N, K, 3)` keypoints no longer break the writer (the planar pair is selected, as
the keypoint metric already does); a joint with no flags at all is written as flag
`0` rather than `2`, so a missing joint does not become a training target at the
image origin; `flip_idx` is preserved; the round-trip precision claim is narrowed to
what the writer actually guarantees and pinned by a test; and
`map_key_points_class_id` deep-copies like `map_detections_class_id` rather than
using `np.copy`, which coerced a Python list in `data` into an array.

One is deliberately left out of this PR. Flag `1` (labelled but not visible) maps to
`visible=False`, the drawing meaning the annotators want, while
`KeyPointMeanAveragePrecision` reads `visible` alone and therefore excludes those
joints from OKS — COCO counts `v=1` toward OKS and ignores only `v=0`. Fixing that
means making the metric read raw visibility `> 0`, a behaviour change in another
module that wants its own PR. The raw flags are stored precisely so that fix stays
small. Happy to open the issue.

### Deliberately out of scope

`from_coco` / `as_coco` and `from_mediapipe` / `as_mediapipe` (@miteshashar's
suggestion on the issue) are left for follow-ups — the visibility field is stored
raw specifically so COCO's identical ternary maps straight across.

One known limitation worth flagging separately: `KeyPoints.__getitem__` narrows `xy`
and `visible` along the keypoint axis but carries `data` entries through whole, so
any keypoint-aligned `data` field comes out mis-shaped. `keypoint_visibility` is the
first such field, so this PR is where it surfaces, but the gap is upstream of it.
The writer raises an error naming the field instead of failing inside NumPy. Happy
to open an issue for it.

title: perf(compact_mask): sum `CompactMask.area` in one NumPy reduction
body:
## Description

`CompactMask.area` built its result with a Python loop, one `_rle_area` call (and one `np.sum`) per mask. This PR sums many masks per NumPy call: it concatenates each RLE's foreground runs (its odd entries, as int64) and adds them up per mask with `np.add.reduceat`, in chunks of about 65,536 runs so the temporary copy stays small. The output is unchanged: an int64 array of shape `(N,)`.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

masks = np.zeros((3, 6, 8), dtype=bool)
masks[1] = True
masks[2, 2:4, 3:6] = True
boxes = np.array([[0, 0, 7, 5]] * 3, dtype=np.float32)
compact = sv.CompactMask.from_dense(masks, boxes, image_shape=(6, 8))
print(compact.area, compact.area.dtype)  # [ 0 48  6] int64 on develop and here
```

## Motivation and Context

CONTRIBUTING asks for vectorized operations in hot paths, and `area` runs on every frame: `_paint_masks_by_area` sorts by it in `MaskAnnotator` and `HaloAnnotator`, `compact_mask_iou_batch` reads it for both inputs, and it backs `Detections.area` and the object-size buckets in metrics. No issue was opened; the per-mask loop showed up while measuring the cost of #2741, which this PR does not depend on.

## Changes Made

- `CompactMask.area`: `np.add.reduceat` over the concatenated foreground runs of consecutive masks, one call per chunk of about 65,536 runs (`_AREA_CHUNK_RUNS`, ~512 KiB of int64). A mask with more runs than one chunk is reduced on its own. Masks without foreground runs are left out of each reduction and keep zero area (`reduceat` cannot express an empty segment), and `N=0` needs no special case. Casting to int64 while concatenating keeps the sums exact where NumPy's default integer is 32-bit and avoids `reduceat`'s slower buffered cast.
- Updated the `Note` in the docstring, which described the loop.
- Tests (`TestArea`):
  - areas equal `_rle_area` per mask and the dense pixel count, with int64 dtype and `(N,)` shape, for: an empty collection; all-False; all-True; a single pixel; a crop whose RLE starts with a zero-length background run; one that ends in foreground; and crops of different sizes in one collection;
  - a seeded random collection with loose, empty and all-True crops, run with chunk sizes 1, 7, 100 and 65,536;
  - a crop whose foreground run was split at the int32 limit.
- Changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

Out of scope: `_rle_area` stays (`_resize_crop` uses it for one crop), and no consumer changes.

## Testing

Windows x64, Python 3.11.9, NumPy 2.3.1, locked environment (`uv sync --frozen`), `develop` at `6ecb279`.

- New tests on `develop`: they pass. This is a refactor with the same results, so they pin behaviour rather than reproduce a bug. The exception is the int32 case under NumPy 1.x on Windows, where the default integer is 32-bit: with NumPy 1.26.4, `develop` returns `-2147483644` for a crop with 2³¹ + 4 foreground pixels (its `np.sum` accumulates in int32), and this branch returns `2147483652`. No public path was found that produces such a crop from validated image sizes, so this is a safeguard, not a bug fix.
- `pytest tests/detection/test_compact_mask*.py tests/detection/test_geometry_dispatch.py tests/annotators/test_core.py tests/detection/utils/test_iou_and_nms.py tests/metrics`: 1,698 passed (NumPy fallback backend).
- `pytest --doctest-modules src/supervision/detection/compact_mask.py`: 31 passed.
- Full suite, `pytest --cov=supervision`: 5,706 passed, 105 skipped, 94% coverage.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: all hooks pass.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

`CompactMask.area`, `develop` time / this PR's time, on a Windows x64 laptop with 1280×720 masks. Each run of one revision was followed by a run of the other. The ranges come from the two pairs whose clock speed stayed constant, one with OpenCV 4.12 and one with the NumPy fallback; a third pair, during which the laptop's clock sped up about 3×, is left out.

| Masks | RLE runs per mask | N=10 | N=100 | N=500 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50×40 rectangles | 2 | 1.2–1.3× | 4.7–6.2× | 6.7–8.6× |
| Ellipses 20–300 px wide | ~330 | 1.2–1.5× | 4.1–6.3× | 5.9–7.4× |
| 100×100 crops of 50 % noise | ~5,000 | 1.4–1.6× | 2.1–2.5× | 2.1–2.4× |

For example, 500 ellipses: 6.08 → 0.82 ms in the OpenCV pair and 1.27 → 0.21 ms in the fallback pair. Absolute times moved about 4× with the laptop's clock, so only ratios within a pair are compared.

The same script on Linux, in a `python:3.11.9-slim` container on the same laptop with the same pinned packages, gave three stable pairs (two with OpenCV, one with the fallback):

| Masks (Linux) | N=10 | N=100 | N=500 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50×40 rectangles | 1.1–1.3× | 4.3–5.4× | 7.2–9.0× |
| Ellipses 20–300 px wide | 1.2–1.7× | 3.0–4.3× | 4.3–5.5× |
| 100×100 crops of 50 % noise | 0.9–1.2× | 1.8–1.9× | 1.7–2.5× |

For example, 500 ellipses went from 1.07 to 0.20 ms. Areas, IoU matrices and annotated frames had the same checksums on Linux and Windows.

- `MaskAnnotator.annotate()` and `sv.mask_iou_batch` on the same masks show no measurable change on either system (mostly 0.8–1.2× within pairs, in both directions). The saving, a few milliseconds with 500 masks, is below their run-to-run variation. Areas, IoU matrices and annotated frames had identical checksums on both revisions.
- Codex review: the first version (2ef4cd1) concatenated the whole collection at once, so the int64 copy was about as large as the full RLE payload. 4299d3d reduces in chunks instead. Chunks also helped heavily fragmented masks: with 500 noise masks the single copy was 1.0× (Windows) and 1.2× (Linux) faster than `develop`, against about 2× with chunks.
- Rejected alternatives, measured in one process on the same masks, on Windows and on Linux:
  - Concatenating all runs and summing the odd positions per mask. These versions copy every background run and build per-run index arrays. On 100–500 noise masks, the first prototype (`np.bincount` on float64 weights) was 16–30× slower than `develop`, int64 prefix sums 4–9× slower, and `reduceat` over strided views up to 4.5× slower.
  - Concatenating the odd-run views as int32 and letting `reduceat` cast. This was 1.3–1.5× slower than copying them as int64 on 500 noise masks.

The benchmark and comparison scripts are synthetic (no downloads) and can be shared.

title: fix(metrics): prevent coordinate overflow in mAP
body:
## Description

`MeanAveragePrecision` can ignore valid float16 detections or misclassify integer boxes by size because box extents and areas are calculated in the coordinate array's dtype. Convert box rows to Python scalars before arithmetic for both targets and predictions.

Minimal reproduction on `develop`:

```python
import numpy as np
from supervision import Detections
from supervision.metrics import MeanAveragePrecision

xyxy = np.array([[0, 0, 512, 512]], dtype=np.float16)
target = Detections(xyxy=xyxy, class_id=np.array([0]))
prediction = Detections(
    xyxy=xyxy.copy(), class_id=np.array([0]), confidence=np.array([0.9])
)
result = MeanAveragePrecision().update(prediction, target).compute()
print(result.map50_95, result.large_objects.map50_95)
```

Before: `-1 -1`. With this fix: `1.0 1.0`. The area `512 * 512` overflows float16 to infinity, so the evaluator ignores the ground truth. With uint16 the same area wraps to zero and puts the large object in the small bucket. Extent subtraction can also overflow for int16 and float16 boxes spanning negative and positive coordinates.

## Motivation and Context

Overflow can also inflate scores: a high-confidence unmatched float16 512×512 box is ignored, turning an expected mAP of `0.5` into `1.0`. Coordinate storage dtype should not determine whether a valid box participates in evaluation.

## Changes Made

- Compute target and prediction box extents and areas using Python scalars, preserving caller arrays and their dtypes.
- Add 11 public-result regression/control cases covering float16, uint16, int16, int32, float32, float64, and int64, including false-positive filtering by area.
- Add an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

- Base `6ecb27963`, new regression cases: **7 failed, 4 passed** for the expected score/size-bucket differences.
- `uv run pytest tests/metrics -q --tb=short`: **669 passed**.
- `uv run pytest src/ tests/ --cov=supervision -q --tb=short`: **5,704 passed, 105 skipped, 1 timed out**. The nested no-OpenCV subprocess exceeded its 180-second limit while other checks were running. Its isolated rerun passed in 52.70 seconds (`uv run pytest tests/cv2/test_integration.py::test_ordinary_suite_passes_when_cv2_is_blocked -q --tb=short`).
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: **all hooks passed** (including mypy, Ruff, formatting, and codespell).
- Untouched base full suite: **5,694 passed, 105 skipped**.
- Final head `20d1c5741d9547df77f89091162dfd0277b78aab` adds only the PR link to the changelog after the source validation. `uv run pytest tests/metrics/test_mean_average_precision_area.py tests/cv2/test_release.py -q --tb=short`: **18 passed**; changelog pre-commit hooks passed.

- [x] Added/updated tests; full-suite results and the passing isolated timeout rerun are recorded above
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API — not applicable; no public API change
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

Public signatures are unchanged. Evaluation still uses the existing COCO area ranges. No optional model downloads are needed to reproduce this issue.
