title: fix(compact_mask): Match dense nearest-neighbor resizing
body:
## Description

I fixed `CompactMask.resize` losing foreground pixels and disagreeing with dense nearest-neighbor resizing. A singleton in a 10x10 image stays one pixel after resizing to 100x100 instead of becoming a 10x10 block. A full foreground image grows to only 91x91. Downscaling also keeps crops that the output grid never samples.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

masks = np.zeros((1, 10, 10), dtype=bool)
masks[0, 2, 3] = True
compact = sv.CompactMask.from_dense(
    masks, sv.mask_to_xyxy(masks), image_shape=(10, 10)
)
print(compact.resize((100, 100)).area[0])  # expected 100, previously 1
```

## Motivation and Context

Scaling inclusive crop endpoints shortens enlarged crops. Resampling each crop independently also uses a different sampling origin and ratio from resizing the full image. I use dense `cv2.resize(..., INTER_NEAREST)` as the reference.

## Changes Made

- Derive the full-image sampling grid through the active resize backend, then select each crop's output interval and source pixels.
- Keep sparse run-length processing, dense cropped processing, and threaded batches. Crops with no sampled pixels become all-False.
- Add 20 exact-parity regression cases and tighten ten existing random cases. Their previous Boolean `max(abs(diff)) <= 1` assertion could not detect a mismatch.
- Update the resize docstring and changelog. Public signatures and encoded mask formats stay unchanged.

## Testing

- Confirmed pristine source: all 30 regression cases fail for pixel mismatches.
- `py -3.13 -m pytest tests/detection/test_compact_mask.py -q`: 337 passed.
- `py -3.13 -m pytest -p pytest_cov --cov=supervision -q`: 5,110 passed, 6 skipped, 40 warnings; total coverage 93%. Pristine `develop` has 5,090 passes and the same skips/warnings.
- Repository pre-commit hooks and whitespace checks pass.
- Identity, empty, all-False, aligned full-foreground downsampling, repeated calls, and source immutability pass on both base and patch.
- 900 random masks per backend match dense resizing, using native OpenCV and the NumPy resize implementation at the compatibility facade.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

I kept processing cropped masks because decoding the full mask collection would lose its memory advantage. The sampling arrays add memory: for eight dense 128x160 masks resized to 96x120, traced peak allocation grows from about 750 KiB to 919 KiB. This is a correctness fix, with no memory or speedup claim.

Linux/macOS and a fresh environment without OpenCV remain untested locally. The explicit NumPy resize check above does not replace that environment's full suite.

title: fix(classification): reject negative top-k counts
body:
## Description

`Classifications.get_top_k(-1)` returned every classification except the lowest-confidence one because the negative count was passed directly to NumPy slicing. This change rejects negative counts with `ValueError("k must be non-negative")`.

Minimal reproduction:

```python
classifications = sv.Classifications(
    class_id=np.array([0, 1, 2]),
    confidence=np.array([0.1, 0.9, 0.5]),
)
classifications.get_top_k(-1)
```

Before this change, the call returned class IDs `[1, 2]` with confidences `[0.9, 0.5]`. It now raises a clear error.

## Motivation and Context

A negative count cannot represent the number of top classifications to retrieve. Silently applying negative-slice semantics can hide invalid caller input and return a plausible but incorrect subset.

## Changes Made

- Validate that `k` is non-negative before sorting classifications.
- Document the new error and cover it with a regression test.

## Testing

- `uv run --no-sync pytest tests/classification -q`: `10 passed`.

body: *One frame, three sources, one line each to load. Left: Depth Anything V3 through Roboflow's hosted API. Middle: YOLO26 depth, in metres; it sees the opening in the rock as far and everything else as close. Right: the dataset's true depth, read from its 16-bit PNG.* ### ▶️📓 [Notebook Playground Demo (all 4 PRs together)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/roboflow/supervision/blob/playground/depth-maps/examples/depth_playground.ipynb) ## Description Every depth model returns its map in its own shape and unit: a base64 16-bit PNG normalised to 0..1, a torch tensor in metres, a `predicted_depth` of unknown kind. These loaders turn each into a `sv.DepthMap` with the right kind, the same way `sv.Detections.from_ultralytics` does for boxes: ```python depth_map = sv.DepthMap.from_inference(result) # depth models served by Roboflow Inference depth_map = sv.DepthMap.from_ultralytics(results[0]) # YOLO26 depth, metres depth_map = sv.DepthMap.from_transformers(output, kind="relative_inverse") depth_map = sv.DepthMap.from_png16("disp_occ_0/000000_10.png", scale=256, kind="disparity_px") # KITTI depth_map = sv.DepthMap.from_pfm("disp0GT.pfm", kind="disparity_px") # Middlebury ``` Part 4 of 4. Needs PR 1 (#2691). ## Motivation and Context Follows #2691, where a map is built from an array by hand. ## Changes Made - `from_inference`: every `depth_map_format` (JSON lists, 8- or 16-bit PNG, and the array the SDK and Workflows decode), plus an in-process model's response, as `relative_inverse`. - `from_ultralytics`: `result.depth.data`, metres at the original image size. - `from_transformers`: `predicted_depth` from the `depth-estimation` pipeline or a model output. Transformers does not say what a model predicts, so `kind` is required. - `from_png16(path, scale, kind)`: 16-bit PNGs divided by the dataset's scale, with 0 as no depth (KITTI disparity uses 256, Ultralytics depth datasets 1000 by default). - `from_pfm(path, kind)`: Middlebury and SceneFlow PFM files, with unknown values as no depth. - Docs: the how-to's loading section, docstring examples and a changelog entry. ## Testing ``` pytest tests/depth --doctest-modules src/supervision/depth 63 passed (24 new) pytest 4856 passed, 79 skipped pre-commit run all hooks pass mkdocs build no new warnings ``` - [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally - [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API - [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` - [x] `from_inference` on hosted `depth-anything-v3/small`, in both `png16` and JSON formats: full image size, every pixel valid, near objects warm (image above) - [x] `from_ultralytics` on `yolo26n-depth.pt`: metres at the image's exact size (image above) - [x] Tests are offline: model outputs are built in the tests, no downloads ## Additional Notes - `inference`, `ultralytics`, `transformers` and `torch` are not imported by supervision. The loaders read the objects these libraries return.

body: *A YOLO26 detection on a frame of the Spring movie. The label is the median distance inside the box, from the dataset's true stereo depth and its camera (focal length 1346.8 px, baseline 6.5 cm).* ### ▶️📓 [Notebook Playground Demo (all 4 PRs together)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/roboflow/supervision/blob/playground/depth-maps/examples/depth_playground.ipynb) ## Description A depth map is most useful as a distance: how far is that person, that car. With the stereo rig's focal length and baseline, a disparity map gives metres, and `measure_detections` stores the median distance under each object in `detections.data`: ```python camera = sv.DepthCamera(fx_px=1346.8, baseline_m=0.065) depth_map = sv.DepthMap(disparity, kind="disparity_px", camera=camera) detections = depth_map.measure_detections(detections) labels = [f"{name} {metres:.2f} m" for name, metres in zip(detections["class_name"], detections.data["depth_m"])] annotated_image = sv.LabelAnnotator().annotate(image.copy(), detections, labels) ``` Part 3 of 4. Needs PR 1 (#2691). ## Motivation and Context Follows #2691. Distance per object is the most asked-for use of depth next to colouring it. ## Changes Made - `sv.DepthCamera(fx_px, baseline_m, doffs_px=0.0)` and `DepthMap.to_depth()`: disparity to metres with `fx_px * baseline_m / (disparity + doffs_px)`. - `DepthMap.measure_detections(detections)`: median depth inside each dense mask, `CompactMask` or box. It is stored under `depth_m` when the map can give metres, else under `disparity_px` or `relative_inverse` (constants in `supervision.config`). Objects with no depth get `NaN`. - `sv.DepthAnnotator(quantity="depth")` colours metres instead of disparity (`sv.DepthQuantity`), with near still warm. - `resize`, `crop` and `value_at`: - Sizes change without blending holes into depth. - `resize(method="foreground")` keeps thin near objects when shrinking. - Disparity and the camera scale with the width. - Docs: the how-to's distance section, reference entries and a changelog entry. ## Testing ``` pytest tests/depth --doctest-modules src/supervision/depth 77 passed (38 new) pytest 4872 passed, 79 skipped pre-commit run all hooks pass mkdocs build no new warnings ``` - [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally - [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API - [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` - [x] The image above: `yolo26n` detection, distance from Spring's ground-truth disparity and its rig (fx 1346.8 px, baseline 6.5 cm) ## Additional Notes - `quantity="depth"` on a map without metres raises `ValueError` naming what is missing (a camera, or a metric map).

title: feat(depth): add `DepthClipRange` for one colour scale across video
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6928ad8e-de69-4630-b2d2-ff6aed4b7263

*The stereo pair as a video: both cameras on top, the matcher's depth and the true depth below, coloured with one range for the whole clip.*

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3eff4c63-5858-4a3f-86ca-5b096862ef3f

*The same 8 s clip twice, coloured from the dataset's true depth, which is steady. Left: each frame coloured with its own range, so the same object changes colour as the scene moves. Right: one range for the whole clip with `sv.DepthClipRange`, so a colour keeps meaning the same distance.*

### ▶️📓 [Notebook Playground Demo (all 4 PRs together)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/roboflow/supervision/blob/playground/depth-maps/examples/depth_playground.ipynb)

## Description

Colouring each video frame with its own range rescales the colours on every frame, so the same distance can change colour as the scene changes. `sv.DepthClipRange` computes one range for the whole clip and keeps the colour scale fixed. Colours then stay put wherever the depth itself is steady (ground truth, calibrated stereo); a model's own frame-to-frame wobble becomes more visible, not less:

```python
depth_maps = [estimate_depth(frame) for frame in sv.get_video_frames_generator(source_path)]  # your depth model
clip_range = sv.DepthClipRange.from_depth_maps(depth_maps)
depth_annotator = sv.DepthAnnotator(display_range=clip_range)

with sv.VideoSink(target_path, video_info) as sink:
    for frame, depth_map in zip(sv.get_video_frames_generator(source_path), depth_maps):
        sink.write_frame(depth_annotator.annotate(frame, depth_map))
```

Part 2 of 4. Needs PR 1 (#2691).

## Motivation and Context

Follows #2691, which colours one frame at a time.

## Changes Made

- `sv.DepthClipRange(display_range)` and `DepthClipRange.from_depth_maps(depth_maps, low=2.0, high=98.0)`:
  - Reads the clip in one pass, so a generator never holds the clip in memory.
  - Memory stays bounded however long the clip is. Each frame adds about 65,536 samples drawn at random, and past about four million samples the clip is thinned at random by half.
  - The random draws are seeded, so the same clip always gives the same range.
- `sv.DepthAnnotator(display_range=...)` accepts a `DepthClipRange`. A metric clip colours as inverse depth, the same as a single map.
- Docs: the how-to's video section, the reference entry and a changelog entry.

## Testing

```
pytest tests/depth --doctest-modules src/supervision/depth   48 passed (9 new)
pytest                                                       4842 passed, 79 skipped
pre-commit run                                               all hooks pass
mkdocs build                                                 no new warnings
```

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`
- [x] A 70-frame clip of a striped frame keeps that frame's own range (catches thinning that lines up with the stripes)
- [x] Both videos above were written with `sv.VideoSink`, 192 frames

## Additional Notes

- Each frame's sample is capped, so a high-resolution frame weighs no more in the range than a low-resolution one.

title: feat(depth): add `DepthMap` and `DepthAnnotator`
body: *Top: one moment seen by two cameras 6.5 cm apart (Spring dataset). Bottom left: the depth a stereo matcher computes from the two views, coloured over the left view. Near things are warm, far things are cool, and pixels the matcher could not match stay uncoloured instead of being painted as far away. Bottom right: the dataset's true depth, for comparison.* *The same depth in each colour table. Turbo is the default. Viridis and Cividis stay readable in grayscale and for colour-blind readers.* ### ▶️📓 [Notebook Playground Demo (all 4 PRs together)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/roboflow/supervision/blob/playground/depth-maps/examples/depth_playground.ipynb) ## Description supervision cannot show a depth map. Depth models (Depth Anything, YOLO26 depth, stereo matchers) all return one, and the usual fix is a hand-written `cv2.applyColorMap` call: it needs OpenCV, which supervision no longer requires, takes only 8-bit input, and paints pixels the model could not measure as if they were far away. This PR adds a depth map type and an annotator that colours it. It does not require OpenCV: ```python import supervision as sv depth_map = sv.DepthMap(disparity, kind="disparity_px") # NaN, inf or <= 0 where there is no depth annotated = sv.DepthAnnotator(opacity=0.6).annotate(image.copy(), depth_map) ``` Near objects come out warm and far ones cool, and pixels without depth stay uncoloured so the image shows through. This is part 1 of 4. Later parts, each built only on this one: one colour range across a video, distance in metres per detection, and loaders for model outputs and dataset files. ## Motivation and Context Part of #1313: this covers depth maps. Normal and gradient maps from that issue are not included. Follows the note there to do it without cv2. ## Changes Made - `sv.DepthMap(values, kind)`: one frame of depth as float32. `sv.DepthKind` says what the values measure: `disparity_px`, `depth_m` or `relative_inverse` (a monocular model's normalised output). `valid_mask` marks the pixels that hold depth. - `sv.DepthAnnotator(colormap, display_range, opacity)`: - `colormap`: Turbo (default), Viridis, Cividis, Inferno, Magma or grayscale (`sv.DepthColormap`), with near always at the warm or bright end. - `display_range`: `"auto"` (the map's 2nd to 98th percentile) or a fixed `(low, high)`. - A metric map is coloured as inverse depth, which gives near detail most of the colours. - NumPy (BGR) and Pillow scenes, like every annotator. The map is stretched to the scene's size. - Colour tables are read from matplotlib's colormaps on first use, so no tables are copied into supervision. Colours are blended between entries so smooth surfaces show no bands. - Docs: reference pages under `docs/depth/`, a how-to (`docs/how_to/visualize_depth.md`) and a changelog entry. - Out of scope here: video colour range, metres and distance, model loaders (parts 2 to 4). ## Testing ``` pytest tests/depth --doctest-modules src/supervision/depth 39 passed pytest 4832 passed, 79 skipped pre-commit run all hooks pass, mypy included mkdocs build no new warnings ``` - [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally - [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API - [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` - [x] A map with depth only on odd rows and columns (sparse LiDAR-style) still gets its real colour range - [x] The images above are this annotator on frames of the Spring dataset (CC BY 4.0, credited in the how-to) ## Additional Notes - The docs example image is hosted on `media.roboflow.com` with the other annotator examples. - `opencv-python` is not needed. Stretching the map to the scene uses NumPy indexing.

title: fix(cv2): map resize pixels with fx and fy when `dsize` is not given
body:
## Description

When `dsize` is not given, OpenCV computes the output size from `fx`/`fy` and also maps destination pixels with `1 / fx` and `1 / fy`. The NumPy fallback for `cv2.resize` computed the same output size but mapped pixels with the ratio of the rounded sizes (`source_width / width`), so it samples different source pixels whenever that ratio isn't exactly `1 / fx`:

```python
import numpy as np, cv2
from supervision._cv2._image import _resize

src = np.random.default_rng(20260717).integers(0, 256, (13, 10, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
_resize(src, None, fx=1 / 7, fy=1 / 7).tolist()   # [[[195, 119, 86]], [[50, 115, 57]]]
cv2.resize(src, None, fx=1 / 7, fy=1 / 7).tolist()  # [[[221, 37, 117]], [[31, 74, 38]]]
```

`sv.PixelateAnnotator` resizes with `dsize=None, fx=1 / pixel_size`, so without OpenCV installed its output differs from the OpenCV backend.

## Motivation and Context

Keeps the fallback in line with OpenCV, like the other recent `_cv2` fixes. No issue.

## Changes Made

- `_resize` uses `1 / fx` and `1 / fy` as the sampling scale when the size comes from the factors, and the size ratio otherwise (unchanged).
- Nearest uses `floor(dst * scale)`, as OpenCV does; the existing exact integer formula is kept for the `dsize` case.
- Linear with factors goes through the existing NumPy path, which clamps at the border. The Pillow fast path is kept for `dsize` only, because Pillow's affine transform fills outside pixels with 0 when upscaling.

## Testing

- Added `test_fallback_resize_with_scale_factors_matches_opencv` in `tests/cv2/test_image.py` (nearest and linear, BGR and gray, several `fx`/`fy` including mixed and `1 / 7`). 18 of its 20 cases fail on `develop` and all pass with this change. A wider local comparison against OpenCV over more shapes, dtypes and factors gives the same 1-LSB linear budget as the `dsize` path.
- `uv run pytest tests/cv2 tests/utils/test_image.py tests/annotators`: 772 passed. The one failure is a collection check that needs `scikit-learn`, which isn't installed here.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files.

- [x] Added/updated tests (I ran the test files listed above, not the full suite)
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

`cv2.resize` with both `dsize` and `fx`/`fy` still uses `dsize`, as OpenCV does.

title: fix: normalize bounding boxes across dataset formats and fix cv2 fallback drawing
body:
## Summary

Fixes three related bugs in the supervision library:

### Fix #2682: Reversed bounding boxes in COCO/PascalVOC/CreateML loaders
- COCO loader now normalizes xyxy corners (x_min <= x_max, y_min <= y_max) after xywh→xyxy conversion to handle negative width/height annotations
- PascalVOC loader now sorts corners after the -1 1-indexed→0-indexed offset
- CreateML loader uses abs(width)/abs(height) for negative dimension annotations
- All corresponding exporters also normalize corners before writing

### Fix #2668: approxPolyDP uses distance to infinite line instead of segment
- Added `_point_to_segment_distance_squared` helper that measures perpendicular distance to line segment (clamping t to [0,1])
- Rewrote `_simplify_slices` to use segment distance, matching OpenCV 4.13+ behavior
- Verified: 0 mismatches across 10000 random contours vs cv2.approxPolyDP

### Fix #2674: NumPy fallback rectangle borders drawn inward only
- `_rectangle` fallback now extends borders outward by `t//2` pixels on all sides, centering the stroke on rectangle edges
- Matches OpenCV's stroke positioning (bounding box extent now identical to cv2.rectangle for all thickness values)

## Tests
- All 385 existing dataset format tests pass
- All 23 existing cv2 drawing/geometry tests pass
- Randomized differential testing for approxPolyDP: 0 mismatches over 10000 random contours

title: feat(metrics): add COCO keypoint mAP (OKS) for `sv.KeyPoints`
body:
## Description

Closes #2686.

Thank you for maintaining supervision! This follows up on the feature proposal in #2686.

Adds `sv.metrics.KeypointMeanAveragePrecision`, the COCO keypoint mAP. It reuses `COCOEvaluator` and replaces only the IoU step with Object Keypoint Similarity, ported from `pycocotools`' `computeOks` with the keypoint parameters (`maxDets=20`, medium/large areas, COCO sigmas). Ignore regions for targets without visible keypoints and crowd targets follow COCO.

```python
import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import KeypointMeanAveragePrecision

metric = KeypointMeanAveragePrecision()  # COCO sigmas for 17-point skeletons
for predictions, targets in zip(predictions_list, targets_list):
    metric.update(predictions, targets)  # one sv.KeyPoints per image

print(metric.compute())
```

The `fix(metrics)` commit is a small related fix: the shared precision guard used `np.finfo(np.float32).eps`, while `pycocotools` uses `np.spacing(1)`, so a perfect box prediction scored 0.99999988 instead of 1.0. It is its own commit so it can be split into a separate PR if you prefer.

## Motivation and Context

There is no pose metric in `sv.metrics` yet; evaluating `sv.KeyPoints` means converting to COCO JSON and running `pycocotools`. Details in #2686. I had no answers to the open questions there yet, so I went with the defaults proposed in the issue and am happy to change any of them:

- Only the metric and its result are public. The OKS helper, COCO sigmas and max detections stay private (`_keypoint_oks_batch`, `_COCO_KEYPOINT_SIGMAS`, `_KEYPOINT_MAX_DETECTIONS`).
- One PR, with the epsilon fix kept as its own commit.
- Targets read `data["area"]`, `data["xyxy"]` and `data["iscrowd"]`; predictions read `data["xyxy"]` for the size bucket.
- The `pycocotools` comparison is a script in this description, not a test dependency.

## Changes Made

- `metrics/keypoint_mean_average_precision.py`: `KeypointMeanAveragePrecision` and `KeypointMeanAveragePrecisionResult` (`plot()`, `to_pandas()`, printable COCO-style summary).
- `detection/utils/iou_and_nms.py`: private `_keypoint_oks_batch`, including the COCO expanded-box branch for targets without visible keypoints.
- `metrics/mean_average_precision.py`:
  - The accumulator reads the largest `max_dets` instead of the literal `100`. Box, mask and OBB results are unchanged with the default settings; a regression test covers it.
  - Plot, pandas and mean helpers are shared between the box and keypoint results instead of duplicated.
  - Separate commit: `EPS = np.spacing(1)`.
- Docs page, mkdocs entry, changelog entries.

- Review follow-up: keypoints given as `(N, K, 3)` use only the planar `xy[..., :2]`; `sigmas` must be positive and finite; docs describe NaN keypoints and zero target areas precisely; more tests for result helpers and edge cases.

## Testing

Compared with `pycocotools` 2.0.11 `COCOeval(..., "keypoints")`, all five summary values (AP, AP50, AP75, APm, APl):

| Data | Max abs difference |
|---|---|
| 200 COCO val2017 images, `yolo11n-pose` predictions, 853 targets incl. 19 crowd and 267 without visible keypoints | 2.8e-9 |
| Synthetic, 60 seeds: multiple classes, 10% crowd, targets without visible keypoints, more than 20 predictions per image | 1.4e-8 |
| Synthetic, 40 seeds incl. a 5-point skeleton with custom sigmas | 1.1e-8 |

Without target boxes, targets with no visible keypoints are skipped and the COCO subset differs by up to 8.6e-3; this is documented.

- `uv run pytest tests/metrics tests/detection`: 2673 passed, 1 skipped. Doctests of the changed modules pass. `pre-commit` on changed files passes (incl. mypy).
- The epsilon test fails on `develop` (`0.9999998807907104 == 1.0`) and passes with the fix. On random data, box, mask and OBB scores move up by at most 5e-8.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

- `keypoint visible` is boolean in `sv.KeyPoints`, so COCO `v=1` and `v=2` are both treated as labelled, as in `pycocotools`.
- Out of scope for now: AR metrics and per-keypoint breakdowns.
- I can add the comparison script to this description or the test suite, whichever you prefer.

Thank you for taking the time to review this. Any feedback is very welcome, and I'm glad to adjust the API, naming or structure to whatever fits supervision best.

title: fix: Probe empty batches before OBB thread dispatch
body:
## Description

`InferenceSlicer(batch_size>1, thread_workers>1)` inspects only the first batch when selecting callback scheduling. If that batch is empty and later batches contain oriented boxes, it dispatches those callbacks to worker threads and omits the existing OBB warning.

Probe leading empty batches on the caller thread until a result identifies geometry. Then apply the existing threaded or sequential branch to the remaining batches. This matches the single-slice path and preserves source ordering.

Minimal reproduction: split eight 16x16 tiles with `batch_size=2` and `thread_workers=4`. Return `Detections.empty()` for the first two tiles and oriented-box detections for the others. Record `threading.get_ident()` inside the callback. On develop, only the first of four callback invocations runs on the caller thread and no OBB warning appears. With this patch, all four run on the caller thread and the OBB warning appears. The added parametrized test provides a runnable reproduction:

```bash
pytest tests/detection/tools/test_inference_slicer.py -k probes_empty_batches_before_serializing_obb -q
```

## Motivation and Context

#2256 established sequential OBB callbacks because some inference backends are not thread-safe, following #1632. #1239 carried that behavior into batching. Empty initial batches currently bypass it. The reproduction verifies callback scheduling; it does not reproduce a native crash.

## Changes Made

- Consume batches synchronously until OBB data or a nonempty result identifies geometry.
- Keep the existing OBB fallback, warning-once behavior and ordered dispatch for the remainder.
- Add four regression cases covering one/two empty batches, batch sizes two/three and a partial final batch.
- Include four maintainer-added real-thread cases covering resumed threaded scheduling, exactly-once callbacks, source order, and partial batches.
- Update the call docstring and Unreleased changelog.

## Testing

Earlier local validation, before the maintainer-added tests:

- New regressions: four failures on pristine develop, four passes with the fix.
- `pytest src/ tests/ -q --tb=short`: 4,936 tests/doctests passed on develop; all 4,940 passed with the patch.
- Focused slicer, GeoTIFF and compact-mask modules: 67 passed on develop, 71 passed with the patch.
- 90 compatibility configurations across two calls each produce matching outputs on develop and the patch, covering OBBs, axis boxes, dense/compact masks, empty results and worker/batch settings.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: every hook passes, including mypy, Ruff, documentation formatting and codespell.

Windows, Python 3.13.3, NumPy 2.2.6. Tests used checkout-first `PYTHONPATH` and `PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1` to avoid an unrelated global Hydra/ANTLR incompatibility. Repository configuration and package doctests remained active. Linux/macOS were not run locally. The initial run did not measure coverage; the later synced-branch run below did.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (the local results above predate the maintainer-added tests)
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

Leading empty batches, including an all-empty run, execute serially until geometry can be identified. A first nonempty non-OBB result retains threaded execution. Existing masks, metadata, output order, public arguments and stored formats remain unchanged.

AI assistance disclosure: AI-assisted development tools were used during investigation and implementation. The local results cover the original implementation and my develop sync. The linked current-head CI covers the maintainer-added tests.

CI follow-up: I merged current develop and retained both this PR's changelog entry and the new upstream entries. This includes develop's removal of the old broken #1625 changelog link. On the synced branch, the focused slicer modules report 71 passes; the full suite and doctests with coverage report 4,988 passes, six skips and 93% coverage. All applicable pre-commit checks pass on the three PR files. Those local runs preceded Borda's four additional real-thread tests.

At head `cd3179c835a5f169557119c5c9f8bf893837f2a2`, all 36 check/status contexts pass. [Pytest/Test Workflow](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/actions/runs/37696188239) passes all 26 jobs, including the platform/Python/OpenCV matrix, clean-wheel checks, package build, and testing guardian. Documentation, link, configuration, coverage, CLA, and pre-commit checks also pass. The maintainer merged develop and added the four real-thread cases; the production fix remains unchanged. title: fix(dataset): reject or order a reversed box in the remaining loaders
body:
Closes #2682. Follow-up to #2663, which covered `yolo` only.

### What changed

The format decides the remedy, following what #2663 established:

- **`coco` and `createml` name an extent**, so a negative width or height is not representable. Both now reject it, with the same message shape the YOLO loader uses:
  `Invalid box extent (-40, 40) in COCO annotation 7; expected a non-negative width and height.`
- **`pascal_voc` names two corners explicitly**, so a reversed pair describes the same rectangle rather than being malformed input. It now orders them, as `labelme._rectangle_to_xyxy` already does.

All three **exporters** measured the extent from raw corner values, so a reversed `Detections` exported as a file the loader refuses to read — the asymmetry that review caught on #2663. Each now orders the corners first, and the COCO exporter writes the ordered origin rather than the raw `xyxy[0], xyxy[1]`.

### Verification

Import side:

| loader | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `coco` `bbox: [50,50,-40,40]` | `area = -1600` | rejected |
| `createml` `width: -40` | `area = -1600` | rejected |
| `pascal_voc` `xmin 70, xmax 30` | `area = -1600` | `xyxy = [29, 29, 69, 69]`, `area = 1600` |

Export side, from `Detections(xyxy=[[70, 70, 30, 30]])`:

| exporter | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `coco` | `bbox: [70, 70, -40, -40]` | `bbox: [30, 30, 40, 40]` |
| `createml` | `width: -40, height: -40` | `width: 40, height: 40`, centre unchanged at `(50, 50)` |
| `pascal_voc` | `xmin 71 > xmax 31` | `xmin 31 < xmax 71` |

The exported box describes the same rectangle in each case, and normal boxes are unchanged.

10 new tests across the three format test files, mirroring `TestYoloAnnotationsToDetectionsBoxExtent`. All 10 fail without the `src/` change and pass with it. The full `tests/dataset/` suite is 554 passing; `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

### Note

`labelme` needed no change — it already normalises on load, and I left its export alone since it writes a rectangle's corner list rather than an extent.

Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

title: releasing `0.30.8` [rebase & merge]
body:
# v0.30.8 — Sharper video, cleaner labels

## 📋 Summary

Video, YOLO labels, masks, VLM parsing and mAP all get more accurate.

- **`VideoSink`** keeps OpenCV's video quality when OpenCV isn't installed.
- **`from_yolo`** reads pose labels as boxes instead of polygons.
- **`MeanAveragePrecision`** scores class-agnostic runs right when only one side has class IDs.
- **`from_vlm`** returns one Florence-2 detection per object, not one per polygon.
- **`from_inference`** masks no longer drift up to a pixel up and left.

Drop-in upgrade. Without OpenCV, videos get larger; YOLO labels with a negative width or height now raise `ValueError`.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### `sv.VideoSink` and `sv.process_video` keep quality without OpenCV

The PyAV fallback left the encoder bit rate unset, so `mp4v` and `MJPG` files came out at under half of what `cv2.VideoWriter` writes. It now uses OpenCV's rate settings for every codec except H.264. Files get larger and `vp09` may encode more slowly; `codec="avc1"` keeps files small where an H.264 encoder is available. ([#2661](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2661))

```python
import supervision as sv

video_info = sv.VideoInfo.from_video_path("in.mp4")
with sv.VideoSink("out.mp4", video_info) as sink:  # OpenCV not installed
    for frame in sv.get_video_frames_generator("in.mp4"):
        sink.write_frame(frame)
# before: mp4v written at under half OpenCV's bit rate, visibly softer
# now:    same bit rate OpenCV's writer uses
```

### YOLO pose labels load as boxes

A pose row is a box followed by keypoints. `from_yolo` used to parse the whole row as a polygon, giving wrong boxes and masks nobody asked for. It now reads the box and skips the keypoints that `kpt_shape` declares. ([#2655](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2655))

```python
ds = sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo(
    images_directory_path="pose/images",
    annotations_directory_path="pose/labels",
    data_yaml_path="pose/data.yaml",  # kpt_shape: [17, 3]
)
# before: polygon-parsed boxes and masks
# now:    one box per row
```

### Class-agnostic mAP with one-sided class IDs

A perfect match scored zero when only one side carried class IDs, such as SAM proposals checked against labeled ground truth. With `class_agnostic=True`, both sides now count as one class.

### One Florence-2 detection per object (#2648)

Florence-2 returns a segmented object as a list of polygons, one per connected region. An object split in two used to come back as two detections; the polygons now merge into one mask with one box around all of them.

### Roboflow masks sit on the right pixels (#2649)

`from_inference` truncated sub-pixel polygon vertices, shifting each mask up and left by up to a pixel. Vertices are now rounded, the way the COCO, YOLO, LabelMe and Pascal VOC loaders already do.

## 🔄 Migration guide

No migration required for this release.

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🌱 Changed

- `sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo` raises `ValueError` naming the annotation file when a label has a negative width or height; it used to load a box with `x_min` past `x_max`, which made `Detections.area` negative and skewed IoU and NMS. `as_yolo` now orders the corners of a reversed box before measuring, so it no longer writes a file the loader refuses. (#2663)

### 🔧 Fixed

- `sv.VideoSink` and `sv.process_video` write `mp4v`, `MJPG` and other non-H.264 video at OpenCV's bit rate when OpenCV isn't installed. A frame rate of zero or less now raises `RuntimeError` in `sv.VideoSink`, as it does with OpenCV. (#2661)
- `sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo` reads the box of Ultralytics pose labels and skips their keypoints; a `kpt_shape` other than `[K, 2]` or `[K, 3]` raises `ValueError`. (#2655)
- `sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo` names a malformed annotation line, one with too few values or, for OBB, not nine, in a `ValueError` instead of failing on an array shape. (#2665)
- `sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision(class_agnostic=True)` treats detections without class IDs as the same class as labeled ones, and unsigned class ID arrays no longer raise `OverflowError` on NumPy 2. (#2650)
- `sv.Detections.from_vlm` with `sv.VLM.FLORENCE_2` merges the polygons of one instance into one detection for `<REFERRING_EXPRESSION_SEGMENTATION>` and `<REGION_TO_SEGMENTATION>`, and skips instances with no usable polygon. (#2648)
- `sv.Detections.from_vlm` with `sv.VLM.QWEN_2_5_VL` or `sv.VLM.QWEN_3_VL` recovers complete detections from a response cut off inside a `bbox_2d` array or right after a complete object. (#2666)
- `sv.Detections.from_inference` rounds polygon vertices to the nearest pixel before rasterising masks, and raises `ValueError` for NaN or infinite vertices. (#2649)
- `sv.xyxy_to_mask` returns an empty mask for a box entirely left of or above the image when its maximum coordinate is a negative fraction. (#2646)
- `sv.Detections.get_anchors_coordinates` computes axis-aligned midpoint anchors without integer overflow. (#2660)
- `sv.LineZone.trigger` ages crossing history on frames whose detections lack `tracker_id`, so a reused track ID no longer creates a false crossing after the track expired. (#2644)
- `sv.LineZoneAnnotator(text_orient_to_line=True)` no longer raises `TypeError` without OpenCV for lines drawn right to left. (#2659)
- The Ultralytics, Inference and YOLO-NAS speed estimation examples measure elapsed time from frame indices; a vehicle missed in one frame of three was reported about 44% too fast. (#2654)
- `examples/speed_estimation/rfdetr_example.py` no longer raises `AttributeError`: `supervision._cv2` now provides `getPerspectiveTransform` and `perspectiveTransform`. (#2652)

## 🏆 Contributors

- **Mohammad Hijjawi** (@MohammadHijjawi97, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mohammadhijjawi)) — fixed video quality without OpenCV, Florence-2 instance merging and Roboflow mask rounding.
- **Kari Pikkarainen** (@kari-pikkarainen, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/karipikkarainen/recent-activity/all/)) — fixed speed estimation timing, the NumPy `flip` fallback and the perspective-transform fallbacks.
- **Miral Amin** (@aminmiral) — made YOLO loading reject negative extents and name malformed lines.
- **NIKHIL** (@Nikhi00718) — fixed `LineZone` history expiry and anchor overflow.
- **kevin** (@kevin9327) — made Qwen parsing recover from cut-off responses.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-aswanth-raj/)) — fixed class-agnostic mAP.
- **Devulapalli Naga Sri Vaishnavi** (@Vaishnavi220506) — fixed masks for off-frame fractional boxes.
- **JANG BYUNGKUN** (@8rulerstar) — fixed YOLO pose label loading.

*Automated contributions: @dependabot*

______________________________________________________________________

**Full changelog**: <https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/compare/0.30.7...0.30.8>

Updates `urllib3` from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

title: perf(detection): crop compact polygon masks to the polygon in `from_inference`
body:
## Description

`Detections.from_inference(result, compact_masks=True)` stores every polygon mask as a `CompactMask` whose crop is the whole image (`_full_image_xyxy`). Two costs follow:

- Building the detections run-length encodes the full frame once per prediction.
- Anything that later works on the masks decodes full frames, notably `with_nms`, where the compact IoU path compares crops.

This PR crops each polygon mask to the polygon's own vertex extent. `cv2.fillPoly` never fills a pixel outside the integer vertices' min/max, so the crop is lossless, and `from_dense` clips it to the image.

Repro: 110 polygons (60 vertices each) on a 4096×3068 image.

```python
import time, numpy as np, supervision as sv

W, H = 4096, 3068
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
preds = []
for _ in range(110):
    cx, cy, r = rng.integers(200, W - 200), rng.integers(200, H - 200), rng.integers(30, 150)
    angles = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 60, endpoint=False)
    points = [{"x": float(cx + r * np.cos(a)), "y": float(cy + r * np.sin(a))} for a in angles]
    preds.append({"x": float(cx), "y": float(cy), "width": 2.0 * r, "height": 2.0 * r,
                  "confidence": 0.9, "class": "a", "class_id": 0, "points": points})
result = {"image": {"width": W, "height": H}, "predictions": preds}

t = time.time(); detections = sv.Detections.from_inference(result, compact_masks=True); print(time.time() - t)
t = time.time(); detections.with_nms(class_agnostic=True); print(time.time() - t)
print(detections.mask.crop(0).shape)
```

| | `develop` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `from_inference(compact_masks=True)` | 5.44 s | 0.58 s |
| `with_nms(class_agnostic=True)` afterwards | 31.1 s | 0.01 s |
| first crop shape | (3068, 4096) | (183, 183) |

## Motivation and Context

Roboflow's Auto Label worker uses `compact_masks=True` to stop dense instance-segmentation jobs from holding full-frame boolean masks: ~2.3 GB per 5280×3956 image with 110 objects. With full-frame crops, it had to call `CompactMask.repack()` after every `from_inference` to get usable NMS times, and it still paid ~5 s per image to build the masks.

## Changes Made

- `process_roboflow_result`: the polygon branch passes the polygon's vertex box, instead of the full image, to `CompactMask.from_dense` when `compact_masks=True`.
- Tests:
  - the compact mask's offset and crop shape follow the polygon, inside the image and across both corners;
  - compact and dense masks are pixel-identical for random polygons, including ones that cross the border.

RLE predictions (already cropped to the detector box), the size-mismatch RLE fallback and `compact_masks=False` are unchanged.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: `test_polygon_prediction_compact_mask_is_cropped_to_polygon` fails in all 3 cases (`assert [0, 0] == [10, 20]`, `assert (60, 64) == (7, 9)`, …). `test_polygon_prediction_compact_masks_match_dense_masks` passes, because pixels were already correct.
- With this change: `uv run pytest tests/detection/utils/test_internal.py` → 134 passed.
- `uv run pytest` → all pass with `--extra metrics` installed. Without the extra, the 7 `tests/metrics/utils/test_aggregate.py` tests and `tests/cv2/test_integration.py::test_ordinary_suite_passes_when_cv2_is_blocked` fail with the missing-extra `ImportError`, as on `develop`.
- `uv run pre-commit run --files <changed files>` → all hooks pass (ruff, ruff format, docformatter, mypy, codespell, doctest fences).

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API — no public API change
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

`polygon_to_mask` still allocates one full-frame `uint8` canvas per polygon before cropping. That is a memset per prediction and no longer dominates (0.58 s above). Filling directly into a crop-sized canvas would remove it, but it means reimplementing `polygon_to_mask`'s clipping, so it is left out.

title: fix(smoother): Age history on frames without tracker IDs
body:
## Description

I found that `DetectionsSmoother.update_with_detections()` freezes cached history when `tracker_id` is `None`. A returning track then averages its new box and confidence with samples outside the configured frame window. Dead tracks also remain cached through any number of missing-ID frames.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

smoother = sv.DetectionsSmoother(length=3)
smoother.update_with_detections(sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10]], dtype=float),
    tracker_id=np.array([7]),
))
for _ in range(3):
    smoother.update_with_detections(sv.Detections.empty())
result = smoother.update_with_detections(sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[100, 0, 110, 10]], dtype=float),
    tracker_id=np.array([7]),
))
print(result.xyxy)
# develop: [[50., 0., 60., 10.]]
# this change: [[100., 0., 110., 10.]]
```

## Motivation and Context

`length` documents a maximum number of frames. Empty frames with an empty tracker-ID array already advance that window, while the missing-ID branch returns before inserting an absent sample and expiring tracks. I found no existing issue for this smoother behavior. The related `LineZone` correction in #2644 applies the same frame-aging principle to crossing history.

## Changes Made

- Reuse the existing absent-frame insertion and track cleanup when IDs are missing.
- Keep the warning, its order before state mutation, and the original unsmoothed return value.
- Add 24 cases covering empty and nonempty missing-ID frames, tracked empty frames, zero through three intervening frames, and axis-aligned and oriented boxes.
- Document the frame-window behavior and add an Unreleased changelog entry.

Existing users keep tracked-frame averaging, short-gap history, current-frame metadata, oriented-corner alignment, and reset behavior. This changes only history aging on missing-ID frames. No stored files, defaults, or new public API are involved.

## Testing

I ran focused CPU checks with native threads capped at one. I disabled unrelated installed pytest plugin autoload because the global Hydra/ANTLR plugin fails during collection; these tests use no repository-specific pytest plugin.

- New matrix on pristine `develop`: **8 failed, 16 passed**. The failures show expired history or a box at x=50 instead of x=100. The 16 compatibility cases pass on both versions.
- Original smoother tests, geometry-contract tests and smoother doctests on pristine `develop`: **24 passed**.
- Final patch: `py -3.13 -m pytest tests/detection/tools/test_smoother.py tests/detection/test_geometry_contract.py src/supervision/detection/tools/smoother.py -q`: **48 passed**.
- `py -3.13 -m pre_commit run --files src/supervision/detection/tools/smoother.py tests/detection/tools/test_smoother.py docs/changelog.md`: all applicable hooks passed, including mypy.
- Warning-as-error compatibility checked on both versions: history stays unchanged when the warning raises.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (tests added; focused checks above passed; I did not run the full suite locally).
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API.
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`.

## Additional Notes

Short gaps still contribute to the average. Clearing all history on the first missing-ID frame would lose that behavior, so this uses the existing window policy instead.

AI assistance disclosure: AI-assisted development tools were used during investigation and implementation. The reported tests were run against the final diff.

title: fix(cv2): center thick rectangle borders on the edge
body:
## Description

The NumPy fallback drew a stroked rectangle entirely inside the rectangle, while OpenCV centers the stroke on the edges. Any box with `thickness >= 2` came out thinner and 1 pixel smaller per side without `opencv-python` installed.

`BoxAnnotator`'s default `thickness` is `2` and OpenCV is no longer a dependency, so this was the default path for a plain `pip install supervision`:

| backend | painted px | painted bbox |
|---|---:|---|
| `opencv` | 596 | x 19-81, y 19-61 |
| `fallback` | 392 | x 20-80, y 20-60 |

Repro, run once with `opencv-python` and once without:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision._cv2 import BACKEND_NAME

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[20.0, 20.0, 80.0, 60.0]]),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
    confidence=np.array([0.9]),
)
scene = np.zeros((80, 100, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
painted = sv.BoxAnnotator().annotate(scene, detections).any(axis=2)
ys, xs = np.where(painted)

print(f"backend        : {BACKEND_NAME}")
print(f"painted pixels : {int(painted.sum())}")
print(f"painted bbox   : x {xs.min()}-{xs.max()}, y {ys.min()}-{ys.max()}")
```

## Motivation and Context

Pillow's `ImageDraw.rectangle(outline=1, width=...)` only grows inward. OpenCV strokes each edge as a band centered on it and rounds the four joints with a filled disc, so the border spreads outside the rectangle as well as inside.

The existing `test_fallback_line_draws_and_matches_opencv_extent` compares only the raster bounding box with `atol=1`, and the error at `thickness=2` is exactly 1 pixel per side, so it passed.

Part of #2674

## Changes Made

- `_rectangle` now rasterizes the stroke directly as four edge bands plus a corner disc, clipped to the canvas, instead of delegating to Pillow's `outline=`/`width=`.
- Added `_rectangle_mask` and `_disc` helpers in `src/supervision/_cv2/_drawing.py`. The disc is built once at its own size and OR-ed into each corner window, so cost scales with the stroke, not the canvas.
- `thickness=1` and filled (`thickness=-1`) rectangles are unchanged, as is the public API.
- Deliberately out of scope: `_line`, `_circle`, `_polylines` and `_ellipse` share the inward-stroke cause and are untouched here. See the two scoping questions in #2674.

## Testing

Band radius is `0` at `thickness=1`, else `(thickness + 1) // 2`, derived from OpenCV and checked against it. The patched `_rectangle` matches `cv2.rectangle` byte for byte on 1310 randomized and hand-picked cases (degenerate, reversed, negative and out-of-bounds corners, float corners, thickness 1 to 25), on both `opencv-python` 4.10.0 and 5.0.0.

New tests fail on `develop` and pass with this change. `thickness=1` passes either way:

```
$ uv run pytest tests/cv2/test_drawing.py -k rectangle_stroke   # fix stashed
```

title: fix(cv2): measure `approxPolyDP` distance to the segment
body:
## Description

Without OpenCV, `_approx_poly_dp` measured perpendicular distance to the *infinite line* through each Douglas-Peucker segment. OpenCV (since 4.13) measures distance to the *finite segment*, so a vertex past an endpoint but near the line's extension was dropped even when it was farther than `epsilon` from the simplified polygon.

## Motivation and Context

Closes #2668

## Changes Made

- `_simplify_slices` now uses squared distance to the finite segment (OpenCV's contract)
- Regression tests for the closed and open cases from the issue
- Changelog entry under Unreleased

## Testing

```text
pytest tests/cv2/test_geometry.py -q
# 14 passed
```

Failing-then-passing: on `develop`, `test_approx_poly_dp_keeps_vertex_beyond_segment_endpoint_closed` expects 5 vertices and gets 4; with this change both new tests pass and the existing suite still does.

title: fix(video): read frames past an unreliable frame count
body:
## Description

`sv.get_video_frames_generator` stopped at OpenCV's `CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT` even when no `end` was given. OpenCV estimates that count from container metadata, and it can be wrong:

- A WebM without a duration in its header (what a browser's `MediaRecorder` writes) reports a huge negative count. The generator yields no frames, `end=10` raises `Requested frames are outbound`, and `sv.process_video` writes an empty video.
- A variable frame rate MKV or WebM can report fewer frames than it holds. A 60-frame MKV reported 23, so the generator dropped the last 37 frames without any warning.

The PyAV fallback used without OpenCV already counts frames by decoding them, so only the OpenCV backend is affected.

Minimal repro (opencv-python 4.14.0):

```python
import av, numpy as np
import supervision as sv

with av.open("recording.webm", "w", options={"live": "1"}) as container:  # no duration, like MediaRecorder
    stream = container.add_stream("libvpx", rate=30)
    stream.width, stream.height, stream.pix_fmt = 64, 48, "yuv420p"
    for index in range(45):
        frame = av.VideoFrame.from_ndarray(np.full((48, 64, 3), index, np.uint8), format="rgb24")
        container.mux(stream.encode(frame))
    container.mux(stream.encode())

print(sv.VideoInfo.from_video_path("recording.webm"))
print("frames:", sum(1 for _ in sv.get_video_frames_generator("recording.webm")))
print("end=10:", sum(1 for _ in sv.get_video_frames_generator("recording.webm", end=10)))
```

On `develop`:

```
VideoInfo(width=64, height=48, fps=30.0, total_frames=-276701161105643264)
frames: 0
end=10: Exception('Requested frames are outbound')
```

With this change:

```
VideoInfo(width=64, height=48, fps=30.0, total_frames=-276701161105643264)
frames: 45
end=10: 10
```

## Motivation and Context

Without `end`, the generator is documented to read the video to the end. The frame count is only metadata, so the end of the stream should decide when reading stops. `process_video` already treats a non-positive count as unknown when it clamps `max_frames`; the generator did not.

## Changes Made

- `_validate_and_setup_video` keeps `end=None` instead of replacing it with the frame count, so `get_video_frames_generator` reads until `read()` fails. `prefetch` and `process_video` go through the same path.
- A positive frame count still rejects an `end` past it, as before. A non-positive (unknown) count no longer rejects every `end`.
- Left out of scope: `VideoInfo.total_frames` still reports OpenCV's raw count, which is negative for such files. Mapping it to `None` would change a public value, so I kept this fix to frame reading.

## Testing

- `tests/utils/test_video.py::test_get_video_frames_generator_reads_past_unreliable_frame_count` uses a fake capture that decodes 5 frames while reporting a negative, zero or too small count, plus a negative count with `end=2`. All 4 cases fail on `develop` (`[] == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`, `[0, 1, 2] == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`, `Requested frames are outbound`) and pass with this change.
- `pytest tests/utils/test_video.py`: 46 passed, with OpenCV 4.14.0 and with the NumPy fallback.
- `pytest` (full suite, doctests included): 4409 passed, 24 skipped.
- Checked against real files with OpenCV: the live WebM gives 45 of 45 frames (also with `prefetch=4`, `stride=2` and `start`/`end`), the VFR MKV/WebM give 60 of 60, and `process_video` processes all 45 frames, or 10 with `max_frames=10`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files: ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, codespell and the other hooks pass. I ran mypy 2.3.1 separately: no issues.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

An explicit `end` above a positive but underestimated count (the VFR case) still raises `Requested frames are outbound`, as before. I kept that check for known counts to keep this change small.

title: fix(key_points): handle empty Transformers pose results
body:
## Description

`KeyPoints.from_transformers([])` raises `IndexError` on an image with no pose instances. The Transformers pose post-processor returns a per-image list, which can be empty when there are no boxes. This change returns `KeyPoints.empty()` for that case.

## Motivation and Context

The converter indexes the first pose before checking whether the per-image result contains any poses. A frame without detected people therefore stops a pose-processing loop instead of producing an empty result.

## Changes Made

- Handle an empty per-image Transformers pose result before accessing the first element.
- Cover both empty and nonempty results, document the empty case, and add a changelog entry.

## Testing

- On `develop` (`09e0b53`), `tests/key_points/test_core.py::TestFromTransformers::test_no_poses_returns_empty_key_points` fails with `IndexError: list index out of range`.
- `python -m pytest tests/key_points/test_core.py -q --disable-warnings`: 168 passed.
- `python -m pytest --cov=supervision -q --disable-warnings`: 4,407 passed, 24 skipped.

The regression uses the per-image result shape without downloading a Transformers model.
