title: ⬆️ update pydeprecate requirement from <0.13,>=0.9 to >=0.9,<0.14
body:
Updates the requirements on [pydeprecate](https://github.com/Borda/pyDeprecate) to permit the latest version.
Release notes

Sourced from pydeprecate's releases.

v0.13.0: PEP 702 metadata and deprecation policy lint

pyDeprecate v0.13.0 aligns __deprecated__ with PEP 702: it's now the plain conformant message string every PEP-702-aware tool expects, with pyDeprecate's own config moved to the new __deprecation_config__ attribute and read through the public get_deprecation_config(). Alongside the metadata split, a deprecation-governance lint (validate_deprecation_policy() / pydeprecate policy) checks that each deprecation gives callers a fair grace window before the removal PR lands, and every audit-scanning function gained an exclude= filter to keep frozen legacy trees out of package-wide scans.

✨ Spotlights

__deprecated__ now follows PEP 702

from deprecate import deprecated, get_deprecation_config

def new_func():
return "new behavior"


@​deprecated(target=new_func, deprecated_in="1.0", remove_in="2.0")
def old_func():
return new_func()


get_deprecation_config(old_func).target is new_func  # True — replaces old_func.deprecated.target

Deprecation policy lint

pydeprecate policy path/to/your/package
# exit 1 on a violation, e.g. too-short grace window or a message naming no replacement

exclude= on every audit scan

from deprecate import find_deprecation_wrappers

find_deprecation_wrappers("my_package", recursive=True, exclude=["my_package.tests", "._legacy"])

🔄 Migration guide

__deprecated__ is now a plain PEP 702-conformant message string, not the DeprecationConfig object. The config object moved to __deprecation_config__. Code reading func.__deprecated__.target, .deprecated_in, .args_mapping, or any other config field, or checking isinstance(func.__deprecated__, DeprecationConfig), now gets a plain str and either raises AttributeError or evaluates False. Affects every wrapper kind — functions, methods, class proxies, instance proxies, and modules.

# BEFORE (v0.12 and earlier)
config = old_func.__deprecated__
target = config.target

AFTER (v0.13+)


from deprecate import get_deprecation_config


</tr></table>

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from pydeprecate's changelog.

[0.13.0] — 2026-09-18 — PEP 702 metadata, deprecation policy lint, & the coding-agent plugin

Added

  • Deprecation policy governance lint — validate_deprecation_policy() and pydeprecate policy. Checks whether each deprecation was scheduled responsibly against two independently disable-able rules: min_grace (remove_in must be one clean single-component bump beyond deprecated_in, at least a version-shaped delta away — "0.3" three minors by default, "1.0" one major, "0.0.2" two patches, or a one-key unit table {"major": 1}; a bare "1" is rejected as ambiguous; every spelling is converted up front into the strict deprecate.audit.GraceWindow(count, unit), which may also be passed directly; a mixed bump such as 1.2 → 2.3 never passes) and message_required (warning must name a replacement). Exports validate_deprecation_policy, PolicyRule, GraceWindow, and VersionBump. The pydeprecate policy CLI subcommand takes no --version, exits 1 on violations, 2 on a malformed --min-grace, and 0 with an install hint when the [audit] extra (packaging) is absent and message_required finds nothing to flag — message_required runs without packaging and can still exit 1 on its own. pydeprecate all runs the check in advisory-only mode — violations are printed as a [WARNING] but never change all's exit status. The CLI resolves each rule as flag → [tool.pydeprecate.policy] table in the nearest pyproject.toml (keys are the rule slugs; min-grace = { minor = 3 } or a quoted dotted delta; min-grace = false disables the window) → built-in default, prints a Policy: header naming each value's source, exits 2 on a malformed file value or an unreadable pyproject.toml (in policy and all alike), and warns on unknown keys. (#231)
  • exclude for every audit scan. find_deprecation_wrappers(), validate_deprecation_expiry(), validate_deprecation_policy(), validate_deprecation_chains(), validate_mapping_compatibility() and generate_deprecation_table() take a keyword-only exclude list of fnmatch globs over full dotted module names; the scan itself never imports a matching package nor descends into it, and no wrapper reported under a matching module is returned. Every CLI subcommand takes --exclude (one pattern, comma-separated, or a list), defaulting to the exclude list of [tool.pydeprecate] in the nearest pyproject.toml, prints an Exclude: header naming the source, and exits 2 on a non-string value. The recursive walk replaces pkgutil.walk_packages (which imports a package before it can be skipped) with an iter_modules walk that checks exclusion first. (#231)
  • Public get_deprecation_config(obj) metadata accessor. Reads the v0.13 __deprecation_config__ object and falls back to the pre-v0.13 __deprecated__ configuration layout for mixed-version applications. (#230)
  • pydeprecate coding-agent plugin for Codex and Claude Code. Ships shared sunset and prune skills under plugins/pydeprecate/, with dual-host manifests and marketplace catalogs (.claude-plugin/, .codex-plugin/), separate from the pyDeprecate pip package. (#232)

Changed

  • __deprecated__ now follows PEP 702 and stores a rendered message string. pyDeprecate's configuration moved to __deprecation_config__; audit and documentation integrations use get_deprecation_config() so legacy wrappers remain discoverable during migration. Griffe's RuntimeDocstrings extension now scopes its docstring-replacement guard to get_deprecation_config(obj) is not None instead of a bare __deprecated__ truthiness check, so a foreign object decorated only with warnings.deprecated/typing_extensions.deprecated is no longer mistaken for a pyDeprecate wrapper. (#230)

Fixed

  • Custom message_template placeholders that don't apply to the current target mode no longer raise KeyError. Message rendering now probes the full public placeholder vocabulary up front and substitutes an empty string for any placeholder the target mode doesn't populate, instead of failing when a template references one. (#230)

[0.12.0] — 2026-08-25 — Module deprecation, a strict callable form, & the AUTO front door

Added

  • deprecated_module() — PEP-562-inspired module-level deprecation. Call deprecated_module(__name__, deprecated_in=..., remove_in=...) once at the bottom of a module to install a __class__ reassignment to a wrapper type that emits FutureWarning on every public attribute access (including real attributes already in __dict__). Three modes: in-place warn (Mode 1), redirect to replacement module with optional attrs_mapping (Mode 2), and parent alias via deprecated_instance() (Mode 3). find_deprecation_wrappers() discovers deprecated modules via the __deprecated__ attribute; validate_deprecation_wrapper() accepts module objects directly. Double-call is idempotent (returns early); pre-existing __getattr__ is chained with a UserWarning. (#203)
  • deprecated_callable() — strict callable-only form of @deprecated. Shares every @deprecated parameter and raises TypeError at decoration time when applied to a class. Accepts functions, methods, lambdas, and descriptors (classmethod / staticmethod / property); parallels the deprecated_class / deprecated_instance / deprecated_module family and is exported from the package. (#221)
  • TargetMode.AUTO — decoration-time inference default for the @deprecated front door. @deprecated now defaults target=TargetMode.AUTO (was TargetMode.NOTIFY): an omitted target resolves from the rest of the configuration — a non-empty args_mapping resolves to TargetMode.ARGS_REMAP on functions and methods (an empty {} counts as no mapping) (previously this fell into the NOTIFY default and was flagged as a misconfiguration); a class source forwards the unset target so the proxy auto-resolve applies (args_mapping → ARGS_REMAP); no mapping resolves to warn-only (TargetMode.NOTIFY on callables, target=None recorded on class proxies). AUTO is never stored in DeprecationConfig; the strict forms deprecated_callable() and deprecated_class() reject target=TargetMode.AUTO with TypeError. (#222)
  • skip_if on deprecated_class() and deprecated_instance(). The proxies gained the conditional-skip option previously available only on the callable decorators: while the bool (or zero-argument callable returning strict bool) evaluates True at access time, the proxy transparently serves the wrapped source — no warning, no attrs_mapping redirect, no args_mapping/args_extra handling, no target forwarding, and no read_only enforcement. A non-bool return raises the same TypeError as the callable form. (#222)
  • Public DeprecationProxy protocol for annotating proxies. from deprecate import DeprecationProxy replaces annotating against the private _DeprecatedProxy. It is @runtime_checkable, so isinstance(obj, DeprecationProxy) works; being a data protocol, issubclass() raises TypeError. DeprecationProxy[T] is generic in the type produced by calling the proxy — deprecated_class and deprecated_instance return the concrete _DeprecatedProxy type in every call shape, which is what keeps the proxy's forwarded dunders (int(), with, await) visible to type checkers; annotate the assignment explicitly where the target type should flow into call sites. (#226, #228)
  • AST breadcrumbs on every proxy. deprecated_class and deprecated_instance proxies now carry __wrapped__ (the source object) and __signature__ (the source's signature), so inspect.unwrap, inspect.signature, Sphinx autodoc, griffe/mkdocstrings, and IDEs resolve through the proxy to the original. Reading either attribute emits no deprecation warning. Sources with no introspectable signature (a plain dict, C-level types) get __signature__ = None rather than an error — wrapping stays infallible. (#226)

Changed

  • @deprecated on a class is now first-class and permanent. Applying @deprecated directly to a class dispatches to deprecated_class (full _DeprecatedProxy — isinstance/__class__ transparency, forwarding, budget semantics) and emits a one-time (per module-qualified class name, notice only — removed in 1.0) informational UserWarning — `@deprecated` on class `<Name>` now dispatches to `@deprecated_class`. — suppressed with stream=None. This replaces the v0.6 "will become a TypeError" warning; the threatened TypeError never ships. @deprecated_class stays the explicit, preferred form for classes. (#222)
  • Explicit TargetMode.NOTIFY + a mapping stays flagged; auto-resolve applies only to an omitted target. Passing target=TargetMode.NOTIFY explicitly together with args_mapping (callables and proxies) or attrs_mapping (proxies) emits UserWarning at decoration time (TypeError in v1.0); the mode stays NOTIFY and the mapping is inert at runtime, preserved in audit metadata with misconfigured=True — explicit configuration is never silently rewritten. This flagging is unchanged from v0.11.0; what is new is that it no longer also applies to an omitted target, which now auto-resolves. Legacy proxy sentinels target=True (without a mapping) and target=False now resolve to an unset target and follow the same auto-resolve as an omitted target; warn-only proxies record DeprecationConfig.target=None. (#222)
  • Non-callable sources raise a clear TypeError. Applying @deprecated to a plain object, a __call__ instance without __name__, or functools.partial of a class now raises TypeError naming deprecated_instance, instead of crashing later on __name__ access. (#222)
  • deprecated() front door documented as the arguments common to both dispatch shapes (target, deprecated_in, remove_in, stream, num_warns, message_template, args_mapping, args_extra, skip_if, update_docstring, docstring_style). The class-only attrs_mapping is not among them and never has been — deprecated(attrs_mapping=...) raises TypeError (unexpected keyword argument) in v0.11.0 and v0.12.0 alike; use deprecated_class(attrs_mapping=...) directly. message_template and skip_if passed through @deprecated on a class are now forwarded to the proxy (message_template was previously dropped silently on the class-dispatch path). (#222)
  • @deprecated(target=TargetMode.ATTRS_REMAP) now raises TypeError for a class source too. The mode needs attrs_mapping, which the front door does not expose, so it can never redirect anything through @deprecated; a class source previously built a no-op proxy — not silently: v0.11.0 emitted the class-dispatch notice plus a second UserWarning naming attrs_mapping and pre-announcing this TypeError. The callable path already raised as proxy-only. The error points to deprecated_class(attrs_mapping=...). (#222)
  • Source builds now require setuptools>=82. The [build-system] requires floor moved from >=70 (via >=80 in #225); installing from an sdist on a build environment pinned below that will fail to bootstrap. Wheel installs are unaffected, and the package still declares zero runtime dependencies. (#227)

Deprecated

  • template_mgs renamed to message_template. The custom-notice parameter on @deprecated, deprecated_callable, deprecated_class, and deprecated_instance was a typo (mgs for msg); it is now message_template. template_mgs stays as a deprecated keyword alias that emits a FutureWarning and forwards its value (passing both raises TypeError); it will be removed in v1.0. Audit code reading DeprecationConfig.template_mgs keeps working through a read-only property alias — the stored field is now message_template. (#223)

[0.11.0] — 2026-07-15 — Operator forwarding, PEP 560 subclassing, & proxy identity fixes

Added

  • Deprecated proxies now forward operator and protocol dunders to the wrapped object. Arithmetic (proxy + 1), comparison/ordering, context managers (with proxy:), iteration (next, reversed), numeric conversion (int/float/round/abs), os.fspath, format, and the async protocols (async with, async for, await) now delegate to the active object instead of raising TypeError. Binary operators preserve NotImplemented semantics, so unsupported-operand errors surface normally. The warn-policy contract is documented in the _DeprecatedProxy docstring: data use warns (within the num_warns budget), cheap probes stay silent. Caveat: in-place operators (+=, -=, *=, …) return the active object's result rather than a re-wrapped proxy — after x += 1, the name x is rebound to a plain int and all subsequent uses are silent even if the deprecation window has not closed. (#214)

... (truncated)

title: releasing `0.30.7` [rebase & merge]
body:
# v0.30.7 — Fewer hangs, truer mAP

## 📋 Summary

Eight bug fixes: video processing, dataset export, mAP and Transformers loading no longer fail or hang silently.

- **`process_video`** raises on a failed write instead of hanging.
- **`MeanAveragePrecision`** matches `pycocotools` where recall lands on a threshold.
- **Dataset export** can write back into the folder the images came from.
- **`from_transformers`** reads semantic output that includes per-pixel scores.

Drop-in upgrade, no code changes. Stored mAP baselines may shift slightly.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

**`sv.process_video` stops hanging** ([#2636](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2636))

A frame the writer rejects, or a callback that returns `None`, now raises instead of blocking forever.

```python
import supervision as sv

def callback(frame, index):
    sv.BoxAnnotator().annotate(frame.copy(), detections)  # forgot `return`

sv.process_video("in.mp4", "out.mp4", callback)
# before: hangs after `writer_buffer` frames
# now:    TypeError naming the frame
```

**`sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision` matches `pycocotools`** ([#2638](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2638))

Recall thresholds and recall are float64, as in `COCOeval`. A class whose recall lands exactly on a threshold used to score slightly high: mAP@50 0.7470 instead of 0.7415 in one case.

**Datasets re-export in place** ([#2637](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2637))

```python
ds = sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco(
    images_directory_path="data",
    annotations_path="data/_annotations.coco.json",
)
ds.as_coco(
    images_directory_path="data",
    annotations_path="data/_annotations.coco.json",
)
# before: shutil.SameFileError
# now:    annotations rewritten, images left in place
```

**Transformers semantic output with scores** ([#2643](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2643))

`sv.Detections.from_transformers` accepts results from `return_segmentation_scores=True` instead of raising `KeyError: 'segments_info'`.

## 🔄 Migration guide

No migration required for this release.

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🔧 Fixed

- `sv.process_video` raises `RuntimeError("Writer thread raised: ...")` or `TypeError` instead of hanging when a frame cannot be written or a callback returns `None`. ([#2636](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2636))
- `sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision` computes IoU and recall thresholds, IoUs and recall in float64, matching `pycocotools`. mAP changes only for classes whose recall lands exactly on one of the 101 thresholds, by up to about 0.007 mAP@50. ([#2638](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2638))
- `sv.DetectionDataset.as_yolo`, `as_pascal_voc`, `as_coco`, `as_createml` and `as_labelme` export into the folder the images were loaded from instead of failing with `shutil.SameFileError`. ([#2637](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2637))
- `sv.Detections.from_transformers` accepts semantic segmentation output with `segmentation_scores`; per-pixel scores stay out of per-detection `confidence`. ([#2643](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2643))
- `sv.crop_image` clips finite crop coordinates outside the 32-bit integer range to the image bounds, instead of wrapping to an empty crop. ([#2642](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2642))
- `sv.DetectionDataset.as_labelme` gives disconnected components of one mask a shared group ID, so `from_labelme` rebuilds one detection. ([#2640](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2640))
- `sv.DetectionDataset.as_labelme`, `as_yolo` and `as_pascal_voc` export in-memory grayscale `(height, width)` images. ([#2641](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2641))
- `sv.KeyPoints.with_nms` keeps skeletons with zero joints instead of raising a zero-size reduction error. ([#2639](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2639))

title: fix(vlm): recover Qwen detections when the response is cut inside a bbox
body:
## Description

`from_qwen_2_5_vl` (used by `sv.Detections.from_vlm` for `sv.VLM.QWEN_2_5_VL` and `sv.VLM.QWEN_3_VL`) drops a complete detection when a truncated response is cut off inside the last box's `bbox_2d` array:

```python
from supervision.detection.vlm import from_qwen_2_5_vl

text = (
    '[{"bbox_2d": [1, 2, 3, 4], "label": "a"}, '
    '{"bbox_2d": [5, 6, 7, 8], "label": "b"}, '
    '{"bbox_2d": [9, 10'
)
from_qwen_2_5_vl(text, (10, 10), (10, 10))[2]
# develop: ['a']
# expected: ['a', 'b']
```

Before `json.loads`, the parser narrows the text to `text[text.find("["):text.rfind("]") + 1]`. When the cut lands inside a `bbox_2d` array, the last `]` belongs to the previous object's box (`[5, 6, 7, 8]`), so the narrowed text loses that object's closing `}`. `recover_truncated_qwen_2_5_vl_response` then rebuilds the list up to the last `}` it can see, which belongs to the object before. A cut anywhere else (inside a label, after a `,`) already recovers every complete object, which the existing truncation test covers. Since a box's coordinates are a large share of each object's tokens, a `max_new_tokens` cut often lands inside `bbox_2d`.

## Motivation and Context

The truncated-response recovery exists so a cut-off generation still returns every detection it completed. In this case it silently returned one fewer.

## Changes Made

- `from_qwen_2_5_vl`: on a `JSONDecodeError`, pass recovery the text as it was before the `[`…`]` narrowing (fences already stripped). The narrowed text is still what `json.loads` and the `ast.literal_eval` fallback read, so complete responses and python-style lists parse as before.
- `tests/detection/test_vlm.py`: a case next to the existing truncation case, cut inside the last `bbox_2d`.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

## Testing

The new case on `develop`:

```
FAILED tests/detection/test_vlm.py::test_from_qwen_2_5_vl[...] - AssertionError: (shapes (1, 4), (2, 4) mismatch)
1 failed, 20 passed, 139 deselected
```

With this change:

```
$ pytest tests/detection/test_vlm.py -k qwen
21 passed, 139 deselected
$ pytest tests
4364 passed, 1 skipped
$ ruff check && ruff format --check   # on the changed files, ruff from .pre-commit-config.yaml
All checks passed!
```

Tested on Linux, Python 3.12.

title: fix(dataset): name the malformed YOLO line instead of failing on its shape
body:
## Description

Fixes #2664. Stacked on #2663, which touches the same function; the diff below is only this change.

`yolo_annotations_to_detections` appended a class id for every line but only appended a box when the line matched a known shape, with no `else`. A line of one to four tokens therefore left `class_id_list` one entry longer than `relative_xyxy_list`, and the mismatch surfaced far from its cause:

| input | before |
|---|---|
| `0 0.5 0.5 0.2` | `operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (0,) (4,)` |
| a blank line | `IndexError: list index out of range` |
| one valid line plus one truncated | `class_id must be a 1D np.ndarray with shape (1,), but got shape (2,)` |
| `is_obb=True`, 6 / 8 / 10 tokens | `cannot reshape array of size 5 into shape (2)` |

The third is what a user sees when one row of an otherwise good file is damaged, and it blames `class_id` rather than the short line. None of the four name the offending line, so finding it in a large dataset means bisecting by hand.

After:

```text
Invalid YOLO annotation line '0 0.5 0.5 0.2'; expected at least 5 tokens (class id and four box values), got 4.
Invalid YOLO OBB annotation line '0 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5 0.5'; expected 9 tokens (class id and four corner pairs), got 6.
```

This matches how the parser already rejects a class id that is not a whole number and a non-numeric trailing token.

## Scope

- Five or more tokens are unchanged: boxes, boxes with a trailing confidence or tracker id, and polygons all load as before.
- `is_obb=True` is documented as nine-token four-corner lines only, so any other count is rejected rather than reaching the reshape.

## Type of change

- [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

A file that previously raised one of the errors above now raises a clearer one; nothing that previously loaded stops loading.

## How has this change been tested?

Nine new tests in `tests/dataset/formats/test_yolo.py`: class-only, one, two and three coordinate lines; a blank line; a truncated line among valid ones; and OBB lines that are too few, odd or too many.

Following AGENTS.md §8, with a baseline captured before any change:

```text

after      8 failed, 4408 passed, 24 skipped
```

The failing set is identical in both runs — all eight are pre-existing `ImportError: metrics extra is required` in this environment. `uv run pre-commit run` passes on all changed files, mypy included.

## Docs

- [X] Docs updated? `docs/changelog.md` entry added, linking this PR.

title: fix(dataset): keep YOLO box extents non-negative on both ends
body:
## Description

Fixes #2662.

`_parse_box` built `xyxy` as `x_center ± width / 2` without checking the sign, so a label such as `0 0.5 0.5 -0.4 0.4` produced `[70, 30, 30, 70]` — `x_min` past `x_max`. Nothing downstream expects that ordering and nothing reported it:

| | before | should be |
|---|---|---|
| `Detections.area` | `-1600.0` | `1600.0` |
| `box_iou_batch`, two boxes over the identical region, one reversed | `0.0` | `1.0` |
| `with_nms(threshold=0.5)`, two heavily overlapping boxes, one reversed | keeps `2` | keeps `1` |

A corrupt label therefore skewed evaluation silently rather than failing.

**On load**, a negative extent now raises `ValueError`, matching how this parser already rejects a class id that is not a whole number (`test_rejects_class_id_that_is_not_a_whole_number`) and a non-numeric trailing token (`test_rejects_a_nonnumeric_trailing_token`).

**On export**, `object_to_yolo` now orders the corners before measuring. `Detections` does not enforce `x_min <= x_max`, so without this it would write the very extent the loader rejects, leaving supervision unable to read back a dataset it had just written:

```python
>>> object_to_yolo(xyxy=np.array([70., 30., 30., 70.]), class_id=0, image_shape=(100, 100, 3))
'0 0.50000 0.50000 -0.40000 0.40000'   # before
'0 0.50000 0.50000 0.40000 0.40000'    # after -- same rectangle, now ordered
```

Normal boxes are byte-identical; the `object_to_yolo` docstring example still produces `'0 0.37500 0.37500 0.50000 0.50000'`.

## Scope

- A zero extent is degenerate but still ordered, so it keeps loading — pinned by a test.
- The polygon path is unaffected: `polygon_to_xyxy` takes min and max.
- `NaN` and `inf` extents were already rejected by `Detections`' finite-value check; `-inf` is caught by the new guard.

## Type of change

- [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

Strictly, a label file with a negative extent that previously loaded will now raise. That is the intent — it was loading as a box no consumer could interpret.

## How has this change been tested?

Eight new tests in `tests/dataset/formats/test_yolo.py`, covering both directions: negative width, height and both on load; zero width and height still loading; and reversed x, y and both surviving an export/import round trip.

Following AGENTS.md §8, with a baseline captured before the change:

```text
baseline   8 failed, 4384 passed, 24 skipped
after      8 failed, 4392 passed, 24 skipped
```

The failing set is identical in both runs — all eight are pre-existing `ImportError: metrics extra is required` in this environment. `uv run pre-commit run` passes on both changed files, mypy included.

## Any specific deployment considerations?

One thing I left out deliberately: the error names the offending values but not the annotation file, so a single bad row in a large dataset aborts the load without saying which file. `_parse_class_id` has the same gap, so threading the path through looks like a separate change across all of this parser's errors rather than something to bolt onto this one. Happy to do it in a follow-up if you would like it.

## Docs

- [X] Docs updated? `docs/changelog.md` entry added, linking this PR.

title: fix(cv2): write video at OpenCV's bit rate without OpenCV
body:
## Description

Without OpenCV, `sv.VideoSink` (and `sv.process_video`, which writes through it) produces much lower-quality video than with OpenCV. The PyAV fallback writer leaves the encoder's bit rate unset, while `cv2.VideoWriter` sets it from the frame rate and size, so the same frames come out at well under half OpenCV's bit rate:

```python
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage
import supervision as sv

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
texture = ndimage.gaussian_filter(rng.random((720, 1280, 3)) * 255, (1.5, 1.5, 0))
frames = [np.roll(texture.astype(np.uint8), 4 * i, axis=1) for i in range(30)]

info = sv.VideoInfo(width=1280, height=720, fps=30)
with sv.VideoSink("out.mp4", info) as sink:  # codec="mp4v" by default
    for frame in frames:
        sink.write_frame(frame)
```

Bit rate and mean PSNR of the 30 decoded frames against the frames written:

| codec | OpenCV installed | without OpenCV, `develop` | without OpenCV, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mp4v` (default) | 4,747 kbit/s, 32.4 dB | 1,860 kbit/s, 27.9 dB | 4,766 kbit/s, 32.4 dB |
| `MJPG` | 42,038 kbit/s, 33.4 dB | 9,776 kbit/s, 27.0 dB | 42,723 kbit/s, 33.0 dB |

This PR gives the fallback encoder the rate control that OpenCV's FFmpeg writer sets.

## Motivation and Context

Since 0.30.0 a plain `pip install supervision` has no OpenCV, so the PyAV writer is what new installs use to save annotated video. The 4-6 dB drop shows as blocking around box edges and label text. #2592 fixed the same backend difference for still images (JPEG quality 95, lossless WebP). This is the video counterpart.

OpenCV's settings come from `icv_configure_video_stream_FFMPEG` and `CvVideoWriter_FFMPEG::open` in `modules/videoio/src/cap_ffmpeg_impl.hpp`. Every codec except H.264 gets a bit rate of about two bits per pixel per frame (`bitrate_scale = 3` for MJPEG, so six), the same value as `bit_rate_tolerance`, `qmin = 3` and `gop_size = 12`. For H.264 OpenCV encodes at `crf=23`, which is libx264's default, so the fallback already matches there.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/_cv2/_video.py`: new `_opencv_encoder_options(codec, fps, frame_size)` returns those settings, and `_VideoWriter` applies them to the PyAV stream. The bit rate is capped at `INT_MAX` as OpenCV does. Without the cap, 4K60 MJPEG would overflow PyAV's C `int` `bit_rate_tolerance` and the writer would fail to open.
- `tests/cv2/test_video.py`: `test_opencv_encoder_options_match_opencv_rate_control` (mpeg4, mjpeg, and 4K60 mjpeg capped at `INT_MAX`), `test_opencv_encoder_options_leave_libx264_at_its_crf_default`, and `test_fallback_writer_matches_opencv_video_quality`. The last one writes the same panning texture with `cv2.VideoWriter` and with the fallback (`mp4v` and `MJPG`), and requires the fallback's PSNR to be within 1 dB of OpenCV's. It is skipped without OpenCV, like the other reference tests in that file.
- `docs/how_to/opencv_migration.md`: one sentence next to the JPEG/WebP note, saying that video written with `sv.VideoSink` now has about the same bit rate and quality in both backends.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.
- Out of scope: the BGR to YUV conversion. OpenCV converts with bicubic swscale and PyAV with bilinear, which leaves MJPEG about 0.4 dB below OpenCV. `mp4v` is not affected by it.

## Testing

On `develop` the new test module cannot import `_opencv_encoder_options`. With the helper present but not applied in `_VideoWriter`:

```
E       AssertionError: assert 27.337574089466674 > (32.36734738077006 - 1)
E       AssertionError: assert 27.208126141779854 > (33.30599226957994 - 1)
FAILED tests/cv2/test_video.py::test_fallback_writer_matches_opencv_video_quality[mp4v]
FAILED tests/cv2/test_video.py::test_fallback_writer_matches_opencv_video_quality[mjpg]
2 failed, 18 passed
```

With this change:

- `pytest tests/cv2/test_video.py`: 20 passed, with PyAV 17.1.0 and 18.0.0 (the versions in `uv.lock`).
- `pytest tests/cv2 tests/utils`: 525 passed with OpenCV, and 308 passed, 25 skipped with OpenCV uninstalled. Both runs deselect `test_ordinary_suite_passes_when_cv2_is_blocked`, which runs the whole suite in a subprocess.
- The pre-commit hooks (ruff, ruff-format, docformatter, mdformat, codespell, doctest fences) are clean on the changed files, and mypy is clean on `_video.py` and the test file.

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (ran `tests/cv2` and `tests/utils` with and without OpenCV, not the full suite)
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

- `vp09` takes the same path. With OpenCV's settings it matches `cv2.VideoWriter` (34.26 dB on the 1280x720 clip, against 33.3 dB before), but like OpenCV it encodes several times slower than PyAV's default.
- Output files grow with the bit rate, to OpenCV's sizes. `VideoSink` has no bit rate option either way.

title: fix(detection): prevent integer overflow in anchor coordinates
body:
## Description

`Detections.get_anchors_coordinates` can return an anchor outside a valid integer box. For example, `xyxy=np.array([[20000, 0, 22000, 2]], dtype=np.int16)` returns `[-11768, 1]` for `Position.CENTER` instead of `[21000, 1]`. The same midpoint calculation is used by annotators and zone tools.

This change computes integer midpoints without wrapping the input dtype. Floating-point inputs, direct-corner anchors, oriented-box anchors, and mask centroids keep their existing paths.

## Motivation and Context

NumPy performs `x1 + x2` in the input integer dtype, so the sum wraps before division. Valid `int16`, `int32`, and unsigned integer boxes can silently produce a wrong midpoint.

## Changes Made

- Use one overflow-safe midpoint calculation for the five axis-aligned anchor positions that average corners. For 64-bit integers, keep representable sums in integer arithmetic so opposite large corners retain their midpoint precision; compute overflowing sums exactly before converting the result to `float64`.
- Add regression cases for every midpoint anchor and for signed and unsigned integer coordinate arrays, including 64-bit overflow, cancellation, and rounding.

## Testing

- Final 11 regression cases on `develop` at `9ab70e7`: 10 failed with incorrect coordinates, 1 passed.
- `uv run pytest tests/detection/test_core.py -q --tb=short --color=no` — 210 passed.
- `uv run pytest --cov=supervision -q --disable-warnings --tb=short --color=no` — 4,410 passed, 24 skipped (code commit `931edb4`; current HEAD adds only the PR link to the changelog).
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` — passed.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API — no new API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` linking this PR

## Additional Notes

The overflow handling runs only for integer coordinate midpoints. Floating-point midpoint arithmetic is unchanged. As before, `float64` cannot represent every integer coordinate above `2**53` exactly.

title: fix(cv2): accept OpenCV keyword names in the NumPy `flip` fallback
body:
## Description

Without OpenCV, which is the default since `0.30.0`, `sv.LineZoneAnnotator(text_orient_to_line=True)` raises `TypeError: _flip() got an unexpected keyword argument 'flipCode'` on any line drawn right to left. Labels on such a line are flipped 180° to read upright with `cv2.flip(annotation, flipCode=-1)`. The NumPy fallback is defined as `_flip(image, flip_code)`.

Repro:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

frame = np.zeros((200, 200, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
line_zone = sv.LineZone(start=sv.Point(170, 100), end=sv.Point(30, 100))
sv.LineZoneAnnotator(text_orient_to_line=True).annotate(frame=frame, line_counter=line_zone)
```

The fix is in the fallback, not the caller. `_flip` now takes OpenCV's `src, flipCode`, so any keyword call that works with OpenCV also works without it. `addWeighted`'s fallback already does the same with `src1`/`src2`. This is the same `_cv2` fallback layer as #2652.

## Motivation and Context

Closes #2658

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/_cv2/_image.py`: rename `_flip(image, flip_code)` to `_flip(src, flipCode)`. Behavior is unchanged.
- Tests:
  - `tests/cv2/test_integration.py` checks that the fallback accepts the keyword names and matches the positional call. It runs without OpenCV.
  - `tests/detection/test_line_counter.py` checks that `LineZoneAnnotator` draws oriented labels for a line drawn right to left.
- `docs/changelog.md`: Unreleased entry; `date_modified` bumped.

Out of scope: I checked every `_cv2` fallback against OpenCV's signature and every `cv2.*` call site; only `flip` has a keyword caller that breaks. Other name mismatches (e.g. `cvtColor(image)`, `copyMakeBorder(border_type)`) have only positional callers and are left alone.

## Testing

Without OpenCV (the default dev env):

- New tests on `develop` (9ab70e76e): both fail, with `TypeError: _flip() got an unexpected keyword argument 'src'` and `'flipCode'` (the line is drawn right to left). `test_ordinary_suite_passes_when_cv2_is_blocked` also fails there, because it re-runs the new line-counter test. With this change, all pass.
- `uv run pytest -q`: 4401 passed, 24 skipped.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks pass.

With `opencv-python` 5.0.0: `tests/cv2/test_image.py`, `tests/cv2/test_cv2.py`, `tests/cv2/test_integration.py` (except the blocked-cv2 subprocess test) and `tests/detection/test_line_counter.py` give 189 passed.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API (private API only)
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

The fallback still rejects flip codes other than `0`, `1` and `-1`, while OpenCV accepts any positive or negative value. No caller uses them, so I left this unchanged.

title: feat(detection): let zones follow camera motion with `coord_transform`
body:
## Description

`PolygonZone` and `LineZone` assume a fixed camera. With a panning camera, a parked car drifts across the frame and can be counted as entering a zone or crossing a line.

This PR adds an optional `coord_transform` to `PolygonZone.trigger` and `LineZone.trigger`. The zone stays defined in a reference frame, and detection anchors are mapped into it with `coord_transform.rel_to_abs` before the existing tests.

## Motivation and Context

Refs #2656 (the counting part; drawing would follow separately).

## Changes Made

- `coord_transform=None` on both `trigger` methods. `None` keeps the current behaviour.
- Anchors that map to non-finite or out-of-bounds coordinates are not counted. `LineZone` keeps its crossing history in reference coordinates.
- `sv.CoordinatesTransformation`: a `typing.Protocol` with `rel_to_abs` and `abs_to_rel`, the method names `trackers` and `norfair` use. No new dependency.
- Docs: geometry reference entry, a short how-to section and a changelog entry.

Out of scope: annotators still draw zones at their fixed coordinates.

## Testing

- `uv run pytest`, with and without OpenCV, and `uv run pre-commit run`.
- New tests use explicit expected values: a crossing counted in reference coordinates, a parked object under a moving line, and NaN, inf and far anchors.
- Checked locally with `trackers` 2.6.1: `MotionEstimator` transformations work as `coord_transform` for both triggers.

## Additional Notes

Drawing zones at mapped positions can follow in a separate PR if this direction is accepted.

title: fix(dataset): read the box of YOLO pose labels instead of a polygon
body:
## Description

`DetectionDataset.from_yolo` reads Ultralytics pose labels as polygons. A pose label is `class x y w h` followed by the `K * D` keypoint values declared by `kpt_shape: [K, D]` in `data.yaml`, so every value after the class went to the polygon parser, and the box and mask came from the keypoints.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image
import supervision as sv

Path("images").mkdir(); Path("labels").mkdir()
Image.new("RGB", (640, 480)).save("images/a.png")
Path("data.yaml").write_text("names: ['person']\nkpt_shape: [17, 3]\n")
# class, box, then 17 "x y visibility" triplets; unlabelled keypoints are "0 0 0"
Path("labels/a.txt").write_text(
    "0 0.5 0.5 0.25 0.5 0.45 0.3 2 0.455 0.32 1 0.46 0.34 0 0.44 0.33 2 0.5 0.33 2"
    " 0.42 0.42 2 0.58 0.42 1 0.4 0.52 2 0.6 0.52 0 0.41 0.6 2 0.59 0.6 2"
    " 0.45 0.62 2 0.55 0.62 2 0.45 0.7 1 0.55 0.7 2 0 0 0 0 0 0\n"
)
ds = sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo("images", "labels", "data.yaml")
print(ds[0][2].xyxy, None if ds[0][2].mask is None else ds[0][2].mask.shape)
```

`develop` prints `[[   0.    0. 1280.  960.]] (1, 480, 640)`; with this change, `[[240. 120. 400. 360.]] None`.

## Motivation and Context

`from_yolo` is the only way to load these labels today. Ultralytics fixed the same misreading in its own loader in ultralytics/ultralytics#26357, and this applies the same rule. It is a loader fix, not the keypoint dataset of #1438, which #1477's closing comment says should start from a container/API proposal: the keypoints are not loaded.

## Changes Made

- When `data.yaml` declares `kpt_shape`, a row of exactly `5 + K * D` tokens keeps its first five and drops the keypoints before parsing. Rows of any other length are parsed as before.

title: fix(examples): measure speed estimation time from frame indices
body:
## Description

The Ultralytics, Inference and YOLO-NAS speed estimation examples computed elapsed time as `len(coordinates[tracker_id]) / video_info.fps`. That assumes the vehicle was detected in every frame and counts N stored positions as N frame intervals instead of N − 1, so missed detections inflate speeds and gap-free tracks read slightly slow.

This PR stores each position with its frame index and divides by the frame span, exactly as `rfdetr_example.py` already does (the same fix was logged for that example in 0.30.1). Minimal repro of the old formula: a 90 km/h track with every third detection missed reads 129.6 km/h; the frame-based formula reads 90.0 (full snippet in the issue).

## Motivation and Context

Closes #2653

## Changes Made

In `ultralytics_example.py`, `inference_example.py` and `yolo_nas_example.py` (identical `+`/`-` lines in all three):

- iterate with `enumerate(frame_generator)` and store `(frame_index, y)`;
- `elapsed_frames = history[-1][0] - history[0][0]`; a speed is shown once `len(history) >= 2` and `elapsed_frames >= fps / 2`;
- add the same `calculate_speed(distance, elapsed_frames, fps)` helper the RF-DETR example uses.

`docs/changelog.md`: Unreleased entry.

Visible side effect: because the warm-up now counts elapsed frames rather than samples, the first speed label appears one frame later than before (on the 14th frame of a track instead of the 13th at 25 fps), matching the RF-DETR example.

Deliberately out of scope (the first three are noted in the issue; all are separate changes if wanted): the `.astype(int)` truncation of road coordinates, the `WIDTH - 1` / `HEIGHT - 1` `TARGET` corners, along-road-only distance, the `int(fps)` history length, a missing `strict=True` in `yolo_nas_example.py`, and adopting the RF-DETR example's `process_frame` structure.

## Testing

The examples have no tests in the suite, so "added tests" is left unchecked. Evidence instead:

- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks pass. `uv run pytest -q`: 4607 passed, 1 skipped (unchanged by this PR).
- **Accuracy before/after.** The speed logic was extracted from the files themselves (`ast`) and run on synthetic scenes with exact ground truth (exact detections, tracker ids supplied by the scenario, no tracker, the examples' own `ViewTransformer` and `TARGET`). Median signed error:

  | Scenario | develop | this PR | RF-DETR example |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 100 km/h, detector misses 1 frame in 3 | +44.0% | +0.0% | +0.0% |
  | 100 km/h, lost for 10 frames (worst reading) | +36.8% | +5.0% | +5.0% |
  | 90 / 110 / 130 km/h, 25 fps, no gaps | −5.1% | −1.1% | −1.1% |

  The patched examples produce the same readings as the RF-DETR example on every frame. The remaining error (about −1% without gaps, up to +5% on the first reading after a 10-frame gap) comes from the out-of-scope whole-meter truncation and `TARGET` scale.
- **Smoke run.** Each example's `main()` ran end to end on a rendered 125-frame 1080p video, with the models, `from_*` converters and ByteTrack stubbed to return known boxes and ids for a 100 km/h car whose detection is dropped in every third frame: no errors, 63 speed labels per run, median 100 km/h (develop: 144).

title: fix(_cv2): add `getPerspectiveTransform` and `perspectiveTransform`
body:
## Description

`examples/speed_estimation/rfdetr_example.py` builds its `ViewTransformer` with `cv2.getPerspectiveTransform` and `cv2.perspectiveTransform` through `from supervision import _cv2 as cv2`. The private `supervision._cv2` layer exported neither, under either backend, so the example raised `AttributeError` before processing the first frame:

```python
from supervision import _cv2 as cv2

print(cv2.BACKEND_NAME, hasattr(cv2, "getPerspectiveTransform"), hasattr(cv2, "perspectiveTransform"))
# develop, OpenCV installed:  opencv False False
# develop, OpenCV missing:    fallback False False
```

This PR exports both from `supervision._cv2`, following the existing pattern: OpenCV's functions when OpenCV is installed, NumPy fallbacks otherwise.

## Motivation and Context

Closes #2651

The RF-DETR speed example is the variant the speed-estimation README recommends, and as shipped it has raised this error since it was added in #2497. The other speed examples import `cv2` directly and are unaffected. Switching this example to `import cv2` would be a one-line alternative, but it would make the example require OpenCV; this PR keeps the example on `supervision._cv2` and fills the gap there.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/_cv2/_transform.py`: `_get_perspective_transform` solves OpenCV's eight-equation system in float64 and returns a `(3, 3)` float64 matrix with `m[2, 2] == 1`; it accepts the float32 `(4, 2)` / `(4, 1, 2)` / `(1, 4, 2)` inputs OpenCV accepts. `_perspective_transform` maps float32/float64 `(rows, cols, 2)` point arrays (e.g. `(N, 1, 2)`, `(1, N, 2)`), vectorised, keeping shape and dtype; points whose `w` is NaN or `|w| <= FLT_EPSILON` map to `(0, 0)` as in OpenCV; empty input returns `None`.
- `src/supervision/_cv2/__init__.py`: both names added to the OpenCV import list, the fallback assignments and `__all__`.
- `tests/cv2/test_transform.py`: parity against OpenCV on seeded random convex quads, the speed example's own `SOURCE`/`TARGET` and a uniform scale; both point layouts and dtypes; thin (ill-conditioned) quads compared with OpenCV by projected corners; a singular system; non-finite input, the `|w|` threshold, empty input and invalid inputs.
- `tests/cv2/test_cv2.py`: both names added to `REQUIRED_SYMBOLS`.
- `tests/cv2/test_integration.py`: regression test that maps the speed example's `SOURCE` onto `TARGET` through `supervision._cv2`; it has no module-level skip, so it also runs in the `cv2: none` job.
- `docs/changelog.md`: Unreleased entry.

The fallback solves the same eight-equation system as OpenCV in float64 and raises `ValueError` only when that system is singular; OpenCV returns a degenerate matrix there instead of raising. (Updated after review: an earlier revision rejected thin but valid quads with an angular collinearity check.)

Out of scope: `solveMethod` is not supported by the fallback (nothing in the repo uses it).

## Testing

New tests fail on `develop` and pass on this branch:

```

tests/cv2/test_transform.py   ImportError: cannot import name '_get_perspective_transform'
test_facade_exports_required_opencv_symbol[getperspectivetransform]  FAILED
test_facade_exports_required_opencv_symbol[perspectivetransform]     FAILED
test_facade_maps_speed_example_source_onto_target  AttributeError: module 'supervision._cv2' has no attribute 'getPerspectiveTransform'
```

| OpenCV 5.0.0 | `uv run pytest -q` | 4654 passed, 1 skipped (rasterio) |
| OpenCV 4.14.0 | `pytest tests/cv2 -q` | 328 passed |

| — | `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` | all hooks passed (incl. mypy, ruff, docformatter) |

The real example's `ViewTransformer` maps `SOURCE` onto `TARGET` with a max error of 1.7e-13 (OpenCV 5.0 and 4.14) and 1.9e-15 (NumPy fallback).

title: fix(metrics): Score mixed class-agnostic detections
body:
## Description

Fix class-agnostic mAP when predictions or targets omit `class_id`. A perfect match scores `0.0` on `develop` when only one side has class IDs:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MeanAveragePrecision

predictions = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10]], dtype=float),
    confidence=np.array([0.9]),
)
targets = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=predictions.xyxy.copy(), class_id=np.array([3])
)
result = MeanAveragePrecision(class_agnostic=True).update(predictions, targets).compute()
print(result.map50_95)  # develop: 0.0; patched: approximately 1.0
```

`update` maps present class arrays to `-1`, while COCO preparation maps absent arrays to `0`. The evaluator separates these categories before matching geometry.

## Motivation and Context

`Detections.from_sam` returns unlabeled detections, so evaluating SAM proposals against labeled ground truth reaches this path. The class-agnostic contract in [#1566](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/issues/1566) requires predictions and targets to count as one class.

## Changes Made

- Normalize missing class arrays before COCO preparation when accumulated inputs include labeled detections. This also handles labels supplied in a later update.
- Preserve category `0` and mapping behavior for all-unlabeled inputs. Class-aware scoring and caller-owned arrays remain unchanged.
- Add 26 regression and compatibility cases covering boxes, masks, oriented boxes, mappings and multiple updates. Each parameter row states its expected category.
- Clarify the argument docstring and add an Unreleased changelog entry.

The change operates on the copies already owned by the metric. It changes no stored files, defaults, public APIs or dependencies.

## Testing

Python 3.13, one native thread:

- Current pristine `develop` at `09e0b53`, with the imported source path asserted: **13 failed, 13 passed**. Twelve mixed-label cases score zero instead of one; the cross-update case reports two classes instead of one.
- Focused mAP test modules and source doctests: **73 passed**.

title: fix(detection): round Roboflow polygon vertices before rasterising masks
body:
## Description

`sv.Detections.from_inference` rasterises polygon predictions about one pixel off. `process_roboflow_result` built the vertex array with `np.array(..., dtype=int)`, which truncates. Roboflow and Inference return polygon points as sub-pixel floats (e.g. `{"x": 363.5, "y": 185.0}`), so every polygon mask moved up and to the left by up to a pixel:

```python
result = {"image": {"width": 12, "height": 12}, "predictions": [{
    "x": 5.1, "y": 5.1, "width": 5, "height": 5, "confidence": 0.9,
    "class": "a", "class_id": 0,
    "points": [{"x": 2.6, "y": 2.6}, {"x": 7.6, "y": 2.6},
               {"x": 7.6, "y": 7.6}, {"x": 2.6, "y": 7.6}],
}]}
mask = sv.Detections.from_inference(result).mask[0]
# develop:  rows 2-7, cols 2-7
# this PR:  rows 3-8, cols 3-8
```

This PR converts the vertices to float, rounds them to the nearest pixel, and then casts to `int32`, the same way `from_coco` (#2587), `from_yolo`, `from_labelme` and `from_pascal_voc` do.

## Motivation and Context

This is the same bug class as #2587 (COCO) and #2080 (YOLO), in the Roboflow/Inference connector. The shift is systematic, so it biases every polygon mask in the same direction. For small objects it costs a noticeable share of IoU against the true outline, and the same polygon loads differently from Inference than from an exported COCO/YOLO dataset.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/detection/utils/internal.py`: `process_roboflow_result` rounds polygon vertices before the `int32` cast, with a short comment on why. This applies to both the dense and the `compact_masks=True` paths, which share the rasterised mask.
- `tests/detection/utils/test_internal.py`: `test_polygon_prediction_rounds_decimal_vertices` checks the exact mask for a decimal square, for `compact_masks=False` and `True`.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.
- Out of scope: RLE predictions and box-only predictions are unchanged.

## Testing

- The new test on `develop` gives `2 failed`, with masks at rows/cols 2-7.
- With this change, `pytest tests/detection/test_core.py tests/detection/utils/test_internal.py tests/key_points/test_core.py` gives 495 passed, and the doctests for `detection/utils/internal.py` pass.
- The pre-commit hooks (ruff, docformatter, codespell) are clean on the changed files, and mypy is clean on `internal.py`.

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (ran the test files that use `from_inference` / `process_roboflow_result` and the module doctests, not the full suite)
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

Integer vertices load exactly as before. `Detections.from_sam3` and the Florence-2 segmentation parser still truncate float vertices the same way.

A polygon vertex that is NaN or infinite now raises a `ValueError` before rounding, as `from_coco` does (on `develop` the `dtype=int` conversion raised `ValueError` or `OverflowError`); `test_polygon_prediction_rejects_non_finite_vertex` covers it.

title: fix(vlm): merge the polygons of one Florence-2 instance into one detection
body:
## Description

`sv.Detections.from_vlm(sv.VLM.FLORENCE_2, ...)` turns every polygon of a segmentation result into its own detection. Florence-2 groups polygons per instance: its processor returns `{"polygons": [[poly_a, poly_b], ...], "labels": [...]}`, with one polygon list and one label per instance. An instance has several polygons when the object is not one connected region, e.g. a car cut in two by a pole. Supervision iterated over the inner lists as well, so one instance came back as several detections:

```python
result = {"<REFERRING_EXPRESSION_SEGMENTATION>": {
    "polygons": [[[1, 1, 3, 1, 3, 3, 1, 3], [6, 6, 8, 6, 8, 8, 6, 8]]],
    "labels": [""],
}}
detections = sv.Detections.from_vlm(sv.VLM.FLORENCE_2, result, resolution_wh=(10, 10))
# develop:   len(detections) == 2, xyxy [[1, 1, 3, 3], [6, 6, 8, 8]]
# this PR:   len(detections) == 1, xyxy [[1, 1, 8, 8]], mask covers both parts
```

## Motivation and Context

One referring expression ("the car") should produce one object. Splitting it inflates counts, breaks tracking, and gives each fragment its own box. `from_sam3` already merges the polygon fragments of an instance into one mask.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/detection/vlm.py`: for `<REFERRING_EXPRESSION_SEGMENTATION>` and `<REGION_TO_SEGMENTATION>`, rasterise all polygons of an instance into one mask, and take the box around all their vertices.
- `tests/detection/test_vlm.py`: `TestFromFlorence2Segmentation` covers a two-part instance for both tasks, two single-polygon instances staying separate, an empty instance next to a valid one, and an all-empty result through `Detections.from_vlm`.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.
- Out of scope: vertices are still truncated with `astype(np.int32)` rather than rounded. That is left unchanged here to keep this PR to the grouping.

## Testing

title: fix(detection): keep off-frame fractional boxes out of masks
body:
## Description

`sv.xyxy_to_mask` fills edge pixels for an inclusive box that is entirely left of or above the image when its maximum coordinate is a negative fraction. The conversion to `int` truncates `-0.2` to `0`, turning an off-frame box into one that includes the first column or row. This change checks the original maximum coordinates before conversion.

## Motivation and Context

For example, `sv.xyxy_to_mask(np.array([[-2, 1, -0.2, 2]]), (5, 5))` currently sets two pixels in column zero. The box has no overlap with the image, so its mask should be empty. Existing converter tests already establish that partially visible negative boxes are clipped and invalid boxes produce empty masks.

## Changes Made

- Leave inclusive masks empty when a box ends left of or above the image, before fractional coordinates are truncated.
- Add regression cases for both axes and both coordinate conventions. The exclusive convention already produces empty masks.
- Document the behavior and add an Unreleased changelog entry.

title: releasing `0.30.6` [rebase & merge]
body:
# 0.30.6: Pillow-conversion, dataset-export, and line-crossing correctness fixes

## 📋 Summary

supervision 0.30.6 is a patch release closing 12 library correctness bugs and landing 2 behavior refinements across datasets, annotators, key points, line-crossing counting, and the Pillow-based fallback backend, plus a new docs guide and a notebook dead-link fix. No new public API, no breaking changes. The broadest-reach fix rewrites `pillow_to_cv2`, the entry point every annotator except `RichLabelAnnotator` and several image helpers use to convert a Pillow image: it used to pass raw mode bytes straight through, so a 1-bit mask, a 16-bit depth map, an `LA`/`PA` image, or a CMYK JPEG all drew wrong or crashed. Two fixes close silent-wrong-data bugs rather than crashes: `LineZone.trigger` let unconfirmed tracks inflate crossing counts, and `DetectionDataset.as_yolo`/`.as_pascal_voc` silently dropped box-only objects from a mixed polygon/box COCO dataset. `DetectionsSmoother` no longer crashes when two tracked objects first seen on different frames carry different metadata (e.g. RF-DETR's `source_image`); its own docstring pipeline was broken. Every library fix ships a regression test.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### `sv.pillow_to_cv2` now converts every Pillow mode the way `cv2.imread` would

Raw mode bytes used to pass straight through: a 1-bit mask came back as `0`/`1` instead of `0`/`255`, a 16-bit depth map wrapped modulo 256 and drew as noise, an `LA`/`PA` image crashed in `cvtColor` on its 2-channel array, and a CMYK JPEG drew its cyan/magenta/yellow ink as red/green/blue. This function is the entry point for every annotator except `RichLabelAnnotator` (which stays on the Pillow path) plus `crop_image`, `resize_image`, `letterbox_image`, `scale_image`, `tint_image`, `grayscale_image`, and `plot_image` whenever handed a Pillow image, so the bug reached the whole drawing surface, not just one call site. A single-channel grayscale image also drew from a read-only buffer view before this fix. Annotating into it silently failed; it now hands back a writable copy.

```python
from PIL import Image

depth_map = Image.open("depth.tif")  # mode "I;16"
scene = sv.pillow_to_cv2(depth_map)
# clipped to the 16-bit range and keeps its high byte, instead of wrapping mod 256
```

RGB, RGBA, grayscale, and palette images are unchanged.

### `sv.LineZone.trigger` no longer lets unconfirmed tracks inflate counts

Detections with a negative `tracker_id` (how trackers like `ByteTrackTracker` mark an unconfirmed track) all keyed under one shared id. Two distinct unconfirmed objects crossing on opposite sides in the same frame read as one track oscillating, silently inflating `in_count`/`out_count` with crossings no confirmed track ever made. Confirmed tracks (`tracker_id >= 0`) are counted exactly as before.

### `sv.DetectionDataset.as_yolo` / `.as_pascal_voc` stop dropping box-only objects

`from_coco` gives an all-zero mask to any annotation without its own `segmentation` when a sibling annotation has one, and to every annotation when `force_masks=True`. The exporters only ever wrote the polygon traced from a mask, so a mixed polygon/box COCO dataset silently lost its box-only objects on export, and a box-only COCO dataset loaded with `force_masks=True` wrote empty YOLO label files or object-less Pascal VOC files. A detection with an empty or contour-less mask now exports as its bounding box instead.

### `sv.DetectionsSmoother` no longer crashes on a second tracked object

Each smoothed track was built on the oldest frame in its window, so two objects first seen on different frames carried different frames' `metadata` (exactly what the RF-DETR / `inference` connectors attach), and `Detections.merge` rejected the mismatch. `class_id` and `data` (e.g. `class_name`) now follow the current frame instead of lagging up to `length - 1` frames behind a class change; `xyxy`, `confidence`, and oriented-box corners are still averaged as before.

### Dataset splits reject an out-of-range ratio instead of silently mis-splitting

`sv.DetectionDataset.split`, `sv.ClassificationDataset.split` (both take `split_ratio`), and the internal `train_test_split` helper they call (takes `train_ratio`) never validated the ratio. A finite out-of-range value looked like a successful split: for 10 images, a ratio of `-0.2` returned 8/2 via negative slicing, and `1.2` (or an accidental percentage like `80`) returned 10/0 with no held-out data, no error either way.

```python
train, test = dataset.split(split_ratio=80)  # meant 80%
# now raises ValueError naming the problem, instead of silently returning
# every image as train and none as test
```

`0` and `1` keep their existing meanings. Not an API break: no signature changed, only previously-silent input now raises.

## 🔄 Migration guide

No breaking changes in this release.

No deprecations or removals landed in 0.30.6 either. All scheduled `remove_in` markers in the codebase target `0.31.0` or `0.32.0` and are untouched by this patch release.

Two entries change *output values* rather than only fixing a crash or a silently-wrong count; not API breaks, but worth checking if your code depends on the old values:

- `sv.KeyPoints.from_ultralytics` / `.from_inference` / `.from_detectron2`: `as_detections().confidence` now carries the model's own detection score, not the mean of the per-keypoint confidences.
- `sv.DetectionsSmoother`: `class_id` and `data` fields on a smoothed track now follow the current frame instead of lagging behind a class change.

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🔧 Fixed

**Annotators / key points**

- `sv.VertexEllipseHaloAnnotator` now draws the whole halo of a key point whose covariance ellipse is not horizontal. A vertical or diagonal ellipse used to be clipped to a thin band because the fade box was sized as if the major axis always ran along the image x axis. Horizontal ellipses are drawn exactly as before. ([#2634](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2634))
- `sv.KeyPoints.from_ultralytics`, `.from_inference` and `.from_detectron2` now keep each object's detection score as `detection_confidence` instead of dropping it, which previously made `sv.KeyPoints.with_nms` raise `ValueError` and `as_detections()` report the mean keypoint confidence instead of the model's own score. ([#2633](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2633))
- `sv.LabelAnnotator` now sizes the label background correctly for a label containing a blank line. Text drew each blank line at full height while the background measured it as zero, pushing the last line outside the box. Labels without blank lines are unchanged. ([#2632](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2632))
- `sv.IconAnnotator` now draws a palette icon that carries its own alpha channel (Pillow `PA` mode, storable in TIFF) instead of raising `ValueError`. Palettes without alpha, and every read with OpenCV installed, are unchanged. ([#2624](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2624))

**Datasets**

- `sv.DetectionDataset.as_yolo` / `.as_pascal_voc` now write a detection whose mask is empty or has no valid contour as its bounding box instead of silently leaving it out of the label file. ([#2631](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2631))
- `sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo` now loads a label row carrying a trailing confidence or tracker id (written by Ultralytics `save_txt` with `save_conf=True` or tracking on) instead of raising `ValueError`, for both box and segmentation rows. The extra token is ignored; box and polygon geometry are unchanged. An odd-length polygon row with no extra field now loses its last value rather than raising, since coordinate parity is the only signal separating the two cases. ([#2619](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2619), [#2626](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2626), [#2635](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2635))

**Tracking**

- `sv.DetectionsSmoother` no longer raises `ValueError: Conflicting metadata` when a second tracked object, first seen on a different frame, enters the smoothing window. ([#2628](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2628))
- `sv.LineZone.trigger` now ignores detections with a negative `tracker_id` (the value trackers such as `ByteTrackTracker` report for an unconfirmed track) instead of letting them silently inflate `in_count`/`out_count`. ([#2623](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2623))

**Detection utils**

- `sv.polygon_to_mask` now accepts a list/tuple/array-like of `[x, y]` vertices (not just a NumPy array) and returns an all-zero mask for an empty or under-3-vertex polygon instead of crashing inside OpenCV/NumPy with an opaque error. A malformed polygon now raises `ValueError` naming the problem. ([#2622](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2622))
- `sv.Detections.from_sam3` now keeps SAM 3 PVS contour fragments with fewer than 3 vertices instead of dropping them. Single points and 2-point edges are rasterized directly into the mask and bounding box. ([#2625](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2625))

**Image / IO**

- `sv.pillow_to_cv2` now converts every Pillow mode to the 8-bit array `cv2.imread` would produce, reaching every annotator plus `crop_image`, `resize_image`, `letterbox_image`, `scale_image`, `tint_image`, `grayscale_image`, and `plot_image`. ([#2614](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2614))
- `sv.CSVSink` now writes UTF-8 on every platform, preserving non-English detection labels and custom fields on Windows. ([#2615](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2615))

**Docs**

- Dead documentation links fixed across the published notebooks (`quickstart.ipynb`, `annotate-video-with-detections.ipynb`, `underestand-visitors-with-yolo-world.ipynb`). ([#2630](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2630))

### 🌱 Changed

- `sv.DetectionDataset.split`, `sv.ClassificationDataset.split`, and the internal `train_test_split` helper they call now reject a ratio outside `[0, 1]` (`NaN` and `±inf` included) with a `ValueError` naming the problem, instead of silently mis-splitting or dropping the held-out set. ([#2611](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2611))
- `sv.tint_image` and `sv.grayscale_image` now accept a single-channel `(H, W)` array or grayscale `Image`, as `sv.letterbox_image` already did. ([#2614](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2614))
- New docs guide: "Evaluate targets from a PyTorch DataLoader" in `docs/metrics/mean_average_precision.md`, cross-linked from `docs/how_to/benchmark_a_model.md`. `Detections.from_transformers` gained a docstring note that it expects post-processed predictions, not raw DataLoader targets. ([#2620](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2620))

title: fix(detection): expire LineZone history on untracked frames
body:
## Description

`LineZone.trigger()` retains crossing history when a nonempty frame has no `tracker_id`. After enough such frames, a reused tracker ID on the opposite side of the line is counted as a crossing. This change ages that history by the same policy used for empty frames.

Minimal reproduction: trigger ID `7` below a horizontal line, trigger two nonempty detections without tracker IDs, then trigger ID `7` above the line. On `develop`, the final call returns `crossed_in=[True]` and increments `in_count` to `1`; the expected result is `False` and `0`, as after two empty frames.

## Motivation and Context

The missing-ID path warns and returns before `_evict_stale_crossing_history()` runs. Existing tests and the `minimum_crossing_threshold` docstring establish that short absences preserve state while absences of `crossing_history_length` frames expire it.

## Changes Made

- Age existing crossing history on nonempty frames without tracker IDs before issuing the existing warning.
- Test both a one-frame gap, which preserves a crossing, and a two-frame gap, which expires the state.

## Testing

Verified on HEAD `0c01f8d88fa8f686fa80cdc65f5f9c7ebc8fc9ef` after merging `develop`:

- New regression on unmodified `develop`: 1 passed, 1 failed for the expected stale crossing (`[True] != [False]`).
- `uv run pytest tests/detection/test_line_counter.py -q --disable-warnings`: 77 passed, 1 warning.
- `uv run pytest -q --disable-warnings`: 4329 passed, 24 skipped, 25 warnings.
- `uv run pre-commit run --files src/supervision/detection/line_zone.py tests/detection/test_line_counter.py`: passed.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: passed on the pre-merge head; focused checks on the changed files passed after merging `develop`.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

The warning and return arrays for detections without tracker IDs are unchanged. A single missing-ID frame still preserves the track's crossing state.

title: fix(detection): accept Transformers semantic outputs with scores
body:
## Description

`Detections.from_transformers` raises `KeyError: 'segments_info'` when passed a semantic segmentation result from `post_process_semantic_segmentation(return_segmentation_scores=True)`. Transformers returns a dictionary-like output with `segmentation` and `segmentation_scores` for this option, without `segments_info` ([DETR](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/detr/image_processing_detr.py), [SegFormer](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/segformer/image_processing_segformer.py), [EOMT](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/eomt/image_processing_eomt.py)). Supervision currently routes every dictionary with `segmentation` to the instance/panoptic parser, which requires `segments_info`.

This change routes score-bearing semantic results through the existing class-map parser used for bare semantic tensors. The per-pixel scores are not mapped to `Detections.confidence`, which represents one score per detection.

## Motivation and Context

The supported `return_segmentation_scores=True` option makes semantic post-processing output unusable with `sv.Detections.from_transformers` despite carrying the same class map as the default tensor output. A regression test using a dictionary-like output fails on current `develop` with `KeyError: 'segments_info'` and passes with this change.

## Changes Made

- Distinguish semantic output carrying `segmentation_scores` from instance and panoptic results carrying `segments_info`.
- Document the accepted semantic output and the treatment of per-pixel scores.
- Add a public adapter regression test covering masks, class IDs, class names, and confidence behavior.

## Testing

- Regression test on `develop`: fails with `KeyError: 'segments_info'`.
- `python -m pytest tests/detection/test_from_adapters.py tests/detection/tools/test_transformers.py -q --disable-warnings --tb=short --color=no` — 71 passed (local dev virtual environment, `PYTHONPATH=src`).
- `python -m pytest -q --disable-warnings --tb=short --color=no` — 4,320 passed, 24 skipped (same environment).
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — passed.
- No model download or PyTorch integration test was run; the regression uses a dictionary-like output and the repository's fake tensor helper.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs for changed public behavior
- [x] Added a changelog entry under `Unreleased` with this PR linked

## Additional Notes

Results that include `segments_info` continue through the existing instance/panoptic parser. A dictionary missing both `segments_info` and `segmentation_scores` still follows the prior error path.

title: fix(utils): clip crop bounds before integer conversion
body:
## Description

`crop_image` rounds its coordinates and casts them to `int32` before clipping them to the image. A finite box such as `(-4294967296, 0, 4294967296, 3)` around a 4×3 image wraps to zero, so both NumPy and Pillow return an empty crop instead of the full image. Keeping the rounded values as `float64` until after clipping preserves the documented crop behavior without changing in-range coordinates.

## Motivation and Context

`crop_image` is used directly and by the inference slicer and crop annotator. This is a correctness fix for valid finite coordinates outside the `int32` range. There is no linked issue.

## Changes Made

- Clip the rounded coordinates to image bounds before converting them to Python integers.
- Add regression cases on both image backends for bounds just beyond `int32`, at `2**32`, and far outside the image as floats. All six cases fail on `develop` with an empty crop and pass with the fix.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/utils/test_image.py tests/detection/tools/test_inference_slicer.py tests/annotators/test_core.py -q --disable-warnings --tb=short --color=no` — 304 passed (local dev virtual environment, `PYTHONPATH=src`).
- `python -m pytest -q --disable-warnings --tb=short --color=no` — 4,325 passed, 24 skipped (same environment, rebased HEAD).
- `pre-commit run --all-files` — passed.
- `pre-commit run --files docs/changelog.md` — passed after adding the PR-linked changelog entry.
- `uvx ruff check src/supervision/utils/image.py tests/utils/test_image.py` and `uvx ruff format --check src/supervision/utils/image.py tests/utils/test_image.py` — passed.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API (not applicable: no API change)
- [x] Added a changelog entry under `Unreleased` with the PR link

## Additional Notes

The implementation is deliberately one line: the existing per-backend clipping and integer conversion already do the right thing once the premature `int32` cast is removed.

title: fix(dataset): export annotations for in-memory grayscale images
body:
## Description

Exporting a `DetectionDataset` containing a two-dimensional grayscale image raises a dimension-unpacking error in LabelMe and YOLO, or an `IndexError` in Pascal VOC. Read height and width independently of channels, and write Pascal VOC depth as `1` for grayscale images.

Minimal reproduction on `develop` at `8c7df2388ce46f16139edc498c2bc3874493b4bc`:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

dataset = sv.DetectionDataset(
    classes=["object"],
    images={"gray.png": np.zeros((16, 24), dtype=np.uint8)},
    annotations={
        "gray.png": sv.Detections(
            xyxy=np.array([[3, 2, 15, 10]], dtype=np.float32),
            class_id=np.array([0]),
        )
    },
)
dataset.as_labelme(annotations_directory_path="labels")
# ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)
# as_yolo fails the same way; as_pascal_voc raises IndexError.
```

## Motivation and Context

In-memory image dictionaries remain supported until their scheduled removal in 0.33.0. COCO export already accepts these grayscale arrays. The other three exporters should preserve their dimensions and annotations too.

[PR #2410](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2410) addressed image modes during loading. [PR #2637](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2637), currently open, addresses copying images into their source folder. Neither fixes grayscale annotation dimensions.

## Changes Made

- Read the first two shape dimensions in LabelMe and YOLO; document the supported YOLO shape tuples.
- Set Pascal VOC depth to `1` for two-dimensional images without changing image pixels.
- Add 12 format-local regression cases covering grayscale/color images, boxes/masks, dimensions, coordinates, and unchanged source arrays.
- Add an Unreleased changelog entry. The in-memory API's deprecation schedule remains unchanged.

## Testing

On unmodified production code, the new tests failed for all six grayscale cases with the expected dimension errors; all six color controls passed:

```text
uv run pytest tests/dataset/formats/test_labelme.py tests/dataset/formats/test_yolo.py tests/dataset/formats/test_pascal_voc.py -k ImageShapes
6 failed, 6 passed, 161 deselected
```

With the fix:

```text
uv run pytest tests/dataset/formats/test_labelme.py tests/dataset/formats/test_yolo.py tests/dataset/formats/test_pascal_voc.py
173 passed

uv run pytest --cov=supervision
4329 passed, 24 skipped; 91% coverage

uv run pre-commit run --all-files
All hooks passed

uv run pytest --doctest-modules src/supervision/dataset/formats/labelme.py src/supervision/dataset/formats/yolo.py src/supervision/dataset/formats/pascal_voc.py
5 passed
```

The clean base passed 4316 tests with the same 24 skips and 91% coverage; its pre-commit checks also passed. Validation ran on macOS with Python 3.13.9 using the NumPy fallback backend. Native OpenCV and rasterio were not installed; their existing optional reference tests account for the skips. No test skips were added.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

No public API, dependencies, coordinate conventions, or image pixels are changed.
