title: fix(dataset): preserve `LabelMe` instance grouping
body:
## Description

LabelMe export writes each disconnected region of a detection mask as a polygon, but previously left every `group_id` null. Import also ignored explicit groups, so one instance became multiple detections. This change exports shared IDs for disconnected components and imports shapes with the same `(label, group_id)` as one detection with a union mask and enclosing box.

Minimal reproduction on `develop`:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.dataset.formats.labelme import (
    detections_to_labelme_shapes,
    labelme_shapes_to_detections,
)

mask = np.zeros((1, 48, 64), dtype=bool)
mask[0, 5:15, 5:15] = True
mask[0, 30:40, 30:40] = True
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[5, 5, 39, 39]], dtype=np.float32),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
    mask=mask,
)
shapes = detections_to_labelme_shapes(detections, ["dog"])
result = labelme_shapes_to_detections(shapes, {"dog": 0}, (64, 48), True)
len(result)  # Before: 2; after: 1
```

## Motivation and Context

Instance membership must survive LabelMe conversion. LabelMe's own [instance-segmentation converter](https://github.com/wkentaro/labelme/blob/main/examples/instance_segmentation/labelme2coco.py) groups by `(label, group_id)`, unions masks, and treats only missing/null group IDs as ungrouped.

[#2299](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2299) introduced LabelMe support; its multicomponent test checked polygon output without checking preserved instance count. Open [#2637](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2637) concerns image copying into the source folder and addresses a separate failure.

## Changes Made

- Import explicit groups, including `group_id=0`, using mask unions and enclosing component boxes. Missing/null IDs, different groups, and different labels remain independent.
- Export a shared numeric group ID for each mask with multiple polygon components. Existing single-polygon, rectangle, and empty-mask fallback behavior remains intact.
- Add focused grouping and round-trip regression coverage, update the affected public docstrings, and add an Unreleased changelog entry.

## Testing

All commands ran in this branch's own worktree using Python 3.11 and the default NumPy fallback backend:

- Clean `develop` baseline, `uv run pytest -q`: **4316 passed, 24 skipped**.
- New/updated tests against unmodified production code, `uv run pytest tests/dataset/formats/test_labelme.py -q`: **15 failed, 44 passed**. Failures show explicit groups remaining split, missing export group IDs, and round trips producing two/four detections instead of one/two.
- With the fix, the same focused command: **59 passed**.
- `uv run pytest --cov=supervision`: **4335 passed, 24 skipped**, **91% total coverage**.
- `uv run pytest --doctest-modules src/supervision/dataset/formats/labelme.py src/supervision/dataset/core.py`: **3 passed**.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: **all hooks passed**, including mypy.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

The base is `8c7df2388ce46f16139edc498c2bc3874493b4bc`. Polygon rasterization fidelity is unchanged; numeric group IDs are regenerated on export because `Detections` stores instance membership, not LabelMe IDs. The 24 skips also occur on the clean baseline. Native OpenCV was not installed for these runs.

title: fix(key_points): preserve empty-joint skeletons during NMS
body:
## Description

`KeyPoints.with_nms()` raises a zero-size reduction error after boolean filtering removes every joint from a nonempty batch. It now preserves those skeletons and their aligned fields, consistent with skeletons whose joints are all unusable.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

key_points = sv.KeyPoints(
    xy=np.array([[[10., 10.], [20., 20.]]]),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
    detection_confidence=np.array([0.9]),
)
filtered = key_points[np.array([[False, False]])]
filtered.with_nms()  # Previously raised ValueError; now keeps the skeleton.
```

## Motivation and Context

Public keypoint filtering can produce valid `(N, 0, 2)` coordinates. The bounding-box reductions ran before the existing no-valid-joints handling and could not reduce the empty joint axis.

[#2401](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/issues/2401) and merged [#2402](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2402) addressed indexing and `as_detections`. Merged [#2563](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2563) addressed nonfinite joints in NMS. Open [#2633](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2633) populates detection confidence in pose connectors. This change addresses the separate empty-axis failure.

## Changes Made

- Give the four bounding-box reductions their existing positive/negative infinity sentinels as initial values, allowing empty axes to reach the existing zero-area-box handling.
- Keep the usual NMS validation and selection path, preserving class-aware and class-agnostic behavior, aligned fields, and returned-object semantics.

title: fix(metrics): compute mAP recall thresholds in float64 like pycocotools
body:
## Description

`sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision` does not match `pycocotools` when a class's recall lands exactly on one of the 101 recall thresholds. That happens whenever a class's number of ground-truth objects shares a factor with 100. In those cases sv reports a higher mAP:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MeanAveragePrecision

targets_xyxy = np.array([[i * 20, 0, i * 20 + 10, 10] for i in range(10)])
misses_xyxy = np.array([[i * 20, 100, i * 20 + 10, 110] for i in range(10)])
# seven hits, ten false positives, then an eighth hit
predictions_xyxy = np.vstack([targets_xyxy[:7], misses_xyxy, targets_xyxy[7:8]])

targets = sv.Detections(xyxy=targets_xyxy, class_id=np.zeros(10, dtype=int))
predictions = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=predictions_xyxy,
    class_id=np.zeros(18, dtype=int),
    confidence=np.linspace(0.99, 0.5, 18),
)
MeanAveragePrecision().update(predictions, targets).compute().map50
# develop:     0.7469746977976053
# pycocotools: 0.7414741474147416   (COCOeval(gt, dt, "bbox").stats[1])
```

`COCOEvaluator` in `src/supervision/metrics/mean_average_precision.py` ports `COCOeval`, but it computes the recall thresholds (`COCOEvaluatorParameters.rec_thrs`) and the recall `rc = tp / n` (`_accumulate`) in float32. `pycocotools` computes both in float64. Precision is then sampled with `np.searchsorted(rc, rec_thrs, side="left")`, so the result depends on which side of the recall each threshold falls.

In float64, `np.linspace(0, 1, 101)[70]` is `0.7000000000000001`, which is just above the recall `7 / 10 = 0.7`. `pycocotools` therefore samples the next detection, after the ten false positives. In float32, both values round to the same number, so sv samples at the seventh hit. For 10 targets this happens at recall 0.7 only. For 20, 50 and 100 targets it happens at 3, 3 and 10 recall levels.

## Motivation and Context

#1834 aligned `MeanAveragePrecision` with `pycocotools`, and the changelog and `docs/deprecated.md` describe the metric as matching it. The leaderboard numbers rely on that. I compared against `pycocotools` 2.0.11:

- Random single-image classes with 100 targets and noisy predictions differed in 29 of 30 trials, by up to 0.007 mAP@50 and 0.002 mAP@50:95. sv was higher on average.
- Small random datasets (1 to 4 images, up to 3 classes) differed in 1 or 2 of 1500 trials, depending on the seed, with float or integer box coordinates.

## Changes Made

- `COCOEvaluatorParameters`: `iou_thrs` and `rec_thrs` are float64, with a comment explaining why.
- `COCOEvaluator._accumulate`: `tp_sum`, `fp_sum` and the recall `rc` are float64. Before, they were cast to float32 and divided by `np.float32(n)`.
- `COCOEvaluator._compute_iou`: returns float64 IoUs (the cast was float32), and the `ious` annotations are updated to match.
- `_mask_iou_with_jaccard`: counts the mask pixels and divides the counts in float64, the way pycocotools does, instead of taking the float32 IoU from `mask_iou_batch`. Without this, the float64 thresholds would reject a mask IoU of exactly 65/100, which `mask_iou_batch` rounds to 0.649999976 (a second commit, after review). Crowd columns keep the COCO rule of dividing by the detection area. The counts use float32 up to 2**24 pixels, as in `mask_iou_batch`, so they stay exact. This part is needed because of the threshold change. Comparing float32 IoUs with float64 thresholds breaks integer boxes: an IoU of exactly 0.65 becomes `0.64999998` in float32 and would no longer match at the 0.65 threshold. On develop that case is correct only because the IoU and the threshold are both rounded to float32.
- `tests/metrics/test_mean_average_precision.py`: new class `TestMeanAveragePrecisionPycocotoolsParity`.
  - The case above, pinned to the `pycocotools` value.
  - A guard with IoUs of exactly 0.65, 0.7, 0.9 and 0.95. It passes on develop too. It fails if only the thresholds move to float64, which I checked.
  - The same guard for `MetricTarget.MASKS`, with rectangular masks whose IoU is exactly 0.65, 0.7, 0.9 and 0.95. It passes on develop, fails on this PR's first commit (0.3 / 0.4 / 0.8 / 0.9), and passes with the mask change.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

Out of scope: `MeanAverageRecall`, `Precision`, `Recall` and `F1Score` have their own code paths and are unchanged. The stored `precision`, `recall` and `scores` arrays stay float32.

## Testing

The new tests on `develop` (before the fix):

```
FAILED tests/metrics/test_mean_average_precision.py::TestMeanAveragePrecisionPycocotoolsParity::test_recall_landing_on_a_recall_threshold_matches_pycocotools - assert 0.7469746977976053 == 0.7414741474147416 ± 1.0e-06
1 failed, 4 passed, 28 deselected
```

With this change:

```
$ pytest tests
4282 passed, 1 skipped
$ pytest tests/metrics
427 passed
$ pytest --doctest-modules src/supervision/metrics/mean_average_precision.py
2 passed
$ ruff check && ruff format --check && docformatter --check   # on the changed files
All checks passed!
```

`mypy` on the changed module reports only the existing missing `pandas` stubs error, the same as on develop.

Differential check against `pycocotools` 2.0.11 (bbox `stats[0:6]`: mAP@50:95, @50, @75, small, medium, large; segm `stats[0:3]`). This was a local script, not part of the test suite:

| data | develop | only thresholds + recall in float64 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 classes of 100 targets | 29/30 differ | 0/30 | 0/30 |
| 1500 small random datasets, float boxes | 1 differs | 0 | 0 |
| 1500 small random datasets, integer boxes | 1 differs | 15 differ | 0 |
| 370 small random mask datasets (`segm`, with crowd targets) | 0 differ | – | 0 |

Tested on Windows only.

title: fix(dataset): export detection datasets into the folder their images are in
body:
## Description

Every `sv.DetectionDataset.as_*` exporter fails when `images_directory_path` is the folder the dataset's images were loaded from:

```python
import supervision as sv

ds = sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco(
    images_directory_path="dataset/train",
    annotations_path="dataset/train/_annotations.coco.json",
)
# ... edit or filter annotations ...
ds.as_coco(
    images_directory_path="dataset/train",
    annotations_path="dataset/train/_annotations.coco.json",
)
# shutil.SameFileError: 'dataset/train/img.jpg' and 'dataset/train/img.jpg' are the same file
```

`save_dataset_images` (`src/supervision/dataset/utils.py`) copies each image that is stored as a path with `shutil.copyfile(image_path, final_path)`. When the destination is the file itself, `copyfile` raises `SameFileError`. The exporters copy images before they write annotations, so the call fails on the first image and no annotation file is written. I reproduced it with `as_yolo`, `as_pascal_voc`, `as_coco`, `as_createml` and `as_labelme`.

## Motivation and Context

Re-saving a dataset in place is common for layouts where images and annotations share one folder, like the COCO layout in the `from_coco` docstring. The same export works if the images are held in memory, because `cv2.imwrite` simply rewrites the file. It only fails for datasets that store image paths, which is now the default.

`ClassificationDataset.as_folder_structure` already handles this case. It wraps the same `shutil.copyfile` call in `contextlib.suppress(shutil.SameFileError)`, and `TestClassificationDatasetFolderRoundTrip::test_export_into_source_folder_keeps_image_files` covers it. `save_dataset_images` is the detection-side sibling that did not get this handling.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/dataset/utils.py`, `save_dataset_images`: a copy onto the image file itself is skipped with `contextlib.suppress(shutil.SameFileError)`, the same way `as_folder_structure` does it. The docstring says so.
- `tests/dataset/test_core.py`: `TestDetectionDatasetExportIntoSourceFolder` runs each of the five exporters into the image's own folder. It checks that the image bytes are unchanged and that the annotation file is written.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

Out of scope: images held in memory, exports into another folder, and the basename-collision checks are unchanged.

## Testing

title: fix(video): stop `process_video` hanging when a frame cannot be written
body:
## Description

`sv.process_video` hangs forever, with no error, when a processed frame cannot be written. Without OpenCV (the PyAV fallback), a callback that returns a frame of a different size is enough:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

def callback(frame, index):
    return frame[: frame.shape[0] // 2]  # e.g. crop, resize, letterbox

sv.process_video("source.mp4", "target.mp4", callback)  # 100-frame video
# Exception in thread (writer_thread):
# ValueError: Video frame must have shape (48, 64, 3), got (24, 64, 3)
# ...then the call never returns
```

The writer thread in `process_video` calls `video_sink.write_frame` with no error handling. When a write raises, the thread dies, but the main loop keeps putting frames into the bounded `writer_buffer` queue with a blocking `put()`. Once the queue is full, `put()` never returns.

The same hang happens with either backend when the callback returns `None`, for example a callback that annotates the frame but forgets to `return` it. `None` is the writer's end-of-stream sentinel, so the writer exits on the first frame and the main loop blocks on the full queue in the same way.

## Motivation and Context

#2022 fixed the hang on callback exceptions, and #2546 fixed the hang when `max_frames` exceeds the video length. A failing writer is the remaining way to block this pipeline. Without OpenCV, the PyAV writer (`_VideoWriter.write`) rejects any frame that is not a `uint8` array of the source video's shape. A callback that changes the frame size therefore hangs the call after `writer_buffer` frames, instead of failing on frame 0 with that error.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/utils/video.py`, `process_video`:
  - `writer_thread` keeps the first `write_frame` exception. After that it keeps taking frames off the queue and discards them until the sentinel, so the blocking `put()` in the main loop can always complete.
  - The main loop stops reading once the writer has failed. After the usual shutdown, the error is raised as `RuntimeError(f"Writer thread raised: {exc!r}")` from the original exception, the same way reader errors are raised.
  - A `None` return from `callback` raises `TypeError` naming the frame index, instead of being queued as the writer sentinel.
  - The `Raises` section of the docstring documents both errors.
- `tests/utils/test_video.py`: two tests use the existing `_run_process_video_with_deadline` helper, so a regression fails instead of hanging the session. One makes `VideoSink.write_frame` raise `OSError`. The other uses a callback that returns `None`.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

Out of scope: with OpenCV, `cv2.VideoWriter.write` does not raise for a frame of the wrong size. It logs `Failed to write frame` and skips the frame. That is OpenCV's own behaviour, and this PR does not change it.

## Testing

The new tests on `develop` (before the fix):

```
FAILED tests/utils/test_video.py::test_process_video_propagates_writer_thread_errors - Failed: process_video did not return within 30s
FAILED tests/utils/test_video.py::test_process_video_rejects_callback_returning_none - Failed: process_video did not return within 30s
2 failed, 39 deselected
```

With this change:

```
$ pytest tests
4275 passed, 1 skipped
$ pytest tests/utils/test_video.py tests/utils/test_sinks.py
51 passed
$ pytest tests/utils/test_video.py   # with cv2 blocked, i.e. the PyAV fallback
41 passed
$ ruff check && ruff format --check && docformatter --check   # on the changed files
All checks passed!
```

`mypy src/supervision/utils/video.py` reports no errors in `video.py`.

I also ran the repro above on a 100-frame video. It now raises `RuntimeError: Writer thread raised: ValueError('Video frame must have shape (48, 64, 3), got (24, 32, 3)')` after 0.3 s without OpenCV. The `None` callback raises `TypeError` with and without OpenCV. Before the fix, both runs were stopped by a 40 s watchdog. Tested on Windows only.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

A writer that is still running when the existing bounded `writer_worker.join(timeout=10)` expires keeps today's behaviour. If such a slow final write fails after the timeout, that failure is not reported. This PR does not change the timeout handling.

After a write failure the writer drains the queue instead of stopping. That keeps the existing shutdown path unchanged, including the `None` sentinel and the bounded joins that the current tests pin. A `put()` with a timeout would have needed changes to those tests.

title: fix(key_points): draw rotated ellipses in full in `VertexEllipseHaloAnnotator`
body:
## Description

`sv.VertexEllipseHaloAnnotator` cuts off any covariance ellipse whose major axis isn't horizontal. It computes the fade only inside a region `ax + 2` px wide and `ay + 2` px tall, but `_iter_ellipse_params` returns `ax` as the *major* semi-axis along `angle`, not the extent along the image x axis. When the ellipse is vertical or diagonal, most of it falls outside that region and is never drawn.

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

def lit(cov):
    kp = sv.KeyPoints(
        xy=np.array([[[100.0, 100.0]]], dtype=np.float32),
        data={"covariance": np.array([[cov]], dtype=np.float32)},
    )
    out = sv.VertexEllipseHaloAnnotator(sigma=1.0, color=sv.Color.WHITE, opacity=1.0).annotate(
        np.zeros((200, 200, 3), dtype=np.uint8), kp
    )
    ys, xs = np.nonzero(out.any(axis=2))
    return f"x {xs.min()}..{xs.max()}, y {ys.min()}..{ys.max()}"

print(lit([[400, 0], [0, 1]]))  # horizontal: x 81..119, y 100..100
print(lit([[1, 0], [0, 400]]))  # vertical   develop: x 100..100, y 97..102
                                #            this PR: x 100..100, y 81..119
```

The docstring example of the class is affected too: the key point with covariance `[[400, 0], [0, 800]]` is clipped to y 478..521 instead of 473..527. `VertexEllipseOutlineAnnotator` and `VertexEllipseAreaAnnotator` draw the same covariances correctly because they use `cv2.ellipse`.

## Motivation and Context

Pose-uncertainty covariances are usually elongated and rotated, so the halo is wrong for most real key points, not just an edge case.

## Changes Made

- Size the halo's region of interest from the rotated ellipse's bounding box (`hypot(ax·cosθ, ay·sinθ)` wide, `hypot(ax·sinθ, ay·cosθ)` tall, plus the existing 2 px pad). Horizontal ellipses get exactly the same region as before.
- Regression test for horizontal / vertical / diagonal halos; changelog entry.

## Testing

`pytest tests/key_points/test_annotators.py -k major_axis`: on `develop` the `vertical` and `diagonal` cases fail (`2 failed, 1 passed`); with this change `3 passed`. `pytest tests/key_points` and the annotator doctests pass (243 passed); `ruff check`/`ruff format` and `docformatter --check` clean on the changed files (mypy's existing PIL `Image` errors in this file are unchanged).

title: fix(key_points): keep the detection score in pose connectors
body:
## Description

`sv.KeyPoints.from_ultralytics`, `sv.KeyPoints.from_inference` and `sv.KeyPoints.from_detectron2` drop each object's detection score and only keep the per-keypoint scores, so `detection_confidence` is always `None` on their output. Two things follow:

- `KeyPoints.with_nms()` cannot be used on connector output at all:

  ```python
  key_points = sv.KeyPoints.from_ultralytics(model("image.jpg")[0])
  key_points.with_nms()
  # ValueError: KeyPoints detection_confidence must be given for NMS to be executed.
  ```

- `KeyPoints.as_detections()` falls back to the mean keypoint confidence, so the confidence it reports differs from the score the model returned and from `sv.Detections.from_ultralytics` / `sv.Detections.from_inference` on the same result. For Inference it is pulled down further: key points below the request's `keypoint_confidence` are omitted and loaded as zero-confidence slots (#2575), so a person scored 0.9 with two of three key points returned at 0.6 and 0.4 became a detection with confidence 0.33.

This PR reads the score each framework already provides (`boxes.conf`, each prediction's `confidence`, `instances.scores`) into `detection_confidence`.

## Motivation and Context

`detection_confidence` was added in #2286, but none of the connectors populate it, so everything built on it (`with_nms`, `as_detections`) only works on hand-built `KeyPoints`.

## Changes Made

- `from_ultralytics`: `detection_confidence` from `boxes.conf`.
- `from_inference`: `detection_confidence` from each prediction's `confidence`. A hand-built result dict without a prediction `confidence` still loads, with `detection_confidence=None`.
- `from_detectron2`: `detection_confidence` from `instances.scores`.
- Updated the `Returns` docstrings of those connectors.
- Out of scope: `from_yolo_nas`, `from_transformers` and `from_mediapipe`, and the mean-keypoint fallback in `as_detections` itself.

## Testing

New tests in `tests/key_points/test_core.py` (Ultralytics, Inference, Detectron2) fail on `develop` (`3 failed`: `assert None is not None`) and pass with this change. `pytest tests/key_points`: 237 passed; doctests for `key_points/core.py` pass; `ruff check`/`ruff format`, `mypy` and `docformatter --check` clean on the changed files.

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (added tests; ran `tests/key_points` and the doctests, not the full suite)

- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

`as_detections()` on connector output now returns the model's detection score instead of the keypoint mean, which is a visible (intended) behavior change noted in the changelog.

title: fix(annotators): size `LabelAnnotator` background for labels with blank lines
body:
## Description

`LabelAnnotator` draws the text of a label with a blank line (e.g. `"car\n\n0.95"`, or a label starting with `"\n"`) partly outside its background box. `_draw_labels` advances a blank line by the height of a line of text (it measures `"Tg"`), but `_get_label_properties` sized the background with `cv2.getTextSize("")`, which is 0 pixels tall. So every blank line pushes the text one line height further down than the background reaches.

Repro (`text_padding=10`, default `text_scale`, white text on a blue background; rows are image y coordinates):

```python
det = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[20, 100, 120, 140]], dtype=np.float32), class_id=np.array([0]))
ann = sv.LabelAnnotator(color=sv.Color.BLUE, text_color=sv.Color.WHITE, text_padding=10)
out = ann.annotate(np.zeros((200, 200, 3), np.uint8), det, labels=[label])
```

Before:
```
'car\n0.95'   background y: (42, 100)  text y: (58, 89)
'car\n\n0.95' background y: (32, 100)  text y: (48, 103)   <- text runs 3 px past the background
```
After:
```
'car\n0.95'   background y: (42, 100)  text y: (58, 89)
'car\n\n0.95' background y: (18, 100)  text y: (34, 89)
```

## Motivation and Context

Blank lines are a natural way to separate a class name from extra info in a multi-line label; today they make the last line spill out of the label box onto the image, and each extra blank line makes it worse.

## Changes Made

- `LabelAnnotator._get_label_properties` measures a blank line with the same `"Tg"` height that `_draw_labels` uses to skip it, so the background and the drawn text agree. Line widths are unchanged, and labels without blank lines are sized exactly as before.
- `RichLabelAnnotator` is left alone: its sizing and drawing both treat a blank line as zero height, so they already agree.
- Regression test in `tests/annotators/test_core.py`; changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

## Testing

- New test fails on `develop` (3 failed) and passes with this change (3 passed): `pytest tests/annotators/test_core.py -k blank_line`
- `pytest tests/annotators src/supervision/annotators/core.py`: 303 passed

title: fix(dataset): export a box for detections with an empty mask in YOLO and Pascal VOC
body:
## Description

`DetectionDataset.as_yolo` and `DetectionDataset.as_pascal_voc` silently leave out every detection whose mask is empty. Both exporters write only the polygons traced from a detection's mask, and an all-zero mask traces to no polygon, so the object disappears from the label file without a warning.

`DetectionDataset.from_coco` produces such masks in two ordinary cases: a box-only annotation (no `segmentation`) in an image where another annotation has a polygon, and every annotation when `force_masks=True`. So exporting a COCO dataset that mixes polygons and boxes loses its box-only objects, and exporting a box-only COCO dataset loaded with `force_masks=True` writes empty YOLO label files and Pascal VOC files with no `<object>`. `as_labelme` already falls back to the box in this case (`detections_to_labelme_shapes`: "so no detection is silently dropped"); this PR does the same for YOLO and Pascal VOC.

Repro (COCO file with one polygon annotation and one box-only annotation, 100x100 image):

```python
ds = sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco(root, "ann.json")   # 2 detections
ds.as_yolo(annotations_directory_path="labels")
ds.as_pascal_voc(annotations_directory_path="voc")
```

Before (`labels/img.txt`, VOC object count):
```
0 0.10000 0.10000 0.10000 0.50000 0.50000 0.50000 0.50000 0.10000
voc objects: 1
```
After:
```
0 0.10000 0.10000 0.10000 0.50000 0.50000 0.50000 0.50000 0.10000
1 0.75000 0.75000 0.30000 0.30000
voc objects: 2
```
With a box-only COCO file and `force_masks=True`, `labels/img.txt` was `''` before and is `'0 0.75000 0.75000 0.30000 0.30000\n'` after.

## Motivation and Context

Converting a dataset from COCO to YOLO or Pascal VOC should not lose annotations, and here the loss is silent, so it only shows up later as missing objects in training labels.

## Changes Made

- `detections_to_yolo_annotations` and `detections_to_pascal_voc`: a detection whose mask has no foreground pixel is written as its bounding box, matching the LabelMe exporter.
- Masks with any foreground pixel are exported as polygons exactly as before. `min_image_area_percentage` / `max_image_area_percentage` still drop polygons outside their range; the fallback applies only to empty masks.
- Regression tests in `tests/dataset/formats/test_yolo.py` and `tests/dataset/formats/test_pascal_voc.py`; changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

## Testing

- New tests fail on `develop` (3 failed) and pass with this change (3 passed): `pytest tests/dataset/formats/test_yolo.py tests/dataset/formats/test_pascal_voc.py -k EmptyMask`
- `pytest tests/dataset src/supervision/dataset/formats/yolo.py src/supervision/dataset/formats/pascal_voc.py`: 438 passed
- `ruff format` / `ruff check` on the changed files: clean

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (added tests; ran the dataset tests above, not the full suite)
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

Making `from_coco` rasterise the box as a mask for box-only annotations would change what loading returns (and `as_coco` round-trips), so the fix is on the export side, where LabelMe already handles it.

title: fix(smoother): build smoothed tracks on the current frame
body:
## Description

`sv.DetectionsSmoother` crashes as soon as a second track appears when detections carry per-frame `metadata`, and it reports stale `class_id`/`data` for tracks whose class changes.

`get_track` built every smoothed track as `deepcopy(valid[0])`, i.e. on the **oldest** frame in the track's window, and only averaged `xyxy`, `confidence` and oriented-box corners. Tracks first seen on different frames therefore carry different frames' `metadata`, and `Detections.merge` (strict about metadata) rejects them. RF-DETR attaches the frame as `metadata["source_image"]` (same root cause as #2594, fixed in #2596 for `InferenceSlicer` only), and `ByteTrackTracker.update` returns `detections[idx]`, which keeps metadata, so the RF-DETR -> tracker -> smoother pipeline in the class docstring crashes on every frame once a second object enters.

Minimal repro:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

smoother = sv.DetectionsSmoother()
smoother.update_with_detections(sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10]], dtype=float),
    tracker_id=np.array([1]), metadata={"frame_index": 0}))
smoother.update_with_detections(sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[1, 1, 11, 11], [30, 30, 40, 40]], dtype=float),
    tracker_id=np.array([1, 2]), metadata={"frame_index": 1}))
# ValueError: Conflicting metadata for key: 'frame_index'.
```

Same line, second symptom: `class_id` and `data` (e.g. `class_name`) came from the oldest frame, so a track whose class changes kept reporting the old class for up to `length - 1` frames.

## Motivation and Context

The documented RF-DETR + tracker + smoother pipeline should run without crashing, and smoothed output should describe the current frame. No existing issue; related: #2594 / #2596.

## Changes Made

- `DetectionsSmoother.get_track` now builds on `valid[-1]`, the newest frame. Every emitted track is active in the current frame, so this is its current detection: `metadata` agrees across tracks and `class_id`/`data` are current.
- `xyxy`, `confidence` and oriented-box corner averaging are unchanged (corner alignment still uses the oldest frame as reference, so output corner order is as before).
- The `get_track` docstring notes where the non-averaged fields come from.
- Two regression tests in `tests/detection/tools/test_smoother.py`; changelog entry under Unreleased.

## Testing

- New tests fail on `develop` (`2 failed, 15 passed`: `ValueError: Conflicting metadata for key: 'frame_index'` and `assert [0] == [1]`) and pass with this change.
- `pytest tests/detection/tools/test_smoother.py tests/detection/test_geometry_contract.py` -> 22 passed; `pytest --doctest-modules src/supervision/detection/tools/smoother.py` -> 2 passed.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files: ruff check/format, docformatter, mdformat, codespell pass; mypy on the changed files: no issues.

- [ ] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (added tests; ran the targeted files above, not the full suite)
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

Averaging `class_id` isn't meaningful, so it follows the latest frame, which matches what the smoothed box represents (the object now). This is a small behaviour change for tracks whose class flips within the window; previously they showed the oldest class.

title: ITZ-700: Load the Roboflow tracking carrier (utm.js) before Segment ends
body:
## Why

Segment ends 2026-09-30. `utm.js` (`https://app.roboflow.com/scripts/utm.js`) sends page views to Roboflow's own pipeline and keeps this site's page-view history continuous under its existing page source once Segment is gone. It also carries the marketing pixels that Segment used to fan out to.

## What changed

Added `https://app.roboflow.com/scripts/utm.js` to `mkdocs.yml`'s `extra_javascript` list, immediately before `javascripts/segment.js`, so it renders ahead of the Segment stub on every docs page.

## Note

The existing Segment snippet (`docs/javascripts/segment.js`) is intentionally left in place until a later cleanup.

## Already-published trees

The `mkdocs.yml` include only reaches a tree `mike` actually rebuilds: a `develop` merge rebuilds `develop/`, and a `release/latest` push rebuilds `latest/`. It never touches a numbered version directory, which is never rebuilt at all. Since 99% of the docs' page views in the last week were on `/latest/` and none on `/develop/`, that gap matters.

The Backfill Docs workflow (`.github/workflows/docs-backfill.yml`) now also runs `.github/scripts/inject_tracking_carrier.py`, which inserts the carrier before `javascripts/segment.js` directly in the published HTML under `latest/`, `develop/`, and every numbered version directory — idempotently, so re-running it is a no-op. After this PR merges, dispatch that workflow with `confirm: BACKFILL` to patch the already-published trees immediately, rather than waiting on the next `release/latest` push, which will rebuild `/latest/` with the tag natively anyway.

## When

Merges Monday 2026-09-28, ahead of the Segment cutover. Tracked in Linear ITZ-700.

## How to verify

Load any page on supervision.roboflow.com and check the Network tab for one POST request to `app.roboflow.com/query/event`.

body:
<details>
<summary>Before submitting</summary>

- [x] Updated documentation (parser docstring and changelog)

## Description

`DetectionDataset.from_yolo` raises `ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 7 into shape (2)` on a segmentation label with one trailing confidence, such as `1 0.1 0.1 0.9 0.1 0.5 0.9 0.87`. The first seven tokens form a valid three-point polygon; the last token is the confidence written by Ultralytics `Results.save_txt(..., save_conf=True)`.

## Type of Change

- 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Motivation and Context

[Ultralytics `Results.save_txt`](https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/blob/main/ultralytics/engine/results.py) appends confidence after polygon coordinates. The YOLO loader currently passes every value after the class id to `_parse_polygon`, so the extra value makes reshaping fail and aborts the dataset import. The recent box-label fix in #2619 handles the analogous sixth token for boxes; this change covers segmentation labels.

## Changes Made

- Ignore one numeric trailing value on non-OBB polygon rows with an even total token count. A normal polygon has one class id followed by coordinate pairs, so its total token count is odd.
- Preserve the polygon box and mask, and reject a nonnumeric trailing value.
- Document the behavior and add unit and end-to-end dataset import coverage.

## Testing

On base `6f87031`, the new tests produced 3 failures for the two trailing-token cases and the dataset import, with `ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 7 into shape (2)`.

- `uv run pytest --cov=supervision -q --tb=short` (fallback backend): 4,306 passed, 24 skipped.
- `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/dataset -q --tb=short` (OpenCV backend): 435 passed.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

The row format with both confidence and track id is not handled here: two extra values cannot be distinguished from another polygon coordinate pair by token count alone.

N/A — the regression is covered by a local dataset fixture.

## Screenshots/Videos (optional)

N/A

OBB parsing is unchanged. No confidence or track id is added to `Detections`, matching the existing box-label behavior.

title: fix(cv2): read a palette image with alpha as color, not index and alpha
body:
## Description

`sv.IconAnnotator` fails on a palette icon that carries its own alpha channel
(Pillow's `PA` mode, which a TIFF can store) when OpenCV is not installed.

```python
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import supervision as sv

rgba = np.zeros((16, 16, 4), dtype=np.uint8)
rgba[..., :3] = (200, 30, 90)
rgba[..., 3] = 255
Image.fromarray(rgba, mode="RGBA").convert("PA").save("icon.tif")

sv.IconAnnotator(icon_resolution_wh=(16, 16)).annotate(
    scene=np.zeros((48, 48, 3), dtype=np.uint8),
    detections=sv.Detections(
        xyxy=np.array([[8.0, 16.0, 40.0, 40.0]]), class_id=np.array([0])
    ),
    icon_path="icon.tif",
)
# ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (16,16,2) into shape (16,16,3)
```

`IconAnnotator` reads icons with `cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED`, for which OpenCV expands any
palette to BGR. `_opencv_unchanged_mode` maps `P`, `LA`, `1` and `CMYK` to the mode
whose pixels match that, but not `PA`, so it returns `None` and Pillow's own array is
used unchanged. That array's two channels are palette index and alpha — the first is a
lookup index, not a color:

    cv2.imread("icon.tif", cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED).shape   # (16, 16, 3)
    _imread("icon.tif", _IMREAD_UNCHANGED).shape         # (16, 16, 2)

`sv.draw_image` rejects the same array with `ValueError: Image must have 3 or 4 channels.`

## Motivation and Context

The function's own docstring states that OpenCV "never returns a two-channel or boolean
array the way Pillow's own modes do", and for `PA` it does.

#2614 fixed this same two-channel `PA` array in `sv.pillow_to_cv2`, which converts an
in-memory Pillow image. This is the file-reading path beside it, which that change did
not cover. #2591 (grayscale PNG icon read as a 2-D array) and #2602 (CMYK icon read as
ink values) are the same class of gap in the same function.

## Changes Made

- `_opencv_unchanged_mode` now takes `PA` through the existing palette branch, so a
  palette image with alpha is expanded to color like any other palette. `PA` files
  carry no `transparency` key, so this resolves to `RGB` — what `cv2.imread` returns.
- Updated the docstring to say palettes are expanded whether or not they carry an
  alpha channel of their own.
- Left out of scope: `LA` TIFFs, where OpenCV returns a 2-D array and the fallback
  returns BGRA. That is a separate divergence and not a crash.

## Testing

Added `tests/cv2/test_image.py::test_fallback_imread_unchanged_expands_palette_with_alpha_like_opencv`,
which compares the fallback against `cv2.imread` as the neighbouring mode tests do.

On `develop` it fails:

    assert ((4, 4, 2), dtype('uint8')) == ((4, 4, 3), dtype('uint8'))

With this change it passes.

    python -m pytest          # 4492 passed, 1 skipped  (opencv-python installed)
    python -m pytest          # 4277 passed, 24 skipped (opencv-python uninstalled)

The second run matches the pre-change baseline exactly; the new test is in the module
skipped when OpenCV is absent, since OpenCV is its reference implementation.

`pre-commit run --all-files` passes for check-doctest-fences, trailing-whitespace,
end-of-file-fixer, mixed-line-ending, ruff-check, ruff-format, docformatter and
mdformat. I could not run the mypy hook locally as it pins `language_version:
python3.11`; running mypy directly reports the same single pre-existing error in this
file before and after the change.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

`PA` is how Pillow reads any palette TIFF carrying an alpha extra-sample

title: fix(LineZone): ignore unconfirmed tracks with negative `tracker_id`
body:
## Description

`LineZone.trigger()` keys crossing state by `tracker_id`. Trackers such as
`ByteTrackTracker` from the `trackers` package report `-1` for tracks they have
not confirmed yet, so several distinct objects can carry that id in the same
frame. All of them were treated as one track, and their apparent movement
between each other read as crossings, silently inflating `in_count` and
`out_count`.

Minimal repro (from the issue): two `-1` boxes on opposite sides of the line,
swapping sides each frame, with no confirmed track anywhere:

```python
import supervision as sv
from tests.helpers import _create_detections

zone = sv.LineZone(start=sv.Point(0, 0), end=sv.Point(10, 0))
below, above = [4, 4, 6, 6], [4, -6, 6, -4]
for _ in range(3):
    zone.trigger(_create_detections(xyxy=[below, above], tracker_id=[-1, -1]))
    zone.trigger(_create_detections(xyxy=[above, below], tracker_id=[-1, -1]))
print(zone.in_count, zone.out_count)  # develop: 3 1   expected: 0 0
```

Detections with a negative `tracker_id` are now unconfirmed and invisible to
the counter: not counted, no crossing state, and always `False` in both
returned arrays.

## Motivation and Context

Found while building a tripwire counter on `inference` + `trackers` +
`supervision`: a live RTSP feed produced 97 / 95 crossings on a clip with 15
real ones, all of it from unconfirmed detections sharing id `-1`.

Closes #2578

## Changes Made

- `LineZone.trigger()`: compute an `unconfirmed = tracker_id < 0` mask once;
  leave those ids out of `current_keys` passed to `_evict_stale_crossing_history`,
  and skip them at the top of the crossing loop before any state is touched.
- Docstrings: one sentence on the rule in `trigger()` and in the class-level
  `tracker_id` note.
- Tests: `TestLineZoneUnconfirmedTracks` (4 cases): the issue repro; a confirmed
  track counted once beside a `-1` flicker; no crossing state ever created for
  negative ids; an object seen as `-1` for two frames, then assigned an id,
  then crossing, counted exactly once (the live-tracker lifecycle).
- Changelog entry under Unreleased.
- Out of scope: `PolygonZone` (checked, keeps no per-track state, unaffected).

## Testing

New tests on `develop` before the fix (4 failed):

```
FAILED ...::test_ignores_unconfirmed_objects_that_trade_sides - assert not True
FAILED ...::test_counts_confirmed_track_despite_unconfirmed_flicker - assert [[np.False_, ...e_, np.True_]] == [[False, ...]]
FAILED ...::test_keeps_no_crossing_state_for_unconfirmed_ids - assert {-1, 3} == {3}
FAILED ...::test_counts_once_when_object_is_confirmed_after_unconfirmed_frames - assert (3, 1) == (1, 0)
```

With the fix:

```
uv run pytest tests/detection/test_line_counter.py src/supervision/detection/line_zone.py
76 passed

uv run pytest   # full suite, src + tests, doctests included; dev group + metrics extra
4281 passed, 24 skipped

SKIP=prettier uv run pre-commit run --files src/supervision/detection/line_zone.py tests/detection/test_line_counter.py docs/changelog.md
ruff check, ruff format, docformatter, mypy, codespell, mdformat (mkdocs), whitespace/EOF fixers: all Passed
```

`prettier` was skipped locally: the hook's node install fails on this machine's
npm (`Unknown cli flag: --ignore-prepublish`), unrelated to this change. It only
touches the markdown changelog entry; CI will run it.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

- Eviction keys are filtered too, not just the loop. Skipping `-1` only inside
  the loop still feeds it to `_evict_stale_crossing_history` every frame; with
  an unconfirmed detection present in most frames, that key would look
  permanently "present". Nothing observable happens today because no history is
  created for it, but the invariant "unconfirmed ids touch no state" is simpler
  to hold than to reason around, and the third test pins it.
- Considered and rejected: slicing to `detections[detections.tracker_id >= 0]`
  up front. The returned `crossed_in`/`crossed_out` must stay aligned with the
  input, so a mask is cleaner than remapping indices.
- Per-element `None` ids cannot occur in an integer array; the existing
  whole-array `tracker_id is None` warning path is unchanged.
- Precedent in this repo: the `DetectionsSmoother` example already drops
  `detections.tracker_id != -1` before use.

title: fix(detection): skip unconfirmed (negative tracker_id) tracks in LineZone
body:
## Description

`LineZone.trigger()` keys its crossing state by `tracker_id`, so every detection with `tracker_id = -1` (the value ByteTrack-style trackers assign to unconfirmed tracks) was collapsed into one shared track. On a busy frame, distinct unconfirmed objects all carried `-1`, and their independent motion made that single phantom track cross the line repeatedly, silently inflating `in_count`/`out_count`.

Minimal repro (before this change):

```python
lz = sv.LineZone(start=sv.Point(0, 100), end=sv.Point(200, 100))
for y in (20, 160, 20, 160, 20, 160):
    lz.trigger(sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[80, y, 120, y + 40]]), tracker_id=np.array([-1])))
print(lz.in_count, lz.out_count)  # 2 3
```

## Motivation and Context

Unconfirmed detections (`tracker_id` of `-1`) should not take part in crossing counts, and must not be collapsed into one shared track. Closes #2578.

## Changes Made

- In `LineZone.trigger()`, skip detections whose `tracker_id` is `None` or negative before updating crossing state.
- Exclude negative `tracker_id` values from the current-frame key set so stale `-1` history is evicted.
- Added a regression test reproducing the count inflation.
- Added a changelog entry under `Unreleased`.

## Testing

- New test: `tests/detection/test_line_counter.py::test_line_zone_skips_unconfirmed_tracks` passes.
- Full `test_line_counter.py` suite: `72 passed`.

- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

Left `Detections` with `tracker_id=None` handled as before (whole-frame warning), since that path was already covered. This only changes behavior for negative IDs.

title: docs(metrics): evaluate PyTorch DataLoader targets with `sv.Detections`
body:
## Description

Issue #1683 asks how to turn ground-truth labels from a PyTorch `DataLoader` (Hugging Face DETR) into `sv.Detections`, so they can be compared with `Detections.from_transformers` predictions in `MeanAveragePrecision` and `ConfusionMatrix`.

This PR adds a short guide for it. The main trap: DETR training targets store boxes as **normalized `(cx, cy, w, h)`**, so `sv.xywh_to_xyxy` (the converter suggested in the issue thread) returns wrong boxes. Targets need `sv.xcycwh_to_xyxy` and then scaling by the same `orig_size` used to post-process the predictions.

## Motivation and Context

Closes #1683

## Changes Made

- `docs/metrics/mean_average_precision.md`: new section "Evaluate targets from a PyTorch DataLoader" with:
  - a typed helper `normalized_targets_to_detections` (normalized cxcywh → pixel `xyxy` `sv.Detections`), with a worked example and notes on images without objects;
  - a full evaluation loop: DETR inference → `post_process_object_detection(threshold=0.0)` → paired prediction/target `Detections` per image → `MeanAveragePrecision` and `sv.ConfusionMatrix`;
  - caveats: padding when images are processed as a batch, geometric augmentations, contiguous class IDs, and keeping low-confidence predictions for mAP.
  - Added an `## API reference` heading so the new section and the API docs are separate.
- `docs/how_to/benchmark_a_model.md`: link to the new section from "Running a Model".
- `Detections.from_transformers` docstring: says it expects post-processed predictions (`boxes`/`labels`/`scores`), not training targets (`class_labels`), and links to the guide.

Out of scope: no new public API. The conversion is a few lines built on `sv.xcycwh_to_xyxy`, and a `from_*` connector for training targets would depend on whichever collate function a user writes.

## Testing

- Ran the guide's code end to end with a mocked DETR model and image processor (real `torch`, real supervision): the helper gives `[[240. 120. 400. 360.]]` as documented, keeps the `(0, 4)` shape for empty images, and doesn't change its inputs; with matching boxes the loop gives `map50_95 == 1.0` and the expected confusion matrix.
- `uv run pytest -q` → 4277 passed, 24 skipped.
- `uv run pre-commit run --files <changed files>` → all hooks pass.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally (docs only, no new tests)
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [ ] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skipped, docs-only change)

## Additional Notes

The coordinate note follows the [Hugging Face object detection evaluation example](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/tasks/object_detection#preparing-function-to-compute-map), which also restores targets with `orig_size`.

title: fix(dataset): load YOLO labels with a trailing confidence or tracker id
body:
## Description

`sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo` fails on YOLO label files that carry a sixth token after the box. `yolo_annotations_to_detections` treated every line with more than five tokens as a polygon, so a single such row aborted the whole load:

```python
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import supervision as sv

Image.new("RGB", (100, 80)).save("images/a.png")
open("labels/a.txt", "w").write("1 0.5 0.5 0.2 0.4 0.87\n")
open("data.yaml", "w").write("names: ['cat', 'dog']\n")

sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo("images", "labels", "data.yaml")
# ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 5 into shape (2)
```

That sixth column is what Ultralytics `Results.save_txt` writes when `save_conf=True` (`class x y w h conf`) or when tracking is enabled (`class x y w h id`). Five leftover numbers cannot form xy pairs, so the polygon reshape is guaranteed to fail. This PR loads those lines as the same axis-aligned box as the five-column form and ignores the extra token.

## Motivation and Context

People export Ultralytics predictions with `save_txt=True, save_conf=True` (or from `model.track`) and then try to load the labels as a `DetectionDataset`. Ultralytics trains on the first five columns and does not require the sixth; supervision previously could not load the same files. A three-point polygon still needs seven tokens (class plus three xy pairs), so six tokens are unambiguous.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/dataset/formats/yolo.py`: six-token lines (`class x y w h extra`) take the box path using the first four coordinates. `_with_seg_mask` now requires more than six tokens before treating a file as segmentation, so a confidence-only label file no longer forces box-from-polygon masks.
- `tests/dataset/formats/test_yolo.py`: trailing confidence, tracker id, and `np.savetxt` notation load as the expected box; a three-point polygon still builds a mask; `DetectionDataset.from_yolo` loads a `save_conf` label file end to end.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

Out of scope: the extra token is not stored as `confidence` or `tracker_id`, because the sixth column is either a score or an id and the files do not say which. OBB four-corner lines (nine tokens) and polygon lines (seven or more tokens) are unchanged. A seven-token line remains a three-point polygon, not `box + conf + id`.

## Testing

New tests on `develop` (before the fix), 6 failed and 6 passed:

```
FAILED ...::test_loads_box_that_has_a_trailing_token[0.95] - ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 5 into shape (2)
FAILED ...::test_loads_box_that_has_a_trailing_token[3] - ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 5 into shape (2)
FAILED ...::test_loads_box_that_has_a_trailing_token[numpy-savetxt-confidence] - ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 5 into shape (2)
FAILED ...::test_from_yolo_loads_labels_saved_with_ultralytics_save_conf - ValueError: cannot reshape array of size 5 into shape (2)
FAILED ...::test_with_mask[lines5-False-exception5] - assert True == False
FAILED ...::test_with_mask[lines6-False-exception6] - assert True == False
6 failed, 6 passed
```

With this change:

```
$ pytest tests/dataset/formats/test_yolo.py
64 passed
$ pytest tests/dataset/formats
276 passed
$ ruff check && ruff format --check   # on the changed files
All checks passed!
2 files already formatted
```

`mypy` on the changed files reports no errors.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

A six-token OBB `xywhr` line is still not a four-corner OBB and is not handled here. Segmentation `save_txt` with a trailing confidence (odd leftover count after a real polygon) is also left alone, because that form collides with valid polygons.

title: releasing `0.30.5` [rebase & merge]
body:
# 0.30.5: Tracking, metrics, and image-drawing correctness fixes

## 📋 Summary

supervision 0.30.5 is a patch release closing 11 correctness and crash bugs across line-crossing tracking, mAR@K scoring, model connectors, key points, and image drawing/loading — no new public API of note, no breaking changes. The most consequential fixes are silent, not crashes: `LineZone.trigger` miscounted crossings by one per flicker whenever a tracker briefly touched the far side of the line, and `MeanAverageRecall` scored mAR@K against the wrong predictions when a lower-ranked one fit a target more tightly than one within the top K. The remaining fixes close a hard crash in `InferenceSlicer` on conflicting slice metadata (plus two related `Detections.__eq__` bugs), bring the OpenCV-free fallback backend to parity with OpenCV for rotated videos, CMYK images, transparent/1-bit PNGs, and default JPEG/WebP write quality, fix two drawing bugs that reproduce with OpenCV installed (16-bit `draw_image`, grayscale `IconAnnotator` icons), and fix two isolated bugs in `KeyPoints.as_detections` and `plot_images_grid`. Every fix ships a regression test.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### `sv.LineZone.trigger` no longer counts flicker as a crossing

A crossing was confirmed whenever the oldest entry of a `minimum_crossing_threshold + 1` frame history differed from every later entry, which never verified the tracker had actually settled on the side it supposedly came from. With `minimum_crossing_threshold=2` the side sequence `A,A,A,B,A,A,A` counted a crossing *into* `A` — the side the object never left — so counts drifted by one per flicker, in the wrong direction; three separated flickers gave `in_count=3` instead of `0`.

```python
line_zone = sv.LineZone(
    start=sv.Point(0, 0), end=sv.Point(0, 100), minimum_crossing_threshold=2
)
# a tracker that flickers to the far side for one frame and back
# no longer registers a phantom crossing; only a sustained crossing counts
```

Crossings are now measured against the last side a tracker was confirmed on, not against the oldest history entry. Sustained crossings and `minimum_crossing_threshold=1` (the default) are unchanged.

### `sv.metrics.MeanAverageRecall` now scores mAR@K from each image's own top K

The matcher pairs predictions to targets by highest IoU, not confidence, so a prediction ranked below K could take a target away from one ranked within it. Adding a low-confidence duplicate that fit a target more tightly than the top prediction actually *lowered* mAR@1 — one target with a top prediction at IoU `0.71` scored mAR@1 `0.5` alone but `0.0` once a second, unrelated prediction at IoU `1.0` and confidence `0.1` was added. Each detection limit now matches only its own top K predictions.

### `sv.InferenceSlicer` no longer crashes when slices disagree on `metadata`

RF-DETR and `inference`-package connectors attach a `source_image` array per slice; any mismatch across slices previously crashed the merge outright. Any metadata key that isn't identical across every slice is now dropped with a one-time warning naming the dropped keys; `source_image` is reattached afterward as the full input image.

```python
slicer = sv.InferenceSlicer(callback=callback)
detections = slicer(image)  # metadata.source_image is the full input image again
```

Fixing this also closed two `Detections.__eq__` bugs: `NaN` in a float-array metadata value now compares equal to itself, and a list-valued value against an ndarray-valued one now returns `False` instead of raising `ValueError`.

### Rotated videos read upright without OpenCV

OpenCV's FFmpeg backend applies a video's display-rotation matrix to decoded frames and to the reported width/height; the OpenCV-free fallback ignored it, so a portrait phone video came back sideways with its width/height swapped.

### `sv.KeyPoints.as_detections` drops invisible key points from the derived box

`as_detections` stretched each box over every key point that wasn't `[0, 0]` or non-finite, ignoring `visible` — unlike `with_nms`, which already respected it. A pose whose low-confidence joints were predicted off-frame no longer produces an inflated box.

## 🔄 Migration guide

No breaking changes in this release.

No deprecations or removals landed in 0.30.5 either. All scheduled `remove_in` markers in the codebase target `0.31.0` and are untouched by this patch release.

`sv.config.SOURCE_IMAGE_METADATA_FIELD` is a new public constant (added alongside the `InferenceSlicer` fix) naming the `Detections.metadata` key RF-DETR/`inference`-package connectors use for the source image — additive, no existing code needs to change.

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🔧 Fixed

**Tracking / metrics**

- `sv.LineZone.trigger` no longer counts a spurious crossing in the opposite direction when a tracker flickers to the far side of the line for fewer than `minimum_crossing_threshold` frames. Crossings are now measured against the last side a tracker was confirmed on, and once a tracker has a confirmed side, a new one replaces it only after being held for the full threshold. Sustained crossings, `minimum_crossing_threshold=1` (the default), and per-tracker isolation are unchanged. ([#2600](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2600))
- `sv.metrics.MeanAverageRecall` now scores mAR@K from each image's K most confident predictions alone, instead of matching every prediction first and only then keeping the top K by confidence. mAR@1 and mAR@10 now equal the recall of the top 1 and top 10 predictions per image, as documented; mAR@100 changes only for images with more than 100 predictions. ([#2604](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2604))

**Model connectors**

- `sv.InferenceSlicer` no longer raises when slices disagree on `metadata` (e.g. a `source_image` NumPy array attached per-slice by RF-DETR/`inference`-package connectors), which previously crashed the merge outright. Any metadata key that isn't identical across every slice is now dropped from the merged result, with a `SupervisionWarnings` warning naming the dropped keys, emitted once per slicer instance. `source_image` is a special case: removed from each slice before the lenient merge, then reattached afterward as the full input image. Fixing this also closed two related `Detections.__eq__` bugs: metadata holding `NaN` in a float array now compares equal to itself instead of always reading unequal, and comparing a list-valued metadata value against an ndarray-valued one now returns `False` instead of raising `ValueError`. ([#2596](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2596))

**OpenCV-free fallback backend**

- `sv.VideoInfo.from_video_path`, `sv.get_video_frames_generator` and `sv.process_video` now turn a rotated video upright when OpenCV is not installed, as they already do with OpenCV. The fallback now applies quarter and half turns, the same angles OpenCV applies, using the container's display-rotation matrix. Videos without a display rotation, and every read with OpenCV installed, are unchanged. ([#2601](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2601))
- `sv.IconAnnotator` and `sv.draw_image` now draw CMYK JPEG and TIFF images in their colors when OpenCV is not installed, instead of returning the four ink channels as if they were blue/green/red/alpha. Other images, and every read with OpenCV installed, are unchanged. ([#2602](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2602))
- `sv.ImageSink` and the dataset exports that encode in-memory images now write JPEG and WebP files at OpenCV's default quality (JPEG 95, lossless WebP) when OpenCV is not installed, instead of Pillow's defaults (JPEG 75, lossy WebP). The fallback's in-memory encoder also now accepts `.jpe`, `.tif`, `.jp2`, and `.pgm`, which it previously rejected even though file writes already accepted them. PNG and every write with OpenCV installed are unchanged. ([#2592](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2592))
- `sv.IconAnnotator` and `sv.draw_image` now keep the transparency of grayscale PNGs with alpha, RGB PNGs with a transparent color, and 1-bit PNGs, when OpenCV is not installed — the fallback previously returned Pillow's pixel layout for `IMREAD_UNCHANGED` rather than OpenCV's, causing shape-mismatch `ValueError`s or black-drawn transparent pixels. Other images, and every read with OpenCV installed, are unchanged. ([#2588](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2588))

**Annotators / drawing**

- `sv.draw_image` now scales a 16-bit PNG down to 8 bits on load, instead of blending it into an 8-bit scene and clipping channel values above 255 — this reproduces with OpenCV installed, since `IMREAD_UNCHANGED` keeps a 16-bit PNG at 16 bits. Eight-bit images, and images passed as arrays, are drawn as before. ([#2603](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2603))
- `sv.IconAnnotator` now draws grayscale PNG icons instead of failing with `IndexError` — the overlay only handled BGR and BGRA arrays, and `cv2.imread(..., IMREAD_UNCHANGED)` returns a 2-D array for a grayscale PNG without alpha, with or without OpenCV installed. A grayscale icon is now expanded to BGR on load, and a 16-bit icon is scaled to 8 bits, as `cv2.imread` does by default. Eight-bit color icons are drawn as before. ([#2591](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2591))

**Key points / utils**

- `sv.KeyPoints.as_detections` now leaves key points marked not visible out of the box it derives for each skeleton, as `sv.KeyPoints.with_nms` already does. A skeleton with no visible key point is now dropped, as one with only missing key points already was. Key points without `visible` convert as before. ([#2605](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2605))
- `sv.plot_images_grid` now plots a single image in a `grid_size=(1, 1)` grid, instead of failing with `AttributeError` — `plt.subplots` returns a lone `Axes` rather than an array for a 1x1 grid. Grids with more than one cell plot as before. ([#2590](https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/pull/2590))

## 🏆 Contributors

- **kevin** (@kevin9327) — the OpenCV-free fallback backend fixes for rotated video, CMYK, transparent/1-bit images and default JPEG/WebP quality, the 16-bit `draw_image` and grayscale `IconAnnotator` drawing fixes, plus the `MeanAverageRecall`/`plot_images_grid`/`KeyPoints.as_detections` fixes
- **Souptik Chakraborty** (@Souptik96, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/souptikchakraborty/)) — the `LineZone` flicker-crossing fix
- **RAJVARDHAN** (@vardhans07) — the `InferenceSlicer` conflicting-metadata fix and the two `Detections.__eq__` bugs it uncovered

______________________________________________________________________

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/compare/0.30.4...0.30.5

title: perf(detection): dense-fallback fragmented unions

Add _should_union_densely/_union_bbox/_dense_union to compact_mask.py: a cheap O(masks) run-count check flags mask sets fragmented enough that the interval union's O(K log K) sort costs more than a bbox-local dense OR, bounded to a 16 Mi-pixel bbox so it never re-introduces a full-canvas allocation. _compact_mask_union dispatches to this before building intervals; _empty_union factors out the shared all-background result. title: fix: preserve Unicode in CSV detection exports
body:
## Description

CSV detection exports now preserve non-English labels and custom fields on Windows systems whose default encoding is not UTF-8.

Minimal reproduction on a machine using cp1252:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[1, 2, 3, 4]]),
    data={"class_name": np.array(["猫"])},
)
with sv.CSVSink("detections.csv") as sink:
    sink.append(detections)
```

Previously this raised `UnicodeEncodeError`. A label such as `café` could be written but produced bytes that failed to decode as UTF-8.

## Motivation and Context

The same export should be readable as UTF-8 regardless of the machine's locale. The new tests emulate a cp1252 default so they exercise both failures even on systems that already default to UTF-8.

## Changes Made

- Write CSV files with an explicit UTF-8 encoding, retaining `newline=""` and existing CSV quoting.
- Cover accented and Chinese labels alongside quoted, multiline custom data; document the encoding and add a changelog entry.

## Testing

- New regression tests before the fix: 2 failed (`UnicodeDecodeError` and `UnicodeEncodeError`); after: 2 passed.
- `uv run pytest --cov=supervision`: 3,986 passed, 23 skipped, 91% coverage. Used a writable temporary directory on Windows; optional OpenCV reference tests were skipped.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

Consumers that explicitly read exported CSV files using a legacy encoding should switch to UTF-8.

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation

Smoke-test a non-English export by reading it as UTF-8. Changed row counts, broken quoting, or lost text would warrant reverting the change; this library path has no deployment telemetry.

title: fix(utils): convert every Pillow mode to 8-bit BGR or grayscale in `pillow_to_cv2`
body:
## Description

`pillow_to_cv2` passed raw mode bytes through: a 1-bit image came back as `0`/`1`, a 16-bit or 32-bit integer image wrapped modulo 256, `LA`/`PA` crashed `cvtColor` with a two-channel array, and CMYK ink values were drawn as RGB. Every annotator, `crop_image`, `resize_image`, `letterbox_image`, `plot_image` and friends go through this helper when handed a `PIL.Image`.

```python
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import supervision as sv

sv.pillow_to_cv2(Image.new("1", (2, 1), color=1)).tolist()
# develop: [[1, 1]]              this PR: [[255, 255]]
sv.pillow_to_cv2(Image.fromarray(np.array([[55000]], dtype=np.uint16))).tolist()
# develop: [[216]]               this PR: [[214]]   (= cv2.imread of the same 16-bit PNG)
sv.pillow_to_cv2(Image.new("RGB", (1, 1), (10, 20, 30)).convert("CMYK")).tolist()
# develop: [[[225, 55, 245]]]    this PR: [[[30, 20, 10]]]
sv.BoxAnnotator().annotate(Image.new("LA", (20, 20), color=(0, 255)), sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[2, 2, 17, 17]], dtype=np.float32), class_id=np.array([0])))
# develop: cv2.error             this PR: annotated LA image
```

Every mode is now reduced to what `cv2.imread` returns for the same picture: 1-bit becomes `0`/`255`; alpha is dropped (RGBA -> BGR, LA -> grayscale); 16-bit keeps its high byte, as libpng's `png_set_strip_16` does when OpenCV reads a 16-bit PNG as 8-bit (32-bit integers are clipped to the 16-bit range first); `F` is clipped like Pillow's own `convert("L")`; CMYK, YCbCr, HSV and RGBX are converted to color through Pillow. `RGB`, `RGBA`, `L` and `P` are byte-identical to before.

## Motivation and Context

Closes #2613. Same OpenCV-parity stream as #2591, #2592, #2601, #2602 and #2603, for in-memory Pillow images rather than files.

## Changes Made

- `utils/conversion.py`: `pillow_to_cv2` routes single-channel modes (`L`, `1`, `LA`, `La`, `F`) to 8-bit grayscale, deep integer modes (`I`, `I;16*`) to their high byte, and everything else through `convert("RGB")` to BGR. Docstring and doctest.
- `tests/utils/test_conversion.py`: per-mode expectations (1-bit, LA, 16-bit, 32-bit, float, CMYK, HSV, RGBX, PA), YCbCr within Pillow's round-trip tolerance, a real-OpenCV parity test (`pytest.importorskip("cv2")`) comparing against `cv2.imread` of the same picture written to disk, and `BoxAnnotator` on an `LA` scene.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

Out of scope: the annotator wrapper pastes the 8-bit result back into the caller's image, so annotating an `I;16` image in place still yields a dark 16-bit image. That is the paste-back, not the conversion.

## Testing

- New tests on `develop`: the 1-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, CMYK and LA cases fail with the values above; the `LA` annotator case fails with `cv2.error`. With this change they pass.
- Without OpenCV (NumPy fallback): `tests/utils tests/annotators tests/key_points` 735 passed, 1 skipped; full suite 3749 passed, 24 skipped (`develop`: 3737 / 23).
- With OpenCV 5.0: `tests/utils/test_conversion.py` 27 passed, including the on-disk parity test.
- Doctests pass; `ruff`, `docformatter`, `codespell` clean; `mypy` reports the same errors as `develop`.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

While checking parity I found that the OpenCV-free `imread` fallback (`_read_pil_source`, #2602) and `IconAnnotator` (#2591) scale 16-bit with `rint(v / 256)`, whereas OpenCV keeps the high byte; the two differ by one whenever the low byte is >= 128 (5000 -> 20 vs 19). This PR follows OpenCV for `pillow_to_cv2`. Happy to align the fallback in a follow-up if you want them identical.

title: feat(metrics): score `ConfusionMatrix` on masks with `MetricTarget.MASKS`
body:
## Description

`sv.ConfusionMatrix` raised `MetricTarget.MASKS is not currently supported` while `Precision`, `Recall`, `F1Score`, `MeanAveragePrecision` and `MeanAverageRecall` all score masks. An instance segmentation model could only be scored on its boxes, so two instances that share a box but not a shape counted as a match:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MetricTarget

tri = np.tril(np.ones((16, 16), dtype=bool))
target_mask = np.zeros((1, 32, 32), dtype=bool)
predicted_mask = np.zeros((1, 32, 32), dtype=bool)
target_mask[0, 4:20, 4:20] = tri        # lower-left triangle
predicted_mask[0, 4:20, 4:20] = ~tri    # upper-right triangle, same box
box = np.array([[4, 4, 19, 19]], dtype=np.float32)
targets = [sv.Detections(xyxy=box, mask=target_mask, class_id=np.array([0]))]
predictions = [sv.Detections(xyxy=box, mask=predicted_mask, class_id=np.array([0]), confidence=np.array([0.9]))]

sv.ConfusionMatrix.from_detections(predictions, targets, classes=["box"]).matrix
# [[1, 0], [0, 0]]   box IoU is 1.0 -> TP
sv.ConfusionMatrix.from_detections(predictions, targets, classes=["box"], metric_target=MetricTarget.MASKS).matrix
# develop:  ValueError: MetricTarget.MASKS is not currently supported for ConfusionMatrix.
# this PR:  [[0, 1], [1, 0]]   the shapes share no pixel -> FN + FP
```

`from_detections` and `benchmark` now accept `MetricTarget.MASKS` and match by mask IoU (`mask_iou_batch`; dense `(N, H, W)` or `CompactMask`). The validation grids from `benchmark(save_directory_path=...)` fill each mask, so a panel shows the geometry the outcome was decided on.

## Motivation and Context

Closes #238. The direction agreed there was a single `sv.ConfusionMatrix` for boxes and masks; `metric_target` is that switch, it just did not accept masks yet.

## Changes Made

- `metrics/detection.py`: the greedy same-class-first, IoU-descending matching the box and OBB paths used is extracted into `_confusion_matrix_from_iou` and shared by all three targets; `_evaluate_mask_batch` scores one image from `Detections.mask`; `_split_detections_by_outcome` and the grid panels get the mask branch.
- Validation: a non-empty `Detections` without `mask`, or predictions and targets whose masks differ in resolution, raise `ValueError`; `Detections.empty()` needs no masks. `from_detections` also raises when `predictions` and `targets` differ in length instead of silently scoring the shorter list.
- `from_tensors`, `evaluate_detection_batch` and `detections_to_tensor` still reject masks, which have no tensor row layout; the message now points at `from_detections`.
- Docstrings (with a mask doctest) and a changelog entry under Unreleased.

## Testing

- `tests/metrics/test_detection.py::TestConfusionMatrixMasks`, 18 cases: boxes agree / masks disagree, disjoint shapes in one box, multi-class misclassification, IoU threshold applied to mask IoU, confidence filter, empty images without masks, missing-mask and resolution-mismatch errors, length mismatch, `CompactMask` parity with dense, split-by-outcome on masks, `benchmark` grid fills. On `develop` they fail with the `ValueError` above.
- `pytest tests/metrics`: 413 passed. Full suite without OpenCV: 3755 passed, 23 skipped (`develop`: 3737 / 23). Doctests pass; `ruff`, `docformatter`, `codespell` clean; `mypy` reports the same errors as `develop`.
- Real data: `yolo11n-seg` on `coco128-seg` (128 images, 929 GT masks via `DetectionDataset.from_yolo(force_masks=True)`, conf 0.25, IoU 0.5). BOXES: TP 476 / FP 126 / FN 439. MASKS: TP 440 / FP 164 / FN 477. The 36 box matches that fail on mask IoU are mostly `person` (-16), `dining table` (-5) and `umbrella` (-4): boxes that overlap while the shapes do not. Mask IoU over all 128 images took 1.4 s on CPU.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased`

## Additional Notes

#240 (2023) implemented this against the pre-`metric_target` API and has been in conflict since; this PR does not build on it.

title: fix(dataset): reject split ratios outside [0, 1]
body:
## Description

Closes #2610

`DetectionDataset.split()` and `ClassificationDataset.split()` delegate to `train_test_split`, which computed `int(len(data) * train_ratio)` and sliced with it without validating the ratio. A finite out-of-range value therefore looked like a successful split:

```python
import supervision as sv

paths = [f"image_{i}.jpg" for i in range(10)]
dataset = sv.DetectionDataset(
    classes=["object"], images=paths,
    annotations={path: sv.Detections.empty() for path in paths},
)
for ratio in [-0.2, 1.2, 80.0]:
    train, test = dataset.split(split_ratio=ratio, shuffle=False)
    print(ratio, len(train), len(test))
# -0.2 8 2     <- negative slicing
# 1.2 10 0     <- no held-out data
# 80.0 10 0    <- accidental percentage
```

`NaN` and `±inf` already failed, but with `int()` conversion errors (`ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer`, `OverflowError`) rather than a message naming the problem.

### Changes

- `train_test_split` now raises `ValueError` for any ratio outside the inclusive range `[0, 1]`. A single chained comparison covers NaN and `±inf` too (NaN fails both comparisons), so all invalid inputs get the same message: `Expected a split ratio within the inclusive range [0, 1], got -0.2.` The check runs before shuffling or slicing, so an empty dataset is rejected as well.
- Both dataset `split()` methods inherit the fix through the shared helper. No new API, no change to rounding or to valid splits. `0` and `1` remain valid and keep their existing meaning.
- Documented the accepted range and `Raises:` on `train_test_split`, `DetectionDataset.split` and `ClassificationDataset.split`.
- Changelog entry under *Unreleased*.

### Tests

- `tests/dataset/test_utils.py` — `TestTrainTestSplitRatioValidation`: 9 invalid ratios (`-2`, `-0.2`, `-0.01`, `1.01`, `1.2`, `80`, `nan`, `inf`, `-inf`) × both shuffle modes, invalid ratio on empty input, and boundaries `0`/`1` (int and float) preserving their partitions.
- `tests/dataset/test_core.py` — rejection tests added to `TestDetectionDatasetSplit`; new `TestClassificationDatasetSplit` covering the `0`/`1` boundaries and rejection (there were no split tests for `ClassificationDataset` before).

Dataset tests: 374 → 423 passed. Full suite: no new failures vs. `develop`. Existing split tests from #2399 (ratios `0` and `1`) are unchanged and still pass.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

## How has this change been tested, please provide a testcase or example of how you tested the change?

Ran the reproducer above against the branch (`PYTHONPATH=src`):

```text
-0.2 ValueError: Expected a split ratio within the inclusive range [0, 1], got -0.2.
1.2 ValueError: Expected a split ratio within the inclusive range [0, 1], got 1.2.
80.0 ValueError: Expected a split ratio within the inclusive range [0, 1], got 80.0.
nan ValueError: Expected a split ratio within the inclusive range [0, 1], got nan.
0.0 0 10
0.8 8 2
1.0 10 0
```

Plus `pytest tests/dataset`, `pytest --doctest-modules src/supervision/dataset`, and ruff / docformatter / mypy at the versions pinned in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.

## Any specific deployment considerations

None. Callers that relied on out-of-range ratios being silently clamped by slicing will now get a `ValueError`; that was never documented behavior.

## Docs

- [x] Docstrings updated (`Args`/`Raises` on all three functions)
- [x] `docs/changelog.md` updated
