title: perf(detection): keep compact mask NMM unions in RLE form
body:
## Description

Compact-mask NMM currently expands masks back to full images at two points: every greedy candidate update concatenates dense full-frame masks, and final detection merging builds another full-frame union. Consequently, `InferenceSlicer(compact_masks=True, overlap_filter=NON_MAX_MERGE)` can exhaust memory during postprocessing even when its tile masks are small.

This PR performs both unions directly on crop RLE. A private `CompactMask._union()` splits foreground runs at column boundaries, translates them into a tight common crop, and coalesces overlapping intervals. It never decodes pixels. Long counts are split with zero-length opposite runs to preserve the existing int32 representation, including union crops larger than 2**31 pixels.

## Motivation and Context

This completes the compact-mask memory behavior introduced in #2159 for NMM. Collection concatenation was already compact; logical mask union was still dense. No public API changes are needed.

The included benchmark reproduces the problem without models or downloads:

```sh
python examples/compact_mask/benchmark_nmm.py --canvas 512 2048 4096 --repeats 5
```

Twelve fixed 64×64 masks, Windows/Python 3.13, NumPy 2.2.6; median wall time over five calls, with peak traced Python/NumPy allocation measured in separate calls:

| Canvas / pattern | Base time → PR | Base peak → PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096² / solid | 209.5 → 3.9 ms | 96.01 → 0.10 MiB |
| 4096² / checkerboard | 212.5 → 9.5 ms | 96.21 → 0.81 MiB |
| 512² / checkerboard | 6.1 → 10.0 ms | 1.71 → 0.81 MiB |

The same fixed crops on a 100000² logical canvas use 0.10 MiB for solid masks and 0.81 MiB for checkerboards with this change. These are synthetic postprocessing measurements, not model FPS or process RSS. The small-canvas checkerboard case shows the extra interval-processing cost rather than hiding it.

## Changes Made

- Private RLE union and two helpers for foreground intervals and long counts.
- Use the union for incremental NMM candidates and final merged detections.
- Preserve exact dense matching, class grouping, confidence, winner data/tracker IDs, metadata, and foreground outside detection boxes.
- Add 45 tests, a standalone benchmark, compact-mask guide section, and changelog entry.

## Testing

title: fix(key_points): leave invisible key points out of `as_detections` boxes
body:
## Description

`KeyPoints.as_detections` ignores `visible`, so key points you marked as not visible still stretch the box:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

key_points = sv.KeyPoints(
    xy=np.array([[[100, 50], [120, 90], [640, 0]]], dtype=np.float32),
    detection_confidence=np.array([0.9]),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
    visible=np.array([[True, True, False]]),
)
key_points.as_detections().xyxy
# develop:     [[100.   0. 640.  90.]]   the hidden (640, 0) sets two sides of the box
# this branch: [[100.  50. 120.  90.]]
```

`visible` (#2286) is how callers hide unreliable key points without deleting them, as the class docstring suggests: `key_points.visible = key_points.keypoint_confidence > 0.3`. The key point annotators skip hidden points. `with_nms` derives a box per skeleton from key points that are "finite and not all-zero, and its `visible` flag is `True` (if `visible` is set)", and its code comment says "`as_detections` applies the same rule". But `as_detections` only drops `[0, 0]` and non-finite points. For the same `KeyPoints`, the two methods therefore build different boxes, and the one you get from `as_detections` reaches out to points you excluded. Pose models still regress coordinates for joints they aren't confident about, such as legs below the bottom of the frame when a person is cut off at the waist, so those boxes grow toward wherever the model guessed.

This PR adds the `visible` mask to the validity test in `as_detections`, sliced by `selected_keypoint_indices` when those are given. It's the same rule `with_nms` uses.

## Motivation and Context

`as_detections` is the bridge from pose output to everything that takes `Detections`: trackers, zones, box annotators and metrics. A skeleton whose only visible joints are on the upper body should get the box of those joints, and the box it gets there should match the one `with_nms` suppresses with.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/key_points/core.py`: `as_detections` applies `visible`, sliced by `selected_keypoint_indices` when given. The docstring now says which key points are left out.
- `tests/key_points/test_core.py`: `test_key_points_as_detections_ignores_invisible_keypoints`, with all key points and with `selected_keypoint_indices`. A skeleton with one hidden key point gets the box of its visible ones, and a skeleton with no visible key point is dropped.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

A skeleton with no visible key point is now dropped, the same way a skeleton with only `[0, 0]` key points already was (`detections.select(has_valid)`). `KeyPoints` without `visible` convert exactly as before.

## Testing

New test on `develop`:

```
E       (shapes (2, 4), (1, 4) mismatch)
E        ACTUAL: array([[ 10.,  20., 300., 400.],
E              [ 50.,  60.,  90., 100.]], dtype=float32)
E        DESIRED: array([[10., 20., 30., 40.]], dtype=float32)
FAILED tests/key_points/test_core.py::test_key_points_as_detections_ignores_invisible_keypoints[all-keypoints]
FAILED tests/key_points/test_core.py::test_key_points_as_detections_ignores_invisible_keypoints[selected-keypoints]
2 failed
```

With this change:

```
$ pytest tests/key_points src/supervision/key_points
250 passed
$ pytest tests/key_points          # without OpenCV
234 passed      (develop: 232 passed)
$ pytest            # src doctests + tests, OpenCV installed
4107 passed, 1 skipped      (develop: 4105 passed, 1 skipped)
$ ruff check && ruff format --check && docformatter --check   # changed files
All checks passed!
2 files already formatted
```

`mypy` on the changed files reports the same errors on `develop` and on this branch.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

I left the confidence fallback alone. Without `detection_confidence`, the detection's confidence is still the mean `keypoint_confidence` over all (selected) key points, hidden ones included. Whether hidden points should count toward that score seemed like a separate call, so I kept this PR to the box.

title: fix(metrics): score mAR@K from each image's top K predictions only
body:
## Description

`MeanAverageRecall` can lower mAR@1 or mAR@10 when you add a prediction that ranks below the limit:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MeanAverageRecall

targets = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10]], dtype=float), class_id=np.array([0]))
top = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 14]], dtype=float), class_id=np.array([0]), confidence=np.array([0.9]))
duplicate = sv.Detections(xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10]], dtype=float), class_id=np.array([0]), confidence=np.array([0.1]))

MeanAverageRecall().update(top, targets).compute().mAR_at_1                                   # 0.5
MeanAverageRecall().update(sv.Detections.merge([top, duplicate]), targets).compute().mAR_at_1  # 0.0 on develop, 0.5 here
```

The class docstring says "mAR @ 1 considers only the highest confidence detection for each image", and #2136 introduced per-image top-K for that reason. But `_compute` matches **all** of an image's predictions to its targets first, and only then drops the ones ranked below K (`prediction_indices < max_detections`). The shared matcher (`_match_detection_batch_with_target_indices`, #2380) is greedy by highest IoU, not by confidence. So in the example, the `0.1` duplicate with IoU `1.0` takes the target, the `0.9` prediction with IoU `0.71` is left unmatched, and then the duplicate is cut off at K=1. Nothing counts.

pycocotools doesn't have this problem because it matches in score order, so a lower-ranked detection can never take a target from a higher-ranked one. With the IoU-first matcher, the limit has to be applied before matching.

This PR adds `_match_top_predictions`, which runs the same matcher once per detection limit on that image's top K predictions and stores the result along a new last axis of `matches`, `(P, Th, K)`. `_compute_average_recall_for_classes` then reads the slice for each limit. Nothing else changes: not the matcher, not the per-image definition of K, and not the size buckets, which go through the same `_compute`.

## Motivation and Context

Duplicates are the typical trigger: after NMS, two overlapping predictions of the same object can both survive when their mutual IoU is below the NMS threshold, and the less confident one may fit the target more tightly. Crowded images with more than 10 predictions hit the same effect at mAR@10. A random check makes the scale visible. I generated 300 three-image scenes with jittered duplicates and compared `mAR_at_K` against `MeanAverageRecall` run on each image's top-K predictions only, which is the documented definition:

| | mAR@1 differs | mAR@10 differs | mAR@100 differs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `develop` | 168 / 300 | 52 / 300 | 0 / 300 |
| this branch | 0 / 300 | 0 / 300 | 0 / 300 |

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/metrics/mean_average_recall.py`: new `_match_top_predictions`. `_compute` sorts by confidence first and stores per-limit matches, and `_compute_average_recall_for_classes` indexes them by limit. It also gains a docstring.
- `tests/metrics/test_mean_average_recall.py`: `test_mar_at_k_ignores_predictions_ranked_below_k` is the example above: mAR@1 `0.5`, since the top prediction's IoU of `100/140` passes 5 of the 10 thresholds, and mAR@10 and mAR@100 `1.0`.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

## Testing

New test on `develop`:

```
E       assert 0.0 == 0.5 ± 5.0e-07
FAILED tests/metrics/test_mean_average_recall.py::test_mar_at_k_ignores_predictions_ranked_below_k
1 failed
```

With this change:

```
$ pytest tests/metrics/test_mean_average_recall.py
18 passed
$ pytest tests/metrics          # without OpenCV
396 passed      (develop: 395 passed)
$ pytest            # src doctests + tests, OpenCV installed
4106 passed, 1 skipped      (develop: 4105 passed, 1 skipped)
$ ruff check && ruff format --check && docformatter --check   # changed files
All checks passed!
2 files already formatted
```

The existing mAR tests pass unchanged, including `test_complex_integration_scenario` and the per-image top-K tests from #2136. `mypy` on the changed files reports the same errors on `develop` and on this branch.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [ ] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

Matching now runs three times per image, once for each limit, instead of once. Each run only sees up to K predictions, so the extra cost is small next to the IoU matrix, which is computed once as before.

I left the matcher itself alone. `sv.match_detections`, `Precision`, `Recall` and `F1Score` use it on purpose without ranking by confidence, and they don't truncate by rank, so this problem doesn't apply to them.

title: fix(draw): scale 16-bit images down in `draw_image`
body:
## Description

With OpenCV installed, `sv.draw_image` draws a 16-bit PNG with every nonzero channel saturated to `255`:

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision import _cv2 as cv2

logo = np.zeros((8, 8, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
logo[:] = (0, 0, 200)                                   # BGR red
cv2.imwrite("logo16.png", logo.astype(np.uint16) * 257)  # the same red, saved at 16 bits

scene = np.full((20, 20, 3), 50, dtype=np.uint8)
scene = sv.draw_image(scene, "logo16.png", opacity=1.0, rect=sv.Rect(x=5, y=5, width=8, height=8))
print(scene[8, 8])
# develop:     [  0   0 255]
# this branch: [  0   0 201]
```

`draw_image` reads an image path with `cv2.IMREAD_UNCHANGED` to keep the alpha channel. That flag also keeps a 16-bit PNG at 16 bits, but the rest of the function assumes 8 bits: `cv2.convertScaleAbs` saturates both the alpha and the blended pixels to `0..255`, so any 16-bit value from `256` up draws as `255`. A dark gray logo is drawn white, and so is any color whose three channels are all nonzero.

`sv.IconAnnotator` reads its icons the same way, and #2591 added the fix there: `_load_icon_from_path` scales a 16-bit icon down with `np.clip(np.rint(icon / 256), 0, 255)`. This PR applies the same scaling in `draw_image` when it reads an image from a path.

## Motivation and Context

Image editors export 16-bit PNGs when a document is in 16 bits per channel, and a logo or watermark file passed to `draw_image` can be one of them. Without OpenCV, the fallback reader already returns a 16-bit color PNG at 8 bits, because Pillow can't hold 16-bit RGB, so the same call drew correctly there and only the OpenCV path was affected.

## Changes Made

- `src/supervision/draw/utils.py`: after `cv2.imread`, scale a `uint16` image down to `uint8` in the same way as `_load_icon_from_path`. The `image` argument docs say so.
- `tests/draw/test_utils.py`: `test_draw_image_16_bit_file_draws_its_colors`, for BGR and BGRA, returns a 16-bit image from a patched `cv2.imread` (as `TestIconAnnotator.test_draws_16_bit_color_icon` does) and expects the 8-bit colors in the scene. The patch keeps the test independent of which backend is installed, since the fallback can't write 16-bit color PNGs.
- `docs/changelog.md`: entry under Unreleased.

Out of scope: arrays passed directly are drawn as before. The parameter is typed `NDArray[np.uint8]`, and the caller controls what they pass. Grayscale files are still rejected, as the docstring states.

## Testing

New tests on `develop`:

```
E       Mismatched elements: 300 / 1200 (25%)
E        [5, 5, 0]: 255 (ACTUAL), 100 (DESIRED)
E        [5, 5, 1]: 255 (ACTUAL), 50 (DESIRED)
E        [5, 5, 2]: 255 (ACTUAL), 200 (DESIRED)
FAILED tests/draw/test_utils.py::test_draw_image_16_bit_file_draws_its_colors[3]
FAILED tests/draw/test_utils.py::test_draw_image_16_bit_file_draws_its_colors[4]
2 failed
```

It fails the same way without OpenCV, where the fallback's `convertScaleAbs` saturates just as OpenCV's does.

With this change:

```
$ pytest tests/draw/test_utils.py -k 16_bit
2 passed
$ pytest tests/draw tests/annotators          # without OpenCV
383 passed      (develop: 381 passed)
$ pytest            # src doctests + tests, OpenCV installed
4107 passed, 1 skipped      (develop: 4105 passed, 1 skipped)
$ ruff check && ruff format --check && docformatter --check   # changed files
All checks passed!
2 files already formatted
```

`mypy` on the changed source and test files reports the same errors on `develop` and on this branch. I also ran the snippet above on real 16-bit BGR and BGRA PNGs with OpenCV installed: `[0 0 255]` before, `[0 0 201]` after. Without OpenCV, both give `[0 0 200]`.

- [x] Added/updated tests, and the full suite passes locally
- [x] Updated docs (docstrings / mkdocs entry) for new or changed public API
- [x] Added a changelog entry in `docs/changelog.md` under `Unreleased` (skip for lint/type/format-only or pure doc changes)

## Additional Notes

The rounding matches the icon loader, so `200 * 257` becomes `201` rather than the fallback's `200`, which keeps the high byte. I kept the icon loader's rounding rather than add a second convention. The logic is two lines, so I repeated it instead of moving it into a shared helper between `annotators/core.py` and `draw/utils.py`. I'm happy to extract one if you'd prefer.
